signals.title: [Bug][ROCm/gfx942]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash silent retrieval corruption for prompts ≥ ~4-5k tokens (AITER sparse indexer)
signals.text:
## Environment - 8× AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.14.0, amdgpu 6.19.14 - Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (2026-08-12, v0.26.1rc1.dev668+g3ee2df303) - plus local backports of #51821 (merged 08-13) and #52058 / #51252 (open) — reproduces identically without the two open-PR backports - Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, TP=8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, attention backend `DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA` ## 🐛 Describe the bug Needle-in-haystack retrieval works perfectly for short prompts and collapses to 0/3 somewhere between **3,611 tokens (3/3 retrieved)** and **5,294 tokens (0/3)**. Above the threshold the model claims the needles do not exist and output quality degrades broadly (often rambling to `max_tokens`). No crash, no error — **healthy server, silently wrong results**. GSM8K-style short-prompt correctness is unaffected (facts probes pass). Measured (3 needles at 10%/50%/90% depth, `temperature=0`): | prompt tokens | retrieved | |---|---| | 1,913 | 3/3 | | 3,611 | 3/3 | | 5,294 | 0/3 | | 7,003 / 10,411 / 12,061 / 27k / 84k / 253k / 506k | 0/3 (10,411 once gave 2/3 with a corrupted digit string) | ## Ruled out experimentally - `max_model_len` (fails identically at 131,072 and 1,048,576) - chunked-prefill boundary (`max_num_batched_tokens=16384`; 12k prompts are single-chunk and still fail) - #51252 (sparse-indexer prefill buffer budget) — backported, no change on this path - AITER `fp8_mqa_logits` split-KV heuristic (`seq_len_kv >= 4096` → splits>1): forced `num_splits=1`, no change Looks like the gfx942 sibling of #40018 (gfx950 `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` garbage for prompt_len > ~20K), with a lower threshold (~4-5k). ## Repro Self-contained script (generates haystack, inserts 3 needles, checks retrieval): expand below. Run against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: `python3 needle_test.py <api-key> 6000` → RETRIEVED 0/3; `... 4000` → 3/3. <details><summary>needle_test.py</summary> ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """長上下文 needle 測試:產生約 targetTok 的 haystack,插 3 根 needle(10%/50%/90% 深度),要求模型取回。""" import json, time, random, urllib.request, sys KEY = sys.argv[1] TARGET_TOK = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 600_000 MODEL = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "deepseek-v4-flash" random.seed(42) subjects = ["The quarterly report", "A municipal committee", "The research station", "An old lighthouse", "The logistics team", "A regional archive", "The observatory", "A harbor authority", "The botanical survey", "An engineering guild"] verbs = ["documented", "reviewed", "misplaced", "catalogued", "audited", "transferred", "digitized", "inspected", "renovated", "commissioned"] objs = ["seventeen ledgers", "a set of brass instruments", "the annual rainfall data", "three shipping manifests", "the訪客紀錄", "a collection of maps", "the maintenance schedule", "several personnel files", "the calibration records", "an inventory of spare parts"] years = list(range(1951, 2026)) NEEDLES = { "ZEPHYR-CODE": "738291", "MARLIN-KEY": "460517", "ONYX-TOKEN": "092384", } def sentence(): return f"{random.choice(subjects)} {random.choice(verbs)} {random.choice(objs)} in {random.choice(years)}. " # 估 1 token ≈ 4 chars(英文混雜),目標字元數: target_chars = TARGET_TOK * 4 parts, n = [], 0 while n < target_chars: s = sentence() parts.append(s) n += len(s) keys = list(NEEDLES.items()) for frac, (k, v) in zip((0.10, 0.50, 0.90), keys): idx = int(len(parts) * frac) parts.insert(idx, f"[IMPORTANT] The secret value of {k} is {v}. Remember it. ") haystack = "".join(parts) prompt = (haystack + "

---
From the document above, report the secret values of ZEPHYR-CODE, MARLIN-KEY, and ONYX-TOKEN. " "Answer in exactly this format:
ZEPHYR-CODE=<value>
MARLIN-KEY=<value>
ONYX-TOKEN=<value>") print(f"haystack chars: {len(haystack):,}", flush=True) body = {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "max_tokens": 4000, "temperature": 0} req = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}", "content-type": "application/json"}) t0 = time.time() with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=3600) as r: d = json.load(r) dt = time.time() - t0 u = d["usage"] content = d["choices"][0]["message"].get("content") or "" print(f"prompt_tokens={u['prompt_tokens']:,} completion_tokens={u['completion_tokens']} time={dt:.0f}s", flush=True) print("--- model answer ---") print(content[-500:]) ok = sum(1 for k, v in NEEDLES.items() if v in content) print(f"RETRIEVED {ok}/3") ``` </details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary When any GPU kernel on the main stream never terminates, the EngineCore parks forever in `AsyncModelRunnerOutput.get_output()` → `copy_event.synchronize()` — **there is no timeout, no diagnostic, and no recovery**. The engine process stays alive, `/health` keeps returning 200, engine logs go silent, and SIGTERM is ignored (SIGKILL required). In our production fleet this presented as inference instances serving nothing for **14 hours undetected**. The concrete kernel that triggered this for us was flashinfer 0.6.13's `RadixTopKMaskLogitsKernel_MultiCTA` deadlocking on its inter-CTA barrier on SM120 under multi-process GPU contention (details below). That kernel bug is **already fixed** in flashinfer 0.6.16.post3 (bundled from v0.27.0) — we verified our reproducer no longer fires there. **This issue is about vLLM's behavior while the kernel was stuck**, which is unchanged through v0.27.1 and will recur identically with the next never-terminating kernel from any library: ``` # both runners park the same way (captured with py-spy on wedged engines): Thread (idle): "MainThread" synchronize torch/cuda/streams.py:254 ← blocks forever, no timeout get_output vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py:50 (V2 runner) — or — vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:301 (V1 runner) result vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py:38 step_with_batch_queue vllm/v1/engine/core.py:595 ``` Aggravating detail: `_process_aborts_queue()` is the statement immediately after the blocking `result()` in `step_with_batch_queue`, so queued request aborts are never drained once the engine parks — cancellations pile up invisibly. ## How we hit it (production + controlled reproduction) - Production: upgrading 0.22.1 → 0.25.1 flipped our dense Gemma-3/Gemma-4-class models to configurations whose per-step top-k/top-p sampling runs flashinfer's multi-CTA radix kernel. On GPUs shared by several busy instances (time-sliced, no MPS/MIG), three instances wedged the same evening. GPU signature during the wedge: **100% SM utilization at ~100 W with ~0% memory throughput** — a spinning kernel, confirmed with cuda-gdb attached to three independent wedged engines (twice V2 runner, once V1): ``` 0x... in void flashinfer::sampling::RadixTopKMaskLogitsKernel_MultiCTA<1024u, 4u, false, float, int>(...)<<<(88,1,1),(1024,1,1)>>> () Kernel Dev Grid Status GridDim BlockDim Invocation * 0 0 313947 Active ... (88,1,1) (1024,1,1) RadixTopKMaskLogitsKernel_MultiCTA... # SASS at PC: LDG → CCTL.IVALL → YIELD → ISETP.GE → @!P4 BRA (spin re-reading a # RadixRowState arrival counter that never reaches its target) ``` - Controlled reproduction (fires in 1–6 rounds): two `vllm serve` instances of a dense model on ONE SM120 GPU, requests carrying top_k=64/top_p=0.95; per round, against both simultaneously: 250 streaming requests (deep queue via --max-num-seqs 8) → RST-abort all connections at once → repeat → 8 fresh streaming requests. Results across configurations: | configuration (identical dual-instance load) | result | |---|---| | v0.25.1, V2 runner (default) | both engines wedged, round 1 | | v0.25.1, V1 runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | both wedged, rounds 4 and 6 | | v0.25.1, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` | 15/15 + 15/15 clean | | v0.27.1 (flashinfer 0.6.16.post3), sampler ON, V2 | 15/15 + 15/15 clean | Single-instance soak (60 rounds across three engine configurations) never reproduced — the trigger needs multi-process contention, which is also why CI would not see it. ## What I expected A GPU operation that never completes should surface as a loud engine failure within some bounded time — not an engine that accepts connections, reports healthy, ignores SIGTERM, and generates nothing forever. ## Asks 1. **A bounded wait + diagnostic around `AsyncModelRunnerOutput.get_output()`** (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py` and the V1 twin in `gpu_model_runner.py`). Even a generous multi-minute timeout that logs the stall and aborts the engine would turn a silent multi-hour outage into a fast-failing restart that orchestration can see. The sampler deadlock is fixed, but this failure mode is generic: any future stuck kernel (from any library) reproduces it. 2. For released 0.25.x / 0.26.x on SM120 (bundled flashinfer ≤0.6.15): consider a release-note warning recommending `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` under multi-process GPU sharing, and/or merging #44405 for those class of GPUs. ## Related — this failure genus keeps recurring with different kernels Searching for prior reports turned up at least four open issues with the same signature (GPU kernel never terminates → engine wedges silently → health endpoints keep lying), each with a different trigger: - #43885 — GB10, v0.21.0: engine stuck in `get_output()` on a stuck CUDA stream, GPU 96% util at abnormally low power; reporter built the same external watchdog-restart mitigation we did - #40350 — B200/B300 NVFP4 MoE: silently stops generating under concurrency, `/metrics` 200, hangs until externally killed - #49203 — GB10 hybrid model: intermittent livelock, 96% util, 0 tok/s, no crash, no Xid - #50880 — B300, v0.25.1: 100% SM, 0 tok/s, `/health` 200 (different thread state from ours) - #48720 (RFC) — proposes a step-consensus deadlock guard for TP; adjacent in spirit to ask 1 below None of them identifies its kernel; ours does (cuda-gdb capture + SASS), which is why we can show the engine-side behavior is independent of which kernel gets stuck. A bounded wait at the one choke point every one of these reports flows through (`AsyncModelRunnerOutput.get_output()` and its V1 twin) would convert this whole class from silent multi-hour outages into visible fast failures. Kernel-specific references for OUR trigger: - #42987 / #43013 — same flashinfer kernel hanging on SM120 (RTX 5090) at startup (`_dummy_sampler_run`); ours is the runtime variant under multi-process contention - #44405 (open) — default-disable FlashInfer sampler on SM120/SM121 - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4131 / flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3625 (open) — remaining multi-CTA barrier fixes - Full artifacts available: py-spy dumps, cuda-gdb kernel focus + SASS disassembly of the spin loop, per-process SM utilization, and the load generator (stdlib-only Python). Happy to attach or test candidate patches — we have the affected hardware and a reproducer that fires within minutes on 0.25.1.

signals.title: [Bug]: MRv2: --enable-prefix-caching (mamba_cache_mode 'all') + dspark spec decode crashes at startup — prev_last_scheduled_idx never passed by MambaHybridAttnMetadata
signals.text: ### Your current environment ```text vLLM version: v0.27.1 (release tarball, built from source; commit 6e448d0ea9) Platform: Linux aarch64 — NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121a), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.10.0a0+cu130 GPU count: 1 (TP=1) Model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (NemotronHForCausalLM, hybrid Mamba2 + full attention, declares SupportsMambaPrefixCaching) Draft: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark (dspark, num_speculative_tokens=4) ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug On Model Runner V2 (which `dspark` forces via `use_v2_model_runner`, `vllm/config/vllm.py:594-600`), passing `--enable-prefix-caching` without an explicit `--mamba-cache-mode` auto-selects `mamba_cache_mode='all'` for NemotronH (`vllm/model_executor/models/config.py:615-619`), and the engine then **crashes at startup during CUDA graph capture**: ```python (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] AssertionError (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 332, in _initialize_kv_caches (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] self.model_executor.compile_or_warm_up_model() (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 326, in capture (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] forward_fn(CUDAGraphMode.NONE) # PIECEWISE warmup, for_capture=False (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 589, in build_attn_metadata (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] metadata = attn_metadata_builder.build(...) # no prev_last_scheduled_idx (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py", line 985, in conv_ssm_forward (EngineCore pid=217) ERROR [core.py:1349] assert block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step_d is not None ``` Full reproduce command (extracted from the API server log): ```bash vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":4}' \ --mamba-backend flashinfer \ --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \ --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \ --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-num-seqs 3 \ --async-scheduling --trust-remote-code ``` (Also crashes without the mamba-backend/stochastic-rounding extras; `mamba_cache_mode='all'` + spec decode is the trigger. Same crash with `--mamba-backend triton`.) ### Root cause In MRv2, `MambaHybridAttnMetadata.get_extra_attn_kwargs` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py:43-56`) forwards only `num_accepted_tokens` and `num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu` to `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` — it never passes `prev_last_scheduled_idx`. Consequently `_compute_common_metadata` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mamba_attn.py:504-513`) leaves `block_idx_last_scheduled_token_prev_step = None`, and the decode branch of `conv_ssm_forward` asserts when `mamba_cache_mode == "all"` and `num_spec > 0`. The legacy V1 runner handles this correctly: it allocates `self.mamba_prev_last_scheduled_idx` when `mamba_cache_mode == "all" and num_spec_tokens > 0` and passes it through (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:948-951` and `:2518-2525`). Only the MRv2 path (`model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`) is missing the wiring — consistent with MRv2 having only 'align' support wired so far (#42406). ### Expected behavior Either of: 1. MRv2 passes `prev_last_scheduled_idx` so `'all'` + spec decode works, or 2. `'all'` + spec decode is rejected/falls back to `'align'` at config validation time, instead of an assertion crash during engine init. Option 2 matches the direction from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39809 (that issue covered the V1-runner crashes on v0.19.0; this is the MRv2 equivalent on v0.27.1 — a different assert site). ### Additional context Workaround confirmed working on the same hardware/model: ```bash --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align ``` Engine starts, dspark stays active, prefix cache hits verified end-to-end (identical 37.6k-token prompt: cold prefill 5.71 s → warm 0.85 s, ~33.3k tokens served from cache, byte-identical outputs at temperature 0). FYI for hybrid users: with this model/KV config the scheduler block size is forced to 2304 tokens (mamba page size vs fp8 attention KV bytes, `vllm/platforms/interface.py:895-918`), and `use_eagle()` (true for dspark) holds back one block in `last_cache_position` (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:389-394`), so prompts shorter than ~2 blocks (~4.6k tokens) never register a hit — worth documenting even once 'all' mode is fixed.

signals.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4 FlashMLA sparse prefill phase1.cuh:614 on H20-3e TP8 at ~161K context
signals.text: ### Your current environment - **GPU**: 8× NVIDIA H20-3e - **vLLM**: 0.26.0 - **Image**: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0-w4a16-patched2` - **Model**: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a16` - **Parallelism**: TP=8, expert parallel enabled - **KV cache dtype**: FP8 - **Block size**: 256 - **Max model length**: 614400 - **Chunked prefill**: enabled (`max_num_batched_tokens=8192` from startup log) - **Max num seqs**: 32 - **Speculative decoding**: ```json { "method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "draft_sample_method": "greedy" } ``` Relevant launch arguments: ```bash vllm serve /data/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a16 \ --tensor-parallel-size=8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --max-model-len=614400 \ --gpu-memory-utilization=0.85 \ --kv-cache-dtype=fp8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --max-num-seqs=32 \ --block-size=256 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser=deepseek_v4 \ --speculative-config='{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}' ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` crashes during the FlashMLA **SM90 sparse prefill** path with a TMA descriptor initialization failure. All 8 TP workers report the same assertion and the EngineCore exits. This looks related to #49922 / #50660 / #49883, but I am filing separately because this reproduction is on **H20-3e, TP=8** and occurs at only about **161K context**, rather than only at very large (>600K) prefills. Immediately before the crash, FlashMLA prints: ```text TMA Desc Addr: 0x7ffcc4269000 format 9 dim 3 gmem_address 0 globalDim (512,64,0,1,1) ... Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor Assertion `res == CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS` failed (/workspace/.deps/flashmla-src/csrc/sm90/prefill/sparse/instantiations/../phase1.cuh:614) ``` The worker traceback reaches: ```text vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py -> forward_mqa vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py -> _forward_prefill vllm/third_party/flashmla/flash_mla_interface.py -> flash_mla_sparse_fwd flash_mla_cuda.sparse_prefill_fwd -> sm90/prefill/sparse/phase1.cuh:614 ``` All TP workers then fail with: ```text RuntimeError: Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/flashmla-src/csrc/sm90/prefill/sparse/instantiations/../phase1.cuh:614): Assertion `res == CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS` failed. ``` ### Scheduler state at the failing step The V1 engine dump at the crash shows two cached/running requests: ```text num_computed_tokens=[27019, 161008] num_scheduled_tokens: request A: 8 request B: 312 total_num_scheduled_tokens=320 ``` So one request had already computed about **27K** tokens, while the second had computed about **161K** tokens and was scheduled for another **312** tokens in that step. This appears to be a **mixed decode + chunked-prefill** iteration, which may be a useful trigger condition to investigate. I am not claiming that mixed batching is the root cause; this is only the scheduler state captured at the failing iteration. ### Memory does not look exhausted Startup reported: ```text Available KV cache memory: 92.93 GiB GPU KV cache size: 6,819,501 tokens Maximum concurrency for 614,400 tokens per request: 11.10x ``` The scheduler dump at the failing iteration reported: ```text kv_cache_usage=0.0100178 ``` So this does not look like a KV-cache OOM condition. ### Reproducibility I have observed the same `phase1.cuh:614` / `Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor` crash more than once on this deployment. The service starts normally and can serve requests before the crash occurs. ### Related issues / possible fix This looks very close to #49922 and #50660. In #49922, `de6ec294ef07` / #49302 is discussed and reported to fix the zero-query / phantom-request condition on other hardware. I have **not yet verified** whether `v0.26.0-w4a16-patched2` contains that change, nor whether cherry-picking it fixes this H20-3e reproduction. If maintainers believe this is the same root cause, I am happy for this issue to be marked duplicate. The main additional data point here is that the same TMA descriptor shape (`gmem_address=0`, zero extent) is reproducible on **H20-3e TP8 around 161K context** during a mixed decode/chunked-prefill step. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I searched existing issues and found #49922, #50660 and #49883. I am filing this separately because of the different hardware and significantly lower context length / scheduler state at failure.

signals.title: [Bug]: Client stop strings match inside the reasoning segment for think-in-prompt models, truncating CoT and yielding content=None
signals.text: ### Your current environment Reproduced on 0.21.1 and 0.25.2.dev (V1 engine), 2x DGX Spark GB10 TP=2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4` and `--reasoning-config '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"<think>","reasoning_end_str":"</think>"}'`. The mechanism is model-agnostic for any think-in-prompt template (DeepSeek V4, Qwen3-style). ### 🐛 Describe the bug With think-in-prompt templates, generation begins INSIDE the reasoning segment. The V1 detokenizer evaluates client `stop` strings against the whole output stream, so a stop string that the chain-of-thought naturally restates fires mid-`<think>`: `</think>` never arrives, the reasoning parser cannot close the segment, and the response returns `content: None` with `finish_reason: stop`. This is easy to hit unintentionally at scale: lm-evaluation-harness sends `stop[:4]` (e.g. `"Question:"`) on every request, and CoT loves restating `Question:`. On GSM8K n=50 at temp 0.6 we measured 8-15/50 responses decapitated this way (score 0.66-0.84); with stops suppressed inside reasoning it dropped to 1/50 nulls (0.98). Hosted deployments of the same checkpoints are immune because they scope stops to content — that behavior gap is the bug. It also masquerades as a model failure ("the model returned nothing"), which cost the community significant misdiagnosis time (see tonyd2wild/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-0731-DSpark-1M-NVFP4-KV-2x-DGX-Spark issue #18, where ~30% of eval nulls traced to this). ### Repro sketch 1. Serve any think-in-prompt reasoning model with a reasoning parser configured. 2. Send a request whose prompt ends inside `<think>` (standard chat template behavior with thinking enabled) plus `stop: ["Question:"]` and a prompt the model will deliberate about. 3. When the CoT restates "Question:", the response truncates mid-reasoning: no `</think>`, `content: None`. ### Expected behavior Stop strings should stay dormant while the reasoning segment is open and be evaluated only against text FOLLOWING the reasoning end marker (matching hosted-API behavior). EOS and max_tokens unaffected; non-thinking requests untouched. One subtlety for spec decoding: `update()` receives up to k+1 tokens per step, so the chunk that carries the end marker also carries the reasoning that precedes it — on closing, the stop-check offset must advance past the marker or a stop in the last <=k reasoning tokens still fires. ### Existing community fix A per-request guard implementing exactly this (markers from `--reasoning-config` with `<think>`/`</think>` fallback, process-wide opt-out env var, spec-decode one-chunk handling) has been running in production in the DSpark community for 10+ days across vLLM 0.21.1 and a 0.25.2.dev port: patch at tonyd2wild/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-0731-DSpark-1M-NVFP4-KV-2x-DGX-Spark `patches/0005-suppress-stops-in-reasoning.patch` (and PR #32 there for 0.25.x trees). Happy to adapt it into a proper vLLM PR with tests if maintainers agree with the direction — main design question is whether the guard should be default-on (hosted-parity) or opt-in via a sampling/serving flag. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

I could not confirm against a recent `main` build (recent main builds don't include this job in their step subset), so this is not verified as "failing on main". Signals suggesting an environment/node issue rather than a code issue: - The AMD mirror of the same suite (`AMD: Multi-Modal Models (Standard 4, other + whis…`) **passed** in the same build. - The PR's diff ([#52311](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52311)) touches only the Model Runner V2 bad-words sampler kernel + a new unit test; the failure happens during gemma4 engine-core warmup, before any sampling. - Both runs show `TritonBundler` "Cubin file saved by TritonBundler not found" warnings pointing at the same cached `torch_compile_cache` hash dirs immediately before the crash, i.e. the node(s) are reusing a stale/poisoned AOT compile cache. - The crash itself is a PyTorch-internal NVML assert (`please report a bug to PyTorch`). ### Failure signature Engine core init fails during model warmup forward (`compile_or_warm_up_model` → gemma4 `torch.clamp`): <details> <summary>Logs:</summary> ```text (EngineCore pid=18815) ERROR [core.py:1344] File ".../transformers/models/gemma4/modeling_gemma4.py", line 192, in forward (EngineCore pid=18815) ERROR [core.py:1344] hidden_states = torch.clamp(hidden_states, self.output_min, self.output_max) (EngineCore pid=18815) ERROR [core.py:1344] RuntimeError: NVML_SUCCESS == r INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at "/__w/pytorch/pytorch/c10/cuda/CUDACachingAllocator.cpp":1407, please report a bug to PyTorch. preceded by repeated: (EngineCore pid=17850) W torch/_inductor/triton_bundler.py:242] RuntimeError: ('Cubin file saved by TritonBundler not found at %s', '/root/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/83690e9e.../inductor_cache/triton/0/.../triton_red_fused_1.cubin') test summary: FAILED models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_vit_cudagraph_image[gemma4] - RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. signals.title: [Bug]: 4 B200 GPU ，DP 4 + EP（or TP 4 + EP），Deepseek V4 Flash 0731 , simultaneously processing hundreds of text extraction tasks, outputting garbled characters.
signals.text: ### Your current environment Ubuntu 22.04, vllm docker v0.27.1 image, B200 server ### 🐛 Describe the bug I used four B200 GPUs, with Ubuntu 22.04 as the operating system, and the latest Docker image for VLLM, vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1. I started the DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 model (https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) using the following docker-compose.yml ``` # DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on the host's B200 GPUs 4,5,6,7. # The model directory on the host must contain config.json and the weight files. # Before starting, create ./cache/vllm, or set: # VLLM_CACHE_DIR=/fast-nvme/vllm services: vllm: image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1 container_name: deepseek-v4-flash-0731 init: true restart: unless-stopped ipc: host network_mode: host stop_grace_period: 2m environment: NCCL_DEBUG: "${NCCL_DEBUG:-WARN}" volumes: - /data/deepseek:/models/deepseek:ro # Put the compilation cache on fast local NVMe in .env for production use. - "${VLLM_CACHE_DIR:-./cache/vllm}:/root/.cache/vllm" ulimits: memlock: soft: -1 hard: -1 deploy: resources: reservations: devices: # Prefer the four GPU UUIDs here if host indices may change. - driver: nvidia device_ids: ["4", "5", "6", "7"] capabilities: [gpu] # The image ENTRYPOINT is already `vllm serve`. command: - /models/deepseek - --served-model-name - deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 - --host - 0.0.0.0 - --port - "7800" # Model and KV cache. - --trust-remote-code - --kv-cache-dtype - fp8 - --block-size - "256" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.95" - --max-model-len - auto # Throughput-oriented layout for four dedicated B200s: DP4 + EP. - --data-parallel-size - "4" - --enable-expert-parallel - --enable-ep-weight-filter - --moe-backend - deep_gemm_mega_moe - --attention-config - '{"use_fp4_indexer_cache":true}' # Scheduler and Blackwell compilation settings from the vLLM recipe. - --max-num-batched-tokens - "8192" - --max-num-seqs - "256" - --compilation-config - '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' # DeepSeek-V4 OpenAI-compatible tool calling and reasoning. - --tokenizer-mode - deepseek_v4 - --tool-call-parser - deepseek_v4 - --enable-auto-tool-choice - --reasoning-parser - deepseek_v4 - --reasoning-config - '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"","reasoning_end_str":""}' - --disable-uvicorn-access-log ``` **Then I wrote a simple Python script named "X.py" to request this large model API. The script's task was to process hundreds of document content extraction programs in parallel.** The documents came from the website [3gpp](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs). While running this script, I connected to this large model API using OpenCode. The contents of opencode.json are as follows: ``` { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "model": "vllm/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", "provider": { "vllm": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "name": "Local vLLM", "options": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:7800/v1" }, "models": { "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731": { "name": "DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 Max", "limit": { "context": 1048576, "input": 655360, "output": 393216 }, "reasoning": true, "tool_call": true, "interleaved": { "field": "reasoning" }, "options": { "reasoningEffort": "max" } } } } }, "agent": { "build": { "model": "vllm/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95 }, "plan": { "model": "vllm/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731", "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95 } } } ``` **I first used OpenCode to connect to this large model API, and the model output was normal. I used it normally for half a day. Then I ran X.py, then launched OpenCode, and asked a question in OpenCode, but the model output was all garbled characters. I tried creating a new dialogue in OpenCode and asking a question, but the model output was still garbled. After that, I stopped x.py and then asked a question on OpenCode. The model output was normal.** **After that, I stopped the container and modified the docker-compose.yml file to use 4 tensor parallelism + expert parallelism.** After running X.py and using OpenCode to connect to the large model API, it worked normally for a while, but suddenly the output of the large model started to become garbled again. I tried creating a new dialogue in OpenCode and asking a question, but the model output was still garbled. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, loading an NVFP4 (`modelopt_fp4`) model crashes at engine initialization. Batch invariance disables the hardware NVFP4 kernels and forces the emulation MoE backend, and that path's `break_fp4_bytes` indexes a CPU lookup table with GPU indices, raising a device-mismatch `RuntimeError`. Without `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the same model loads and serves normally. ### Minimal reproduction ```python import os os.environ["VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT"] = "1" from vllm import LLM # NVFP4 / modelopt_fp4 model — crashes during engine init, before any generation llm = LLM(model="nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4", max_model_len=8192) ``` Any `modelopt_fp4` / NVFP4 model reproduces it, since the failure is in the shared NVFP4 emulation utility rather than the model. ### Observed result The engine core fails to initialize (under `vllm serve` the container crash-loops; it never reaches "Application startup complete"). Relevant log line + traceback: ``` [nvfp4.py:283] Using 'EMULATION' NvFp4 MoE backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL', 'FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'VLLM_CUTLASS', 'MARLIN', 'EMULATION']. ... File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/nvfp4_emulation_utils.py", line 38, in break_fp4_bytes values = kE2M1[abs_vals] * torch.where(signs, -1.0, 1.0) RuntimeError: indices should be either on cpu or on the same device as the indexed tensor (cpu) ... RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. ``` ### Root cause (suspected) In `break_fp4_bytes`, the lookup table `kE2M1` comes from `kE2M1ToFloat_handle.val` (CPU) and is indexed by `abs_vals` (GPU): ```python abs_vals = (combined & 0x07).to(torch.long) # on GPU kE2M1 = kE2M1ToFloat_handle.val # on CPU # Device-aware lookup and sign application values = kE2M1[abs_vals] * torch.where(signs, -1.0, 1.0) # CPU tensor indexed by GPU indices ``` The comment says "Device-aware lookup," but `kE2M1` is never moved to the indices' device. ### Suggested fix ```python kE2M1 = kE2M1ToFloat_handle.val.to(abs_vals.device) ``` ### Expected behavior `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` should either work with NVFP4 (the deterministic emulation path runs), or fail fast with a clear "batch invariance not supported for this quantization" message, rather than crash at engine init with a device-placement error. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

This is a parser-only reproduction against vLLM source commit [`925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749); it does not require a model or GPU. ## 🐛 Describe the bug Gemma 4 has two different defaults for an omitted `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`: - The [reasoning documentation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749/docs/features/reasoning_outputs.md#L31-L35) says Gemma 4 reasoning is disabled by default. - The [bundled Gemma 4 chat template](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749/examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja#L177-L181) uses `enable_thinking | default(false)`. - The [Gemma4 parser](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749/vllm/parser/gemma4.py#L396-L404) instead uses `chat_kwargs.get("enable_thinking", True)`. As a result, when a request omits the flag, the template produces a non-thinking prompt but the parser behaves as if thinking was enabled. This is directly observable in [`is_reasoning_end`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749/vllm/parser/gemma4.py#L458-L477) for a prompt ending at a new model turn. Minimal reproduction: ```python from vllm.parser.gemma4 import Gemma4Parser class FakeTokenizer: bos_token_id = None eos_token_id = None pad_token_id = None def __init__(self): self._vocab = { "<|channel>": 100, "": 101, "<|tool_call>": 102, "": 103, "<|turn>": 104, "<|tool_response>": 105, } def get_vocab(self): return self._vocab def decode(self, token_ids): inverse = {value: key for key, value in self._vocab.items()} return "".join( inverse.get(token_id, f"") for token_id in token_ids ) tokenizer = FakeTokenizer() new_model_turn = [tokenizer.get_vocab()["<|turn>"]] for kwargs in ({}, {"enable_thinking": False}, {"enable_thinking": True}): parser = Gemma4Parser(tokenizer, chat_template_kwargs=kwargs) print( kwargs, "thinking_enabled=", parser._thinking_enabled, "reasoning_ended=", parser.is_reasoning_end(new_model_turn), ) ``` Actual output on the commit above: ```text {} thinking_enabled= True reasoning_ended= False {'enable_thinking': False} thinking_enabled= False reasoning_ended= True {'enable_thinking': True} thinking_enabled= True reasoning_ended= False ``` Expected output for the omitted case: ```text {} thinking_enabled= False reasoning_ended= True ``` The omitted case should resolve to the same policy as explicit `enable_thinking=False`; explicit `enable_thinking=True` should continue to enable reasoning. This would keep the parser aligned with the template, the documentation, and the [`reasoning_effort` request handling](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py#L582-L588). The closest issues I found are #39130 (structured output with explicit `enable_thinking=false`) and #48217 (channel-less output with explicit `enable_thinking=true`). Neither covers the omitted flag resolving to the opposite default from the Gemma 4 template. Downstream context: ai-dynamo/dynamo#12287 and ai-dynamo/dynamo#13061 gate Gemma 4 reasoning parsing on an explicit effective enable signal to avoid this mismatch. ## Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Alignment specialization on causal_conv1d metadata pointers forces inference-time JIT compiles; raced shared-cache writes produced silent all-NaN outputs
signals.text: ### Summary `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` let Triton specialize on the 16-byte alignment of their metadata pointers (`cache_indices_ptr`, `query_start_loc_ptr`, `conv_state_indices_ptr`, ...). Three facts make this a problem: 1. **The specialization buys nothing here.** These arrays are read one scalar at a time (a block index, an offset), so the aligned and unaligned binaries run at the same speed. Alignment specialization only pays off for wide vectorized loads (`x_ptr`, `w_ptr`, ... — not these args). 2. **Their alignment flips at runtime.** They are per-step slices of batch metadata, so the address offset depends on the batch layout of that step. 3. **Warmup can never cover the unaligned variant.** Warmup tensors are freshly allocated and therefore always aligned. So the first compile of the unaligned variant is guaranteed to happen *during inference* — this is (part of) the latency spike tracked in #43009, and `jit_monitor` (#45631) duly warns about it. In a multi-node deployment this goes from a latency nuisance to a correctness bug. ### What we hit GRPO RL training, Nemotron-3-Super-120B, 6 vLLM engines on 6 GB200 nodes, with a shared `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` on Lustre (for warm starts). Engines intermittently returned **all-NaN logits from the first prefill token** — only for long prompts, only on some engines, and unreproducible afterwards. Disk forensics (no repro needed): - These kernels compiled to disk exactly 3 times; the mtimes match the 3 NaN windows one-to-one. After the cache filled up: 40+ clean rounds, zero recurrence. - Two cache hash dirs for the same kernel appeared **within the same minute**, differing only in the `tt.divisibility=16` attribute on `cache_indices_ptr` — two nodes concurrently compiling the aligned/unaligned variants into the same shared dir. Triton's cache group write (`__grp__*.json` + cubin) is not atomic across writers. - Every failing request was ≥143K tokens (its `cache_indices` slice lands at an unaligned offset); every success ≤138K. Only some engines were poisoned — the race losers. A race loser ends up running the aligned-assumption binary on unaligned `cache_indices` → reads wrong block indices → garbage → all-NaN logits, silently. Sharing `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` across nodes is on us, and we now scope it per node. But the variant axis itself has no upside, and single-node users still pay the inference-time compile spike for it. ### Proposed fix Add the metadata pointers to `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` — the same mechanism #50000 already applied to `num_cache_lines` in these exact kernels: ```python @triton.jit(do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[ "num_cache_lines", "cache_indices_ptr", "has_initial_states_ptr", "query_start_loc_ptr", "batch_ptr", "token_chunk_offset_ptr", "block_idx_first_scheduled_token", "block_idx_last_scheduled_token", "initial_state_idx", "num_computed_tokens", ]) def _causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel(...) @triton.jit(do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[ "num_cache_lines", "batch", "conv_state_indices_ptr", "num_accepted_tokens_ptr", "query_start_loc_ptr", "block_idx_last_scheduled_token", "initial_state_idx", ]) def _causal_conv1d_update_kernel(...) ``` Effect: one binary per config, compiled without the alignment assumption, correct for any address. Warmup covers it naturally, nothing left to JIT during inference, no variants to race. Zero perf cost (scalar loads only); the wide data pointers keep their specialization. Relation to #48363: complementary. That PR warms the fwd kernel by sweeping 8 alignment combinations; with the specialization removed the sweep collapses to a single call, and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` (not covered there) is fixed as well. We're happy to open a PR (change verified against Triton 3.6: the flag drops the divisibility bit from the specialization key for pointer args, `triton/runtime/jit.py`). ### Environment Observed on vLLM 0.25.1 (aarch64, GB200, Triton 3.6.0); the kernel decorators are unchanged on current `main` (f97e502969).

signals.title: [Bug] XPU qnorm/rope kernel: overlapping stores in one program corrupt the KV cache nondeterministically
signals.text: **File:** `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_qnorm_rope_kv_fp8_insert.py` **Confirmed present in v0.27.1** (tag `6e448d0ea9bf`) and on `main`. ## Summary In the KV branch, the kernel stores all 512 elements of `kv` — RoPE region included, still unrotated — and then overwrites that region with the rotated values at stride-2 addresses: ```python # lines 93-94 kv_full = tl.load(kv_base + offs) tl.store(kv_out_base + offs, kv_full) # writes the unrotated rope region ... # lines 106-107 tl.store(kv_out_base + even_offs, new_even) # overwrites it, stride-2 addresses tl.store(kv_out_base + odd_offs, new_odd) ``` Two stores to the same addresses within one program, with different lane-to-address mappings and no ordering between them. Nothing guarantees the rotated store wins. ## Evidence On MTT S5000 (MUSA), 4096 tokens × 64 heads, compared against FlagGems' fused kernel, which is byte-exact against the pure-torch reference on the same inputs: - **30 tokens** of 4096 have a cache RoPE region that differs - **29 of those 30** hold values exactly equal to the **unrotated** `kv` — i.e. the bulk store landed last - the remaining one is partially overwritten, consistent with a lane-granular race - a **second run on identical inputs gives 29, not 30** — nondeterministic Concretely, token 96: the cache holds `[1.023, 0.262, -1.516, -0.277]`, exactly the raw `kv` values, where the correct rotated values are `[-0.441, 0.961, 1.531, -0.132]`. ## Fix One line, and it is also cheaper — mask the bulk copy so the overlap never exists: ```python tl.store(kv_out_base + offs, kv_full, mask=offs < NOPE_DIM) ``` This skips 64 redundant stores per KV token as well. With it applied, output is byte-identical to the reference. ## Note XPU scheduling may simply never expose this, but the ordering assumption does not hold on any backend. We found it because MUSA schedules differently.
signals.author: cheersluvs

signals.title: [Bug] XPU qnorm/rope kernel: int32 overflow in the address computation past 2^31 q elements
signals.text: **File:** `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_qnorm_rope_kv_fp8_insert.py`, lines 40-41 and 57 **Confirmed present in v0.27.1** (tag `6e448d0ea9bf`) and on `main`. ## Summary `tl.program_id` is left as int32: ```python token_idx = tl.program_id(0) # int32 head_idx = tl.program_id(1) ... q_base = q_ptr + token_idx * num_heads * HEAD_DIM + head_idx * HEAD_DIM ``` so `token_idx * num_heads * HEAD_DIM` is computed in 32 bits and wraps once `q` exceeds 2^31 elements. ## Evidence The boundary matches the arithmetic to within one token. `(num_tokens - 1) * num_heads * 512` versus 2^31 = 2,147,483,648, against what we observed on MUSA: | shape | max offset | | observed | |---|---|---|---| | 65536 × 64 | 2,147,450,880 | fits, by 32768 | **works** | | 65536 × 128 | 4,294,901,760 | overflows | fails | | 98304 × 64 | 3,221,192,704 | overflows | fails | | 98304 × 128 | 6,442,385,408 | overflows | fails | | 131072 × 64 | 4,294,934,528 | overflows | fails | | 131072 × 128 | 8,589,869,056 | overflows | fails | Failure surfaces as `RuntimeError: MUSA error: unknown error`. FlagGems' kernel runs correctly at every one of these shapes because it casts the program id. ## Fix ```python token_idx = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) head_idx = tl.program_id(1).to(tl.int64) ``` ## Note Not backend-specific — a 32-bit wrap will corrupt or crash anywhere. 131072 tokens × 128 heads is an ordinary prefill size for this model, so we suspect the implementation was only exercised at small shapes. The same is true of VLLM-1: both defects are invisible below a few thousand tokens.

signals.title: [Bug][ROCm] Kimi-K3 a8w4 SiTU MoE: AITER_SITUV2_A8W4 without VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4 silently produces garbage
signals.text: ## Summary On ROCm/gfx950 (MI350X), running **Kimi-K3** (2.8T MXFP4 compressed-tensors, SiTU MoE) with the AITER a8w4 fp8-activation MoE produces **silent degenerate garbage** (e.g. `2 + 2 =` → `' 0. 4. 0. 0. 4'`, `The capital of France is` → `' the 4. The (B. 1'`) whenever the aiter-library flag is enabled but the matching vLLM flag is not. The two flags are separately named and easy to mismatch: | env var | layer | effect when set | |---|---|---| | `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` | aiter library | forces `q_dtype_a=fp8` → selects the afp8 `_gui_` gate/up **interleave** FlyDSL MoE kernel | | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4` | vLLM (`is_fused_moe_situv2_a8w4_enabled()`) | interleaved weight **shuffle** in `Mxfp4MoEMethod._convert_k3_situ_weight_to_kernel_format` (`guinterleave=True`) + `gate_mode=INTERLEAVE` | Setting **only** `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1` makes aiter run the interleave kernel, but vLLM shuffles the weights in the **separated** layout (because `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4` defaults to `0`) → interleave-kernel-reads-separated-weights → silent garbage. No error, no warning. ## Root cause confirmation Instrumented `aiter.fused_moe.fused_moe`: with only `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1` set, the call arrives with `gate_mode=separated` while aiter has already chosen the afp8 `_gui_` (interleave) kernel — that layout mismatch is the whole failure. Verified the afp8 kernel itself is correct via an isolated harness (real K3 experts, afp8-gui vs abf16-separated vs torch ref → cos 0.9991), so this is purely the env/shuffle mismatch, not a kernel bug. ## Fix / workaround Setting **`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1`** resolves it (vLLM then shuffles interleaved to match the kernel). Correct + fast afterwards (2954 tok/s @ N=256 aggregate on 8×MI350X). `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` is *not* required. ## Request Guard against the silent-mismatch: either 1. have `Mxfp4MoEMethod` derive the interleave layout from `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` as well (so the shuffle always matches the kernel aiter will pick), **or** 2. emit a warning/hard error when `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` is set but `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4` is not (K3 SiTU MoE), since the combination silently corrupts output. Env: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (v0.27.2rc1.dev77+gac7509e2b), ROCm 7.2.3, 8×MI350X (gfx950), Kimi-K3 mxfp4, `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
signals.author: stefanskiasan

signals.title: [Bug]: Harmony browser.* streaming emits both MCP and web-search events
signals.text: ### Your current environment vLLM `0.27.2rc1.dev100+g925ea7e60.d20260815`, Python 3.12.13, macOS arm64. This is a platform-independent streaming-event classification issue. ### 🐛 Describe the bug In the Harmony Responses API streaming path, a `browser.*` recipient is first classified as an MCP call and later handled again as a built-in browser action. As a result, one `browser.search` call emits both: ```text response.mcp_call.* response.web_search_call.* ``` It should emit only the `response.web_search_call.*` lifecycle. The cause is `is_mcp_tool_by_namespace()` in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/streaming_events.py`. It classifies every non-function recipient as MCP, including `browser.*`. The same completed message is subsequently handled by `emit_tool_action_events()`, which correctly emits the web-search events. The existing TODO in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py` identifies the problem: ```python # TODO: Fix browser emitted as MCP calls ``` The fix should exclude `browser.*` recipients from MCP classification and add a regression test ensuring that browser calls emit only web-search events. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature]: Support NVFP4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with FP4 KV cache + DSpark speculative decoding on SM121 (DGX Spark)
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Summary Requesting first-class support for serving **NVFP4** DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoints (e.g. `Rarri/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4`) with **FP4 KV cache** (`nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla`) **and DSpark speculative decoding** on SM121 (NVIDIA GB10 / DGX Spark, 2-node TP=2). Today this combination does not work on vLLM main. We currently run it on a fork of jasl's branch (PR #41834) which serves the NVFP4 checkpoint but **cannot** do DSpark speculative decoding with it (draft loader fails with `KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_input_scale'`). vLLM main v0.27.1 fails earlier at startup on SM121 with the DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation" error (see #51884). ## Environment - **Hardware**: 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), compute capability 12.1 / SM121, Linux ARM64, two-node TP=2 - **Model (NVFP4)**: `Rarri/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4` - ModelOpt mixed-precision conversion: `producer: dsv4-nvfp4-experts-mtp-fallback` - `quant_method: fp8`, `quant_algo: MIXED_PRECISION`, `moe_quant_algo: NVFP4`, `group_size: 16`, `format: e4m3` - **Model (FP8)**: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` - **vLLM versions tested**: - v0.27.0 / v0.27.1 (main) — fails at startup on SM121 (DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation") - jasl fork branch `codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` (PR #41834), image `vllm-jasl-41834:latest` — serves NVFP4 but no DSpark - **KV cache dtypes**: `fp8`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `nvfp4`, `nvfp4_ds_mla` - **Speculative decoding**: DSpark, 5 speculative tokens, `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'` - **Serving config**: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, `--block-size 256`, `MTP_NUM_TOKENS=5`, `MAX_MODEL_LEN=131072`, `MAX_NUM_SEQS=4` ## What we want 1. Serve the **NVFP4** DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoint on SM121 with **FP4 KV cache** (`nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla`). 2. Enable **DSpark speculative decoding** on top of that NVFP4 target (MTP draft), without the draft loader failing on missing NVFP4 scale tensors. 3. Have the DSpark draft built under its **own model/quant config** so an NVFP4 target does not corrupt the MXFP4 draft experts (see abandoned PR #49133). ## What fails today ### On vLLM main (v0.27.1, official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1-aarch64-cu129`) Startup fails on SM121 with the DeepGEMM scale-layout error: ``` RuntimeError: Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/layout.hpp:60): Unknown SF transformation ``` This is the same class of failure as #51884 / #51758 (DeepGEMM SM120/121 regression). Full report: #51884. ### On jasl's fork (PR #41834) — NVFP4 serves, but DSpark fails The NVFP4 checkpoint loads and serves, but enabling DSpark fails during draft weight loading: ``` KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_input_scale' ``` The draft loader expects a scale tensor that is absent from the NVFP4 draft params, so speculative decoding cannot be enabled for the NVFP4 target. ## Related issues / PRs - **#51884** — DeepGEMM "Unknown SF transformation" on SM120/121 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 + DSpark (blocker on main) - **#51758** — v0.26→v0.27 DeepSeek-V4-Flash load regression (DeepGEMM SM120) - **#50720** — DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + DSpark fails on SM120 (FlashInfer sparse MLA topk=256 dispatch) - **#49133** (PR, closed/abandoned) — "DSpark: build draft under its own model/quant config (NVFP4 target corrupts MXFP4 draft experts)". Closed by author with note: *"we have nvfp4 drafter for dsv4-nvfp4 now"* — but that drafter does not work for this checkpoint on SM121. - **#51835** (PR, open) — "Restore DeepSeek-V4 DSpark draft quantization" (restores `deepseek_v4_fp8` for the draft) - **#41834** (PR) — "Add SM12x support for DeepSeek V4 Flash with essential fixes" (jasl's branch we currently run) - **jasl/vllm#43** — our original issue on jasl's fork for this exact scenario ## Request Please add/validate end-to-end support for **NVFP4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + FP4 KV cache + DSpark speculative decoding** on SM121, including: - Making the DSpark draft loader work with NVFP4 targets (missing `w13_input_scale` / NVFP4 scale tensors). - Building the DSpark draft under its own model/quant config (revive #49133) so NVFP4 targets don't corrupt MXFP4 draft experts. - Confirming the `nvfp4` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV cache path works with DSpark on SM121. Happy to test any branch / provide logs.

signals.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash think-until-cap / empty turn under concurrent DSpark + breakable CUDA graphs
signals.text: ## Summary On **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** with the official DSpark recipe, concurrent `/v1/chat/completions` requests (same greedy tool-calling turn) intermittently **never leave the reasoning channel**. Generation runs to `max_tokens` with: - `finish_reason: "length"` - empty `message.content` - **no** `tool_calls` - `reasoning_content` is a tight loop (never emits a think-end token), repeating e.g. `Wait, the user wants to upgrade XEHM4B to business, then cancel it.` This is a **real decode loop**, not only a parser mis-bucket. Healthy replies on the same prompt are short tool-calls (~181 tokens). Failed replies burn the full cap (`max_tokens=16384` in the numbers below). The high-rate failure needs **all three**: 1. **DSpark** speculative decoding 2. **Breakable CUDA graphs** (this nightly auto-enables `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`) 3. **In-flight concurrency ≥ 10** `--enforce-eager` does **not** reproduce. The same prompt at the same concurrency is **0/1024** on SGLang (DSPARK) and TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc23 / 1.3.0rc25 (DSpark). ## Environment | Item | Value | |------|--------| | Image | `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-acb0f1dcdb668d90bbbf50e57552d2f6f0987c87` | | Digest | `sha256:6b084be85c1806afcb69df24d853ebf240b9f0dfca3eaa2252d0096a46a12c58` | | Version | `0.27.2rc1.dev110+gacb0f1dcd` | | Hardware | 2× NVIDIA B200, TP=2 + expert parallel | | Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` | | HF snapshot | `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062` | | Startup log | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` auto-enabled; `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`; separate DSpark CUDA-graph capture | Hub image `ENTRYPOINT` is `["vllm","serve"]`. ## Serve command (repro / default recipe) Flags follow [recipes.vllm.ai DeepSeek-V4-Flash](https://recipes.vllm.ai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash), adapted to TP2. ```bash # SNAP = local HF snapshot of deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 # (7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062) docker run --gpus '"device=0,1"' --network=host --ipc=host --shm-size=32g \ -v "$HF_HOME:$HF_HOME" -e HF_HOME -e PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \ vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-acb0f1dcdb668d90bbbf50e57552d2f6f0987c87 \ "$SNAP" \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}' \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \ --max-model-len 70000 \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune ``` ## Payload + curl Multi-turn airline tool-calling conversation (tau2-style): system policy, prior `get_reservation_details` / `get_flight_status` / `get_user_details` results, last user turn: > Upgrade XEHM4B to business first, then cancel it. Use the card ending in 2135. Also, do I have any other upcoming flights? What’s the total cost of those? Full body: **17 messages, 14 tools**, `temperature: 0`. Gist: **https://gist.github.com/dsingal0/8973a0fb9166beb38e6aaf1fb1df20e9** ```bash # force the length-cap path curl -sS -L -o payload.json https://gist.githubusercontent.com/dsingal0/8973a0fb9166beb38e6aaf1fb1df20e9/raw/deepseek_v4_flash_airline_toolcall.json jq '.max_tokens=16384 | .temperature=0' payload.json > /tmp/req.json # single request curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary @/tmp/req.json | jq '{ finish: .choices[0].finish_reason, content: .choices[0].message.content, n_tools: (.choices[0].message.tool_calls|length), reasoning_len: (.choices[0].message.reasoning_content|length), completion: .usage.completion_tokens }' ``` **Hit** = `finish_reason=="length"` AND empty/whitespace `content` AND no `tool_calls`. **Healthy** = `finish_reason=="tool_calls"`, ~181 completion tokens. A hit’s `reasoning_content` never contains a think-end token; it loops the upgrade/cancel sentence until the cap. Concurrent repro (need **≥ 10** in flight; **32** is reliable). Fire N identical POSTs, then repeat sequential waves: ```bash # example: 8 sequential waves of 32 in-flight python3 - <<'PY' import json, time from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed from urllib.request import Request, urlopen url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions" payload = json.load(open("/tmp/req.json")) payload["max_tokens"] = 16384 payload["temperature"] = 0 def one(i): t0 = time.time() req = Request(url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST") body = json.loads(urlopen(req, timeout=7200).read()) ch = (body.get("choices") or [{}])[0] msg = ch.get("message") or {} content = (msg.get("content") or "").strip() tools = msg.get("tool_calls") or [] finish = ch.get("finish_reason") hit = finish == "length" and not content and not tools return {"i": i, "finish": finish, "hit": hit, "n_tools": len(tools), "sec": round(time.time() - t0, 2), "completion": (body.get("usage") or {}).get("completion_tokens")} for wave in range(8): with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=32) as ex: rows = [f.result() for f in as_completed(ex.submit(one, i) for i in range(32))] hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"]) print(f"wave {wave}: {hits}/32 hits") PY ``` ## Conditions required | Condition | Needed for high-rate repro? | |-----------|-----------------------------| | Greedy (`temperature=0`) | Yes (all numbers below) | | Tools + this multi-turn prompt | Yes | | `max_tokens` large enough (4096 often misses; **16384** used) | Yes | | In-flight concurrency **≥ 10** | Yes | | DSpark `num_speculative_tokens: 7`, greedy draft | Yes for ~30% rate | | Breakable CUDA graphs (default on this nightly) | Yes for ~30% rate | | Prefix caching | On in all runs (not ablated) | | `--enforce-eager` | **Suppresses** the bug | | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | **Almost suppresses** | Serial (`c=1`) after a polluted server: rare (1/16). Cold start + high concurrency: the first ~256 requests can be clean, then the rate climbs. ## Observed frequencies Same image, same weights, same payload, `max_tokens=16384`, `temperature=0`. **Default recipe (DSpark + breakable graphs), 64 in-flight, 1024 requests: 298 / 1024 (29.1%)** `finish`: 697 `tool_calls`, 309 `length`, 18 `stop`. All 298 hits used the full 16384 tokens. By 64-id bucket: first 256 requests **0%**, then 23% → **67%** on the last bucket. **Default recipe, sequential waves of 32 (already-warm server), 256 req: 103 / 256 (40%)** | Wave | Hits | Local slots that hit | |------|------|----------------------| | 0–3 | **6/32 each (18.75%)** | **always 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31** | | 4 | 11/32 | spreading downward | | 5–7 | 21–24/32 (66–75%) | high slots dominate | **Concurrency threshold** (3 waves each, polluted default server): | In-flight | Hits | Rate | |-----------|------|------| | 4 | 0/12 | 0% | | 7 | 0/21 | 0% | | 8 | 0/32 | 0% | | 9 | 0/27 | 0% | | **10** | **4/30** | **~13%** (first consistent hits) | | 12 | 9/36 | 25% | | 16 | 21/48 | 44% | | 24 | 49/72 | 68% | | 26 | 55/78 | 71% | | 28 | 61/84 | 73% | | 32 | 103/256 | 40% (escalating across waves) | **Ablations** (same prompt/cap; 8×32 waves = 256 unless noted): | Setup | Hits | Rate | |-------|------|------| | DSpark + breakable graphs (**default**) | 298/1024 | **29.1%** | | DSpark + `--enforce-eager` (`cudagraph_mode=NONE`) | **0/256** | **0%** | | DSpark + `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | 2/256 | 0.8% | | **No** `--speculative-config` (graphs still on) | 10/512 | 2.0% | | SGLang nightly + DSPARK, same payload, 64 in-flight | 0/1024 | 0% | | TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc25 + DSpark, same payload | 0/1024 | 0% | | TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc23 + DSpark, same payload | 0/1024 | 0% | DSpark without breakable graphs ≈ 0–2%; graphs without DSpark ≈ 2%; **both + c≥10 ≈ 30% and climbing**. The last-6-of-32 slot pattern on early waves is deterministic enough that this is unlikely to be sampling noise (`temperature=0`). ## Notes - `ParserEngine.adjust_initial_state_from_prompt` is a no-op in this build. Empty `content` here is because generation never leaves reasoning, not only a CONTENT↔REASONING flip. - Think-parser `initial_state` issues (e.g. #51296) can also empty `content` when think-end is missing; they do **not** explain the 16k self-loop or the CUDA-graph / batch-index dependence. - Workarounds that held here: `--enforce-eager`, or `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, or keep concurrency ≤ 9. Eager is the only config that was **0/256**. ## Expected The same greedy prompt should keep producing the ~181-token tool-call path at c=32, as SGLang and TensorRT-LLM do, and as vLLM does under `--enforce-eager`.

signals.title: [Bug]: 0.27.1 crashes in custom_all_reduce (illegal memory access) during CUDA graph capture on Hopper TP=4; identical config works on 0.26.0
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ```text vLLM (failing) : 0.27.1+cu129 vLLM (working) : 0.26.0+cu129 PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu129 (0.26.0 env: 2.11.0+cu129) CUDA (torch built): 12.9 Python : 3.10.12 OS : Linux-5.15.0-94-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 GPU : NVIDIA H800, compute capability 9.0 (Hopper / SM90) Driver : 575.57.08 Parallelism : TP=4, single node, no PP, no DP, no EP Model : deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (FP8 checkpoint) KV cache dtype : fp8 ``` The two vLLM versions are installed in **separate virtualenvs** on the same host, so the comparison below changes exactly one variable: the vLLM version. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug A TP=4 configuration that has been serving reliably on **0.26.0** for weeks fails to start on **0.27.1**. The engine dies during CUDA graph capture with an illegal memory access originating in the custom all-reduce kernel: ``` Failed: Cuda error /workspace/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:164 'an illegal memory access was encountered' torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` Immediately before the crash, 0.27.1 logs: ``` Auto-enabling VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1. Set VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 to opt out. VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH is set, disabling vLLM's torch.compile pipeline. Equivalent to -cc.mode=none. ``` followed by `Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 0%| | 0/51` and then the fault on all four ranks. #### Reproduction The command line is **copied verbatim** from the working 0.26.0 systemd unit — same model, same `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, same `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, same `--gpu-memory-utilization`, same environment variables. Only the interpreter (virtualenv) differs: ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8012 ``` - On **0.26.0**: starts normally, serves traffic. - On **0.27.1**: crashes as above, reproducibly, every attempt. #### What I ruled out I ran this twice with different configurations to isolate the cause: | Run | Config | Result | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0.27.1 **with** `--speculative-config` (DSpark), `gpu-mem-util 0.88`, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` | illegal memory access | | 2 | 0.27.1 **without** speculative decoding, no `expandable_segments`, parameters byte-for-byte identical to the working 0.26.0 unit | **same crash**, `custom_all_reduce.cuh:164` | So the failure is **not** caused by speculative decoding, not by the lowered memory utilization, and not by `expandable_segments` — run 2 has none of them and still crashes. The only remaining variable is the vLLM version itself. #### Possibly relevant `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh` was heavily refactored between the two releases — `git diff v0.26.0..v0.27.1` shows **+20 / −296** for that file, with the implementation moved into a new `custom_collective_common.cuh`. Given the crash site, that refactor seems like a plausible place to look. #### Not a duplicate of I checked the closest-looking existing reports; none match this configuration: - **#51758** — same headline symptom ("upgrade 0.26.0 → 0.27.0, DeepSeek V4 Flash error"), but that environment is **RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) + CUDA 13.0**, and the comments trace it to a DeepGEMM scale-factor layout regression missing the `arch_major == 12` branch. This report is **Hopper SM90 / cu129**, and the fault is in the all-reduce kernel, not DeepGEMM. - **#46253** — illegal memory access under `breakable_cudagraph`, but that is a **cross-node** GB10 setup where NCCL falls back to a host-staged transport without GPUDirect. This is a **single-node** TP=4 case. - **#45604** — same file, 4 GPUs, but the reported fault is `invalid argument` in the FlashInfer AllReduce **norm fusion** path with MXFP8. - **#42609** — `custom_all_reduce` IPC handles vs `expandable_segments`, requires DP>1 **and** TP>1; here DP=1, and run 2 does not set `expandable_segments` at all. #### Happy to help I have both versions installed side by side on the same host and can run additional diagnostics (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, compute-sanitizer) if that would help narrow it down — just say which would be most useful. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lengthy documentation-related questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Under async scheduling, stateful logits processors that read output_token_ids values see -1 placeholders — logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids only counts CLI custom processors
signals.text: ### Your current environment Observed on `releases/v0.27.1` (`6e448d0ea9`), reading the same code paths on current main. Runtime: vLLM 0.27.2.dev1 (source install), torch 2.13.0+cu130, 2x NVIDIA L20, TP=2, Python 3.12. The issue is scheduling logic, not environment-specific. ### 🐛 Describe the bug The v1 `LogitsProcessor` interface documents `output_tok_ids` as a live view of each request's generated tokens: > Key assumption: the `output_tok_ids` list (which is an element of each tuple in `added`) is a reference to the request's running output tokens list; via this reference, the logits processors always see the latest list of generated output tokens. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/interface.py#L45-L48 Under async scheduling (default-on since 0.27), that assumption only holds conditionally. The worker-side lists are extended with `-1` placeholders each step (real ids stay on the GPU in `prev_sampled_token_ids`): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L3823-L3846 A repair mechanism exists precisely for this: `set_async_sampled_token_ids` / `update_async_output_token_ids` patch the `-1`s with real ids right before the logits processors run: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L1030-L1056 But the repair is gated by `needs_output_token_ids` (penalties / bad_words / thinking budget / `logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids`): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L908-L922 and the logitsprocs contribution to that gate only counts **CLI-passed custom processors**: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L714-L726 ```python # We currently don't know whether a particular custom logits processor # uses output token ids so we set this conservatively. ... logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids=bool(custom_logitsprocs), ``` So there are three under-/over-approximations of the same unknown: 1. **Entry-point plugins** (`vllm.logits_processors` group) are not counted — being fixed by #38199. 2. **Builtin-registered processors are never counted.** The three in-tree builtins happen to only read the list's *length* (`MinTokensLogitsProcessor`), never its *values*, so nothing in-tree notices. Any stateful processor registered via `BUILTIN_LOGITS_PROCESSORS` that reads values silently computes on placeholder garbage: full per-step overhead is paid, results are wrong, and there is no warning or error. 3. Conversely, CLI custom processors that *don't* read values still force the repair path (the conservative `True`), paying an unnecessary sync in async mode. ### Reproduction / real-world impact We integrated Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text watermarking (via the HF `transformers` processor) as a builtin stateful logits processor on top of `releases/v0.27.1` — the first "reads values" consumer of this contract we know of: - with `--no-async-scheduling`: 8/8 watermarked outputs detected, mean-g z-score avg **7.86** (range 5.51–11.47), 0 false positives on controls; - with default async scheduling and identical code: **0/8 detected** (z avg 0.39 ≈ control 0.33), while still paying ~11% per-request latency for the watermark compute — the context window degrades to `[-1, -1, -1, -1]`. Branch with the processor and a fail-safe guard (refuses to watermark and warns when async scheduling is detected): https://github.com/danbo610/vllm/tree/feature/synthid-watermark (see commit `f18c17a3bb` for the guard). Minimal repro sketch: register any processor that prints `output_tok_ids` from `apply()` in `BUILTIN_LOGITS_PROCESSORS`, run with defaults (no penalties, no CLI `--logits-processors`), and observe `[-1, -1, ...]`; pass `--no-async-scheduling` (or any CLI custom processor, which flips the flag) and observe real ids. ### Suggested fix A declarative capability on the interface would solve all three cases at once, mirroring `is_argmax_invariant()`: ```python class LogitsProcessor(ABC): @classmethod def needs_output_token_ids(cls) -> bool: return True # conservative default for out-of-tree processors ``` - the three in-tree builtins override it to `False` (no behavior change, removes today's over-approximation for value-agnostic CLI procs); - `build_logitsprocs` ORs the declarations across builtin + entry-point + CLI processors and feeds `logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids`; - the `interface.py` "Key assumption" docstring gains a note that the live view is only guaranteed when this capability is declared (or async scheduling is off). Short of that, amending the docstring plus a startup warning when async scheduling is enabled with non-in-tree processors would at least make the failure mode discoverable — today it is completely silent. Happy to help validate a fix against the watermarking use case; we can also upstream the SynthID processor itself as a separate PR if there is interest.

signals.title: [Bug][DP] Tie-break rotation from #47420 destroys prefix-cache locality for multi-turn traffic under internal DP LB
signals.text: ### Your current environment vLLM nightly `ac7509e2b1db` (also reproduced on the release path — see bisect below), 8×H100 SXM (one node), `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --api-server-count 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 1000000 --block-size 256`, prefix caching enabled (default). ### 🐛 Describe the bug **#47420 ("Rotate load-balancer tie-break to avoid systematic engine bias") destroys prefix-cache locality for multi-turn / shared-prefix traffic under internal DP load balancing.** `DPLBAsyncMPClient.get_core_engine_for_request` resolves score ties by scanning from `eng_start_index`, and since #47420 that start index rotates after every decision. A multi-turn conversation at low load is exactly a stream of tied decisions, so consecutive turns rotate across DP ranks — and every turn misses the prefix its previous turn left in that rank's KV cache. Before #47420 the fixed scan start accidentally pinned each frontend client's tied decisions to one rank, which is what kept sessions cache-local. Measured with an aiperf mooncake-trace replay matched to production shape (multi-turn sessions, ~34k-token prompts, trace designed for **81.7%** prefix reuse), identical client and trace on both engines: | | prefix-cache hit rate (c=1 … c=128) | designed | |---|---|---| | v0.23.0 (pre-#47420) | **81.6%** measured run-wide | 81.7% | | current main (`ac7509e2b1db`) | **37.6% / 52.9% / 20.0% / 16.0% / 10.9% / 7.8%** | 81.7% | Per-rank counters confirm the mechanism: at c=1 (strictly sequential turns), `vllm:prefix_cache_queries` spreads *evenly* across all 4 DP ranks (~350k each) while hits concentrate on the ranks that happened to repeat. End-to-end cost on this workload: **−2% to −13% per-user output throughput vs v0.23.0** despite main being +6–17% faster on a cache-defeating random-token ladder (same hardware, same recipe) — the re-prefill of ~34k-token prompts swamps the decode-side wins. #47420's own benchmark ran with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, so the fairness fix never saw this cost. The fairness problem it fixed was real; the tie-break just shouldn't rotate *related* requests away from their cache. ### Partial mitigation (PR incoming) and why the full fix needs a design decision PR from this account: remember which engine served a prompt's first-block prefix (small LRU keyed on `cache_salt` + LoRA id + first `block_size` prompt token ids) and prefer that engine **only when scores tie**. Load-aware decisions are unchanged; unrelated tied requests still rotate, preserving #47420's fairness. A/B on the hardware above (same trace, same engine, only the tie-break differs): c=1 hit rate 37.6% → **61.5%** (+6% per-user throughput), c=32 16.0% → 23.2%. It does **not** restore the 81.6% baseline, for a structural reason: with `--api-server-count N`, each frontend process has its own `DPLBAsyncMPClient` (and now its own affinity map), and SO_REUSEPORT spreads one session's connections across processes — client-side affinity can only see the requests that land on its process. The pre-#47420 behavior dodged this by pinning *every* client's ties to a per-client rank, at the cost of the fairness bias #47420 fixed. A complete fix needs prefix-awareness at a shared layer — the DP coordinator, or a shared affinity table across frontend processes — which is a design decision for the maintainers. Filing this issue so the tie-break mitigation and that larger conversation have a home.
