signals.title: [Core] DBO ++: Overlap TP all-reduce with compute
signals.text: ## Purpose ### TL;DR The overlap yield wrappers on `main` are inside the EP all-to-all path. TP all-reduce contributes a noticeable fraction of prefill latency (~19% on Qwen3-32B TP=4), with even higher communication cost on PCIe than NVLink systems. **Make TP all-reduce run in parallel with model compute, instead of serially.** On Qwen3-32B + TP=4 this delivers up to **−7.5%** prefill wall / **+8.1%** prefill throughput and **−4.4%** e2e wall / +4.6% e2el (matrix below). The mechanism is Dual-Batch Overlap (DBO): split a forward into two micro-batches and issue each ubatch's all-reduce on a separate CUDA stream while the other ubatch keeps using the compute stream. AR latency that today serializes with compute becomes **hidden behind** compute. ### What "AR ↔ compute overlap" looks like A single TP forward pass on `bs=4, pl=4096`, Qwen3-32B, looking at one TP rank's GPU streams (this is from the nsys traces attached in `Test Result` below; exact numbers, not sketches): ``` Without DBO (today, vllm0.21): compute_stream: [ GEMM_0 AR_0 GEMM_1 AR_1 GEMM_2 AR_2 ... ] wall = 1110 ms comm_stream: (unused) └────────── 1086 ms busy, AR is 248 ms inline ──────┘ With DBO (this PR): compute_stream: [ GEMM_0a GEMM_1a GEMM_2a ... GEMM_0b GEMM_1b ... ] wall = 1047 ms comm_stream: [ AR_0a AR_1a AR_2a ... AR_0b ... AR_Nb ] ↑ overlapped 95.7% with compute_stream ``` The AR kernels (`ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_bf16_RING_LL`) move from the compute stream to a dedicated comm stream and run **concurrently** with the next ubatch's GEMMs. 95.7% of AR kernel time is hidden behind compute. ### How DBO achieves this DBO is two-thread-per-rank micro-batching: 1. The forward is split into 2 ubatches (`UBatchSlice`) along the token axis. 2. Two Python threads run each ubatch's forward concurrently. They share GPU but use **two separate CUDA streams**: a `compute_stream` and a `comm_stream`. 3. Every TP all-reduce site (`tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`) yields between the two threads: - thread A: `yield_to_comm()` → issue AR on `comm_stream` → `yield_to_compute()` - while A's AR is in flight on `comm_stream`, thread B's compute for the next layer keeps running on `compute_stream` 4. `dbo_enabled()` checks at runtime whether a yield context is live so the same `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` works as a vanilla AR when DBO is off. This matches the `comm_stream / compute_stream` design vLLM already uses for EP all-to-all DBO (`fused_moe/modular_kernel.py`, `prepare_finalize/deepep_ht.py`). What this PR does is **plug it into the dense TP all-reduce path**. ### What this PR changes 1. **TP AR yield wrapper** in `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`: issue the AR with `dbo_yield_and_switch_*` so it runs on `comm_stream` when DBO is active. Behaves as a vanilla AR otherwise. 2. **Custom-op registration** to survive `torch.compile`. AR is registered as `torch.ops.vllm.vllm_dbo_all_reduce`, which dynamo treats as opaque, so the runtime `dbo_enabled()` check survives tracing. 3. **DP=1 entry to the DBO scheduling path**: `coordinate_batch_across_dp` no longer early-exits on `dp_size==1`; the gate in `gpu_model_runner` becomes `num_ubatches > 1`; `gpu_ubatch_wrapper` accepts `dp_metadata=None`. This documentation was AI-assisted (Claude). We reviewed every line. ## Files changed 9 files, +153 / −37 lines. 0 model files. 0 C++/CUDA. 0 fusion-pass files. 0 new env vars (and 4 previously-required env vars folded into config). | File | + | − | Role | |---|---:|---:|---| | `vllm/distributed/communication_op.py` | 43 | 2 | DBO AR yield wrapper + always-on custom-op registration | | `vllm/v1/worker/dp_utils.py` | 37 | 2 | DP=1 fast path; pass through `num_scheduled_tokens_per_request` | | `vllm/v1/worker/ubatching.py` | 12 | 1 | Brief busy-spin before blocking yield wait | | `vllm/v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py` | 16 | 3 | `check_ubatch_thresholds` reads new gates | | `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` | 6 | 4 | `cache_key += ubid`; gate on `num_ubatches > 1` | | `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py` | 18 | 14 | Allow `dp_metadata=None` for DP=1 | | `vllm/config/vllm.py` | 11 | 11 | Loosen EP-only assert | | `vllm/config/parallel.py` | 4 | 0 | `dbo_prefill_min_seq_len: int = 2048` | | `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` | 6 | 0 | `--dbo-prefill-min-seq-len` CLI flag | ## Usage This PR is opt-in. No environment variables — all behavior is controlled by `LLM(...)` kwargs (or the equivalent `vllm serve` flags). The new public surface introduced by this PR is exactly **one** kwarg: | New (this PR) | Type | Default | Effect | |---|---|---:|---| | `ParallelConfig.dbo_prefill_min_seq_len` | `int` | `2048` | Skip DBO on prefill batches whose `max_prompt_len` is below this. Below the floor, DBO setup overhead dominates and the cell regresses. Set `0` to disable the gate. | CLI counterpart: `--dbo-prefill-min-seq-len `. The other flags below already exist in vLLM today; this PR makes them **actually deliver speedup when combined**, by fixing the torch.compile + DBO incompatibility and adding the dense-TP yield path. ### Minimal — turn the optimization on Three additional kwargs vs an unoptimized `LLM(...)` call: ```python from vllm import LLM from vllm.config import CompilationConfig from vllm.config.compilation import CompilationMode, CUDAGraphMode llm = LLM( model="Qwen/Qwen3-32B", tensor_parallel_size=4, dtype="bfloat16", enable_dbo=True, # existing flag — flip on compilation_config=CompilationConfig( # existing API mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE, cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE, ), ) ``` ### Tunable — recommended production config ```python llm = LLM( model="Qwen/Qwen3-32B", tensor_parallel_size=4, dtype="bfloat16", enable_dbo=True, # existing dbo_decode_token_threshold=8, # existing, tunable dbo_prefill_token_threshold=64, # existing, tunable dbo_prefill_min_seq_len=2048, # NEW (this PR), tunable; # 0 disables the gate compilation_config=CompilationConfig( # existing API mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE, cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE, ), async_scheduling=False, # existing flag; recommended # for prefill DBO (avoids # extra prefill chunking, # ~+1 pp speedup). gpu_memory_utilization=0.92, ) ``` CLI equivalent: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --enable-dbo \ --dbo-decode-token-threshold 99999 \ # disable DBO on decode --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 64 \ --dbo-prefill-min-seq-len 2048 \ # NEW (this PR) --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": 1}' ``` ## Test Plan ### Microbenchmark — prefill + e2e wall Each cell runs **one** LLM instance and measures both timings on it: - `max_tokens=1` × 10 reps → **prefill wall** (TTFT) - `max_tokens=128` × 10 reps → **e2e wall** (prefill + 127 decodes) Both `baseline` and `ours` use `mode=VLLM_COMPILE + cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE + async_scheduling=True` (vLLM defaults). The only delta is `enable_dbo` (and the three `dbo_*` knobs). Decode never ubatches: `dbo_decode_token_threshold=99999` (see Usage). Fresh `~/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache` per run. ```python # bench_pr.py import argparse, json, os, statistics, time E2E_MAX_TOKENS = 128 def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--config", required=True, choices=["baseline", "ours"]) ap.add_argument("--bs", type=int, required=True) ap.add_argument("--pl", type=int, required=True) ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=10) ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="./bench_results") args = ap.parse_args() os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARNING") from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams from vllm.config import CompilationConfig from vllm.config.compilation import CompilationMode, CUDAGraphMode extra = {} if args.config == "ours": extra = { "enable_dbo": True, "dbo_decode_token_threshold": 99999, # decode does NOT ubatch "dbo_prefill_token_threshold": 64, # dbo_prefill_min_seq_len uses default (2048). } llm = LLM( model="Qwen/Qwen3-32B", tensor_parallel_size=4, max_model_len=8192, max_num_batched_tokens=131072, enforce_eager=False, compilation_config=CompilationConfig( mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE, cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE), gpu_memory_utilization=0.92, dtype="bfloat16", disable_log_stats=True, enable_prefix_caching=False, **extra, ) sp_p = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1, ignore_eos=True) sp_e = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=E2E_MAX_TOKENS, ignore_eos=True) def make(seed): return [{"prompt_token_ids": list(range(1+i*args.pl+seed, 1+(i+1)*args.pl+seed))} for i in range(args.bs)] for _ in range(2): llm.generate(make(int(time.time()) % 1000), sp_p, use_tqdm=False) llm.generate(make(int(time.time()) % 1000), sp_e, use_tqdm=False) p_walls, e_walls = [], [] for r in range(args.reps): t0 = time.perf_counter() llm.generate(make(12345 + r * 1000), sp_p, use_tqdm=False) p_walls.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000) t0 = time.perf_counter() llm.generate(make(54321 + r * 1000), sp_e, use_tqdm=False) e_walls.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000) p_med, e_med = statistics.median(p_walls), statistics.median(e_walls) p_sd = statistics.stdev(p_walls) if len(p_walls) > 1 else 0.0 e_sd = statistics.stdev(e_walls) if len(e_walls) > 1 else 0.0 out = { "config": args.config, "bs": args.bs, "pl": args.pl, "prefill_median_ms": p_med, "prefill_stdev_ms": p_sd, "e2e_median_ms": e_med, "e2e_stdev_ms": e_sd, "e2e_output_tps": (args.bs * E2E_MAX_TOKENS) / (e_med / 1000), "prefill_walls_ms": p_walls, "e2e_walls_ms": e_walls, } os.makedirs(args.out_dir, exist_ok=True) json.dump(out, open(f"{args.out_dir}/{args.config}_bs{args.bs}_pl{args.pl}.json", "w")) print(f"CSV,{args.config},bs={args.bs},pl={args.pl}," f"p={p_med:.2f}±{p_sd:.2f},e2e={e_med:.2f}±{e_sd:.2f}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Driver — runs the full 8-cell × 2-config matrix: ```bash #!/bin/bash set -e for cell in "4 2048" "4 4096" "8 2048" "8 4096" \ "16 2048" "16 4096" "32 1024" "32 2048"; do bs=${cell% *}; pl=${cell#* } for cfg in baseline ours; do rm -rf ~/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache mkdir -p ~/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache python3 bench_pr.py --config $cfg --bs $bs --pl $pl --reps 10 done done ``` ### Online serving (vllm bench serve) Real-traffic validation: start a vLLM server, then run the official serving benchmark client against ShareGPT V3. ``` python # 1. start server (baseline: drop --enable-dbo and the dbo-* flags) --tensor-parallel-size 4 --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": 1}' \ --enable-dbo \ --dbo-decode-token-threshold 99999 \ --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 64 \ --dbo-prefill-min-seq-len 2048 \ --port 8765 & # 2. wait for /v1/models, then run client vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8765 \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --dataset-name sharegpt \ --dataset-path /path/to/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --num-prompts 500 --request-rate inf \ --save-result --result-dir ./serve_results ``` ## Test Result ### Hardware / software - 4× NVIDIA H200, 144 GB/card, driver 13.1, CUDA 13 - vLLM 0.21.0, torch 2.11.0, Python 3.12 - Qwen3-32B bf16, TP=4, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92`, `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_batched_tokens=131072` ### Wall-time matrix | Cell | baseline wall (p / e2e) | ours wall (p / e2e) | Δ_wall (p / e2e) | baseline tps (p / e2e) | ours tps (p / e2e) | Δ_tps (p / e2e) | | ----------------- | ----------------------: | ------------------: | ----------------: | ---------------------: | -----------------: | ----------------: | | bs=4 pl=2048 | 277 / 1217 | 276 / 1224 | −0.3% / +0.6% | 29,570 / 421 | 29,652 / 418 | +0.3% / −0.6% | | bs=4 pl=4096 | 560 / 1497 | 553 / 1497 | −1.2% / −0.0% | 29,275 / 342 | 29,644 / 342 | +1.3% / +0.0% | | bs=8 pl=2048 | 543 / 1499 | 527 / 1485 | −3.0% / −0.9% | 30,182 / 683 | 31,116 / 689 | +3.1% / +0.9% | | bs=8 pl=4096 | 1101 / 2083 | 1049 / 2039 | −4.8% / −2.1% | 29,754 / 492 | 31,243 / 502 | **+5.0%** / +2.2% | | bs=16 pl=2048 | 1074 / 2080 | 1010 / 2055 | −6.0% / −1.2% | 30,510 / 984 | 32,455 / 996 | **+6.4%** / +1.2% | | bs=16 pl=4096 | 2207 / 3225 | 2051 / 3104 | −7.0% / −3.8% | 29,698 / 635 | 31,951 / 660 | **+7.6%** / +3.9% | | bs=32 pl=1024 | 1057 / 2122 1,331** | **+8.1% / +4.6%** | ### Online serving (`vllm bench serve`) Real-traffic validation against the same `vllm serve` HTTP stack users deploy: 500 random prompts, input_len=2048, output_len=128. signals.title: [Model] Add Orthrus model support
signals.text: ## Summary Adds first-class Orthrus checkpoint support for vLLM's standard autoregressive serving path. - Adds an `OrthrusConfig` so `model_type="orthrus"` checkpoints can load without requiring remote config code. - Registers `OrthrusLM` and `OrthrusForCausalLM` as text-generation architectures. - Adds an Orthrus model implementation based on Qwen3, including the extra Orthrus diffusion projection/norm parameters so public Orthrus checkpoints can map their weights. - Adds focused config and registry coverage for the public `chiennv/Orthrus-Qwen3-1.7B` checkpoint family. This PR intentionally does not expose Orthrus diffusion-mode speculative decoding yet. That path needs additional scheduler/attention metadata work to share the autoregressive KV cache with diffusion queries safely. The implementation uses vLLM's normal AR model path. Addresses part of #43786. ## Duplicate-work check Required checks were run before opening this PR: - `gh issue view 43786 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments` showed no existing implementation discussion in the CLI output. - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "43786 in:body"` returned no open PRs. - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Orthrus speculative decoding"` returned no open PRs. ## Tests - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_orthrus_config.py -v` passed. - `.venv/bin/python -c 'from vllm.model_executor.models import is_text_generation_model; from vllm.model_executor.models.registry import ModelRegistry; cls = ModelRegistry._try_load_model_cls("OrthrusLM"); assert cls is not None; assert is_text_generation_model(cls); cls2 = ModelRegistry._try_load_model_cls("OrthrusForCausalLM"); assert cls2 is cls; print("Orthrus registry import ok")'` passed. - `.venv/bin/python -c 'from tests.models.registry import HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS; from vllm.model_executor.models.registry import ModelRegistry; missing = ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs() - HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS.get_supported_archs(); assert not missing, missing; print("registry coverage ok")'` passed. - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/models/registry.py tests/transformers_utils/test_orthrus_config.py vllm/model_executor/models/orthrus.py vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py vllm/transformers_utils/config.py vllm/transformers_utils/configs/__init__.py vllm/transformers_utils/configs/orthrus.py` passed. ## AI assistance codex

signals.title: Fix discarded speculative rows leaking logprobs
signals.text: ## Summary Fix V1 speculative output parsing so discarded request rows cannot return stale logprobs. When a request row is discarded, the output token list is cleared. However, logprobs were filtered before applying the discard mask, so a discarded row could still contribute logprob entries. This can produce inconsistent API output such as: ```text tokens: [] logprobs: [ ... ] ``` This PR makes token and logprob parsing use the same validity mask: - apply `discard_req_indices` before filtering `LogprobsTensors` in `RejectionSampler.parse_output` - route single-token V1 runner outputs through the shared parser when logprobs are present - keep the old lightweight single-token path when logprobs are absent ## Duplicate check I checked the related open speculative-logprobs work before opening this PR. The closest open PR is #44727, but it fixes a different issue: `logprob_token_ids` / generative scoring can make the internal rejection-sampler logprob tensors have the wrong shape. This PR does not change `logprob_token_ids` handling, sampler gathering, or generative scoring behavior. This PR is limited to a separate discard-mask invariant: > if a request row is discarded, both its sampled tokens and its sampled-token logprobs must be discarded. I did not find an open issue or PR for either of these specific paths: - `discard_req_indices` being applied after logprob filtering in `RejectionSampler.parse_output` - the V1 single-token runner paths bypassing `RejectionSampler.parse_output` when logprobs are present AI assistance was used for this change. ## Tests ```bash .venv/bin/ruff check vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py .venv/bin/python -m py_compile vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py::test_parse_output_filters_discarded_logprobs tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_async_output_filters_discarded_single_token_logprobs tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_bookkeeping_sync_filters_discarded_single_token_logprobs ``` OpenShift A100 validation: AppWrapper Succeeded, Job Complete, targeted pytest 3 passed.

signals.title: fix: reset KV load recompute placeholders
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #45138. When a KV load failure is handled with `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, the scheduler truncates `num_computed_tokens` so the request can recompute from the first invalid block. If the request already had output placeholders reserved by async scheduling, those placeholders were left in place. That leaves the retried request in a mixed prefill/decode state: `num_output_placeholders` keeps contributing to `num_new_tokens` and to the max-token guard even though the request is being sent back to prefill work. This can keep a load-failure retry from making normal progress. This PR clears stale output placeholders when a request is affected by invalid KV blocks. If there are older async outputs still in flight, they are counted in `async_tokens_to_discard`; the current scheduled output is already skipped by `failed_kv_load_req_ids`, so it is not double-counted. ## Test Plan To verify: ```bash python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py::test_sync_recompute_blocks_not_freed_for_running_requests -q python -m ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py python -m ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py python -m py_compile vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py git diff --check ``` ## Test Result Passed locally: ```text python -m ruff check vllm\v1\core\sched\scheduler.py tests\v1\kv_connector\unit\test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py All checks passed! python -m ruff format --check vllm\v1\core\sched\scheduler.py tests\v1\kv_connector\unit\test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py 2 files already formatted python -m py_compile vllm\v1\core\sched\scheduler.py tests\v1\kv_connector\unit\test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py # no output git diff --check # no output ``` Local pytest did not reach the test body in this Windows base environment because the installed `transformers==5.8.1` / `kernels==0.15.2` combination fails during import of `tests/conftest.py`: ```text ValueError: Either a revision or a version must be specified. ```

signals.title: [Bugfix] Parser engine: count reasoning tokens when <think> is pre-filled in the prompt
signals.text: ## Purpose `ParserEngine.count_reasoning_tokens` returned `0` for Qwen3.5 / `*-Thinking` templates (where `<think>` is pre-filled in the prompt, so the output only contains `</think>`), under-reporting `reasoning_tokens` in the Responses API usage. The fix seeds the reasoning state from `initial_state` instead of requiring a `<think>` token in the output, and applies to all engine-based parsers (Qwen3 / NemotronV3 / Gemma4). The fix and test originate in #40783 (against the pre-#45413 parser); this PR ports the count fix to the engine-based parser that replaced it. Not a duplicate of #44398: that PR fixes the same count for the text-based parsers (DeepSeek-R1) and adds Chat Completions reporting, but it does not touch `ParserEngine`, so the engine parsers introduced by #45413 stay affected. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_reasoning.py::TestCountReasoningTokens -v pytest tests/reasoning/test_qwen3_reasoning_parser.py::test_count_reasoning_tokens -v pytest tests/parser/engine/ -q ``` ## Test Result - `TestCountReasoningTokens`: 3 passed (the pre-prompt-`<think>` case failed before the fix). - `test_count_reasoning_tokens`: 3 passed on all three real tokenizers (failed on all three before the fix). - `tests/parser/engine/`: 191 passed, no regression. `ruff` clean. *AI assistance was used to adapt the test from #40783 and implement the fix; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.*

signals.title: [Perf][Kernel][ROCm] Add Triton split-KV paged decode fallback for gfx12
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR adds a split-KV Triton paged-decode fallback for ROCm gfx12x devices. As discussed in #34579, some ROCm gfx11/gfx12 workloads cannot use the native ROCm custom paged-attention kernel because its current eligibility constraints. For example, Qwen3.5 uses `head_dim == 256`, so it falls back to the existing Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d` implementation in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py`. The existing Triton fallback works correctly, but there is no split-KV option. For small-batch long-context decode, especially `batch_size == 1`, the launch has very low occupancy because each sequence/head pair is handled by a single program over the full KV length. This makes decode attention a major bottleneck on gfx12. This PR adds a gfx12-targeted split-KV decode path for the Triton fallback, currently enabled for: - ROCm gfx12x - `torch.float16` / `torch.bfloat16` query tensor - `head_size == 256` - no ALiBi - no sliding window - no attention sinks - no FP8 KV/output path The fallback keeps the existing non-split Triton kernel for unsupported shapes and features. Currently this kernel is only tuned for bf16/fp16 and `head_dim == 256` on gfx1201. I will work to expand the supported precision and features. However I only have 1 AMD AI Pro R9700 GPU (32G VRAM), so I didn't manage to test this kernel with gpt-oss models (which has head_dim == 64). ## Changes - Add split-KV paged decode Triton kernels: - `kernel_paged_attention_2d_splitkv` - `kernel_paged_attention_2d_splitkv_reduce` - Add `paged_attention_2d_splitkv_decode` launcher. - Add a split-count heuristic for small-batch decode occupancy. - Route eligible gfx12x decode fallback cases through the split-KV path. - Preserve existing behavior for unsupported features and shapes. - Add focused kernel tests comparing split-KV output against the existing non-split Triton paged decode reference. - Add coverage for mixed prefill/decode batches where prefill queries must be filtered out and left untouched by the decode path. ## Test Plan ### Unit test Added `tests/kernels/attention/test_splitkv_paged_decode.py` as test for the newly added kernel. Use the existing attention kernel ### Integration test #### E2E Performance Test Tested with Qwen 3.5-9B model. Benchmark the end to end latency with built in benchmark (Concurrency 1,2,4,8, Context length 1, 2, 4, 8,..., 32k, Output length 128). Serve the model with `vllm serve --model Qwen3.5-9B --max-model-len 34K --served-model-name qwen-3.5-9b` and test with `vllm bench serve` and designated `input-len`, `output-len` and `max-concurrency`. #### E2E Precision Test Test model with RULER data set (context length 4K, 8K, 16K) with lm-eval. As we are using dynamic `num_splits` in the new kernel, this test uses `enforce eager` to cover more `num_splits`. ## Test Result ### Unit Test Passed the newly added tests. ### Integration Test #### E2E Performance Test | Concurrency | Input tokens | TPOT before (ms) | TPOT after (ms) | TPOT reduction | Output tok/s before | Output tok/s after | Throughput gain | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 4096 | 43.87 | 37.90 | -13.6% | 20.39 | 23.21 | +13.8% | | 1 | 8192 | 49.76 | 38.07 | -23.5% | 16.48 | 20.40 | +23.8% | | 1 | 16384 | 62.17 | 39.12 | -37.1% | 11.67 | 15.91 | +36.4% | | 1 | 32768 | 86.84 | 41.19 | -52.6% | 7.10 | 10.46 | +47.2% | | 2 | 4096 | 47.23 | 41.49 | -12.2% | 36.55 | 40.83 | +11.7% | | 2 | 8192 | 56.12 | 44.44 | -20.8% | 27.67 | 32.70 | +18.2% | | 2 | 16384 | 78.19 | 56.08 | -28.3% | 18.04 | 22.56 | +25.1% | | 2 | 32768 | 127.69 | 82.85 | -35.1% | 10.01 | 13.08 | +30.7% | | 4 | 4096 | 55.26 | 50.43 | -8.7% | 60.11 | 64.99 | +8.1% | | 4 | 8192 | 75.04 | 64.94 | -13.5% | 41.88 | 46.68 | +11.5% | | 4 | 16384 | 119.20 | 99.75 | -16.3% | 25.13 | 28.76 | +14.4% | | 4 | 32768 | 222.68 | 183.11 | -17.8% | 12.87 | 14.97 | +16.3% | | 8 | 4096 | 83.73 | 80.98 | -3.3% | 81.65 | 84.21 | +3.1% | | 8 | 8192 | 123.69 | 118.22 | -4.4% | 54.00 | 56.25 | +4.2% | | 8 | 16384 | 211.63 | 200.41 | -5.3% | 30.81 | 32.39 | +5.2% | | 8 | 32768 | 421.97 | 396.77 | -6.0% | 15.16 | 16.11 | +6.2% | There is no obvious change in TTFT metrics. signals.title: [Bugfix] Accept logprobs=-1 in the Completion API
signals.text: ## Purpose The Completion API rejects `logprobs=-1`, even though `-1` ("return all logprobs") is accepted everywhere else in the request path: - In the very same `check_logprobs` validator, `prompt_logprobs` is allowed to be `-1`: ```python if prompt_logprobs < 0 and prompt_logprobs != -1: raise VLLMValidationError("`prompt_logprobs` must be a positive value or -1.", ...) ``` - `SamplingParams.__post_init__` accepts it: `if self.logprobs is not None and self.logprobs != -1 and self.logprobs < 0`. - The Chat Completion API accepts `top_logprobs=-1` the same way. Only the Completion `logprobs` check was missing the `!= -1` exception, so a request like `{"prompt": "...", "logprobs": -1}` is turned away at the protocol layer before it ever reaches the engine that would have honored it. ## Change Add the `!= -1` exception (and align the message with `prompt_logprobs`): ```python if (logprobs := data.get("logprobs")) is not None and logprobs < 0 and logprobs != -1: raise VLLMValidationError("`logprobs` must be a positive value or -1.", ...) ``` `-1` now passes; `-2` and below are still rejected. ## Test Added two cases to `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py` (same direct-construction style as the existing validation tests there): `logprobs=-1` builds a valid `CompletionRequest`, and `logprobs=-2` still raises with the "positive value or -1" message. I could not build `vllm._C` in my local environment, so I verified the validator's boolean logic in isolation (old condition rejects `-1`; new condition accepts `-1`, still rejects `-2`/`-3`, and leaves `0`/`5`/`None` untouched) and ran `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean. The unit tests run in CI.

signals.title: [Feature] Initial support for fault tolerant ep using scale-down
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR adds **scale-down** and **auto-recovery** support to the vLLM fault tolerance (FT) framework for DP+EP MoE deployments (external LB mode). The existing FT framework (`--enable-fault-tolerance`) supports `retry` — reinitializing the DP process group after a transient fault where all ranks survive. When a DP rank permanently dies (hardware failure, OOM kill, etc.), `retry` alone is insufficient: the dead rank's expert slots become unreachable and EPLB placement tables reference non-existent slots. This PR introduces two complementary capabilities: 1. **Scale-down** (`POST /fault_tolerance/apply` with `instruction: "scale_down"`): Removes dead DP ranks, masks the corresponding EP ranks at the all2all kernel level, redistributes orphaned logical experts onto surviving ranks using EPLB redundant slots, selectively reloads only reassigned expert weights from disk, rebuilds the DP Gloo group over the surviving slots, and resumes inference — all without a full restart. 2. **Auto-recovery** (`--fault-tolerance-config='{"auto_recovery": true}'`): Lets the engine self-heal without external orchestrator commands. On fault, the engine queries the all2all mask from its workers and unions it cluster-wide via the DP store: if no new dead ranks are detected (transient fault), it auto-retries; otherwise it derives the dead DP ranks from the EP mask and auto-scales-down. ### Design - **Slots model: EP topology unchanged** From vLLM's point of view, a removed rank remains as an empty slot: `parallel_config.data_parallel_size` / `data_parallel_rank` stay frozen at their initial values and DP rank ids never change, so there is exactly one coordinate system (original) and no densification anywhere. `removed_dp_ranks` is always in original coordinates and is cumulative-safe — it may include ranks removed by earlier rounds; the engine applies only the increment. Likewise the all2all kernel keeps the original EP world size with dead EP ranks masked via `update_mask()` (both `deepep_low_latency` and `nixl_ep`), which avoids model re-init, graph recompile, and CUDA graph re-capture. Only the rebuilt Gloo `cpu_group` uses dense internal ranks over `sorted(alive)`, computed at reinit time and never written back to config. - **EPLB is disabled after scale-down and re-enabled by a future scale-up.** Post-scale-down the EP/EPLB groups still span the original EP world size, so dynamic rebalancing would attempt collectives with dead ranks; EPLB async rebalancing is therefore suppressed (`eep_eplb_suppressed`) until a scale-up restores the slots. - **Failed recovery is retryable.** The engine commits the topology change (`data_parallel_master_ip`, cumulative dead set) only after the Gloo group reinit succeeds, so a failed attempt leaves a consistent state that can be re-dispatched. Invalid commands (own-rank removal, fully stale removal, <1 survivor) are rejected up front with an observable `ft_error` — the orchestrator re-reads status and re-issues. - **The orchestrator can pass an explicit `request_id` to identify the recovery round.** All engines in one round share the same `request_id`, which namespaces that round's coordination keys in the DP store so concurrent or stale rounds cannot cross-talk. When empty, it falls back to the engine's local reinit epoch. - **Auto-recovery rejects external commands while it is in progress.** A `_recovery_lock` serializes auto-recovery (busy-loop thread) against external commands (input-sockets thread); a command arriving during an ongoing recovery is rejected with a recorded `ft_error`, keeping a single recovery driver per engine at any time. ### Implementation Notes - **TP sibling lockstep barrier (TP > 1).** `_synchronize_dp_ranks` (v1) and `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` (v2) run a per-step Gloo barrier over the TP CPU group when FT is enabled and `tp_size > 1`, preventing intra-TP deadlock: a sibling whose peer stopped arriving fails on the host within `cpu_distributed_timeout_seconds`, never leaving an orphaned TP collective (e.g. fused allreduce kernels without timeout) running on its device stream. The TP CPU group is rebuilt during worker `retry`. - **nixl_ep dispatcher sync.** After masking, each MoE layer's cached `num_dispatchers` is rewritten to the nixl_ep kernel's `active_rank_bound` (highest surviving EP rank + 1); the kernel sizes combine output by `active_rank_bound` and asserts the width matches. DeepEP-LL keeps a fixed num_ranks-wide layout and needs no sync. - **Dead-column neutralization.** Under the slots model the DP allreduce tensors keep their original width and a dead rank's column stays 0 after the SUM allreduce, which is not neutral for min/`all(==1)` aggregations. After the allreduce, each rank locally fills dead columns (from `get_dp_group().dead_dp_ranks`) with aggregate-neutral values. - **EPLB async state reset.** A new `ft_reset_epoch` on the EPLB state lets the async worker detect a recovery and abandon in-flight transfers instead of applying stale results; the async thread survives exceptions when FT is enabled. - **Side-stream mask query.** Worker `query_mask` runs on a separate CUDA stream so a poisoned main stream cannot block the mask read that auto-recovery and status reporting depend on. ### Known limitations - `scale_down` requires EPLB with `num_redundant_experts > 0`. - Requires an FT-capable all2all backend (`deepep_low_latency` or `nixl_ep`) and external LB mode with one engine per API server. - EPLB dynamic rebalancing stays suppressed after scale-down (lifted by a future `scale_up`). - Recovery is not guaranteed for faults occurring at certain stages (e.g. mid weight-transfer in EPLB). - Auto-recovery cannot self-heal the death of DP rank 0 (the coordination TCPStore master is hosted by rank 0); the engine fails closed and waits for an external `scale_down` command with `dp_store_port`/`dp_master_ip`. ## Test Plan E2E tests live in `tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_fault_tolerance_e2e.py` (gated on `has_nixl_ep`): 1. `test_injected_fault_retry_recovers_all_ranks` (DP=2) — injected fault, all ranks UNHEALTHY, `retry`, all ranks HEALTHY and serving. 2. `test_scale_down_removes_dead_rank_and_recovers` (DP=4, EPLB with 32 redundant experts) — SIGKILL rank 1's worker; survivors go UNHEALTHY, victim's engine goes DEAD and rejects `retry` with a recorded `ft_error`; `scale_down(removed_dp_ranks=[1])` to all survivors; all survivors return to HEALTHY and serve completions. Manual cluster validation (external LB, 4 independent API servers, one engine each): - Model: DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MoE, 64 logical experts), `--data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 2` (EP world size 8), `--enable-expert-parallel`, `--all2all-backend nixl_ep`, `--enable-eplb` with 64 redundant experts (async), `--enable-fault-tolerance`, `--cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30`, `engine_recovery_timeout_sec=500`. - Drive baseline inference on all ranks; kill one worker of DP rank 1 (TP1 sibling) during active inference; verify survivors detect the fault and go UNHEALTHY while the victim's engine goes DEAD; send `scale_down(removed_dp_ranks=[1])` to the 3 survivors; verify expert redistribution + weight reload, Gloo group rebuilt over the surviving slots (original rank coordinates unchanged), all survivors HEALTHY and serving. ## Test Results Manual scale-down validation (2026-08-12, config above): **PASSED**. This run exercises the TP=2 single-worker-kill scenario end to end. Sanitized full log (host IP / GPU model / local paths redacted) attached. | Phase | Observation | Timestamp | |---|---|---| | Cluster ready | 4 ranks (DP=4 × TP=2, EP world 8) initialized, serving baseline traffic | 17:49:24 – 17:50:48 | | Fault injected | One worker of DP rank 1 (TP1 sibling, EP rank 3) killed during active inference | 17:50:48 | | First survivor-side error | Survivors' TP1 workers hit gloo `Connection reset by peer` on the per-TP-rank DP group | 17:50:48 | | Victim DEAD | Engine 1's executor shut down its remaining worker; busy loop cancelled → status DEAD; its API server stays up and keeps answering `/fault_tolerance/status` | 17:50:57 | | Survivors UNHEALTHY | Engines 0/2/3 raise from the nixl_ep kernel timeout with mask `[0,0,1,1,0,0,0,0]` (EP ranks 2,3 = DP rank 1, both TP workers) | 17:51:18 | | scale_down dispatched | `POST /fault_tolerance/apply` `removed_dp_ranks=[1]` → 202 on R0/R2/R3 | ~17:51:44 | | Expert redistribution | 257 (layer, expert) pairs reloaded from disk per worker (652–733 tensors); `num_dispatchers` synced to `active_rank_bound=8` | 17:51:45 | | Scale-down complete | Gloo DP group rebuilt 4→3 (dense group ranks R0→0, R2→1, R3→2; original `data_parallel_rank` frozen); Engines 0/2/3 → HEALTHY, `cumulative dead_dp_ranks=[1]` | 17:51:45 | | Post-recovery inference | All 3 survivors resume serving `/v1/chat/completions` with HTTP 200 | 17:51:45 – 17:52:07 | Key observations: - Recovery itself (mask replay + redistribution + weight reload + group reinit) completes in ~1s once dispatched; end-to-end latency is dominated by fault detection (immediate for the TP1 siblings via gloo connection-reset; ~30s for the surviving engines via the nixl_ep kernel timeout). - No hangs, no orphaned TP collectives — the TP sibling lockstep barrier keeps survivor device streams clean. E2E pytest: ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_fault_tolerance_e2e.py -v -s ``` <!-- TODO: paste CI result once the fault-tolerance e2e step runs --> - **AI assistance**: this change was developed with AI assistance (kimi-k3); every changed line was reviewed by the human submitter. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. - [ ] (Optional) Release notes update. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Validate sparse MLA top-k buffer
signals.text: ## Purpose Addresses #46726. This PR improves SM120 FlashInfer sparse MLA construction error handling and adds regression coverage for skip-topk layers that rely on a shared `topk_indices_buffer`. The current implementation already supports the valid skip-topk path where `indexer is None` and the implementation falls back to the shared `topk_indices_buffer` passed by the upper MLA path. This PR keeps that behavior, and adds targeted tests to make sure it remains covered. This PR also replaces the internal assertion for the missing top-k buffer case with an explicit `ValueError`. This makes the failure mode clearer when neither an `indexer` nor a shared `topk_indices_buffer` is available. I checked for duplicate work before opening this PR: ```bash gh issue view 46726 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "46726 in:body" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "SM120 sparse MLA topk_indices_buffer" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "FlashInfer sparse MLA indexer" ``` Results: * No open PR directly references #46726. * I did not find an existing open PR that adds this specific SM120 FlashInfer sparse MLA API coverage or replaces the missing top-k buffer assertion with an explicit `ValueError`. AI assistance was used while investigating the issue, reasoning about the sparse MLA construction path, and drafting parts of the PR description. I personally reviewed the changed code, verified that the implementation matches the intended behavior, and ran the tests listed below before submitting. ## Test Plan Run the relevant SM120 FlashInfer sparse MLA API tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -v tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py ``` Run the sparse MLA backend tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -v tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py ``` Run pre-commit on the modified files: ```bash pre-commit run --files \ tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py ``` The targeted tests cover: * Models without `index_topk` are rejected by the SM120 sparse backend. * Skip-topk layers with `indexer=None` can be constructed when a shared `topk_indices_buffer` is provided. * A clear `ValueError` is raised when both `indexer` and the shared top-k buffer are missing. ## Test Result Passed: ```text tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py: all relevant tests passed tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py: all relevant tests passed pre-commit run --files tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py: passed ``` Not fully validated locally: I do not have access to the original SM120 setup from the issue report, so validation from the issue reporter or maintainers on the original failing environment would be appreciated.

signals.title: [Core] Use FlashInfer workspace sizing helper
signals.text: ## Purpose Use FlashInfer's caller-owned workspace sizing helper when available so vLLM can reserve the workspace size required by FlashInfer attention planning instead of always reserving the default FlashInfer workspace size. This keeps the existing fallback path intact: if the helper is unavailable or cannot size a particular shape, vLLM still uses FlashInfer's default workspace allocation behavior. The workspace state shared by FlashInfer wrappers now keeps only weak references to wrappers, so profiling-time or temporary wrappers do not stay alive solely because the shared workspace state saw them once. This PR requires a FlashInfer build that includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3741 for the caller-owned workspace sizing helper. That FlashInfer change has been merged to FlashInfer main, but it is not part of the 0.6.13 release. Until the first FlashInfer release containing it is available and the vLLM pins are bumped to that version, this PR should be tested with a FlashInfer main checkout/build. signals.title: [Core] Use FlashInfer for pre-SM100 NVFP4 KV cache updates
signals.text: ## Purpose I wanted to use `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` on my RTX 3090 setup, but it was only usable on the SM100 native path. This PR makes the pre-SM100 path use FlashInfer's slot-mapping API for NVFP4 paged KV appends, so Ampere and Hopper systems can use the smaller NVFP4 KV cache without relying on the Blackwell-only path. The main benefit is KV cache capacity. On the tested RTX 3090 setup, NVFP4 gives about 3x more KV cache tokens, with quality on par with the auto dtype in the MRCR runs below. The tables compare against auto and TurboQuant 4bit_nc; TurboQuant did not start for the Gemma4 models on this setup. AI assistance: Codex and Claude Fable 5 were used during implementation and PR preparation; the submitter reviewed the changes. ## Changes - Use FlashInfer's `nvfp4_quantize_append_paged_kv_cache_with_slot_mapping` for pre-SM100 NVFP4 KV cache updates. - Add an FA2 prefill fast path that dequants FP4 KV pages to BF16 and runs `flash_attn_varlen_func`. If the FlashInfer paged-dequant helper is unavailable, this path falls back. - Keep native FA2 query tensors in model dtype. FP8-Q is only used when the trtllm-gen path is selected. This extends the Q dtype gating from #47485 to the `nvfp4` branch, which that fix did not cover. - Handle mixed K/V head dimensions by splitting packed NVFP4 data/scale views with explicit layout checks. - Cache the derived FlashInfer KV views per bound KV cache tensor. The update path and forward path now share the same canonicalized split views. - Centralize KV cache shape/stride handling for attention backends without changing backend method signatures. - Log the NVFP4 FA2 prefill scratch workspace reservation at startup. Sliding-window layers currently reserve full-context scratch; a future window clamp can reduce this to the active window. ## Dependencies Required FlashInfer API: - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3740 — slot-mapping NVFP4 paged KV append. Merged into FlashInfer main; not in a released package yet. Optional fast path: - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3748 — paged NVFP4 KV dequantization helper. Merged into FlashInfer main; not in a released package yet. Gemma4 selector support: - vllm-project/vllm#47547 — allows Gemma4 to choose FlashInfer when FA4 is unavailable. FlashInfer large-head FA2 support: - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3739 is merged into FlashInfer main, but may not be in a released package yet. There is no FlashInfer version bump in this PR. Until these merged FlashInfer changes are included in a release, testing needs a FlashInfer build from main. ## Test Plan Unit tests: ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -q -k nvfp4 pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -q -k "q_dtype or q_quantization_disable" pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -q -k fa2_prefill_reservation pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -q ``` Static checks: ```bash python -m py_compile <modified Python files> ruff check <modified Python files> ruff format --check <modified Python files> pre-commit run --files <modified files> ``` Runtime smoke on RTX 3090 (SM86): Qwen3.6-27B GPTQ int4, TP=1, `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`, without `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization`. Benchmarks on RTX 3090 x 2, TP=2: KV cache capacity, MRCR quality (30 samples, 32K context), and `vllm bench serve` (random 8K prompts, output length 64, 16 requests, `max_num_seqs=64`). ## Test Result Unit tests on the current head after merging latest main: 23 passed (nvfp4), 5 passed (q dtype), 3 passed (reservation), 5 passed (attn_utils). Static checks passed. Runtime smoke: resolved query dtypes logged as `prefill=torch.bfloat16`, `decode=torch.bfloat16`, `decode_backend=flashinfer-native`; server ready; `/v1/completions` returned 200 OK. The benchmarks below were measured on this branch before the latest main merge; the attention code paths are semantically unchanged by the merge. Gemma4 rows were measured with the Gemma4 FlashInfer selector change (#47547) stacked locally. ### KV Cache Capacity | Model | KV dtype | GPU KV cache size | vs auto | Backend | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | Qwen3.6-27B | auto | 291,999 tokens | 1.00x | Flash-attn | | Qwen3.6-27B | nvfp4 | 884,736 tokens | **3.03x** | FlashInfer | | Qwen3.6-27B | TQ 4bit_nc | 943,250 tokens | 3.23x | TurboQuant | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | auto | 724,640 tokens | 1.00x | Flash-attn | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | nvfp4 | 2,129,920 tokens | **2.94x** | FlashInfer | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | TQ 4bit_nc | 2,380,148 tokens | 3.29x | TurboQuant | | Gemma4-31B | auto | 122,360 tokens | 1.00x | Triton | | Gemma4-31B | nvfp4 | 392,369 tokens | **3.21x** | FlashInfer | | Gemma4-31B | TQ 4bit_nc | startup failed* | - | TurboQuant | | Gemma4-26B-A4B | auto | 590,793 tokens | 1.00x | Triton | | Gemma4-26B-A4B | nvfp4 | 1,802,224 tokens | **3.05x** | FlashInfer | | Gemma4-26B-A4B | TQ 4bit_nc | startup failed* | - | TurboQuant | \* Gemma4 TQ 4bit_nc did not start on this setup. ### Quality — MRCR 30 samples, 32K context. | Model | KV dtype | Match ratio | n8 match ratio | tok/s | Backend | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Qwen3.6-27B | auto | 0.9388 | 0.8245 | 29.39 | Flash-attn | | Qwen3.6-27B | nvfp4 | **0.9388** | **0.8245** | 29.47 | FlashInfer | | Qwen3.6-27B | TQ 4bit_nc | 0.9433 | 0.8378 | 27.86 | TurboQuant | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | auto | 0.8973 | 0.6999 | 118.94 | Flash-attn | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | nvfp4 | **0.9006** | **0.7097** | 120.74 | FlashInfer | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | TQ 4bit_nc | 0.8983 | 0.7028 | 64.61 | TurboQuant | | Gemma4-31B | auto | 0.7109 | 0.4714 | 14.59 | Triton | | Gemma4-31B | nvfp4 | **0.7134** | **0.4767** | 14.14 | FlashInfer | | Gemma4-26B-A4B | auto | 0.4337 | 0.3584 | 50.59 | Triton | | Gemma4-26B-A4B | nvfp4 | **0.4950** | 0.3262 | 49.86 | FlashInfer | NVFP4 was on par with auto in the Qwen runs. The Gemma4 results are from 30-sample runs with some metric movement: Gemma4-26B-A4B shows a higher overall match ratio (+0.06) and a lower n8 match ratio (-0.03) in this run. ### Serving Benchmark `vllm bench serve`, random 8K prompts, output length 64, 16 requests, `max_num_seqs=64`. | Model | KV dtype | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Output tok/s | Status | Backend | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | | Qwen3.6-27B | auto | 42.07 s | 574.22 ms | 12.93 | completed | Flash-attn | | Qwen3.6-27B | nvfp4 | 41.31 s | 567.70 ms | **13.16** | completed | FlashInfer | | Qwen3.6-27B | TQ 4bit_nc | 75.03 s | 1038.18 ms | 7.24 | completed | TurboQuant | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | auto | 9.57 s | 131.23 ms | 55.40 | completed | Flash-attn | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | nvfp4 | 9.50 s | 129.67 ms | **55.85** | completed | FlashInfer | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | TQ 4bit_nc | 18.12 s | 260.88 ms | 29.20 | completed | TurboQuant | | Gemma4-31B | auto | 83.60 s | 1040.14 ms | 6.47 | completed | Triton | | Gemma4-31B | nvfp4 | 65.97 s | 937.40 ms | **8.13** | completed | FlashInfer | | Gemma4-26B-A4B | auto | 25.45 s | 362.40 ms | 21.00 | completed | Triton | | Gemma4-26B-A4B | nvfp4 | 15.58 s | 224.26 ms | **34.08** | completed | FlashInfer | ## Notes - SM100 is not locally verified. The trtllm-gen direct path is unchanged. On SM100, wrapper-based fallback cases where trtllm-gen is not selected now use the auto backend with model-dtype output instead of forcing trtllm-gen with FP8 output. - OpenPanGU and MIMO V2 mixed-head runtime is not verified with real model weights. The mixed-layout split view behavior is covered by unit tests. - Sliding-window FA2 prefill currently reserves full-context scratch workspace. A window clamp can reduce this later; this PR only logs the current reservation size. - The FA2 fast path is optional. If the FlashInfer paged-dequant helper is not present, the code falls back instead of failing startup. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results. - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: fix(build): respect explicit VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE on macOS
signals.text: Fixes #47339 macOS forced `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` whenever the target wasn't already cpu — even if the caller set it explicitly (e.g. `tpu`), so `setup.py egg_info` produced `.cpu` metadata + CPU requirements for a non-cpu build. Linux only auto-detects when the env var is absent; this makes macOS follow the same rule (guard on `os.getenv(...) is None`). One-liner; the affected path is macOS-only so I can't run the repro here (on Linux the darwin branch never executes) — behavior mirrors the existing Linux guard right below it.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Allow untyped tool schemas to coerce JSON values
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #47557. Tool schemas that omit `type` currently fall back to string-only coercion, so JSON values such as `"5"` are preserved as strings even though an omitted JSON Schema type accepts any JSON value. This changes schema type extraction to return all JSON Schema types when a schema object has no explicit type, while keeping the existing string fallback for invalid schema inputs such as `None` or non-dicts. It also marks the pure tool parser utility test module with `skip_global_cleanup` so the targeted tests do not touch global accelerator cleanup state. I checked for duplicate work with: - `gh issue view 47557 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "47557 in:body"` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "tool schema missing type coerce string"` No open PR covering this fix was found. AI assistance was used to help review this change and run tests. ## Test Plan - `uv pip install -r requirements/common.txt tblib urllib3` - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py -q` - `.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py` - `git diff --check` ## Test Result - `tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py`: 82 passed, 3 warnings in 0.13s - `compileall`: passed - `git diff --check`: passed

signals.title: [Bugfix] Drop incomplete tool-call markup in non-streaming to match streaming
signals.text:
## Purpose Fixes #47137 When generation terminates (`max_tokens`/`length` or a `stop` string) inside a `<tool_call>` opener that has not been promoted to a tool call, the streaming path drops the buffered markup but the non-streaming path returned it as `content` — the two paths disagreed for identical model output. Contrary to the hope in the issue thread that #46875 had fixed this, I re-ran the issue's no-server unit reproduction on current main (`978de83`) and **the divergence still reproduces** (confirming @TheDuyIT's July 1 retest): ``` 2 '<tool_call>
' stream= '' nonstream= '<tool_call>
' DIVERGE 3 '<tool_call>
<' stream= '' nonstream= '<tool_call>
<' DIVERGE 4 '<tool_call>
<function' stream= '' nonstream= '<tool_call>
<function' DIVERGE ``` Root cause: in `DelegatingParser._extract_tool_calls`, the no-tool-calls branch returned the raw `content` instead of `tool_call_info.content` — the tool parser's cleaned content, which already strips incomplete tool-call markup while preserving any real content generated before the opener. This is "Direction B" from the issue, matching @bbrowning's stated expected behavior ("non-streaming should now match streaming and drop the incomplete markup until we have a valid tool call"). ## Changes - `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`: the auto-tool-choice no-tool-calls branch now returns the tool parser's content (scoped to engine-based parsers per review). - `vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py`: deferred-content flush keeps original text order around unpromoted tool blocks (review round 2, patch by @TheDuyIT). - `vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py` + `adapters.py`: `skip_reasoning_parsing` flag so tool parsers pass reasoning markup through verbatim when no reasoning parser is configured (review round 3, reported by @TheDuyIT). - `tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py`: regression tests for all of the above — truncated-opener parity cases, content-order preservation, think-markup passthrough for both engine failure modes, and sanity checks that complete tool calls still promote. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR The issue timeline has no cross-referenced PRs and `gh pr list --search "47137"` returns none (checked immediately before opening). @IMvision12 and @Kronten28 expressed interest in the thread (Jun 30 / Jul 1) but no PR was opened in the days since, and the thread stalled on the open question of whether the bug still exists — which the reproduction above settles. ## Test Plan As of 5b35c31b8 (current merge state with `main`): ``` $ pytest tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py -k "TruncatedToolOpener or ThinkMarkup" -v 10 passed $ pytest tests/parser/ # full parser suite 3779 passed $ pytest tests/tool_parsers/ 885 passed, 3 skipped, 34 xfailed $ pre-commit run --files <changed files> ruff check / ruff format / typos / mypy: Passed ``` Also re-ran the issue's part-D reproduction with the fix: all three truncation points now MATCH between streaming and non-streaming. ## Test Result All new and existing parser tests pass on macOS CPU (source build, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`). --- This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude Code); the diff was reviewed and the tests were run locally as described above. cc @bbrowning @TheDuyIT

signals.title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Enable DCP for FlashInfer sparse MLA decode
signals.text: ## Purpose Enable decode context parallelism for the SM120 FlashInfer sparse MLA decode backend (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`). The generic FlashInfer sparse MLA backend already participates in DCP by filtering sparse top-k indices to the local DCP rank, passing valid per-row counts as `seq_lens`, requesting decode LSE, normalizing the LSE shape, and masking empty DCP rows before returning `(out, lse)` to the shared DCP reducer. The SM120 packed sparse MLA wrapper still followed the simpler non-DCP path: it converted sparse indices without DCP filtering, passed `seq_lens=None`, did not request/return LSE, and allocated the output buffer from `self.num_heads`. On RTX PRO 6000 / SM120 GLM-5.2-NVFP4 serving with DCP this prevented startup and/or DCP reduction correctness. One concrete failure from hardware validation was: ```text ValueError: Invalid shape of out: expected (32, 1, 32, 512), got torch.Size([32, 1, 8, 512]) ``` This PR ports the existing sparse FlashInfer DCP wrapper behavior to the SM120 variant while preserving the SM120-specific packed `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache path, BF16 query input, `bmm2_scale=1.0`, and `kv_scale_format` plumbing. Specifically, it: - marks `FlashInferMLASparseSM120Impl` as able to return decode LSE; - uses `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index` when DCP is enabled; - passes compacted valid counts to FlashInfer as `seq_lens`; - requests `return_lse` when the shared DCP reducer needs it; - normalizes FlashInfer LSE to `(num_tokens, num_heads)`; - masks empty DCP rows with `out=0` and `lse=-inf`; - sizes the FlashInfer `out` buffer from the query head count actually passed to FlashInfer. Dependency note: this patch applies cleanly to current `main` and does not require rebasing on another vLLM PR. Runtime validation below used FlashInfer 0.6.14. If `main` still pins 0.6.13 when this is reviewed, full SM120 GLM validation may be easier after #47669 lands. AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex was used to port the locally validated production patch into upstream form, add the focused unit test, run local checks, and draft this PR description. I reviewed the changed lines and own the submission. ## Test Plan Local static/unit checks available in this environment: - `python3 -m py_compile vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py` - `python3 -m ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py` - `python3 -m ruff format --check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py` - `git diff --check` Targeted pytest attempted: - `python3 -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py` Production hardware validation performed separately on an 8x RTX PRO 6000 / SM120 system using `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, vLLM V1, FlashInfer 0.6.14, packed sparse MLA, TP=8, EP enabled, `max_model_len=131072`, FP8 KV cache, DCP=4, and MTP=2. ## Test Result Local: - `py_compile`: passed - `ruff check`: passed - `ruff format --check`: passed after formatting the touched files - `git diff --check`: passed - targeted pytest: not runnable in this local checkout because the Python environment does not have `torch` installed (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'` while importing `tests/conftest.py`) Production SM120 validation summary: - DCP=4 startup succeeded after this wrapper fix. - vLLM reported `GPU KV cache size: 2,096,896 tokens` and `Maximum concurrency for 131,072 tokens per request: 16.00x` for DCP-only. - With DCP=4 + MTP=2, vLLM reported `GPU KV cache size: 1,757,952 tokens` and `Maximum concurrency for 131,072 tokens per request: 13.41x`. - 10 parallel chatbot-style requests completed successfully. - Sustained 3 waves x 10 requests completed 30/30 HTTP 200 with about 239 output tok/s aggregate throughput. - A near-128K request completed HTTP 200 with about 125K prompt tokens. Follow-up validation that would be useful from maintainers with matching hardware: - Run the new unit test in the normal CUDA CI/dev environment. - Re-run GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on SM120 with DCP=2 and DCP=4. - Compare DCP output against non-DCP output on deterministic prompts. - Confirm FlashInfer SM120 sparse MLA LSE base remains `log2`, matching the generic FlashInfer sparse MLA backend.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix corrupted output with FlashInfer + decode context parallelism
signals.text: ## Purpose #29128 moved the seq_lens_np/num_blocks_np computation in FlashInferMetadataBuilder.build() ahead of the DCP adjustment, so decode and prefill plans were built from global sequence lengths and claimed `cdiv(global_len, page_size)` pages, while each DCP rank only owns `cdiv(local_len, page_size)` entries in its block-table row. Every rank therefore attended to pages it does not own, producing corrupted output under decode_context_parallel_size > 1 with the FlashInfer backend (gibberish from the first token in an end-to-end 2-GPU run, likely the cause of #41623). This PR derives the paged-KV metadata from the DCP-local lengths again, clones seq_lens_cpu before the in-place prefill adjustment so the runner's shared buffer is not mutated, and adds a regression test covering both ranks. ## Test Plan **Unit test** ``` pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k test_flashinfer_dcp_paged_kv_metadata_uses_local_seq_lens ``` **E2E** on 2x H100: `unsloth/gemma-2b` (MQA, 1 KV head, so DCP passes the TP > num_kv_heads check), greedy decoding (temperature 0, 128 tokens, logprobs), long prompts plus a warmup phase that fills KV pages so overclaimed pages contain live foreign KV: 1. baseline: TP=2, `attention_backend="FLASHINFER"` 2. repro: TP=2 + `decode_context_parallel_size=2`, same backend, on main 3. fix: same as 2. with this patch applied ## Test Result **Unit test**: fails on current main, passes with this patch. **E2E**: on main, TP=2+DCP=2 produces gibberish from the first generated token. With the patch, TP=2+DCP=2 generates 128/128 greedy tokens identical to the TP=2 baseline on both test prompts. AI-assisted, every line reviewed and tested by the submitter.

signals.title: [Perf] Speed up Mamba chunk metadata computation by ~6x
signals.text: ## Purpose There is a `# TODO (tdoublep): This code could probably be optimized.` in `BaseMambaAttentionMetadataBuilder._compute_chunk_metadata`. I profiled the function and found that most of the cost comes from per-element `.item()` calls (3 per prefill request) and a Python loop that runs once per chunk. For example, an 8k-token request with chunk size 256 goes through the loop 32 times. This PR keeps the chunking logic the same. It converts the two input tensors once with `.tolist()` instead of calling `.item()` per element, and emits the remaining chunk start offsets with `cu_chunk_seqlen.extend(range(...))` instead of the per-chunk loop. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_chunk_metadata.py ``` The new test uses the original implementation as the reference and checks that the outputs are identical on randomized workloads (chunk sizes 8–2048, batch sizes 1–128, aligned/unaligned computed tokens) and edge cases: new tokens smaller than the realigning chunk, exact chunk boundaries, and empty batch. ## Test Result All 76 tests passed. I also ran 400 additional randomized cases and the outputs are bit-identical. Microbenchmark of the function (pure-Python host-side code): | workload | before | after | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | prefill-heavy, bs256 × ~1536 tok | 471.6 µs | 68.5 µs | 6.9× | | long prompts, bs64 × ~8k tok | 166.2 µs | 25.9 µs | 6.4× | | chunked prefill, bs256, unaligned | 476.7 µs | 75.7 µs | 6.3× | | small batch, bs8 × ~2k tok | 15.0 µs | 2.4 µs | 6.2× | --- **AI assistance disclosure** (per `AGENTS.md`): Developed with Claude Code. I refined and refactored every line, and ran all tests locally. **Duplicate check**: I did not find any open PR addressing this function's overhead. The closest one, #33194 (mamba block-size logic for `all` mode), does not touch this code path.

PATH="$PATH:$PWD/.venv/bin" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest 'tests/models/language/pooling_mteb_test/test_st_projector.py::test_embed_models_mteb[model_info1]' -q 1 passed, 19 warnings in 30.05s PATH="$PATH:$PWD/.venv/bin" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/ -q 311 passed, 37 warnings in 1782.18s .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/vllm.py tests/test_config.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py All hooks passed ``` The full `tests/test_config.py` run also completed with 167 passes and one unrelated failure because this environment lacks access to gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` (HTTP 403). signals.title: [Bugfix] Pick KV cache block size from all attention backends
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #48286. `Platform.update_block_size_for_backend()` only consulted the first non-SSM attention backend when auto-picking the KV cache block size. Models that mix a permissive main backend with a stricter secondary one — e.g. DSA models whose `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` only supports block size 64 — kept the default of 16 and crashed later in `select_common_block_size()`: ``` ValueError: No common block size for 16. ``` This change collects all distinct non-SSM backends and takes the largest preferred block size, so the indexer's requirement is honored no matter which layer registers first. Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR addresses #48286 (checked issue timeline and recent PRs). AI assistance was used for this PR; the change was reviewed and tests were run before submitting. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_update_block_size_for_backend_honors_strictest_backend ``` The new test fails on main (`assert 16 == 64`) and passes with this change. Also verified against the real backend on CPU: ```python select_common_block_size(16, [DeepseekV32IndexerBackend]) # reproduces the reported ValueError Platform.update_block_size_for_backend(cfg) # with an indexer layer present cfg.cache_config.block_size # -> 64 ``` No GPU available locally, so no e2e serving run of a DSA model; the sibling `select_common_block_size` unit tests and `pre-commit run` (ruff, mypy) pass. ## Test Result ``` $ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k block_size -q 5 passed, 30 deselected in 1.97s ``` (4 pre-existing block-size tests plus the new one.)

signals.title: [Bugfix] Guard tool call argument JSON parsing in chat message postprocessing
signals.text: Fixes #47761 ## Purpose `_postprocess_messages` in `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py` re-parses the `arguments` string of every assistant tool call a client replays. That parse is unguarded, so an `arguments` value that is not a valid JSON object takes down the request. The important part is that the offending value lives in **conversation history**. The client replays the same assistant message on every subsequent turn and receives the same error each time, so the conversation is unrecoverable rather than merely degraded. The only way out is to discard the session. ### Two independent triggers, one chokepoint | | Reporter | Surface | Model | Cause | Payload | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | @rnogueira-tech | Chat Completions | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 | Generation hit `max_tokens` mid-string | 18,356 chars, later 36,946 chars | | 2 | @iMMIQ | Responses (non-Harmony Simple path) | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Generation stopped at EOS with the string still open | 54 bytes, 297 output tokens | Observed on 0.24.0 and 0.25.1. The two failures are mechanically identical, down to the offsets. Trigger 1's payload begins `{"contents": "` and reports *Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 14 (char 13)*. Trigger 2's begins `{"cmd": "` and reports *line 1 column 9 (char 8)*. In both cases the offset is exactly the index of the opening quote of the value that never closes. They do not share an upstream cause, and no single upstream fix covers both: - Reporting `finish_reason: "length"` on cap-truncated tool calls would not have caught trigger 2, where no cap was involved. - Validating on the Responses Simple path would not have caught trigger 1, which is Chat Completions streaming. `_postprocess_messages` is the only point where both converge, which is why the fix belongs here regardless of what else gets fixed upstream. ### Neither case is a client bug In both reports vLLM generated the malformed string and then reported the tool call as complete: - Trigger 1: generation was cut mid-string by the token cap, and `finish_reason` was reported as `"tool_calls"`, not `"length"`. - Trigger 2: generation stopped at EOS with the string open, and `emit_simple_tool_call_done` emitted the item with `status: "completed"` and no JSON validation. The clients replayed the assistant message they were handed. Reconstructing trigger 1's arguments from the SSE deltas and comparing against the replayed request gives 18,356 bytes on both sides, md5 `d1be3623820564162172c1f5ebff5893` — byte-identical. ### What was ruled out | Hypothesis | Result | |---|---| | Tool parser serialising invalid JSON | Ruled out. `qwen3_coder`, `qwen3_xml` and `mimo` all resolve to `Qwen3EngineToolParser`; `_qwen3_arg_converter` returns `json.dumps(params, ensure_ascii=False)` for both full and partial output | | Client mis-escaping the payload | Ruled out by the byte-identity check above | | Chat template or `--reasoning-parser` configuration | Ruled out; reporter tried `hermes`, `qwen3_xml`, custom templates, and `enable_thinking: false` | | Version regression | Ruled out; reproduced on 0.23.0, 0.24.0 and 0.25.1 | | Raising `max_tokens` as a workaround | Insufficient. 16384 overflows the 32768 context window; 8192 reproduces the same failure at the new cap | ### What this PR changes In `_postprocess_messages`, only `dict` values now reach `function["arguments"]`: - A malformed `arguments` string is coerced to `{}` and a warning is logged with the tool name and payload length. - A value that parses to valid JSON but is not an object (`"[]"`, `"42"`, `"true"`, `'"hello"'`) is also coerced to `{}` with a warning. - Dict values and valid JSON object strings are unchanged. - Missing, empty or `"null"` arguments continue to become `{}`. The payload itself is never logged; the linked issue's payloads contain user source code. ### Design note: coercion vs 400 on the malformed branch An earlier revision of this PR passed the original string through on the failure path. That was wrong and has been removed — chat templates require a mapping, `examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja` raises explicitly on a string, `toolace` and the pythonic templates raise `TypeError`, and `gemma3_pythonic` iterates character by character. Thanks to @bbrowning for the concrete example and to @zqzten for the wider template survey. As of the latest push, this PR and #50861 behave identically on every branch except one: when the JSON is **malformed**, #50861 raises `VLLMValidationError` → 400, and this PR coerces to `{}` with a warning. That branch decides whether #47761 is fixed or relabelled, and this PR coerces for three reasons. 1. **A 400 does not resolve #47761.** The malformed value is in history, so the client replays it every turn and receives the same rejection indefinitely. On the routes in that issue the current behaviour is already a 400, since `json.JSONDecodeError` subclasses `ValueError`. Raising `VLLMValidationError` gives a clearer message for the same dead conversation. 2. **Coercion is already the established pattern.** #43862 (merged) coerces `arguments: "null"` to `{}`. #47555 extends that to scalars, #50861 to lists. Malformed JSON is the same category of unusable input, and currently the only member singled out for a hard failure. 3. **The malformed data originates from vLLM in both reported cases,** and was reported to the client as complete. Clients should not have to re-validate JSON the server has declared finished. That is the only open question left on this PR, and I'm happy to implement whichever behaviour maintainers prefer. ### Scope Deliberately not in this PR, to keep it single-purpose. Both will be filed separately: - Reporting `finish_reason: "length"` when a tool call is truncated by the token cap. - Validating before `emit_simple_tool_call_done` writes `status: "completed"` on the Responses Simple path, plus the missing done event @iMMIQ observed. Related work on the same function: #43862 (merged), #47555, #50861, and #50997 for the Anthropic path. ## Test Plan Unit tests in `tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py` covering: - dict arguments pass through unchanged - valid JSON object string parses normally - malformed JSON from trigger 2, the captured payload `'{"cmd": "mkdir -p /tmp/mmadtest && cat > /tmp/mmadtest'`, coerces to `{}` - malformed JSON at truncation scale, a representative ~18 KB payload cut mid-string, coerces to `{}` - valid but non-object values `"[]"`, `"42"`, `"true"`, `'"hello"'`, `"null"` coerce to `{}` - missing, `None` and empty arguments coerce to `{}` - a warning is logged on coercion and includes the tool name, and no warning is logged for valid dict arguments - with two tool calls in one message, only the malformed one is coerced The two malformed cases use the payload shapes captured in #47761: a tool call cut mid-string by the token cap, and one cut at an EOS token. The behaviour can also be confirmed against a running server without a GPU and without generating anything, since `_postprocess_messages` runs before sampling. Reproducer contributed by @iMMIQ: ```bash curl -sS http://VLLM_HOST:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "ANY_MODEL", "max_tokens": 1, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [ {"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "foo", "arguments": "{\"cmd\": \"mkdir -p /tmp/x"}} ]} ] }'
signals.author: VBS2004

signals.title: [Attention][MiniMax-M3] Add FlashInfer MSA backend for SM120/SM121
signals.text: ## Purpose Give MiniMax-M3 sparse attention a fast path on consumer Blackwell (SM120/SM121). These GPUs currently run the Triton fallback for both the lightning indexer and the block-sparse attend, since the vendored MSA kernels are SM100-only. FlashInfer `vX.Y.Z` <!-- placeholder: first release containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3655 --> ships MSA kernels for SM120/SM121 ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3655](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3655)). This PR wires them into the existing impl dispatch, selected the same way as the SM100 MSA path; every other configuration keeps the Triton fallback. Design: - The indexer issues one scoring call and one top-k call for the entire batch, prefill and decode tokens together, so kernel-launch overhead stays constant per step and there is no separate decode/prefill code path. - FlashInfer's top-k takes batch-wide settings only, so M3's per-token selection rules (the forced local window and the causal range clamp) are applied in Python, before and after the kernel call. - The attend runs the FlashInfer prefill and decode kernels on vLLM's paged KV cache exactly as stored, so the path adds no per-step copy or re-layout of KV data; fp8 KV scales fold into the kernels' existing scale arguments. - The FlashInfer indexer and attend must be enabled together: they exchange top-k results in a different buffer layout than the Triton pair, and a mixed pairing would attend to the wrong blocks without any error. A single predicate (`minimax_m3_use_flashinfer_msa`) therefore drives both selections. - Two feature probes in `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py` gate the path; older FlashInfer releases keep the Triton fallback. Dependencies: - FlashInfer >= `vX.Y.Z` <!-- placeholder: first release containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3655 and #4039 --> for `flashinfer.msa_ops`, including its packed KV-cache support ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4039](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4039)): the attend reads K/V views split from vLLM's packed KV cache, a capability FlashInfer advertises as `msa_ops.SUPPORTS_PACKED_KV`. Scope notes: - The FlashInfer path engages only for `sparse_topk_blocks == 16` and decode GQA group sizes up to 16, narrower than the Triton path; M3 configurations satisfy both limits, and anything outside them keeps the Triton fallback. - `fp8_e5m2` KV caches and `nvfp4` indexer caches also stay on the Triton fallback. ## Test Plan Both new tests are in `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py`: - `test_flashinfer_indexer_impl_matches_triton`: runs the FlashInfer and Triton indexer impls on the same batches through their real metadata builders and asserts they select the same blocks, over bf16/fp8 index caches and local-window settings, including a short decode request. - `test_flashinfer_sparse_attention_matches_reference`: runs the FlashInfer attend at the impl's exact call shape (K/V views split from the contract-allocated cache) against the same reference the Triton kernels are tested with, over both KV-cache layouts, mixed prefill batches, and decode. - End-to-end and performance runs wait on a FlashInfer release containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4039; that is why this PR is a draft. ## Test Result - Indexer and attend parity: all cases pass on RTX 5080 (SM120) with FlashInfer built from source at the #4039 branch. - On FlashInfer releases without packed-KV support the attend rejects the K/V views at call time, so a version mismatch fails loudly instead of producing wrong results. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: fix(openai): bound validation-error response size for malformed requests
signals.text: `validation_exception_handler` renders every `RequestValidationError` entry into the 400 body, and each pydantic error embeds the full offending `input` value. So a single malformed request that fails validation many times echoes the payload once per error. Reported on `/v1/responses` (#49239): one request produced ~12k errors and a **~114MB** body from a few-KB input — a response-amplification vector against clients/proxies. Fix: strip the echoed `input` from each rendered error and cap how many are listed (the true count + a truncation notice are still reported). It's the shared handler, so all OpenAI endpoints benefit. Verified via direct handler call (no server): 12k input-echoing errors → body drops from ~25MB to ~2.2KB; `ctx`-based `param` detection unchanged. Added a regression test. Fixes #49239.

signals.title: [mooncake] support CUSTOM_MEM_POOL in vllm
signals.text: ### Purpose Add support for Mooncake custom memory pools (NVLINK / BAREX) when allocating KV cache in vLLM. This enables KV cache to use NVLink or BAR-exposed device memory instead of the default CUDA allocator, which is required by some MooncakeStoreConnector deployments for RDMA-based KV-cache transfer.When custom_mem_pool is configured in kv_connector_extra_config, MooncakeStoreConnector creates a torch.cuda.MemPool using the corresponding Mooncake allocator (NVLinkAllocator / BarexAllocator). When unset, the existing CuMem/default allocator behavior remains unchanged.Custom pools are incompatible with CuMem allocation and sleep mode. These conflicting configurations are rejected during connector initialization.In some scenarios, a specific allocator is required due to hardware limitations. ### Changes: -mooncake/store/worker.py: Validate custom_mem_pool, create and retain the Mooncake memory pool, detect CuMem/sleep-mode conflicts, and provide actionable errors for unsupported Mooncake versions. -mooncake/store/connector.py: Expose the custom memory-pool context to the GPU worker. -multi_connector.py: Forward a custom pool from child connectors and reject configurations where multiple children provide pools. -vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py: Use a connector-provided pool during KV-cache allocation, while preserving the existing fallback behavior. -test_multi_connector.py: Add coverage for no pool, single-pool forwarding, and multiple-pool conflicts.
