signals.title: [ROCm][K3] Extend FP8 asm MLA prefill to non-divisor small head counts
signals.text: ## Context The AITER FP8 MLA **prefill** path (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`) is gated on `num_heads % 16 == 0`. Kimi-K3 has 96 heads over `kv_lora_rank=512` → **12 heads/rank at TP8**, a non-divisor of 16, so its FP8 prefill falls back to the BF16 FMHA decompress path. That fallback builds a bf16 working set not covered by the FP8 KV-pool accounting and exhausts the activation arena at long context (K3 OOM'd at ~197k tokens, KV pool <4% used). This is the **prefill counterpart to #50578** (asm decode pad 12→16). MLA attention is independent per query head over the shared latent KV, so padding the query heads up to 16 and slicing the result back is exact. Rebased onto current `main` (includes merged #50578). Prefill-only diff: **+48 / −11**, one file (`rocm_aiter_mla.py`). ## Changes **FP8 prefill enablement (this PR):** - Relax the `_fp8_prefill_enabled` gate to also allow `0 < num_heads < 16`, and **gate it on FP8 KV** (`kv_cache_dtype_str == "fp8"` in the metadata builder; `is_quantized_kv_cache(kv_cache_dtype)` in the impl). Without this, a bf16-KV serve would reserve PS workspace unnecessarily. - In `_mla_fp8_prefill_attn`: replicate-pad Q/K/V to 16 via `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` (from #50578), run PS asm prefill + `mla_reduce_v1` at 16 heads, slice output back to `num_heads`. - Set `num_head_k = max(16, num_heads)` in `_init_fp8_prefill_ps_buffers` and `_build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata` so work/reduce maps match padded tensors — also cuts partial tiles (`gcd(16,256)=16` vs `gcd(12,256)=4`), reclaiming **~6 GiB** PS workspace. Decode padding / Gluon routing is **not** in this PR — that is #50578 (merged). ## Dependencies / related - **#50578** (merged) — `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` / asm decode for non-divisor heads. - **ROCm/aiter#4452** (merged `a63ede724`) — 64-bit paged-KV byte offsets for >4 GB addressing. - Composes with **#48712** (gate PS workspace on fp8 KV) — this PR includes the same gate locally. ## vllm serve command **Hardware:** 8× MI355X (gfx950), TP8 **Model:** `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (mxfp4) ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 export GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 export HF_HUB_CACHE=/dev/shm/hf-cache HF_HOME=/dev/shm/hf-cache export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600 export VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 export HIPBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=32768 export CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=32768 MODEL=/path/to/Kimi-K3 # e.g. /shared_nfs/models/Kimi-K3 vllm serve "$MODEL" --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --trust-remote-code --load-format auto --moe-backend aiter \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --enable-prefix-caching --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details --disable-uvicorn-access-log ## Test results ### Long-context prefill (functional) | | Before PR-A | After PR-A | |---|-------------|------------| | Fresh prefill @ util 0.95 | OOM ~197k tokens (BF16 FMHA fallback, KV <4%) | **470k (68 s)**, **590k (28.6 s)** OK | | PS workspace | ~4032 partial tiles (~12 heads) | ~960 partial tiles (~6 GiB saved) | ### Accuracy — GSM8K (lm-eval, full 1319-test split, 5-shot greedy, conc=32, ctx=16384) Patches applied for this run: **#50578 + PR-A + #50618 only** (no cgmem/MoE/kv_b_proj). Server at `gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`. ```bash export HF_HUB_CACHE=/dev/shm/hf-cache HF_HOME=/dev/shm/hf-cache export OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --include_path /path/to/InferenceX/utils/evals \ --tasks /path/to/InferenceX/utils/evals/gsm8k.yaml \ --output_path /tmp/eval_out --log_samples \ --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8888/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=32,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=16384" \ --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=12288,temperature=0,top_p=1" ``` | Run | n | strict-match EM | flexible-extract EM | |-----|---|-----------------|---------------------| | **With PR-A** (MI355X node 193, 2026-08-09) | 1319 | **97.04%** ± 0.47% | **96.97%** ± 0.47% | | Prior stack (cgmem+MoE+PR-A, node 1319, util 0.95) | 1319 | 96.89% ± 0.48% | 96.89% ± 0.48% | | Baseline replicate (stock + ASM deps, node 1319) | 1319 | 96.66% ± 0.49% | 96.66% ± 0.49% | No accuracy regression vs baseline; delta within run noise.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Propagate decode SWA index width for DSpark + FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4
signals.text: DSpark non-causal draft batches allocate `decode_swa_indices` with `noncausal_index_width` (wider than `window_size`). FlashInfer DSV4 sparse MLA still reshaped / passed `self.window_size` into `build_flashinfer_mixed_sparse_indices`, which crashes those drafts, e.g.: ``` RuntimeError: shape '[7, 128]' is invalid for input of size 1792 (at `flashinfer_sparse.py` `_build_sparse_index_metadata` when reshaping `decode_swa_indices`). ``` - Add `decode_swa_width` to `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata` and set it in the SWA builder (`window_size` or `noncausal_index_width`). - Use that width in FlashInfer `_build_sparse_index_metadata` and the ROCM ragged conversion path. ## Test Plan - [x] `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py` - [x] Manual: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark with `attention_backend: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Kimi-K3] MoRIIO KV transfer of hybrid mamba/KDA (conv+ssm) recurrent state (READ + WRITE)
signals.text: ## Purpose Enable MoRIIO 1P1D disaggregated serving for a **hybrid attention + mamba/KDA model running a speculative drafter**. The core of the PR transfers the KDA (Kimi Delta Attention / GDN linear-attention) **conv+ssm recurrent state** alongside the existing attention/MLA KV — without it the decoder starts from an uninitialised recurrent state. The other four commits are what end-to-end bring-up turned out to require; each is small and independently justified: | commit | what it does | without it | |---|---|---| | 1 | transfer the conv+ssm recurrent state (READ + WRITE), per-region sessions, `SupportsHMA` block-group split, producer-side N-1 truncation | hybrid decode starts from empty recurrent state | | 2 | reconcile decode-side geometry under a drafter: lookahead-extended block list, draft-only layers, spec align window | session build raises `KeyError`, or reads land in the wrong slots | | 3 | exclude draft-only buckets when choosing the KV-cache group size | prefill and decode group their mamba layers differently, so the two sides disagree on transfer geometry | | 4 | allow per-layer KV block length instead of asserting one uniform `block_size` | registration aborts: `block size mismatch ... 1536 != 3072` | | 5 | wait for **every** layer's read before the forward, batched, with load-error reporting | a request is judged by one transfer status and can run against KV still in flight | The recurrent-state slot rides the existing `remote_block_ids` channel as `[attn, mamba]`, so the disaggregation router needs **no model-specific changes**. Commit 3 is the only one outside the connector; it keys on the existing `non_causal_multi_token_decode` spec flag, which has a single producer in-tree and defaults to `False`, and it excludes a bucket only when *all* of its specs are marked — so a model without a drafter takes a bit-identical path. ## Test Plan - Unit (CPU): MoRIIO layout geometry, HMA scheduler split / N-1 accounting / offset-cache equivalence, `as_attn_mamba` round-trips, and transfer-completion semantics across both mori generations. - E2E: real Kimi-K3 MXFP4 weights, MI355X (gfx950), ROCm + AITER, **TP8 per leg, 1P1D cross-node over RDMA**, fp8 KV cache, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs, speculative decoding on both legs. - GSM8K 5-shot (`lm_eval`, `gsm8k.yaml`) through the disaggregation proxy, with a **matched single-engine control** on the same image and config, so the disaggregated number has a meaningful reference. - Draft-acceptance sweeps over prompt length, concurrency and multi-turn prefix reuse, against the pair and against a single engine on a dedicated node, since a transferred recurrent state can be wrong in ways that accuracy on short prompts would not reveal. ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_wait_all.py ``` ## Test Result **Unit:** 69 passed. **GSM8K 5-shot, full dataset (1319 questions), concurrency 32**, every arm running the same connector code so that only the transfer mode and the mori build differ: | arm | mori batched wait | exact_match | |---|---|---| | single engine, same image (control) | — | 0.9674 | | 1P1D **READ** | available | **0.9689** | | 1P1D **WRITE** | available | **0.9689** | | 1P1D **READ** | absent → Python-poll fallback | **0.9666** | | 1P1D **WRITE** | absent → Python-poll fallback | **0.9674** | The four disaggregated arms span 0.9666–0.9689, i.e. **three questions out of 1319**, with the single-engine control at 0.9674 sitting inside that span and a standard error of ±0.0048 (≈6 questions) on each. Disaggregated serving is therefore at parity with a single engine, and the two wait paths are indistinguishable. `strict-match` and `flexible-extract` agreed on every arm except fallback WRITE, where they differ by one question (0.9674 / 0.9682). Remaining misses are model arithmetic errors on coherent output, not transfer corruption. Which path was live was read from the logs rather than assumed (`MoRIIO batched transfer wait (wait_all) available: True|False`). **Disaggregation verified from engine counters**, not assumed: on the full run the prefill leg served 1320 requests, *all* `finished_reason=length` with exactly 1320 generation tokens — one per request, i.e. the handoff — while the decode leg served 1320 with `finished_reason=stop` and 151,921 generation tokens, with zero aborts, errors or preemptions on either side. ### Draft acceptance Accuracy alone is a weak signal for the recurrent-state transfer: the decoder recomputes the last prompt token locally, so a slightly wrong `h` can still produce a correct answer. Draft acceptance is far more sensitive, because the drafter conditions on the same state and a corrupted `h` shows up immediately as rejected proposals. With `num_speculative_tokens=2` the ceiling is an acceptance length of 3.0. Measured on the decode leg over the GSM8K runs above: | arm | mean acceptance length | per-position accept | |---|---|---| | 1P1D READ, batched wait | 2.68 | 0.92 / 0.76 | | 1P1D WRITE, batched wait | 2.66 | — | | 1P1D READ, poll fallback | 2.77 | — | | 1P1D WRITE, poll fallback | 2.77 | — | A drafter reading a corrupted recurrent state lands near 1.0 (every proposal rejected), so 2.66–2.77 across all four arms says the transferred state is usable, not merely close enough to keep the answer right. ### Long context, concurrency, and multi-turn prefix reuse GSM8K prompts are ~1k tokens and single-turn, which exercises none of the paths where a recurrent state is hardest to get right: chunked prefill over a long prompt, several requests interleaving their mamba slots, and a partial prefix-cache hit where only part of the prompt is recomputed. Each was measured directly, comparing the pair against a single engine on a dedicated node running the same build. Acceptance is computed per request from the `vllm:spec_decode_num_{drafts,draft_tokens,accepted_tokens}_total` counters read either side of it; two repeats per cell, 256 output tokens, coherent prose. Prompt length, one request in flight: | prompt tokens | single engine | 1P1D READ | |---|---|---| | 1,069 | 2.59 / 2.60 | 2.44 / 2.59 | | 7,785 | 2.22 / 2.31 | 2.27 / 2.62 | | 31,119 | 2.66 / 2.64 | 2.65 / 2.31 | | 99,116 | 2.62 / 2.62 | 2.59 / 2.69 | Acceptance is flat in prompt length and the two arms are indistinguishable at every size, including 99k tokens where prefill is chunked into many passes and the recurrent state must be snapshotted at the final chunk. **Scope:** homogeneous TP between prefill and decode (heterogeneous TP is gated with `NotImplementedError`); both legs must run the same speculative config, since the recurrent-state transfer handles symmetric grouping only; validated on one GPU family. ## Essential Elements checklist - [x] Purpose clearly stated. - [x] Test plan included. - [x] Test results included (unit + real-weights 1P1D E2E with a matched control). - [x] No router-side / proxy changes required; backward compatible with existing MoRIIO deployments. - [x] Models without a drafter are unaffected by the KV-grouping change.

signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Register the offload region in chunks
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51080. `pin_mmap_region` registers the whole offload region with one `cudaHostRegister` call. A single registration of 512 GiB or more fails with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` no matter how much host memory is free, so `cpu_bytes_to_use` at or above ~550e9 is never pinned. Measured on 4×H200 NVL with 1.3 TB free, one process, no model loaded: | region size | result | |---|---| | 20 / 300 / 400 / 500 GB | success, ~0.1 s per GB | | 549.7e9 (511.96 GiB) | success, 55.4 s | | 549.9e9 (512.15 GiB) | **fails, code=2** | | 600e9 | fails, code=2 | This became reachable with #50094: before it each rank pinned its own `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size` buffer, all far below the ceiling; after it one shared region is registered in full by every rank. Our production config (GLM-5.2, TP4/DCP4, `cpu_bytes_to_use=600e9`) stopped starting. Chunks end on block-row boundaries. Rows are page aligned (`kv_bytes_per_block % PAGESIZE == 0` is asserted in `SharedOffloadRegion`), so the driver's page rounding never makes two registrations overlap, and no single block transfer spans a boundary. Registration time scales with the bytes registered, so splitting one call into several costs nothing. On failure the chunks registered so far stay pinned rather than being rolled back — transfers through them keep the fast path, and the warning now says how much of the region was pinned. `cudaHostUnregister` takes the pointer a registration was made with, so cleanup releases each chunk. Not a duplicate: #50070 drains the latched CUDA error that a failed registration leaves behind (which is why this used to surface as a bogus `AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory` in `warm_v1_block_table_kernels`); it does not change what gets registered. The two are complementary and touch the same function, so whichever lands first leaves a small mechanical conflict for the other. Deliberately out of scope, same shape but not reachable in practice today: `ECSharedRegion.pin_memory` and `simple_kv_offload/cuda_mem_ops.py::pin_tensor` register in one call too, but those regions are orders of magnitude smaller. ## Test `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py` — three tests covering chunk boundaries, a failure part way through, and a failure on the first chunk, with `cudaHostRegister` mocked and the chunk cap lowered to two pages. ``` python3 -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py -q # 30 passed ``` The ceiling itself was measured on the 4×H200 box with the standalone probe above. An end-to-end run of the patched build at `cpu_bytes_to_use=600e9` is queued for our next maintenance window; I'll post the result here. AI assistance (Claude) was used for this work; all changes reviewed.
signals.author: drakosha

signals.title: [Bugfix][Model] Pad SigLIP text prompts to the trained sequence length
signals.text: ## Purpose SigLIP is trained with `padding="max_length"` and without an attention mask, so padding tokens are part of the input and the pooled embedding is taken from the last position. Text embeddings computed without padding are not aligned with the image embeddings, which makes image-text similarity unusable. The existing test only passes because it opts into padding explicitly: ```python # tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_siglip.py tokenization_kwargs={ "padding": "max_length", "max_length": 64, }, # siglip2 was trained with this padding setting. ``` Callers that cannot pass tokenization kwargs get silently wrong results. The request still returns 200 with a correctly shaped vector; only the values are wrong, so the failure is easy to miss in production. Two entry points need covering, and they take different routes: | entry point | source of `TokenizeParams` | inherits model defaults | |---|---|---| | `LLM.embed` | `renderer.default_cmpl_tok_params` | yes | | `/v1/embeddings` (text and chat) | `request.build_tok_params()` | **no** | `entrypoints/pooling/base/protocol.py:97-116` builds `TokenizeParams` from scratch, so a model-level default alone does not reach the OpenAI-compatible server. Note that padding text-only prompts inside `SiglipMultiModalProcessor` does **not** work: `inputs/preprocess.py:169-181` routes text-only prompts straight to `_tokenize_prompt` and never reaches the multi-modal processor. I verified this by instrumenting `apply()` — during the text test it is only ever called with dummy profiling data. ## Fix Two small pieces. **1. The model declares its requirement** through the existing `BaseProcessingInfo.get_default_tok_params` extension point, which ten models already override (`paligemma`, `gemma4_mm`, `ovis`, `ovis2_5`, `whisper`, `ultravox`, `cohere_asr`, `lfm2_vl`, `nano_nemotron_vl`, `nemotron_parse`): ```python def get_default_tok_params(self) -> "TokenizeParams": tok_params = super().get_default_tok_params() return tok_params.with_kwargs(pad_prompt_tokens=self.get_text_max_length()) ``` **2. The renderer applies that default** when a frontend builds `TokenizeParams` without one, in `_tokenize_singleton_prompt` and its async twin: ```python if params.pad_prompt_tokens is not None or prompt.get("multi_modal_data"): return params ``` Both guards matter. Explicitly requested padding wins. Multi-modal prompts are skipped because `renderers/base.py:786` tokenizes the prompt *before* multi-modal processing on the online path, so without the guard image requests would be padded too. The padding machinery itself already exists (`TokenizeParams.pad_prompt_tokens`, `_token_padding`); this only turns it on for a model that needs it. Models that declare nothing get `None` and the helper returns the params unchanged. ### Known trade-off A caller who deliberately passes `padding=False` for SigLIP will still get the model default reapplied, so there is no opt-out. Note this is not caused by the fallback alone. `TokenizeParams.with_kwargs` guards the padding mapping with a truthiness check: ```python if padding := tokenization_kwargs.pop("padding", None): if padding == "max_length": pad_prompt_tokens = max_length elif padding in (False, "do_not_pad"): # unreachable pad_prompt_tokens = None ``` `padding=False` is falsy, so the key is popped and the `elif` never runs — `padding=False` is already a no-op on `main` for any model whose default sets `pad_prompt_tokens`. Consequently "disabled" and "unspecified" are indistinguishable to the fallback, and it reapplies the default. I judged that acceptable because unpadded SigLIP is simply incorrect, but I am happy to add an explicit sentinel if maintainers prefer to keep the opt-out. Fixing the dead `elif` branch itself looks like a separate change; happy to send one if that is wanted. ### Alternative considered Setting `pad_prompt_tokens` inside `_build_pooling_tok_params` would avoid touching the renderer, but it only fixes frontends that build `TokenizeParams` and puts a model-specific rule in the entrypoints layer. Happy to move the fix there if preferred. ## Test plan `test_models_text` is parametrized over `explicit_padding`. Both cases compare against the same HF reference computed with padding, so `explicit_padding=False` fails on `main`. `tests/renderers/test_default_padding.py` covers the server route by building `TokenizeParams` exactly the way the pooling endpoints do (no padding field). It runs on CPU in seconds. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_siglip.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/renderers/ -q ``` ## Test result All three models in `MODELS`, on an NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121, aarch64, CUDA 13.0): ``` $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_siglip.py \ tests/renderers/test_default_padding.py -v test_models_text[True-float-google/siglip-base-patch16-224] PASSED test_models_text[True-float-google/siglip2-base-patch16-224] PASSED test_models_text[True-float-google/siglip2-giant-opt-patch16-384] PASSED test_models_text[False-float-google/siglip-base-patch16-224] PASSED test_models_text[False-float-google/siglip2-base-patch16-224] PASSED test_models_text[False-float-google/siglip2-giant-opt-patch16-384] PASSED test_models_image[float-google/siglip-base-patch16-224] PASSED test_models_image[float-google/siglip2-base-patch16-224] PASSED test_models_image[float-google/siglip2-giant-opt-patch16-384] PASSED test_models_text_image_no_crash[float-google/siglip-base-patch16-224] PASSED test_models_text_image_no_crash[float-google/siglip2-base-patch16-224] PASSED test_models_text_image_no_crash[float-google/siglip2-giant-opt-patch16-384] PASSED test_default_padding::test_model_default_is_applied PASSED test_default_padding::test_explicit_padding_is_not_overridden PASSED test_default_padding::test_multimodal_prompts_are_not_padded PASSED 15 passed in 2085.08s (0:34:45) ``` The same suite passes on an RTX 4070 SUPER (sm_89, x86_64, CUDA 12.8, vLLM built from source) for the two base models — 8 passed, giant skipped there for disk reasons. Full renderer suite on that machine, to check the shared `renderers/base.py` change against every other model: ``` $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/renderers/ -q 1 failed, 428 passed in 469.25s ``` The single failure is `test_hf.py::test_resolve_content_format_fallbacks[facebook/chameleon-7b-string]`, which fails identically on unpatched `main` — unrelated to this change. ### Reverse check Reverting only the changed source files and rerunning: | test | unpatched `main` | with this change | |---|---|---| | `test_models_text[False-...siglip-base-patch16-224]` | **FAIL**, cosine 0.5006 vs HF | PASS | | `test_models_text[True-...siglip-base-patch16-224]` | PASS | PASS | | `test_default_padding::test_model_default_is_applied` | **FAIL**, `assert 9 == 64` | PASS | | `test_default_padding::test_explicit_padding_is_not_overridden` | PASS | PASS | | `test_default_padding::test_multimodal_prompts_are_not_padded` | PASS | PASS | ### Lint `pre-commit run --files <the four changed files>` passes, including `mypy` for Python 3.10 and `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`. ## Model evaluation Zero-shot classification through `LLM.embed` on `google/siglip-base-patch16-224`, two images from `vllm.assets.image` against three labels. Cosine similarity, argmax picks the label. Before (unpatched `main`): | image | "a photo of a stop sign" | "a photo of a cherry blossom" | "a scanned tax invoice" | picked | |---|---|---|---|---| | stop sign | −0.0245 | −0.0166 | −0.0422 | cherry blossom (wrong) | | cherry blossom | −0.0684 | −0.0348 | −0.0488 | cherry blossom | After: | image | "a photo of a stop sign" | "a photo of a cherry blossom" | "a scanned tax invoice" | picked | |---|---|---|---|---| | stop sign | **0.1567** | 0.0114 | −0.0974 | stop sign | | cherry blossom | −0.0089 | **0.1033** | −0.0942 | cherry blossom | The accuracy change (1/2 to 2/2) understates it: before the change every similarity is negative and near zero, so there is no signal at all and the one correct pick is accidental. SigLIP's `logit_scale` (~118) and `logit_bias` (~−12.7) put the 0.5 probability threshold at a cosine of about 0.107, which only the patched matching pairs clear. Image-image cosine is 0.5879 in both runs, so the vision tower is untouched and only the cross-modal alignment changed. ## Duplicate check Checked 2026-08-05, no overlapping work found: ```bash gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "siglip" gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "siglip padding" ``` Open PRs mentioning siglip are unrelated (MiniCPM-RobotTrack, a Gemma 4 fp16 overflow fix, PaddleOCR-VL CUDA graph support, DeepSeek-VL2). Open issues mentioning siglip are unrelated. \#29794 added `tokenization_kwargs` to the offline API and is already merged; this PR covers the case where the caller cannot pass them. ## AI assistance This change was prepared with AI assistance. The submitter has reviewed every changed line, run the tests above, and can defend the change.

signals.title: [Feature] IndexCache for DeepSeek-V4 (validated on V4-Flash-0731, including DSpark on to accelerate on top of
signals.text: ## Summary: This work is built to support Dspark + IndexerCache to achieve best deepseek v4 flash serving performance. ## Purpose Adds DSA IndexCache support to DeepSeek-V4, so C4A layers marked shared reuse the top-k the previous C4A layer left in the shared `topk_indices_buffer` instead of running their own indexer. Same config surface as the DeepSeek-V3.2 feature (`use_index_cache` / `index_topk_freq` / `index_topk_pattern`, see [docs/features/index_cache.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/features/index_cache.md)); addresses #45350. The indexer dominates decode KV traffic on this model at long context: per decode token per C4A layer it reads `(S/4) x 132 B` of its own K cache, while the main sparse MLA reads only `index_topk x 576 B`. Across DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's 21 C4A / 20 C128A / 44 SWA caches that is ~65% of decode KV traffic at 32K and ~81% at 128K, and the indexer is TP-replicated so every rank pays it in full. ### Relationship to #49085 #49085 implements the same feature for Hopper and is the earlier work; its authors (@wangyicong52, @zzz3bbb3) got there first on the two non-obvious points — per-PP-rank handling, and keeping skipped indexers' KV-cache specs registered while parking their linear weights on the meta device. Two behavioural differences worth a maintainer decision: 1. This PR gates on `use_index_cache`, matching the documented V3.2 surface. #49085 activates on `index_topk_freq > 1` alone, which would make `--hf-overrides '{"index_topk_freq": 4}'` silently enable on V4 while silently doing nothing on V3.2. 2. This PR uses `c4a_idx % index_topk_freq`; #49085 keeps V3.2's `index_skip_topk_offset` (default 2), so its first two C4A layers always compute. Theirs is more faithful to V3.2 and I am happy to switch. ## Design notes Only C4A layers (`compress_ratio == 4`) carry an indexer in V4, so **the frequency and pattern are indexed over the C4A layers, not over all layers**. Applying the V3.2 absolute-`layer_id` formula to DeepSeek-V4-Flash marks *every* C4A layer as shared (they are all even), so nothing populates the buffer and every layer reads stale contents — silently, with no error. A regression test pins this. Three further constraints, each covered by a test: - `topk_indices_buffer` is rank-local, so the first C4A layer **of each pipeline stage** computes its own top-k (derived from the same `get_pp_indices` split `make_layers` uses). - `compress_ratios` can be longer than `num_hidden_layers` (44 entries on V4-Flash, 46 on V4-Flash-0731, for the MTP/draft slots), so selection slices to `num_hidden_layers`. - A pattern is one `F`/`S` character per C4A layer — 21 on V4-Flash-0731, not 43 — and may not start with `S`. Wrong-length patterns raise rather than silently applying a prefix. Skipped layers keep their indexer allocated and simply never run it, so the change is confined to `attention.py` and needs no KV-cache-grouping or weight-loading changes. Memory savings are left to a follow-up. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_index_cache.py -v ``` E2E hardware: single node, 8xH100 80GB, TP=8, upstream vLLM 0.26.0 with this patch, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`. ```bash # long context / frequency sweep vllm bench latency --model <0731> --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 -tp 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 33792 \ --input-len 32768 --output-len 128 --batch-size 2 \ --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": N}' # quality: GSM8K 200q 5-shot, MMLU 500q 5-shot, greedy # throughput: short prompt + 512 output tokens at fixed concurrency ``` ## Test Result 14/14 unit tests pass. ### Frequency sensitivity 32768-token input x batch 2, and MMLU 500 questions 5-shot. All arms are the same build with only `index_topk_freq` varying, so `freq=1`/off is a true no-skip control (confirmed by the log line firing only on freq>1 arms): | freq | indexers run | 32K latency | Δ | MMLU | |---|---|---|---|---| | off / 1 | 21/21 | 3.004 s | — | 85.4% | | 2 | 11/21 | 2.890 s | -3.8% | 85.6% | | 3 | 7/21 | 2.842 s | -5.4% | 85.0% | | 4 | 6/21 | 2.831 s | -5.8% | 84.8% | | 6 | 4/21 | 2.808 s | -6.5% | 85.0% | The latency curve saturates quickly — freq=2 captures most of the win, and skipping three times as many indexers (freq=6) only reaches -6.5%. MMLU spans 84.8-85.6%, within the ~1.6pp binomial noise at n=500. vLLM 0.25.1 and the older `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` checkpoint reproduce the freq=2/3 numbers within noise. ### Quality and throughput matrix (GSM8K, 200q 5-shot, best of 3 timed passes) | cell | DSpark | IndexCache | accuracy | throughput | |---|---|---|---|---| | c4 | off | off | 96.0%, 96.5% | 4087, 4525 tok/s | | c2 | off | **on** | 96.0%, 96.0% | 4322, 4081 tok/s | | c1 | **on** | off | 96.0%, 97.0% | 3449, 3742 tok/s | | c3 | **on** | **on** | 97.0% | 3873 tok/s | IndexCache changes neither accuracy nor throughput here. Note this shape is ~91% prefill tokens (180K prefill vs 17K decode) and saturates the GPU, so it is not informative about speculative decoding; the concurrency sweep below is. ### Throughput vs concurrency (short prompt, 512 output tokens) | concurrency | c4 baseline | c1 DSpark | c3 DSpark + IndexCache | |---|---|---|---| | 4 | 560 tok/s | **1419** | 1201 | | 16 | 1670 tok/s | 3289 | **3419** | | 64 | 4910 tok/s | 6975 | **7187** | The two features are complementary and stack: at the concurrencies that matter for serving, DSpark + IndexCache is the fastest configuration. Draft acceptance is 63-69% (mean accepted length 4.2-4.5 of 5) with IndexCache both on and off, so IndexCache does not measurably degrade the draft. ### Long-context correctness A needle-in-a-haystack probe (18,930-token prompt, needle at depth 0.15 / 0.5 / 0.85, greedy) retrieves correctly with IndexCache off, at freq=2, and at freq=3. ### DSpark interaction DeepSeek-V4's DSpark draft builds its decoder layers with `topk_indices_buffer=None` and layer ids >= `num_hidden_layers`, so draft layers resolve to `compress_ratio == 1` and never construct an indexer; the two features are structurally orthogonal. Enabling both is exercised end to end at every concurrency above. ## Notes Not covered, stated rather than implied: no Blackwell run (#49085 hard-rejects non-SM90 for this feature; this PR does not gate, which may be wrong); no PP>1 e2e run (the per-stage rule is unit-tested only); Meanwhile, if B200 number testing needed, I will provide later follow up test in NVFP4. AI Assistance are used for this development. --- ## Full measurement set (AIPerf) Everything below is `aiperf profile` against `vllm serve` on the same node: single 8xH100 80GB, TP=8, upstream vLLM 0.26.0 + this patch, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, AIPerf 0.12.0. Output length is pinned with `ignore_eos:true` + `min_tokens` (without it the model stops early and throughput deltas measure differing OSL, not speed), `--request-count` = 16x concurrency, `--warmup-request-count` = concurrency. `ISL x concurrency` is chosen to fit the ~108K-token KV pool at each point; beyond that requests queue and the run becomes a scheduling test rather than a throughput test. ### Controls Two arms exist purely to bound what a real effect must beat: - **`freq=1`** enables IndexCache but skips nothing, so it must land on top of `off`. It does, everywhere. - **`off` re-run** gives the run-to-run noise floor. | control | throughput delta vs `off` | |---|---| | `freq=1`, all five workloads | -0.1% .. +0.1% | | `off` re-run, 3 workloads | -0.1% .. +0.0% | TTFT is the exception: identical configs vary by up to 5.8% on the 4K point, so no TTFT claim below ~6% is meaningful there. ### Output token throughput, delta vs `off` | workload | ISL/OSL | conc | freq=1 | freq=2 | freq=3 | freq=4 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | summarisation (prefill-heavy) | 32K / 16 | 3 | -0.0% | +3.3% | +5.2% | **+5.6%** | | long chat | 32K / 256 | 3 | +0.1% | +3.5% | +4.9% | **+5.2%** | | mid chat | 16K / 256 | 6 | +0.0% | +2.8% | +3.9% | **+4.2%** | | RAG | 7K / 172 | 12 | +0.1% | — | **+3.2%** | — | | short chat | 4K / 256 | 24 | -0.1% | +2.0% | +2.8% | **+3.1%** | Absolute baselines: 13.63, 146.34, 285.82, 466.5, 1057.42 out tok/s respectively. ### Latency, delta vs `off` (freq=4; freq=3 for RAG) | workload | e2e | TTFT | ITL | |---|---|---|---| | 32K / 16 | -5.3% | -5.1% | — | | 32K / 256 | -5.0% | -5.1% | -4.8% | | 16K / 256 | -4.0% | -4.6% | -3.7% | | 7K / 172 | -3.1% | -2.7% | — | | 4K / 256 | -3.0% | -1.9% | -3.2% | ### Accuracy per frequency | freq | GSM8K (200q, 5-shot) | MMLU (500q, 5-shot) | |---|---|---| | off | 96.0% | 85.4% | | 1 (control) | 96.0% | 85.0% | | 2 | 95.5% | 85.4% | | 3 | 96.0% | **86.2%** | | 4 | **96.5%** | 85.0% | No trend: the best GSM8K score is at freq=4 and the best MMLU at freq=3, and the `freq=1` control differs from `off` by 0.4pp on MMLU while being semantically identical to it. All deltas sit inside that noise. **This is a no-harm result, not proof of quality preservation.** Both benchmarks' prompts (~900 and ~500 tokens, i.e. ~225 and ~125 compressed) are below `index_topk=512`, so every layer selects the whole compressed sequence and IndexCache is mathematically a no-op. Long-context quality evidence is limited to the needle probe (retrieved at all three depths with IndexCache off, freq=2 and freq=3); a RULER/LongBench run at 32K is still owed. ### Where the time actually goes A torch-profiler run (eager, prefix caching off, conc 12 at 8K) attributes GPU kernel time as: | bucket | freq=0 | freq=6 | |---|---|---| | TP all-reduce + other | 6176 ms | 5254 ms | | MoE | 1003 ms | 980 ms | | norm/rope | 395 ms | 394 ms | | **indexer** | **91.7 ms (1.2%)** | **30.4 ms (0.4%)** | | compressor | 43 ms | 42 ms | The indexer is 1.2% of kernel time; the single largest kernel is `cross_device_reduce_1stage` (TP all-reduce) at ~69%. Removing 81% of the indexer work saves 61 ms directly, yet wall-clock improves several percent — the rest comes from ranks spending less time waiting inside the all-reduce. This configuration is communication-bound, which is also why the gain saturates between freq=3 and freq=4 (+0.3-0.4pp) and why a faster indexer kernel would not help much. ### Interaction with DSpark speculative decoding Decode-heavy (short prompt, 512 output tokens, `ignore_eos`), output tok/s: | concurrency | baseline | DSpark | DSpark + IndexCache | |---|---|---|---| | 4 | 560 | **1419** | 1201 | | 16 | 1670 | 3289 | **3419** | | 64 | 4910 | 6975 | **7187** | At serving concurrencies the two stack and DSpark + IndexCache is the fastest configuration. Draft acceptance is 63-69% (mean accepted length 4.2-4.5 of 5) with IndexCache both on and off, so IndexCache does not measurably degrade the draft. ### Honest summary of magnitude **+3% to +5.6%** depending on shape and frequency, saturating at freq=3-4, free at inference time, with no measurable accuracy cost in the regimes tested. That is smaller than the 7-8% reported for vllm-ascend in #45350. On this hardware the gap is explained by the profile above (communication-bound, indexer at 1.2%), by the KV pool capping `ISL x concurrency` so the indexer's share cannot grow, and by Hopper reading an FP8 indexer cache at 132 B/token where `use_fp4_indexer_cache` would halve it. ### Measurement caveats - The e2e numbers were produced by the 0.26.0-based build; upstream restructured `attention_impl` in #51430 after 0.26.0, so the rebased branch carries the same gates at the new call sites but has not itself been re-run on GPU. - One RAG data point initially showed +9.8%; its `freq=1` control read +6.6%, which flagged the baseline as un-warmed. A repeat with two independent baseline arms put the true figure at +3.2%. The table above uses the corrected value. - Single node only: no Blackwell run, and no PP>1 run (the per-stage rule is unit-tested only).

signals.title: [V1] Fix CPU sampler ignoring request seeds in mixed batches (#51226)
signals.text: Correct the logic check in TopKTopPSampler.forward_cpu to ensure we only skip to the compiled unseeded random sampler if all requests in the batch have no custom generators (seeds). If even one request in the batch has a seed, we fall back to the native path to correctly isolate and apply each request's seed generator. Also make uvloop optional in llm/v1/utils.py to allow importing and running test suites on Windows/macOS. ## Purpose Fixes issue #51226. Currently, `TopKTopPSampler.forward_cpu` selects the compiled unseeded random sampler whenever `len(generators) != batch_size`. This causes request-specific seeds to be completely ignored on CPU when running in a batch alongside unseeded requests. This PR changes the check to `len(generators) == 0` so that the compiled unseeded sampler is only used when no request in the batch is seeded. If any request is seeded, the sampler falls back to the native Gumbel sampling path which correctly applies the request generators. Additionally, this PR makes the `uvloop` import in `vllm/v1/utils.py` optional (falling back to standard library `asyncio`) so that vLLM V1 can be imported and unit-tested on Windows/macOS. ## Test Plan I added the unit test `test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding` in `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py` which creates a batch of two requests (one seeded, one unseeded) and verifies that the seeded request remains fully deterministic across runs while the unseeded request remains non-deterministic. Run the test command: $env:PYTHONPATH="."; .venv\Scripts\python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -v -k test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding ## Test Result tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py::test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding PASSED [100%] =================== 1 passed, 131 deselected in 3.08s =================== --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [BugFix] Apply length caps in check_stop even when min_tokens is not reached
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes a request hang in the V1 scheduler when `min_tokens` cannot be reached within the model's context window. `check_stop()` in `vllm/v1/core/sched/utils.py` returns early while `num_output_tokens < min_tokens`. That early return was added in #26317 to keep EOS / stop tokens from ending a request too early, but it also skips the `max_model_len` / `max_tokens` length checks below it. So if a request hits `max_model_len` before reaching `min_tokens`, nothing ever stops it: the scheduler computes `num_new_tokens == 0` for it on every step and skips it, and the request sits in the running queue forever holding its KV blocks and a request slot. `llm.generate()` never returns and the engine core keeps spinning on an otherwise idle server. This combination passes parameter validation, so it's easy to hit: - explicitly, with `max_tokens == min_tokens` larger than the remaining context: ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams llm = LLM(model="facebook/opt-125m", max_model_len=128, enforce_eager=True) # hangs forever before this PR llm.generate(["Hello, my name is"], SamplingParams(max_tokens=500, min_tokens=500, ignore_eos=True)) ``` - or implicitly: `min_tokens <= max_tokens` is validated when `SamplingParams` is constructed, but with `max_tokens=None` the input processor later clamps `max_tokens` to `max_model_len - prompt_len`, which can end up below `min_tokens` with no re-check. Per its docstring, `min_tokens` is only supposed to hold back EOS and `stop_token_ids`; the min-tokens logits processor and the stop-string check in the detokenizer already work that way. This PR moves the gate in `check_stop()` so it only defers the EOS / stop-token checks and the length caps always apply. When `min_tokens` is already satisfied the checks run in the same order as before, so behavior there is unchanged. Repetition detection stays behind the `min_tokens` gate as today. I didn't find an existing issue or PR for this: #26317 introduced the early return but only considered EOS, #47489 is about terminal grammars under `min_tokens` and its current diff still skips the length caps below `min_tokens`, and #27640 was a pure reorder that was closed unmerged. AI assistance (GitHub Copilot CLI) was used to prepare this PR. ## Test Plan Added a regression test next to the existing `check_stop` min_tokens test. It fails on current main and passes with this fix: ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_check_stop_length_cap_below_min_tokens \ tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_check_stop_min_tokens ``` Also ran on a single RTX PRO 6000 (torch 2.11.0+cu130): ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/ pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_min_tokens.py pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_engine_core_advanced_sampling \ tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_engine_core pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/utils.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py ``` plus the repro script above and a quick decode-throughput A/B (opt-125m, 256 prompts x 200 tokens, 3 runs each) since `check_stop` runs per generated token. ## Test Result - new regression test: fails on main, passes with the fix - repro script: hangs indefinitely before (killed after 240s, engine spinning with 0 scheduled tokens); finishes with 122 tokens / `finish_reason=length` after - `tests/v1/core/`: 463 passed, 1 failed — `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, which fails identically on clean main - `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_min_tokens.py`: 7 passed, 6 xpassed (stale xfail marks, see #47487) - engine core tests: 2 passed - pre-commit and `git diff --check`: clean - throughput: 38.3k tok/s with the fix vs 38.9k without (median of 3), within run-to-run noise --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip redundant sparse index remap on non-indexer layers
signals.text: ## Summary With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer. The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer. This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip cleaning sparse prefill MQA logits
signals.text: ## Summary The sparse prefill path creates the MQA-logits buffer with `torch.full(..., -inf)`. This launches an FP32 fill before every logits kernel. This PR passes `clean_logits=False` to AITER, so the buffer uses `torch.empty` and the fill is removed. ## Safety The only consumer is `top_k_per_row_prefill`. It reads each row only inside `[cu_seqlen_ks, cu_seqlen_ke)`. Its vectorized path also guards the final partial load, so padding values are never read. signals.title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Revert adaptive C128A metadata packing
signals.text: ## Summary Revert the adaptive C128A top-k width and packed persistent-buffer views introduced by #50004. The C128A metadata builder runs before FULL CUDA graph replay, but the sparse decode consumer is captured and reuses its capture-time row layout. With #50004, runtime metadata writes packed rows using a batch-dependent `active_topk_width`, while the captured consumer retained the capture-time row stride. Row 0 still started at offset 0, but later rows could be read from stale offsets. This change restores: - `c128a_max_compressed` as the metadata width - capacity-strided slices of the persistent decode and prefill buffers - each persistent buffer's `stride(0)` for Triton metadata writes - removal of the test that asserted the packed layout being reverted Fixes #52448. ## Validation ```text git diff --check .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py ``` All applicable hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, lazy-import, and forbidden-import checks. The full revert was also evaluated with the exact #52448 request on 2x NVIDIA GB300 using `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` revision `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062`, TP=2 plus expert parallelism, DSpark-7, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `max_model_len=70000`, concurrency 32, and `max_tokens=16384`: - 256 priming requests plus 256 measured requests - 0/256 issue-signature hits - 0 request errors and 0 `length` finishes - 253 `tool_calls` finishes and 3 `stop` finishes - 8.445 s median measured latency ## Contribution notes - Not a duplicate: `52448 in:body` found no other open PR. The open C128A/sparse-MLA keyword matches (#48805, #41836, and #41834) address warmup, prefill, or model enablement rather than reverting #50004. This updates the existing #51318 instead of opening another PR. - AI assistance was used for investigation, patch preparation, validation, and this PR update. The submitting human must review every changed line and be able to defend the change before merge.

signals.title: [Perf] Cache streaming parser drop metadata
signals.text: ## Summary - cache immutable special-token drop metadata used by streaming parser engines - key the bounded cache by the config and tokenizer content the builder actually reads - verify equivalent per-request parser configs hit the cache ## Why `StreamingParserEngine` is created per request, while its config and tokenizer contents are effectively engine-wide. Each construction currently recompiles escaped special-token regexes and rebuilds the same immutable `LexerShape`. In the originating B200 profile at a batch around 975, parser construction accounted for 1.9% of engine-thread samples, primarily in this builder. The cache is content-keyed rather than object-identity-keyed, so equivalent config instances share an entry and tokenizer special-token changes naturally miss. It is capped at 64 entries. ## Duplicate check I searched open vLLM PRs for `build drop info reasoning parser cache` and `_build_drop_info`. I found no open PR changing or caching this path; the broad search results were unrelated model, parser-regression, and kernel work. ## Measured performance A pinned-hardware Nebius B200 A/B (`qwen35_per_request_patch_ab_2026-08-06.md`) used an Intel Xeon Platinum 8580 host, structured mode, 1,000 concurrency, and 180-second unprofiled runs: - Output throughput was **11,857 → 11,890 tok/s (+0.28%)**, inside the independently measured **0.32% noise floor**; both arms had zero errors. - In separate py-spy captures, `_build_drop_info` fell **1.5% → 0 samples** of the EngineCore main thread. Its `_get_reasoner` parent fell **1.9% → 0.4%**. - `scheduler.schedule` fell **33.5% → 32.0%**, while `gpu_wait` rose **9.7% → 12.1%**, consistent with the removed CPU work becoming main-thread slack on an already GPU-saturated workload. The benchmark used the SafetyKit memo implementation rather than this bounded `lru_cache`, but it memoized the same pure `_build_drop_info` result. The unambiguous result is removal of the targeted parser-construction work; the +0.28% throughput delta is noise, not a claimed serving-throughput win. ## Validation - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py -q` — 38 passed - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q` — 3,738 passed - targeted Ruff check and format hooks — passed - commit-time pre-commit suite — passed The planned Nebius validation adds a serving-level reasoning/tool-call corpus comparison and an A/B/A high-concurrency profile to confirm output identity and reduced parser initialization samples. ## AI assistance This change was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand and defend the implementation, and run the listed Nebius validation before marking the PR ready.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Save exact Mamba boundary states
signals.text: ## Summary Fix Mooncake Store persistence for Mamba `align` mode by saving the exact core-selected boundary-state blocks and keeping those physical blocks alive until every worker rank has finished the asynchronous store attempt. This fixes a correctness bug that could persist null, stale/reassigned, or live speculative Mamba state under a valid prefix hash. A later external prefix hit could then restore poisoned recurrent state and produce garbled or runaway output. ## Root cause Mooncake's normal save path resolved each group's source block positionally from a worker-side snapshot of the request's block IDs. That is valid for append-only attention block tables, but a Mamba `align` table is sparse and mutable: - superseded state positions are replaced by the null block and their physical blocks are freed; - speculative scratch blocks are relocated to different logical positions; - the connector's block-ID mirror is append-only and does not observe those in-place changes. Consequently, a positional Mamba save could interpret `NULL_BLOCK_ID` as a physical source, or read a block that had already been freed, reassigned, or was still speculative, while using the correct chained prefix hash as its key. Mooncake's `batch_is_exist` deduplication could then preserve the bad value and prevent a later correct save from replacing it. The production symptom was exposed by the DSpark/EAGLE lookup path landing on an affected interior key. Without that path, a later valid CoW boundary key could win and mask the corruption. ## Design - Core emits exact `(group_id, block_id, boundary_tokens)` entries for committed Mamba `align` boundary states, including the CoW target for a sub-block partial tail. The connector never reconstructs these source IDs positionally. - Mooncake excludes Mamba groups from the normal positional `store_mask`; exact boundary handoffs are the only Mamba writer. The normal path also skips null or missing source IDs for every group as a defense-in-depth guard. - The scheduler claims each accepted physical block with `BlockPool.touch()` before it can be recycled. Consumer-only roles are gated before claiming or queueing handoffs. - Each claimed block receives a monotonic handoff ID. A one-ID/one-pin mapping makes reference release and the bounded in-flight capacity exact, even though a request-level batch ID could work while all entries in a request complete together. - Workers report a cross-rank completion watermark. After seeing its first handoff, a rank reports watermark `0` while that handoff is pending rather than omitting metadata; this prevents aggregation from ignoring a lagging rank and releasing a block early. Dedup, successful upload, pressure drop, cancellation, and store failure are all terminal outcomes for lifetime purposes. - The scheduler releases the connector-owned refs only through `BlockPool.free_blocks()` after the aggregated watermark says every rank is terminal. The configurable in-flight cap bounds pinned GPU blocks if acknowledgements stop; saves beyond the cap remain best-effort and are dropped. - Resumed prefills use the tracked prefill/save boundary, not the request's original prompt length, so replayed generated tokens retain the same cross-group save coverage. - Mamba speculative scratch relocation remains an in-table move, but now fails closed unless `BlockPool.is_block_writable()` confirms the block is non-null, exclusively owned (`ref_cnt == 1`), and unhashed. If shared or pinned speculative blocks become valid in the future, this path must use CoW instead of relocating them. This implementation is intentionally limited to Mamba `align` mode. Mooncake Store's configuration validation rejects incompatible non-align/`all` Mamba layouts; this PR does not add `all`-mode support. ## Retention semantics `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` remains effective even though Mooncake's positional `store_mask` is false for Mamba: 1. Core `MambaManager.cache_blocks()` applies the retention policy first. 2. Only retained/materialized states receive a block hash. 3. Handoff emission skips null or unhashed blocks. 4. Mooncake stores the exact retained states from those handoffs. Therefore dense default retention, sparse interval checkpoints, and replay-boundary behavior are preserved. External persistence is still best-effort: an eligible checkpoint may be absent if the handoff cap is reached or the store operation fails. ## Scope and overlap This is not duplicate work: - #50359 validates external lookup boundaries. - #46896 and #46906 concern Mamba all-mode support and retention policy. - #51362 independently adds the same defensive null/missing-block check to Mooncake's normal save loop. That check is included here, but this PR also removes unsafe positional Mamba saving and fixes exact source selection, asynchronous lifetime, retention-aware handoff, partial-tail handling, and speculative ownership. In that sense, this PR subsumes #51362's behavior rather than relying on it. ## Validation Focused Mooncake Store and prefix-cache suites were run through the final design, including exact block-ID handoff, dense and sparse retention, partial tails, resumed prefills, more than two Mamba groups, null/missing sources, consumer skip-save behavior, cross-rank watermarking, bounded pins, failure paths, and exclusive speculative ownership. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py ``` Result: 183 passed. Additional focused reruns after the watermark, save-gate, and ownership-invariant changes passed (195 tests), and a broader Mooncake Store + prefix-cache run in the k3-debug container on a GB300 worker passed (219 tests). Ruff and `git diff --check` also passed. Serving/model evaluation on `k3-pd-mooncake aa-lcr`: - post-fix: 0/200 garbled responses; - `llm_judge`: approximately 0.77/0.76; - external prefix hit rate: approximately 91–98%; - pre-fix baseline: garbled/runaway outputs, with `llm_judge` approximately 0.76/0.78. No model kernels or numerical computation were changed. AI assistance was used. The human submitter reviewed the changes and is responsible for understanding, testing, and defending the final submission.

signals.title: [Frontend] Add reusable TP1 initialized-engine snapshots
signals.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 MD041 --> ## Purpose RFC #34303 and #37921/#37925 separate in-process CUDA checkpoint primitives from CRIU disk persistence. #35934 explores a CRIU-safe engine lifecycle. #42790, #46089, and #52132 use provider or runtime-sleep boundaries. #40323 tested a pre-model image containing Python imports and a CUDA context. My closed #48996 measured the earlier boundary at about 29.08 seconds ordinary versus 29.09 seconds restored, n=3 per arm. Engine construction still happened after restore. This PR captures a TP1 engine after initialization and a deterministic generation canary, but before HTTP bind. The same-host artifact serves operators who repeatedly activate the same stopped engine. They exchange local disk and host privilege for activation time. ```bash vllm snapshot create MODEL --snapshot-dir PATH --revision MODEL_SHA [serve args] vllm snapshot inspect PATH vllm snapshot restore PATH --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 ``` Restore validates artifact identity before CRIU, then restores the process tree and CUDA state. It binds HTTP only after the public API reproduces the captured token IDs, text, and sampled-token log probability. It fails closed and does not silently fall back to ordinary startup. ## Measured The largest matched campaign used source `5dd888926ffecb2409874810bd07402f3bc7dd3c`, Qwen3-32B BF16 TP1, and one H100 PCIe 80 GB. Model and generated-cache files were fully resident. Compact artifact files were fully evicted before each restore. Each arm ran three times through the first checked public token. | Path | Median activation | Samples | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Ordinary warm process | 54.7029 s | 3 | | Compact snapshot restore | 20.3795 s | 3 | | Reduction | 34.3234 s, 62.7% | 3 per arm | The compact artifact used 5,879,914,496 allocated bytes, about 5.88 GB. Creation took 78.5275 seconds, n=1. The model files remain external and totaled 65,540,298,478 bytes. Counting creation, the measured saving breaks even on the third activation. Every accepted trial returned token ID `12095` and text ` Paris`. Each completed six additional exact-token requests and left no matching process or GPU process. Restore logs contained no CUDA graph recapture markers after the captured boundary. The earlier matched full-state result used Qwen3-0.6B FP16 TP1 with warm local caches, n=5 per arm: | GPU | Ordinary warm process | Full-state restore | Reduction | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | NVIDIA A10 | 23.9121 s | 9.4234 s | 14.4888 s, 60.6% | | RTX 4090 Laptop GPU | 15.7790 s | 5.5488 s | 10.2302 s, 64.8% | On Qwen3-8B FP16 TP1 on the A10, compact state reduced allocated storage by 78.8 percent, from 24,231,231,488 to 5,144,281,088 bytes. Compact restore was 21.2396 seconds versus 23.7633 seconds for full-state restore, median n=3 per path. This cell uses a different model and starting state from the full-state benchmark, so the savings are not additive. Cold or slow model storage can reverse the compact latency result. ## The fix `vllm snapshot create` defaults to compact capture. The existing sleep level 2 lifecycle releases reloadable model and KV state. Creation restores that state, reruns the canary, then releases it again before capture. Restore reconstructs the released state before HTTP bind. `--include-model-state` keeps full state for local or mutable model sources and speculative decoding. It also supports deployments that prefer a larger artifact over model reload. The user contract includes: - strict manifest validation over the supported host, software, model, engine arguments, selected environment, process tree, sockets, and checkpoint tools, - private atomic artifact publication only after a complete dump, - exact token ID and text validation plus a bounded sampled-token log-probability comparison before readiness, - pidfd-pinned ownership for post-restore cleanup, with no signaling from an untrusted numeric PID, - fail-closed rejection of unsupported topology, external established TCP connections, active `io_uring`, mutable compact model sources, and incompatible runtime options, and - no concurrent initialized-snapshot or external CRIU link-remap workflow in the shared `/dev/shm` namespace. ## Review update This revision addresses the four maintainer review points: - The console entry point is `vllm.entrypoints.cli.main:main`. There is no top-level `vllm_bootstrap` package. - Top-level and snapshot-restore parsing happen before runtime imports. `vllm --help` and the useful core surface of `vllm serve --help` stay lightweight, while rich serve help uses the canonical parser. - Snapshot create and restore preserve the caller's complete `VLLM_*` mapping. Child-only defaults are passed through a copied subprocess environment. - The official Linux x86-64 runtime image builds pinned CRIU 4.2.1 and its matching CUDA plugin from source. It also builds a pinned Apache-2.0 helper from NVIDIA Dynamo against the public CUDA Driver checkpoint APIs. The install is gated to x86-64, and initialized snapshots remain unsupported on arm64. The obsolete `VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1` examples are removed because #51219 is merged. Compact capture is now the default, and `vllm snapshot restore` accepts only the artifact plus frontend bind arguments. The H20 report on the previous public head found three issues. CRIU dump and restore now use `--file-locks`. The documentation includes external package, library, and generated-cache files in the artifact-lifetime contract. GPU identity now comes from the actual CUDA-holder PIDs rather than `nvidia-smi --id=0`. ## Verified on exact current head The feature patch was rebased onto canonical main `925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749`. `git range-diff` reported all 56 feature commits unchanged. The resulting head is `da56fe43ea242bb59c2dd2e3aa64f5536a2a8943`. A fresh exact-head image passed a compact-default V2 acceptance cell on one RTX 4090 Laptop GPU, n=1. Creation took 31.1366 seconds and restore took 2.8608 seconds. The public API returned token ID `12095`, text ` Paris`, and sampled-token log probability `-0.42565488815307617`, exactly matching the captured scalar. The image also passed runtime CUDA allocation, CRIU 4.2.1, CUDA checkpoint helper/plugin, `nvcc`, and RDMA-header compile probes. Cleanup left zero containers and zero GPU processes. The H100 campaign observed two sampled-token log probabilities across separate ordinary engine initializations. Raw pre-capture fit gates produced both values before CRIU was involved, while every restore exactly reproduced its captured oracle. A free 4090 control across ordinary and sleep-enabled processes did not reproduce a snapshot-specific difference. The product therefore keeps the captured-engine restore-fidelity contract instead of treating unrelated cross-process numerical variability as a restore failure. ## Test plan Focused verification on the exact current head: ```bash pytest -q \ tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_launch_cli.py \ tests/cuda/test_cuda_compatibility_path.py ``` ```text 54 passed, 1 unchanged base warning ``` The branch adds 16 test functions and 22 collected feature cases, all folded into the existing CLI suite. There is no standalone snapshot test file. The retained cases cover the four maintainer requests, both lifecycle boundaries, the public canary, cleanup, PID ownership, and private paths. They also cover CRIU file locks, GPU identity, TCP preflight, and `io_uring` preflight. Ruff 0.14.0, scoped mypy, Docker dependency metadata generation, lazy-import checks, `git diff --check`, and all 56 DCO signoffs pass. The current head still needs its upstream CI run after this update. ## Product envelope and tradeoffs - Linux x86-64, one NVIDIA GPU, TP1, PP1, DP1, and prefill-context parallel size 1. - Same trusted host and GPU, with matching driver, kernel, runtime, engine arguments, selected environment, and checkpoint tools. - Compact capture requires an immutable remote model revision. Full-state capture supports local or mutable model sources by retaining model state. - Root or passwordless `sudo`, plus a compatible kernel and NVIDIA driver. - One plaintext HTTP frontend without built-in API authentication, TLS, custom middleware, or a Unix domain socket. - No external established TCP peer at capture and no active `io_uring` descriptors. - A private local artifact that can contain process memory, model state, and secrets. - Package files, shared libraries, model files, and generated-cache roots must remain available for the artifact lifetime. - No cross-host migration, GPU relocation, multi-GPU communicator restore, concurrent restore, or automatic ordinary-start fallback. This is adjacent to, but does not replace, in-process sleep and provider orchestration. The boundary stays narrow because that is where the correctness and hardware evidence stops. AI assistance was used. I reviewed the changes and can defend the implementation, constraints, and measurements.

signals.title: [Core] Release NCCL communicator memory in sleep mode
signals.text: ## Replacement for #46234 This recreates #46234, which became unreopenable after its fork was detached. The original PR was not closed for a technical reason; all its review threads were resolved. ## What Sleep mode releases weights and KV-cache memory, but NCCL communicators retain their dynamic GPU buffers (~1 GiB/rank at TP4). This change releases that memory during sleep via NCCL's native `ncclCommSuspend(NCCL_SUSPEND_MEM)` / `ncclCommResume`, preserving communicator identity, topology, and connection state. Requires NCCL >= 2.29.7 (the vllm/vllm-openai image pins 2.30.7; the CUDA test lock 2.29.7). ## How (updated architecture) - `suspend()` / `resume()` hooks on `DeviceCommunicatorBase` (the generic surface requested in [#46234 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46234#discussion_r3504640029), ready for FlashInfer comm suspension); `CudaCommunicator` delegates to PyNccl. - `PyNcclCommunicator.suspend/resume` are **idempotent** (`_suspended` state). - Orchestration lives in the shared worker dispatch layer (`gpu_worker.sleep/wake_up`) — the same placement #46234 was reviewed with — gated by a new `SleepModeBackend.requires_communicator_suspend()` capability (`cumem` → True; process-checkpoint mechanisms that cover NCCL themselves → False, avoiding double handling). PyNccl-level idempotence makes staged wakes safe: each communicator suspends and resumes exactly once, and the worker holds no extra state. This differs from the first push of this PR, which called the walkers from inside `CuMemBackend`. That shape had a layer inversion (allocator module importing `parallel_state`) and a reproducible crash: the staged RL wake (`/wake_up?tags=weights` → `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`) called `ncclCommResume` twice, and the second call fails with `invalid usage`, killing the engine (`EngineDeadError`). Reproduced on GB200 TP4; fixed here by the PyNccl idempotence guard (unit-tested), with 7 edge scenarios (wake-without-sleep, double sleep, staged wake, mid-walk failure recovery, capability-off parity, XPU, TP=1) adversarially verified safe. ## Test - Unit: `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py` (9 passed) covers the capability contract and staged-wake single-resume ordering; `tests/distributed/test_pynccl.py::test_pynccl_suspend_resume_idempotent` covers the low-level guard. Pre-commit incl. mypy green. - E2E on 1×(4×GB200), vllm/vllm-openai:nightly, NCCL 2.30.7: full sleep/wake cycle and staged wake (weights → kv_cache), greedy 64-token output compared token-exact before/after. | Model | TP | NCCL freed/rank | Sleep L1 total freed/rank | Output preserved (full + staged wake) | |---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking | 4 | 1152 MiB (2 comms: tp, ep) | 155.24 GiB | ✓ | | NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 | 4 | 1152 MiB | 152.26 GiB | ✓ | Original #46234 validation (8×H200, TP2/4/8 ± EP/DP/PP, 958–1438 MiB/rank, output preserved) applies to the unchanged NCCL mechanism. **Additional GSM8K correctness pass, single-node TP4 and cross-node TP8** (vllm/vllm-openai:nightly, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507, 200 questions/run, `--moe-backend TRITON`; checkpoint loaded from `/dev/shm` — Lustre client-side cache tops out well under this model's 56.87 GiB checkpoint, so `--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch` stalls at 0% indefinitely on a network filesystem for a model this size, unrelated to this PR): | Topology | Comm memory released (per rank, both sleep cycles) | `invalid_rate` | Errors/tracebacks | |---|---|---|---| | TP4, single node | `Sleep mode freed 155.22 GiB` then `152.82 GiB` | 0.0000 (600/600 answers parsed) | none | | TP8, cross-node (2×4×GB200) | `Sleep mode freed 151.51 GiB`, `CuMemAllocator: sleep freed 149.10 GiB` — consistent across all 8 ranks on both hosts | 0.0000 (600/600 answers parsed) | none | Both runs show baseline/post-full-wake/post-staged-wake accuracy within ±1 question (TP4) or ±9 questions (TP8, out of 200) of each other — expected batch-composition floating-point non-associativity for greedy decoding under concurrent load, not output corruption (zero invalid/unparseable answers, zero errors across both runs). The TP8 cross-node run also empirically confirms the FlashInfer limitation above: `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: CUDA error code=800 (CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED)` — a non-fatal warning, vLLM falls back cleanly and this PR's NCCL-only release is unaffected. Cluster caveat, unrelated to this PR's code: this rack is GB200 NVL72 with MNNVL (rack-scale NVLink fabric), but the site's Slurm/Pyxis container build has no device-injection option for the IMEX channel — confirmed by bind-mounting `/dev/nvidia-caps-imex-channels` into the container (visible via `nvidia-smi -L`, host IMEX daemon healthy) and still hitting `ncclCommInitRank`/NVLS proxy setup failure. The TP8 run above therefore exercises `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume` over plain socket transport (`NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=0`), not the NVLink fabric path — both are the same NCCL communicator-suspend code this PR adds, but a rack with working IMEX container injection would be a stronger cross-node signal. ## Scope NCCL only. FlashInfer's all-reduce-fusion workspace (and MoE all2all workspace) GPU memory is **not** released during sleep in this PR. Investigated and deferred, not overlooked: - FlashInfer's `AllReduceFusionWorkspace` (MNNVL/TRTLLM) has no suspend/resume primitive analogous to `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume` — only `checkpoint_prepare()`/`checkpoint_restore()` (added for #46877's separate checkpoint lifecycle, flashinfer >= 0.6.16). - Wiring `CudaCommunicator.suspend()`/`resume()` to call those checkpoint hooks directly (reuse, no new machinery) was tried and reverted: `checkpoint_prepare()`/`checkpoint_restore()` are reachable via `async_llm.checkpoint_prepare()`'s independent RPC path with no mutual exclusion against `sleep()`/`wake_up()`, so an interleaved call would double-release/rebuild the same workspace. Matches [galletas1712's #46234 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46234#discussion_r3504640029) that "NCCL checkpoint and ncclCommSuspend are not really composable." - `DeviceCommunicatorBase.suspend()/resume()` (this PR) is the generic override point galletas1712 requested for future FlashInfer comm suspension; it's ready to host a real implementation once flashinfer exposes a dedicated suspend/resume primitive. ## Why this is not duplicate work No open PR implements `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume`. #46877 is the separate process-checkpoint lifecycle (its hooks are deliberately no-ops for NCCL); #35934 tears down communicators for CRIU; RFC #52125 (L3 snapshot) references this PR as the ordinary-sleep counterpart. ## AI disclosure AI assistance (Claude, Codex) was used for the redesign analysis, implementation, and on-node validation; three candidate architectures were implemented and validated head-to-head before choosing this one. The submitter reviewed every changed line.
