signals.title: [ROCm][Quantization] Support AMD Quark per-block FP8 for fused MoE layers
signals.text: ## Purpose `QuarkConfig._is_fp8_w8a8` already accepts per-block (128x128) FP8 weights, and #47972 added `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` so that **linear** layers can consume them. `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` was never updated, so it still rejects the `per_block` qscheme: ``` ValueError: For FP8 Fused MoE layers, only per-tensor and per-channel scales for weights and activations are supported. Found per_block, per_group ``` The result is an asymmetry: for a Quark checkpoint whose routed experts are quantized per-block, every linear layer loads fine but the MoE layers cannot be built at all. ### Concrete case: the MTP layer of an MoE model Models that ship an MTP (multi-token prediction) draft layer make this asymmetry easy to see, because vLLM builds the MTP layer from the *same* decoder-layer class as the main model. For `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B`, `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor` instantiates `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer(layer_type="full_attention")`, which for an MoE config contains a complete `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` with all 512 routed experts. Broken down by quantization path (`{i}` runs over `mtp_num_hidden_layers`, default 1): | Module | vLLM layer | Quant path | Status | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `mtp.embed_tokens` | `VocabParallelEmbedding` | — | not quantized | | `mtp.fc` | `ColumnParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.norm`, `mtp.pre_fc_norm_hidden`, `mtp.pre_fc_norm_embedding` | `Qwen3_5RMSNorm` | — | not quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.self_attn.qkv_proj` | `QKVParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.self_attn.o_proj` | `RowParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.gate` | `ReplicatedLinear`, built with `quant_config=None` | — | never quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert_gate` | `ReplicatedLinear`, built with `quant_config=None` | — | never quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert.gate_up_proj` | `MergedColumnParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert.down_proj` | `RowParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | **`mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.experts`** | **`RoutedExperts`** | **fused MoE** | **rejected — fixed by this PR** | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.experts` is the only module in the MTP stack that takes the fused-MoE path, and it is the only one that fails. It is also not a small module: with `hidden_size=4096`, `moe_intermediate_size=1024` and 512 experts it holds roughly 6.4B parameters, so leaving it unquantized is not a practical workaround. Two related details worth noting: - `mlp.gate` and `mlp.shared_expert_gate` are constructed with a hardcoded `quant_config=None`, so they are never quantized regardless of the Quark config. - When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` is enabled and the shared expert is not excluded from quantization, `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` sets `shared_expert = None` and folds the shared expert into the routed-expert tensors, which moves those weights onto the fused-MoE path as well. ## Changes All changes are inside the existing `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`, following the `BLOCK` strategy of `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` rather than adding a new class: the weight, bias, input-scale and kernel-setup code is shared with the per-tensor and per-channel paths, and only the scale layout, the scale parameter name and a few flags differ. - `__init__`: accept `per_block`; read `block_size` from the weight config; use `kFp8Static128BlockSym` / `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` for backend selection; require dynamic activation quantization for per-block weights; select the scale parameter name (`weight_scale_inv` for per-block, `weight_scale` otherwise) the way `Fp8MoEMethod` already does. - `create_weights`: propagate `layer.weight_block_size`; validate that `intermediate_size_per_partition` is divisible by `block_n` (and by `block_k` when TP > 1) so misalignment fails at weight-creation time rather than silently producing wrong results in the kernel; allocate block-grid weight scales, register them as `w13_weight_scale_inv` / `w2_weight_scale_inv`, and tag them with `FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported.BLOCK` so `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` shards them on the block grid instead of per row. - `process_weights_after_loading`, `_setup_kernel` and `get_fused_moe_quant_config`: look the weight scales up through the selected name, and pass `block_shape` through to `make_fp8_moe_quant_config`. The per-tensor requantization loop and the per-channel `unsqueeze` in `process_weights_after_loading` remain guarded on `weight_qscheme`, and per-block weights require dynamic activations so the static input-scale branch is skipped. The only per-block change there is routing the fnuz normalization through the selected scale name, so per-block also works on MI300. The per-tensor and per-channel paths are unchanged: `block_shape` stays `None`, the scale parameters keep the `weight_scale` name, and the scale shapes are identical to before. ### Why the per-block scales are named `weight_scale_inv` Block-quantized checkpoints store their per-block scales as `weight_scale_inv` (the deepseek-v3 convention Quark follows), and `RoutedExperts.load_weights` derives the parameter name from the checkpoint tensor name by replacing only the module-path portion and carrying the suffix over verbatim — `...experts.0.down_proj.weight_scale_inv` resolves to `w2_weight_scale_inv`, with no aliasing step in between. Registering the scales under `w2_weight_scale` therefore made every per-block checkpoint fail to load: ``` AttributeError: Layer mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts has no parameter 'w2_weight_scale_inv' for checkpoint weight 'mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight_scale_inv' ``` Both names hold the same quantity (a dequantization multiplier, multiplied into the block-scaled GEMM), so this is purely a lookup-key mismatch and it always fails loudly. ## Test Plan Added to `tests/quantization/test_quark.py`: - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_requires_block_size` — a per-block weight config without `block_size` is rejected. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_rejects_per_block_static_input` — static activations are rejected for per-block weights. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_weight_shapes` — `w13`/`w2` weight and scale shapes, that the scales are registered under the `weight_scale_inv` name and not under `weight_scale`, and that both scales carry the `BLOCK` loader attribute. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_rejects_misaligned_partition` — a partition size that is not a multiple of `block_n` fails during `create_weights`. ```bash pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k per_block ``` ## Test Result Hardware: 1x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm. Checkpoint: `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` re-quantized with AMD Quark from `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8` into an NVFP4 backbone plus a per-block FP8 MTP layer (775 MTP modules per-block FP8, 10 kept in BF16 through `exclude`). This reproduces the asymmetry described above: the MTP `mlp.experts` module is per-block FP8 while the main model is NVFP4. ### Load and module routing TP=1, `speculative_config={"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}`: | Model | Module | Bound method | | --- | --- | --- | | target | 40 MoE layers | `QuarkNvfp4MoEMethod` | | drafter (MTP) | `mlp.experts.routed_experts` | `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` | | drafter (MTP) | `self_attn.qkv_proj`, `self_attn.o_proj`, `shared_expert.{gate_up,down}_proj` | `QuarkLinearMethod` / `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` | | drafter (MTP) | `fc`, `mlp.gate`, `mlp.shared_expert_gate` | `UnquantizedLinearMethod` | Backends selected, with no fallbacks reported: ``` Selected TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel for QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock Using TRITON Fp8 MoE backend Using 'EMULATION' NvFp4 MoE backend ``` ### MTP acceptance `Draft acceptance rate: 94.7%-95.9%`, acceptance length 1.96 out of a maximum of 2 for `num_speculative_tokens=1`. This is the most direct evidence that the per-block expert weights and scales are loaded correctly: a scale mismatch drives acceptance towards 0. ### GSM8K `lm_eval` 5-shot over the full 1319 questions, chat template with thinking disabled: | Filter | exact_match | | --- | --- | | flexible-extract | 0.9629 ± 0.0052 | | strict-match | 0.9636 ± 0.0052 | ### Unit tests ``` pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k per_block 8 passed, 35 deselected ``` This covers the four new MoE tests above together with the pre-existing per-block linear tests from #47972, which still pass.

signals.title: [CI][AMD] Simplify failure diagnostics reporting
signals.text: ## Purpose Keep AMD CI failure output concise and let Buildkite's standard post-command artifact phase upload the detailed diagnostics. - Write the existing bounded GPU, resource, cgroup, and network probes to `artifacts/amd-gpu-diagnostics/<job-id>/diagnostics.log` without duplicating command output into the job log. - Remove the runner's custom `buildkite-agent artifact upload` call and timeout. - Replace the non-rendering emoji shortcode with a dependency-free Bash table containing exit status, runtime and pod context, cgroup OOM count, and artifact path. - Keep the native test-log section boundary so Buildkite expands the actual failing test log. The earlier process-tracking and teardown expansion has been removed; this PR now changes one existing script and leaves runner cleanup behavior unchanged. Depends on [vllm-project/ci-infra#475](https://github.com/vllm-project/ci-infra/pull/475), which configures `artifact_paths` for AMD wrapper jobs and should merge first. Its exact new filename does not match the current manual-upload artifact, avoiding duplicate uploads during rollout. ## Test plan - `bash -n .buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-amd-test.sh` - Repository pre-commit hooks for the changed script — passed - Synthetic native failure: verified the diagnostics file, table fields, cgroup OOM row, artifact path, and absence of `:rotating_light:` - Companion ci-infra pipeline-generator suite — 72 passed
signals.author: AndreasKaratzas

signals.title: [ROCm] Give EngineCore cleanup grace after request abort
signals.text: AMD CI exposed a shutdown race where `shutdown_timeout=0` aborted requests as intended but also gave EngineCore no time to release ROCm resources before SIGKILL. This change preserves immediate request abort while giving the ROCm EngineCore process manager a bounded 60-second cleanup grace when both the configured and remaining process timeouts are zero. It keeps exhausted budgets for positive shutdown timeouts unchanged and extends the DP supervisor's outer deadline to cover the cleanup window. - The motivating failure is [AMD CI build 12007](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12007/list?sid=019ffc53-a1ab-472f-8b77-7c52a7d6edc0&tab=output). - The final request completed successfully, but EngineCore was force-killed immediately and GPU memory remained at 11.72 GB for the full 120-second release wait. - The `LLM()` to `vllm_runner()` migration does not cover this path because these tests launch a real out-of-process `vllm serve` server. - Add a ROCm-only 60-second EngineCore process cleanup grace when both the configured request timeout and remaining process timeout are zero. - Keep `shutdown_timeout=0` inside EngineCore so in-flight requests are still aborted immediately. - Preserve exhausted positive shutdown deadlines instead of accidentally granting them a fresh cleanup window. - Extend the DP supervisor's outer wait budget so it does not kill the process tree before EngineCore cleanup can finish. - Add manager and DP supervisor regression coverage in the existing test files.
signals.author: AndreasKaratzas

signals.title: [CI] Harden RemoteVLLMServer GPU cleanup checks
signals.text: This PR is stacked on `akaratza_enginecore_shutdown` and hardens `RemoteVLLMServer` cleanup after a server exits. GPU baselines and cleanup waits are tracked per child-visible physical device, including overlapping multi-server scopes, so one leaked allocation cannot be hidden by a later aggregate baseline. Unavailable telemetry and timed-out cleanup now fail closed and retain affected-scope state until recovery can be verified. The test server's outer termination window also covers the EngineCore cleanup grace introduced by the first PR. - Prevent a teardown failure from ratcheting leaked VRAM into the next server's `_pre_server_gpu_memory` baseline. - Measure the physical devices selected by each child server's visibility environment on ROCm and CUDA. - Preserve parent-logical ordinal measurement on XPU, where `torch.xpu.mem_get_info` cannot consume physical or tile mask IDs. - Retain cleanup poison while intentionally concurrent servers make recovery unverifiable, and fail closed for unsafe partial coverage. - Merge partially overlapping scopes and use the earliest per-device baseline so a broader server cannot hide a leak behind an earlier sibling's allocation. - Keep GPU-less render-server tests outside GPU release accounting.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fall back when zentorch import fails
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52238. On AMD Zen CPU builds, a non-`ImportError` raised while importing zentorch currently escapes `cpu_platform_plugin`. Platform discovery then silently drops the CPU plugin and selects `UnspecifiedPlatform`. This change logs the underlying zentorch import failure and falls back to the standard `CpuPlatform`. A CPU-only regression test covers an incompatible shared library represented by `OSError`. I reviewed the issue comments and searched open PRs for both `#52238` and the zentorch CPU-platform import path. No overlapping open PR was found. AI assistance was used to develop and test this change. I reviewed every changed line of code and the regression test, and I understand and can defend the change end-to-end. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py -q .venv/bin/ruff check --ignore ISC004 vllm/platforms/__init__.py tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check vllm/platforms/__init__.py tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py ``` The repository pre-commit hooks also ran during commit. ## Test Result - Before the implementation, the new regression test failed with the simulated `OSError: incompatible shared library` escaping platform detection. - After the implementation: `5 passed in 0.62s`. - Ruff check and format check passed. - All commit-time pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and repository policy checks. - An additional platform-plugin test was attempted with its required dummy plugin installed. Its platform assertion passed, but the process later segfaulted in the existing macOS PyTorch global cleanup path at `torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache`; this is outside the changed code. - Model evaluations were not run because this change does not affect model outputs, accuracy, or serving behavior. No documentation update is needed.
signals.author: luyixiao95

signals.title: [Model][Generative Recommendation] Add HSTU model support to vLLM
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR adds HSTU-based generative recommendation model support to vLLM. HSTU is a ranking model architecture designed for generative recommendation. Unlike traditional language models, HSTU does not autoregressively generate text tokens. Instead, it synchronously computes ranking scores for all candidate items in a request. The goal of this change is to enable generative recommendation models to reuse the existing vLLM and large-model serving ecosystem, including: - Hugging Face model and configuration loading. - vLLM model registration. - GPU model execution. - Attention backend selection. - Optimized CUDA operators. - Request batching and scheduling. - Asynchronous output handling. - CUDA Graph execution. - Future distributed inference and online serving infrastructure. Generative recommendation and large language models have several common characteristics. Both can be represented as sequence models, use embedding layers and transformer-style computation, and benefit from optimized attention kernels, GPU batching, asynchronous execution, and production-level model serving infrastructure. By integrating HSTU into vLLM, generative recommendation models can reuse the existing large-model ecosystem instead of maintaining an independent inference stack. ## Inference Paradigm Although HSTU and large language models share several model and runtime components, their inference semantics are different. | Aspect | Large language model | Generative recommendation model | | --- | --- | --- | | Decode behavior | Autoregressively generates one token at a time | Synchronously computes scores for all candidates in a request | | Model output | Vocabulary logits for the next token | One ranking score for each candidate item | | Sampling | Requires token sampling and token ID generation | Does not generate a sampled token | | Request progress | Continues until the requested number of tokens is generated | Completes after all candidate scores are returned | | Output format | Usually `[num_tokens, vocab_size]` | Packed candidate-score output | | Scheduler signal | Uses sampled token IDs to update request state | Uses candidate scores to complete the request | The default vLLM generation path is designed around language-model execution: 1. Run the model forward pass. 2. Produce vocabulary logits. 3. Invoke the token sampler. 4. Generate token IDs. 5. Update the request state. 6. Continue decoding until the request is finished. This flow cannot be directly reused for HSTU because HSTU produces candidate ranking scores rather than vocabulary logits. Passing HSTU outputs through the normal sampler would incorrectly interpret candidate scores as vocabulary logits and could produce invalid token IDs. Therefore, this PR adds a score-only execution path: 1. Run the HSTU forward pass. 2. Extract the score corresponding to each candidate item. 3. Convert candidate IDs and scores into `LogprobsTensors`. 4. Return the scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. 5. Skip the standard token sampler. 6. Skip generated-token state updates. 7. Complete the request after all candidate scores are returned. The scheduler is also updated to support score-only recommendation requests. A request can be completed after candidate scores are produced even when no `new_token_ids` are returned. ## Implementation Overview This PR contains five main categories of changes. ### 1. Model Structure and Model Registration Files: - `vllm/model_executor/models/hstu.py` - `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` - `tests/models/registry.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU model implementation. - Add HSTU embedding layers, transformer blocks, normalization layers, and prediction heads. - Register the HSTU model with vLLM. - Support Hugging Face HSTU model loading. - Add HSTU to the model registry test data. - Add model registration and model import coverage. ### 2. Model Configuration and Configuration Registration Files: - `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/__init__.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/hstu.py` Changes: - Add HSTU-specific configuration classes. - Support HSTU model and task configuration fields. - Support `model_type = "hstu"`. - Convert HSTU configuration data from Hugging Face configuration files into the vLLM configuration representation. - Preserve compatibility with the existing vLLM configuration loading flow. ### 3. Model Operators and Operator Registration Files: - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/hstu_attn.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/selector.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU attention backend. - Integrate the external HSTU variable-length attention operator. - Register the HSTU attention backend with vLLM. - Automatically select `HSTU_ATTN` for HSTU or generative recommendation models when no explicit backend is configured. - Preserve explicit attention backend configuration as the highest-priority option. - Validate unsupported attention combinations and return clear errors. - Pass per-request context and candidate metadata to the HSTU attention implementation. Automatic backend selection is only applied when the user has not explicitly selected an attention backend. This preserves the existing backend override behavior. ### 4. Model Runner V1 Adaptation File: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` Changes: - Add generative recommendation metadata collection. - Add HSTU candidate score extraction. - Pass HSTU metadata through the forward context. - Bypass the standard token sampler for HSTU requests. - Return candidate scores through the prompt-logprobs output path. - Add recommendation-specific request completion handling. - Preserve the existing execution path for non-HSTU models. ### 5. Model Runner V2 Adaptation Files: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/gr_state.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py` - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` Changes: - Add `GRState` for request-scoped generative recommendation state. - Store user IDs, candidate count, prompt token IDs, and request stage. - Move candidate score extraction from the Model Runner into `GRState`. - Convert packed HSTU outputs into `LogprobsTensors`. - Add asynchronous score output handling. - Return candidate scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. - Skip token sampling and token-state updates for HSTU requests. - Complete score-only requests in the scheduler when candidate scores are available. - Preserve the one-token early-return behavior required by generative recommendation inputs. ## Test Plan ### 1. Environment Setup The operator is installed inside the following NVIDIA PyTorch container:`nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.06-py3` Install the required system dependency:`apt update && apt install -y libxcb1` ### 2.HSTU Operator Installation and Validation The HSTU attention operator is provided by the NVIDIA `recsys-examples` repository. Clone the recsys-examples repository:`git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/recsys-examples.git && cd recsys-examples/corelib/hstu` For H20 and other Hopper-based devices, enter the corresponding device directory before compiling: `cd hopper` Install the HSTU operator:`Install the HSTU operator:` After the compilation completes successfully, validate the operator installation with: `python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu_op.py` ### 3.vLLM Installation Clone the vLLM repository:`git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git && cd vllm` Install the current vLLM source with CUDA support:`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda pip install -v -e .` ### 4. HSTU Model Inference: After the HSTU changes are included in vLLM, run:`python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu.py` This test validates: * HSTU model loading. * HSTU configuration loading. * HSTU model registration. * HSTU attention backend initialization. * HSTU forward execution. * Candidate score extraction. * Candidate ID and score formatting. * Score-only execution without token sampling. * Recommendation request completion. * Model Runner integration. * CUDA Graph execution. ### 5. Model Registry and Hugging Face Loading Run the model registry tests:`pytest -q tests/models/test_registry.py -k HSTUForCausalLM` This validates that: * HSTUForCausalLM is registered. * The HSTU model class can be imported. * Hugging Face model metadata is available. * The HSTU configuration can be loaded. * The vLLM model registry can resolve the HSTU model. ## Test Result ### HSTU Operator The test returned like: ```text Input q shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Output shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Run success ``` ### HSTU Model Inference The test returned candidate IDs and their corresponding ranking scores. A truncated example of the output is: ```text Request 0: 12676:0.6602 47052:0.5078 45082:0.4336 79131:0.3984 34671:0.4844 5695:0.4570 95647:0.1777 60217:0.5273 70284:0.4258 16361:0.4238 Request 1: 8023:0.4863 24460:0.6094 ... ``` Each line follows the format:`Each line follows the format:` The output confirms that HSTU synchronously computes the scores of all candidates for a request and returns the scores through the generative recommendation output path. The test also confirms that: * HSTU outputs are not passed through the standard vocabulary sampler. * No artificial generated token IDs are produced. * Requests complete after candidate scores are returned. * Candidate scores are returned through prompt_logprobs_dict. * Both Model Runner V1 and Model Runner V2 execution paths are supported. * The HSTU attention backend is initialized and executed successfully. * CUDA Graph execution works in the validated CUDA environment. ### Model Registration and Hugging Face Loading The model registration and Hugging Face loading tests passed. HSTUForCausalLM can be resolved and imported through the vLLM model registry, and the HSTU configuration can be loaded from the Hugging Face model configuration. ### Scheduler and Score-Only Execution The scheduler validation passed for score-only recommendation requests. A recommendation request is correctly completed after candidate scores are produced, even when no new_token_ids are returned. The standard token sampling path is skipped for HSTU requests, and no regular language-model token state update is performed. ### Attention Backend Selection When no explicit attention backend is configured, the HSTU model automatically selects HSTU_ATTN. When an explicit attention backend is configured, the user-provided backend remains authoritative and is not overridden by the HSTU automatic selection logic. ### Current Scope and Limitations This initial integration focuses on bringing HSTU into the vLLM model and serving ecosystem. The current implementation assumes: * Prompt lengths are consistent across users. * Candidate lengths are consistent across users. * HSTU and non-HSTU requests are not mixed in the same batch. * Candidate scores are produced during an unchunked prefill. * Pipeline parallelism is not used. * PD-separated HSTU execution is not supported yet. * KV-cache-based or paged HSTU attention is not supported yet. * request_stage = 1 is not supported. * Each recommendation prompt contains at least one context/candidate pair. These limitations can be addressed in follow-up work after the basic HSTU execution path and serving interface are established.

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable fused KDA decode on gfx942 (MI325X)
signals.text: ## Purpose PR #50654 added the fused Kimi-K3 KDA decode kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu`), but gated it to gfx950 (MI355X) in two places, so it never activates on gfx942 (MI325X): - **Build gate** — `CMakeLists.txt` filtered the HIP source to `gfx950` only, so the kernel was not compiled and `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` (and therefore `torch.ops._C.fused_kda_decode`) was never defined on a gfx942-only build. - **Runtime gate** — `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py` ended with `return on_gfx950()`. This change extends both gates to gfx942 as well, so MI325X can take the fused decode path instead of falling back to the three-launch Triton path. The kernel body is unchanged. It uses only CDNA-common primitives — wave64, DPP row/quad permutes (`quad_perm`, `row_half_mirror`, `row_mirror`), `__builtin_nontemporal_load/store`, and bf16 intrinsics — with no MFMA / FP8 / gfx950-only paths, so no source-level changes are required for gfx942. LDS use is ~2.8 KiB/block and register pressure ~130 VGPR, both well within CDNA3 limits. ## Changes - `CMakeLists.txt`: HIP arch filter `gfx950` -> `gfx942|gfx950` (and comment). - `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py`: gate `on_gfx950()` -> `on_gfx950() or on_gfx942()`. - `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`: extend the module skip guard from gfx950 to gfx942 / gfx950 so the correctness suite runs on MI325X. All other backends and the CUDA path are unchanged; the shape/dtype/head-count guards in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` are unchanged. ## Performance The kernel-level win is large, but the end-to-end win on MI325X is currently small: the Kimi-K3 decode step is dominated by the MXFP4 MoE (int4) and the MLA attention plus the TP8 collectives, which dwarf the KDA linear-attention block. The fusion removes ~66 us of per-layer kernel time (mostly launch overhead), but that is a small fraction of today's total per-token cost. It should become more visible once #50817 (MXFP4 MoE Triton a16w4 for gfx942) lands and shrinks the dominant MoE cost — the fixed KDA saving then represents a larger share of a smaller decode step. ### End-to-end (tp8, 256-in / 256-out, max-concurrency 4) | Metric | Triton fallback | Fused KDA | Delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 425.95 | 422.66 | -0.77% | | P99 TPOT (ms) | 427.64 | 424.19 | -0.81% | | Output tok/s | 9.29 | 9.36 | +0.75% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 1577.24 | 1574.03 | -0.20% (flat) | TTFT is unchanged, as expected for a decode-only kernel. ### Per-layer kernel sequence (torch profiler medians, us) Baseline runs the KDA decode as ~16 separate kernels per layer — the conv1d update, the recurrent delta-rule step, and the gated output RMSNorm decomposed into a chain of launch-overhead-bound (~4 us floor) elementwise ops. Fused collapses all of them into a single kernel: | # | Baseline kernel | us | Fused kernel | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | _causal_conv1d_update_kernel | 5.01 | kda_decode_fusion_kernel<true, 12, true, true, true> | 7.77 | | 2 | fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode_kernel | 6.45 | | | | 3 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.37 | | | | 4 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.41 | | | | 5 | pow (tensor, scalar) | 4.41 | | | | 6 | reduce Mean | 5.01 | | | | 7 | add | 4.45 | | | | 8 | rsqrt | 4.37 | | | | 9 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 10 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.17 | | | | 11 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 12 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.45 | | | | 13 | sigmoid | 5.05 | | | | 14 | mul | 4.33 | | | | 15 | float32->bfloat16 copy | 4.49 | | | | 16 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.57 | | | | | **total (16 kernels)** | **~73.96** | **total (1 kernel)** | **7.77** | ~9.5x less kernel time for the KDA decode block (~74 -> 7.8 us/layer). The `12` template arg is 12 heads/rank (96 KDA heads at TP8). Across the model's KDA layers (~69 per the kernel header) that is ~4.6 ms/token of raw kernel time removed, in the same ballpark as the ~3.3 ms/token TPOT drop measured above (the remainder overlaps with other work). ## Not a duplicate - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA decode gfx942"` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_kda_decode MI325"` ## Test Plan Run on an MI325X (gfx942) box after building with gfx942 in the arch list: 1. Build compiles the kernel and registers the op: `python -c "import torch, vllm; print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, 'fused_kda_decode'))"` -> expect `True`. 2. Kernel correctness: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -v` 3. Model accuracy (output-affecting change) — serve Kimi-K3 on MI325X and run gsm8k, compared against the Triton fallback path: `make gsm8k` 4. Decode latency / throughput before vs after (fused vs Triton fallback): `make bench-kda-mi325` ## Test Result - Op registered: **True** on the gfx942 build (`hasattr(torch.ops._C, "fused_kda_decode")`); the fused kernel appears in the trace (see Performance). - Latency/throughput: **-0.77% mean TPOT**, +0.75% output tok/s - gsm8k (fused vs Triton): **parity** — both 1.00 exact_match on flexible-extract and strict-match (5-shot, limit=100, stderr 0). The fused kernel matches the Triton fallback exactly. - `test_amd_kda_decode.py`: **12/12 passed** on MI325X (gfx942) — fused output matches the Triton reference across heads {12, 24, 96} x tokens {1, 7, 128}, plus the null-slot, no-output-norm, and padding edge cases. ## Checklist - [x] Compiles for gfx942 (kernel present in the .so with gfx942 codegen) - [x] `test_amd_kda_decode.py` passes on MI325X (12/12) - [x] gsm8k parity with the Triton path - [x] AI assistance used (see below) ## AI assistance This change was drafted with AI assistance (Claude). A human must review every line and run the build, tests, and eval on MI325X hardware before merge; the correctness and accuracy results above are not yet filled in.

signals.title: [Attention] Move GDN common metadata compute out of per-group build
signals.text:
## Purpose During profiling I notice GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes a long time (~900µs), because the batch level GDN spec decode metadata (masks, decode/prefill/spec split, token indices, query_start_loc cumsums) is computed repeatedly in each group build(). This compute can be moved one level up out of each group build(). * Compute the batch level GDN spec decode metadata once per step in `compute_spec_metadata` and store it on model_specific_attn_metadata, instead of recomputing it inside each GDN group's build(). Only the block_table dependent state index gathers stay per-group in build(). * e2e output throughput improves 61% at batch size 1, 12% at batch size 16 with DFlash (tested on H200). ## Test Plan ``` pytest -s -v tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py ``` ## Test Result Unit test passed. ## Profiling Main: GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~900µs PR: GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes ~300µs ## Benchmark ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --speculative-config --dataset-path /tmp/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --sharegpt-output-len 300 \ --num-prompts ${num_prompts} \ --max-concurrency ${concurrency} \ --num-warmups 200 \ --ignore-eos ``` Main: Total generated tokens: 18000 Request throughput (req/s): 0.71 Output token throughput (tok/s): 212.22 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 62.00 Peak concurrent requests: 2.00 Total token throughput (tok/s): 405.69 ---------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 113.86 Median TTFT (ms): 131.82 P99 TTFT (ms): 142.84 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------ Mean TPOT signals.title: [Bugfix][Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Fix off-by-one in bad_words draft-prefix matching
signals.text: ## Purpose Fix an off-by-one in the spec-decode branch of `_bad_words_kernel` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/bad_words.py`), present since the kernel was introduced in #33433. The sampler passes `input_ids` gathered at `logits_indices`, so for a spec-decode request the per-request local layout is: local position 0 = last committed sampled token, local position j = draft token d_{j-1}. The sibling kernels index draft tokens accordingly (`_penalties_kernel` uses `start_idx + prev_pos + 1`; thinking budget's `_load_effective_token` uses `+ 1` with an explicit comment). `_bad_words_kernel` read `input_ids_ptr + cur_req_first_pos + spec_offset` without the `+ 1`, so every draft-region read was shifted back by one token (the boundary token was read twice). Consequences when bad_words and speculative decoding are combined and a multi-token bad word's prefix window reaches into the draft tokens: - prefix matches ending in the draft region are missed (the banned token can be sampled/accepted); - matches spanning the committed/draft boundary fire one verification row late; - the duplicated boundary read can spuriously match and ban an innocent token. Single-token bad words and non-spec rows are unaffected. Model Runner V1 has a separate implementation and is unaffected. **Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs/issues for `bad_words` + spec decode / off-by-one / `_bad_words_kernel`; no existing fix found (closest is #34213, which only touches penalties). ## Test Plan New unit test (first coverage for this kernel), following the pattern of `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py`: ```bash pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_bad_words.py ``` Scenario: committed output `[10, 11]`, draft tokens `[12, 13]`. The core regression case is the boundary-spanning prefix (`[11, 12, 30]` must mask at the row where the prefix completes, not one row later); the other three cases pin the remaining coverage axes: a positive match at draft offset >= 1 (`[12, 13, 40]`), a no-double-count guard for the boundary token (`[11, 11, 50]`), and a committed-only baseline (`[10, 11, 60]`). Assertions compare the full logits tensor. ## Test Result Ran on an A100 SXM4 80GB (torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, Python 3.11), with the branch installed editable via `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED` (nightly x86_64 wheel `66728feb1`): - **With the fix (HEAD): `4 passed`.** - **With the pre-fix kernel** (parent commit's `bad_words.py` swapped in): **`3 failed, 1 passed`** — exactly the three spec-branch cases fail; the committed-only baseline passes. - `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass on both changed files. - Cross-validation: the kernel's scalar loop was transcribed to pure Python and checked against an independent reference matcher over 20,000 randomized spec-decode scenarios; with the `+ 1` the kernel matches the reference in all cases, without it ~24% of scenarios diverge. AI assistance was used for this change (Claude); I have reviewed every changed line.

signals.title: [Performance][MRV2] Cache logits-processing request state
signals.text: ## Summary `Sampler._requires_logits_processing()` runs on every sampling step and currently scans multiple per-request NumPy/Python states. This change computes the combined predicate in `add_request()` and stores one boolean per request slot, so the hot-path gate only scans the active rows of one compact array. The cache is overwritten on slot reuse, keeps active-subset filtering through the existing `idx_mapping_np`, and does not change any public or downstream processor API. ## Dependency Depends on #52284, because an active thinking budget must participate in the combined predicate. This branch carries the rebased #52284 change as its first commit; after #52284 lands, rebasing will leave only the performance commit in this PR's diff. ## Why this is not duplicate work There is no linked issue. Immediately before opening this PR I searched open PRs for `_needs_logits_processing`, `logits-processing sampler`, `MRV2 sampler cache`, and `52284 in:body`. No PR implements this cached combined predicate. #50584 adds DRY sampling state, and #48601 addresses FlashInfer top-k/top-p warmup OOM; neither is the same optimization. ## Validation ### Unit and static checks ```bash /tmp/vllm-pr2-venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py -q # 26 passed, 14 warnings in 18.42s uv run --active pre-commit run ruff-check --files \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py uv run --active pre-commit run ruff-format --files \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py uv run --active pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py # all passed ``` A broader relevant pre-commit run also passed all Python checks. `actionlint` could not download its dependency from `proxy.golang.org`, and `update-dockerfile-graph` requires `/bin/bash` on the Windows host; neither hook covers these Python files. The focused tests cover the default and greedy no-op paths, thinking budget, logit bias, penalties, bad words, temperature, min-p, top-k, top-p, warmup, slot reuse, and active-subset filtering. ### Model behavior and quality - Qwen3.5-9B fixed-seed A/B matrix: exact output equality for default, greedy, temperature, top-p, top-k, min-p, penalties, logit bias, bad words, and thinking budget; all requests returned HTTP 200. - Repository GSM8K evaluator (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`), Qwen3.5-9B, 100-question sample, 5-shot greedy, seed 42, max 256 tokens: - baseline: accuracy 0.87, invalid rate 0, 10,644 output tokens - optimized: accuracy 0.87, invalid rate 0, 10,644 output tokens ### Performance Host-side decision-path microbenchmark, 50,000 calls x 9 repeats: | Batch | Baseline median | Optimized median | Change | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 56.708 us | 16.830 us | -70.3% | | 32 | 57.137 us | 16.971 us | -70.3% | | 256 | 62.550 us | 18.908 us | -69.8% | Qwen3-0.6B serving benchmark (4 baseline and 3 optimized runs, 1,024 requests/run, 32 input and 256 output tokens, concurrency 256): ```bash vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8001 \ --model Qwen3-0.6B --tokenizer /model --dataset-name random \ --input-len 32 --output-len 256 --num-prompts 1024 --num-warmups 128 \ --max-concurrency 256 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --temperature 1.0 \ --top-p 1.0 --top-k 0 --min-p 0.0 --disable-shuffle --seed 0 \ --disable-tqdm ``` - median output throughput: 16,731.06 -> 17,488.81 tok/s (+4.53%) - median mean TPOT: 13.713 -> 12.891 ms (-5.99%) - every run completed 1,024/1,024 requests successfully - a fourth baseline run after the optimized runs remained at 16,574.05 tok/s, checking for warmup/order bias Qwen3.5-9B serving benchmark (3 interleaved runs/version, 256 requests/run, 128 input and 128 output tokens, concurrency 32) was intentionally neutral on the GPU-bound model: median output throughput 952.90 -> 953.55 tok/s (+0.07%, within noise). ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance was used to implement the change, and prepare tests and benchmarks. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the reported results and can explain and defend the change end-to-end.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Reference GPU blocks for in-flight store jobs and key the store ledger by save_seq
signals.text: ## Purpose FIX #52360 FIX #51637 This PR fixes two related bugs. ### 1. A store job reads KV from freed GPU blocks and writes data that does not belong to the key (#52360) Storing is asynchronous. At step 0 the worker only enqueues the request into mooncake's queue and returns; the actual GPU read and PUT happen later on a background thread. From step 1 onwards the scheduler is free to preempt that request and return its blocks to the free pool for another request to overwrite. The worker does not learn that a preemption happened until the next IPC, possibly not until the next forward pass. Any PUT issued in that window reads another request's KV. The wrong data does not heal itself: a key names a fixed token range, so once KV that does not belong to it is stored under a key, every later request that hits the same prefix reads the wrong data, and the blast radius grows over time. The only existing protection is `request_finished` → `delay_free_blocks`, which covers the normal-completion path only. Preemption takes a different path: `build_connector_meta` resets the tracker and the blocks are freed immediately, with nothing aware that jobs still queued need to read them. The fix is to have each store job hold its own reference on the GPU block pool, released once every rank has reported that job complete. That reference covers both the normal-completion and the preemption path, so `request_finished` no longer needs to delay the free and the worker no longer needs to report `finished_sending`. Three details: - A job is identified by `save_seq`, a monotonically increasing counter on the scheduler side, rather than by req_id (see item 2 for why). - The partial-tail offload reads a copy-on-write block that core deliberately keeps out of the request's block table (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`), so it is not in `ReqMeta.block_ids`. The worker still DMAs from it asynchronously, so it has to be referenced too. - Since a finished request no longer delays the free of its own blocks, nothing else drives the engine to keep stepping while a PUT is in flight. Outstanding references are reported through `has_pending_push_work()`. ### 2. A preempted request keeps the same req_id when it is rescheduled (#51637) The store thread's counter is keyed by req_id alone, so it cannot tell a job belonging to the current generation of a request from a leftover, not-yet-executed job of the previous one. When a leftover job completes it decrements the new generation's count: - once the count reaches 0 the entry is retired, and saves still in progress for the current generation are silently dropped at the `req_id not in stored_requests` check; - further decrements take it negative, and since retirement tests for `== 0`, a negative count can never satisfy it again. The entry is stuck in the table, `finished_sending` is never emitted, the scheduler never frees the blocks, and the engine ends up starved of KV; - a leftover job can also rewind the new generation's resume offset (`_saved_offset`) or mark it as skipped under pressure. The fix changes that structure from "one count per req_id" to `req_id -> {live save_seqs}`. `save_seq` is unique for the lifetime of the engine, so a leftover job is not in the set the new generation established and cannot affect it. Retirement now tests whether the set is empty, which makes the underflow structurally impossible. ### Relationship to #51662 #51662 is the fix proposed by the reporter of #51637 themselves, using `_StoreRequestJob` + `job.epoch`. The second commit here targets the same issue with a set of save_seqs instead, which does not need the extra epoch layer. Only one of the two is needed; if #51662 lands first, the second commit can be dropped. The first commit is independent and is not covered by #51662. The converse also holds: the first commit removes the end-state symptom of #51637 (blocks held forever, causing a livelock), because block lifetime no longer depends on a per-request counter, but it does not remove the ABA root cause — a leftover job can still rewind the resume offset and can still cause the current generation's save to be dropped. Both need fixing. Other related work: #43742 supplies the decrement that was missed on failure, whereas item 2 here is about a decrement landing on the wrong generation; #51595 aggregates async completions with a per-request count but gives request generations no identity; #43226 / #46240 handle late completions for requests that no longer exist, whereas here the req_id exists again and denotes a new generation, so an existence check cannot catch it. ## Test Plan ### Unit tests ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_prepare_values.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py -q ``` New targeted tests: | Test | Covers | |---|---| | `test_store_job_blocks_are_released_once_every_rank_reports` | the reference is released only after every rank reports; `has_pending_push_work()` opening and closing | | `test_partial_tail_cow_block_is_referenced_for_the_job` | the CoW block outside the block table is referenced and released too | | `test_worker_metadata_aggregates_completions_across_ranks` | completion counts aggregated across ranks | | `test_stale_store_job_cannot_touch_a_reused_request_id` | a leftover job cannot retire the new generation, rewind its resume offset, or mark it skipped | | `test_store_sending_thread_reports_job_when_store_raises` | a job is still reported when the store raises, so the reference is not leaked forever | ### End to end: running the #52360 reproduction against the fix H20, TP2, Qwen3-32B-FP8, `--num-gpu-blocks-override 1024` (the KV pool has to be far smaller than the concurrent working set, or the preempt path is never taken), 96 requests / 48 concurrent / 400-word random prompts / 192 max tokens, each side restarted against a cold store. The criterion is a content fingerprint, the same one used in #52360: a key names a fixed token range, so the KV under it is fixed. An 8-byte `D_pre` is taken on the GPU over the blocks the key covers just before `batch_put`, and `D_post` is taken on the destination blocks just after `batch_get`. A disagreement means the bytes the store returned are not that key's KV, and those bytes are already in a real request's KV blocks, about to be attended over. The instrumentation only records, it does not change behaviour, and it is not part of this PR. It lives on a separate probe branch so reviewers can rerun it: https://github.com/chengy-sysu/vllm/tree/mooncake-preemption-probes ## Test Result ### Wrong KV really is read into the computation; zero after the fix One cold-store run (2026-08-14): | | main + probes | this PR + probes | |---|---|---| | keys written and fingerprinted | 16,738 | 16,752 | | of those, written twice with disagreeing content (excluded as ambiguous) | 0 | 0 | | read-backs checked | 16,830 | 16,678 | | **fingerprint mismatches** | **588** | **0** | | poisoned keys | 438 | 0 | | **requests that read wrong KV** | **8 / 96** | **0 / 96** | | jobs flagged by an independent scheduler-side detector as "block reallocated during the read" | 23 | 0 | The 438 poisoned keys fall on only 8 distinct `save_seq` values, and **all 8 are among the 23 jobs the scheduler-side detector flagged independently** — two unrelated signals agreeing exactly. The fixed side still took 125 preemptions, so the race window was hit repeatedly there as well; it just no longer produces wrong KV. The intensity varies a lot between runs: the run in #52360 (same parameters, same cold-store restart) gave 155 mismatches / 155 poisoned keys / 1 affected request. The direction is consistent, but any specific number should be quoted with the run it came from. ### Performance: no cost observed Clean A/B without instrumentation. The baseline is `64ca614fe`, which was this PR's parent commit at the time of measurement (since rebased onto `e078a2238`; the patches are unchanged): | | `64ca614fe` | this PR | |---|---|---| | wall | 54.5s | 55.2s (+1.3%) | | TTFT p50 / p90 | 9.84s / 13.41s | 8.62s / 13.39s | | output tokens | 18,624 | 18,624 | | preemptions | 165 | 192 | | external prefix cache lookups | 134,777 | **134,777** | The lookup counts are identical, so the workload is deterministic and wall clock can be compared directly. Wall is +1.3%, p50 is in fact 1.2s faster and p90 is essentially the same, so the direction is not consistent. An earlier set of four runs had the fixed side 2–3.5% faster. The conclusion is that no measurable cost was observed. ### Unit tests and lint Across the 10 mooncake test files: **251 passed, 16 failed**. All 16 failures are `RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available` (the node had no GPU allocated) and all of them are in `test_mooncake_connector.py` / `test_mooncake_connector_hma.py` / `test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py`, three P2P transfer-engine files this PR does not touch. None of the four store files this PR changes failed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.0, the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) both pass. <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.text: ## Summary Add an image-only CUDA 13.4rc1 prerelease path for Rubin (`sm_107`): - overlay NVIDIA's `cuda-toolkit==13.4.0rc1` PyPI packages when CUDA 13.4 container images are unavailable - pin mutually compatible CUDA 13.4 PyTorch, torchvision, and torchaudio nightlies - preserve the driver stub and expose linker names/NCCL needed by native extensions - set `TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas` - add a manually gated, multi-arch Buildkite staging pipeline with native image smoke tests The normal CUDA image and release paths are unchanged unless the new build arguments are supplied. Tracks #49735. ## Duplicate-work check Immediately before opening this draft, the required searches found no open PR referencing #49735 and no open PR matching `CUDA 13.4 prerelease image` or `cu134 image`. This PR addresses the CUDA 13.4 developer-preview image workstream in the tracking issue; it does not duplicate the separate SM107 build-support and NVLink workstreams linked there. ## Validation - `uv run --no-project --with dockerfile-parse tools/generate_versions_json.py` - `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/cuda134-prerelease-pipeline.yaml .buildkite/scripts/validate-cuda134-image.sh .buildkite/test_areas/docker.yaml docker/Dockerfile docker/versions.json requirements/cuda134-nightly.txt` — passed - `bash -n .buildkite/scripts/validate-cuda134-image.sh` — passed - parsed both changed Buildkite YAML files with PyYAML — passed - `uv run --no-project --with pytest python -m pytest tests/tools/test_docker_build_metadata_args.py -v` — 7 passed - PyTorch nightly dependency resolution dry runs for `x86_64-manylinux_2_28` and `aarch64-manylinux_2_28` — 33 packages resolved on each architecture - native BuildKit image build on pirate `a100-01` (`linux/amd64`) — passed - native BuildKit image build on pirate `cpu-07` (`linux/arm64`) — passed - native smoke tests on both architectures verified vLLM import/package layout, PyTorch CUDA 13.4, pinned torchvision/torchaudio versions, the Triton PTXAS environment, and CUDA 13.4 `nvcc`/`ptxas` — passed - multi-arch manifest descriptors verified as `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` Staged validation image: ```text quay.io/tms/vllm-rubin:cu134-rc1-5fcb6c4c3d sha256:dd8d3103a2f54216a184511aa514451992fd4d8b2fa1e712d2f81c2644d6aa95 amd64: sha256:dcf57dfbcebcd92f569c6ac6ed5f358618373c6f8cd882fe244285f43b6b8ee2 arm64: sha256:484e2fde994cf254297fff6cbaf4903a5d49b3b1b0bb35e0369c8dd33c6676d9 ``` No model evaluation was run because this changes image construction and release automation, not model output or serving behavior. ## Rubin handoff GPU execution remains to be validated on Rubin. The image is compiled with vLLM CUDA target `10.7f`; the vendored FlashAttention build currently uses its upstream compatibility targets because it does not yet list SM107. ```bash IMAGE=quay.io/tms/vllm-rubin@sha256:dd8d3103a2f54216a184511aa514451992fd4d8b2fa1e712d2f81c2644d6aa95 docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint python3 "$IMAGE" -c ' import os import torch import vllm import vllm._C_stable_libtorch assert torch.version.cuda == "13.4" assert torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (10, 7) assert os.environ["TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH"] == "/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas" print(vllm.__version__, torch.__version__, torch.cuda.get_device_name()) ' docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint python3 "$IMAGE" -c ' import torch def eager(x): return torch.sin(x) * 2 compiled = torch.compile(eager) x = torch.randn(1024, device="cuda") torch.testing.assert_close(compiled(x), eager(x)) print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), torch.cuda.get_device_capability()) ' ``` The Buildkite pipeline deliberately disables the standalone wheel-size gate and the FlashInfer JIT cache for this image-only prerelease. No standalone wheel is published, and a CUDA 13.4 FlashInfer JIT index is not available yet. ## AI assistance and human accountability OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation. This PR must remain a draft until the human submitter has reviewed every changed line, understands the image/toolkit design and the wheel-size exception, and can defend the change end-to-end.

signals.title: [Rust Frontend][gRPC] Preserve skip_special_tokens decoding option
signals.text: ## Purpose Align the native Generate gRPC API with vLLM's existing Python serving APIs by carrying the per-request `skip_special_tokens` decoding option through `ResponseOptions`. The Python chat completions, completions, responses, and token-native APIs default this option to `true`, but the gRPC request did not expose it. Consequently, a gRPC caller could not explicitly preserve tokenizer-defined special markers required by some reasoning and tool parsers. The protobuf field is `optional` so the server can distinguish omission from an explicit `false`. Omitted values retain the established Python default of `true`; explicit `false` values are preserved. This affects decoded text only and does not change sampling, generated token IDs, or EOS behavior. * Python API behavior | Endpoint | Field location | Default | |---|---|---:| | `/v1/chat/completions` | Top-level request field | `true` | | `/v1/completions` | Top-level request field | `true` | | `/v1/responses` | Top-level request field | `true` | | `/inference/v1/generate` | `sampling_params.skip_special_tokens` | `true` | ## Test Plan - Verify Rust formatting. - Run the existing gRPC conversion test module after mapping the new response option into `TextDecodeOptions`. ## Test Result ```text $ cargo fmt --all -- --check $ cargo test -p vllm-server grpc::convert::tests running 13 tests test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 328 filtered out ``` --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. No documentation change is required for this parity fix. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix] Account for local DP workers in startup thread allocation
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52330. `MultiprocExecutor` sized each worker's startup thread pool using only the workers within one engine. With multiple local data-parallel engines, every engine therefore claimed the node's full CPU budget, oversubscribing CPU threads and severely slowing weight loading. This change: - includes `data_parallel_size_local` when counting workers that share the node's startup CPU budget; - preserves the existing behavior for tensor-parallel-only deployments and headless configurations where the local DP size is zero; - adds a regression test covering local DP, TP-only, and zero-local-DP cases. This is not a duplicate of an existing PR. Before submitting, I checked open PRs referencing #52330 and searched open PRs for the affected data-parallel startup/OMP thread-management area; no matching implementation was open. ## Test Plan - Run the targeted executor regression test on Linux CI. - Validate startup with multiple colocated DP engines, ideally using the issue's DP=4 block-quantized checkpoint reproduction on B200 hardware. - Run Python lint, formatting, syntax, and diff whitespace checks locally. ## Test Result - Ruff check on both changed files: passed. - Ruff format check on both changed files: passed. - `.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py tests/distributed/test_multiproc_executor.py`: passed. - `git diff --check`: passed. - Targeted pytest was not run locally because the available host is macOS arm64 and its existing `.venv` does not contain PyTorch or pytest. The test avoids creating GPU workers, but importing the vLLM executor still requires PyTorch. Linux CI and hardware validation are required. AI assistance was used to investigate the issue, implement the change, and draft the regression test and PR description. The human submitter reviewed the changes and is responsible for the contribution. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix][XPU] Skip oneCCL warm-up all_reduce when world_size == 1
signals.text: ## Purpose Skip the oneCCL warm-up all_reduce in `XPUWorker.init_device()` when `world_size == 1`. The warm-up is guarded only by `is_xccl_available()`, so single-device XPU serving still requires a working oneCCL communicator. On platforms where oneCCL cannot enumerate GPU topology this aborts engine startup, even though no collective is issued during inference. Fixes #52386 ## Test Plan - Single XPU (`--tensor-parallel-size 1`): server starts and serves; no behavioral change on hardware where oneCCL already worked, since the communicator is created lazily on first use. - Multi-XPU (`--tensor-parallel-size 2`): warm-up path unchanged. ## Test Result Verified on Intel Arc B390 (Xe3) with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, TP=1: engine starts, `/v1/chat/completions` returns correct output. Multi-device verification would be appreciated from someone with an Arc Pro B60/B70 system. Multi-device (`--tensor-parallel-size > 1`) is not covered by my hardware. The changed condition is a strict narrowing, so the warm-up still runs whenever more than one worker is present. Verification on an Arc Pro B60/B70 system would be appreciated.
signals.author: studioego

signals.title: [Bugfix] Raise `VLLMValidationError` from structured output validators
signals.text: ## Purpose Structured output validators raise raw `ValueError`. `AsyncLLM.generate` re-raises only `VLLMClientError` untouched and wraps the rest in `EngineGenerateError`, so a bad `response_format` schema returns 500 instead of 400. This issue is surfaced from ray serve LLM because vLLM 0.27 wraps validator `ValueErrors` in `EngineGenerateError`, which is treated as a server error. Ray then interprets an invalid `response_format` schema as an engine failure and returns a 500 instead of a 400. This PR updates these validators to raise `VLLMValidationError`, a `VLLMClientError` that generate() re-raises as-is, preserving the correct 4xx error type. This PR migrates the four validators reached from `SamplingParams.verify()` to `VLLMValidationError`, wraps external calls that leak raw exceptions, and updates the `auto` backend's `except` so its fallback chain still works. Related to #48227. ## Test Plan New unit tests are added. ## Test Result Ran unit tests locally and passed. ## AI Assistance Authored with Claude; submitter reviewed every line. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signals.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return all choices from /inference/v1/generate when n > 1
signals.text: ## Purpose closes #52398 `serve_tokens` sets `sampling_params.output_kind` only for streaming requests, so non-streaming ones keep the `SamplingParams` default, `CUMULATIVE`. With `n > 1`, `serve_tokens_full_generator` keeps only the last streamed `RequestOutput` and reads `final_res.outputs`, which under `CUMULATIVE` holds just the sequences updated in that step, the other completions are silently dropped. No error is raised; the response is simply short. `CompletionRequest.to_sampling_params` already uses `FINAL_ONLY` when not streaming, so this makes the token-in-token-out path match it. ## Test Plan 10 non-streaming requests per `n` (2, 4, 8) against `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B` on an H100, before and after the patch, counting the choices returned by `/inference/v1/generate`. Same check with multimodal input (`/v1/chat/completions/render` → `token_ids` + `features`, Qwen2.5-VL-3B). Streaming, `logprobs`, `prompt_logprobs` and `n=1` re-checked after the patch. Adds a regression test asserting the response carries indices `0..n-1`. ## Test Result Before: ``` n=2 -> {1: 6, 2: 4} n=4 -> {2: 5, 3: 3, 4: 2} n=8 -> {5: 2, 7: 5, 3: 1, 6: 2} multimodal, n=4 -> 3 choices on 6/6 runs ``` After: ``` n=2 -> {2: 10} n=4 -> {4: 10} n=8 -> {8: 10} multimodal, n=4 -> 4 choices on 6/6 runs ``` `n=1`, streaming, `logprobs` and `prompt_logprobs` behave as before. The measurements were taken on v0.27.1 with this patch applied to the installed package; the added test follows the existing fixtures in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py` and will get its first full run in CI. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix] Pick the DeepSeek V4 eager cudagraph region per model runner
signals.text: #51430 narrowed the DeepSeek V4 eager cudagraph region, which corrupts MRV1 output, and #51768 responded by defaulting the model to MRV2 and rejecting MRV1 + PIECEWISE. That default costs ROCm, where MRV1 is still the faster runner for this model. Choose the region from the runner instead: MRV1 wraps the whole attention body in `_prepare_and_attn_eager`, restoring the pre-#51430 region it needs, while MRV2 keeps the narrow region and its shorter TTFT. The nested `_sparse_indexer_and_attn` break runs inline, since `add_eager` clears `_capturing` first. MRV1 + PIECEWISE is then correct on every platform, so drop the rejection. CUDA still defaults to MRV2; ROCm defaults to MRV1 until MRV2 is competitive there. Claude was used to help.
signals.author: njhill

signals.title: [ROCm][gfx942] DSv4 sparse-attn indexer: native fp8 MFMA + corrected LDS occupancy gate
signals.text: ## Summary Optimizes the **gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X)** path of `fp8_mqa_logits` — the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-attention *indexer* in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_fp8_mqa_logits.py`. **All changes are confined to `fp8_mqa_logits_gfx942` and its `_gfx942_*` helpers.** The CUDA and other non-gfx942 backends are untouched, so there is no cross-backend regression surface. ## Mechanism - **Native fp8 MFMA via bitcast.** The kernel previously took the software fp8→fp16 expansion path. We bitcast the fp8 operands from OCP `e4m3fn` to `e4m3fnuz` so they feed the native gfx942 fp8 MFMA (`v_mfma_*_f8`) directly. `e4m3fn` and `e4m3fnuz` share the exact same 1-4-3 bit layout; the *only* differing encoding is byte `0x80` (`-0.0` in OCP e4m3, `NaN` in e4m3fnuz), which we scrub host-side so results stay bit-safe. The two-bitcast dot yields `(q·k)/4`, corrected by a compensating scale (free). - **Corrected LDS occupancy gate.** The old gate charged the KV tile at **2 bytes/element** (an fp16-expanded tile). On gfx942 the KV operand reaches the MFMA as **1 byte/element** (native fp8). The corrected estimate (`head_size × BLOCK_KV × 1 + pipeline_slack = 16896 B`) matches `kernel.metadata.shared` exactly, so the default `(BLOCK_KV=128, num_stages=2)` tile now correctly *fits* LDS instead of being needlessly rejected. - **Fused out-of-window −inf epilogue** (`OOW_FILL`) — HIP-graph-safe, replaces a separate masking pass. - `waves_per_eu=3` and a `matrix_instr_nonkdim` heuristic fix for better occupancy. ## Results (MI300X, GLM-5.1-FP8) **Isolated kernel:** **7.85× geomean** speedup, **0.0** err_ratio vs reference. Accuracy held: needle-in-haystack 3/3, gsm8k 11/12. ### E2E — clear wins (>2% total token throughput vs the identical non-patched image) All numbers are peak-concurrency, iso-concurrency A/B (same image, same shape, same concurrency; only the indexer kernel differs). | Topology | GPUs | Shape (ISL/OSL) | con | Baseline tok/s | Recipe 11 tok/s | Δ% | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Single-node TP8 | 8 | 8k/1k | — | 8,092.71 | 8,420.32 | **+4.05%** | | 1P1D disagg | 16 | 8k/1k | 512 | 17,611.11 | 18,597.20 | **+5.60%** | | 1P1D disagg | 16 | 32k/2k | 128 | 13,640.95 | 14,370.07 | **+5.35%** | | 1P1D disagg | 16 | 4k/4k | 512 | 9,687.21 | 10,007.99 | **+3.31%** | | 1P1D disagg | 16 | 8k/4k | 256 | 7,354.28 | 7,535.49 | **+2.46%** | | 1P2D disagg | 24 | 8k/1k | 1024 | 18,358.89 | 19,227.94 | **+4.73%** | | 1P2D disagg | 24 | 32k/2k | 256 | 14,743.82 | 15,522.00 | **+5.28%** | | 1P2D disagg | 24 | 96k/32k | 64 | 2,469.30 | 2,545.12 | **+3.07%** | | 2P2D disagg | 32 | 8k/1k | 1024 | 19,326.84 | 20,592.84 | **+6.55%** | | 2P2D disagg | 32 | 32k/2k | 256 | 15,820.50 | 16,836.50 | **+6.42%** | | 2P2D disagg | 32 | 4k/4k | 1024 | 12,671.83 | 12,961.02 | **+2.28%** | The largest E2E wins are the prefill-dominant, short-output shapes (8k/1k, 32k/2k) across every topology — consistent with the indexer being a prefill-time kernel. Single-node TP8 8k/1k also shows TTFT −6.5% / TPOT −3.0% (mean). Decode-heavy / balanced shapes (e.g. 32k/8k) gain ~1–2%, at the noise floor and Amdahl-limited by the MoE GEMMs and MLA attention that dominate those regimes. Two 1P2D shapes (4k/4k, 8k/4k) are being re-validated after a straggler contaminated their first pass and will be added once clean. ## Tests Adds `tests/kernels/attention/test_fp8_mqa_logits_gfx942.py` (gated to AMD gfx942, skipped elsewhere), covering exactly the features this PR introduces: - **native fp8 MFMA bitcast** — output matches the `fp8_mqa_logits_torch` reference via per-row cosine + top-k index overlap (the indexer's functional signal); - **`OOW_FILL`** — out-of-window positions are exactly `-inf`, in-window entries finite; - **`0x80` fnuz scrub** — planting `-0.0` (`0x80`) K bytes yields no `NaN`/`Inf`. (Thresholds are principled — both arms share the same fp8 inputs and differ only in matmul precision — but may want a light hardware calibration; happy to adjust.) ## Safety / review notes - Change is gated to the existing gfx942 dispatch; no effect on other platforms. - The `0x80` host-side scrub is the only correctness-sensitive step for the fnuz bitcast; the new test locks it down. - Base is current `main` (file blob `619d0ec`), so the diff is exactly one source file + one test file. cc **@tuukkjs** (authored the DSv4 gfx942 path), **@tjtanaa** **@dllehr-amd** (ROCm CODEOWNERS), **@LucasWilkinson** **@MatthewBonanni** (`vllm/v1/attention` owners) — review welcome.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return all n choices from /inference/v1/generate
signals.text: FIX #52398 ## Purpose A non-streaming `POST /inference/v1/generate` with `sampling_params.n > 1` returns fewer than `n` choices, non-deterministically and without an error — the response is a well-formed `GenerateResponse`, the completions are simply missing. `/v1/completions` with the same `n` always returns `n`. Root cause, as diagnosed in the issue and confirmed here on `main`: `serve_tokens` set `output_kind` only for streaming, ```python if request.stream: sampling_params.output_kind = RequestOutputKind.DELTA ``` so non-streaming requests kept the `SamplingParams` default, `RequestOutputKind.CUMULATIVE`. `serve_tokens_full_generator` keeps only the last output it sees (`final_res = res` in the `async for`) and then iterates `final_res.outputs`. Under `CUMULATIVE` that last output carries only the sequences updated in that step, so sequences that finished earlier never reach `choices`. This is the outlier: `openai/completion/protocol.py:392`, `openai/chat_completion/protocol.py:738`, `openai/responses/protocol.py:448`, both speech-to-text protocols and `offline_utils.py:561` all use `DELTA if stream else FINAL_ONLY`. ## Test Plan `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_generate_returns_all_choices`, parametrized over `n = 2, 4`, asserts `len(choices) == n` and that the indices are exactly `0..n-1`. The existing tests in that file only ever request `n = 1`, which is why this went unnoticed. ## Test Result I have no GPU on this machine, so I could not run the `RemoteOpenAIServer`-backed suite locally — that run is CI's. What I did verify locally: the diagnosis against current `main` (the `CUMULATIVE` default reaching `serve_tokens_full_generator`, and the sibling entrypoints that already do this correctly), and `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on both files. The reporter's own numbers on the unpatched server, 10 runs per `n`, expected `{n: 10}`: ``` 2 {1: 6, 2: 4} 4 {2: 5, 3: 3, 4: 2} 8 {5: 2, 7: 5, 3: 1, 6: 2} ``` and they confirmed 10/10 correct for `n = 2/4/8` when `output_kind` is forced to `FINAL_ONLY` through the request body, which is exactly what this patch makes the default. ## Contribution notes (per `AGENTS.md`) - Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52398 in:body"`, `--search "output_kind"` and `--search "serve_tokens output_kind"` all return nothing; no other PR touches `scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py` for this. - Not a model-affecting change: it selects the `RequestOutputKind` used to assemble the response, so no eval results apply. - AI assistance was used in preparing this change. I reviewed every changed line, confirmed the root cause against `main` myself, and can defend it end-to-end. The uncertain part I want a reviewer's eye on is whether any caller depends on passing `output_kind` explicitly in `sampling_params` (the workaround in the issue); this makes `FINAL_ONLY` the default, and unlike the OpenAI-compat endpoints it still overrides an explicitly supplied value, which I kept for consistency with those endpoints rather than changing here.
signals.author: Chessing234

signals.title: [Bugfix] Don't split a multimodal item that a prefill chunk starts exactly on
signals.text: FIX #52306 ## Purpose Under `disable_chunked_mm_input=True` the scheduler still splits a multimodal item when the chunk begins exactly on it. `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` guards the split with ```python self.scheduler_config.disable_chunked_mm_input and num_computed_tokens < start_pos # (A) and (num_computed_tokens + num_new_tokens) < (start_pos + num_encoder_tokens) # (B) ``` (A) is false when `num_computed_tokens == start_pos`, so (B) never runs and a chunk too small to cover the item is allowed through. That equality is not an exotic state — it is exactly what the guard itself produces: the rollback sets `num_new_tokens = start_pos - num_computed_tokens`, so the next step starts on the item. If the budget cannot fit the whole item on that step, the item is split at the precise point the flag exists to prevent. For models with bidirectional attention over the item, the tokens that should cross-attend silently cannot. The fix is `<=` in (A). Only the equality case changes: - `num_computed_tokens < start_pos` — unchanged, rolls back to just before the item. - `num_computed_tokens == start_pos` and the chunk does not cover the item — now yields `num_new_tokens = 0`, so the request waits for a step that can fit it. This matches the neighbouring `can_allocate` branch, which already returns 0 rather than scheduling a partial item. - `num_computed_tokens > start_pos` (prefix caching landing mid-item) — unchanged. Returning 0 cannot starve the request: `_verify_args` already rejects a `max_num_batched_tokens` smaller than the longest multimodal item when this flag is set (`test_no_mm_input_chunking` asserts that `ValueError`), so a step that can fit the item always exists. ## Test Plan `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_no_mm_input_chunking_at_item_boundary` drives `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` on a real scheduler and request (mm item at offset 400, length 800) across the three cases: starting before the item, starting on it without room, and starting on it with room. The existing `test_no_mm_input_chunking` only exercises the first, which is why this went unnoticed. ## Test Result I have no GPU or vLLM build on this machine, so I could not execute the suite — that run is CI's, and I will follow it. What I verified locally: the condition and the surrounding branches on current `main`, the neighbouring `can_allocate` handling that this now matches, and the `max_num_batched_tokens` validation that rules out starvation. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both files. The reporter's direct-call reproduction on unpatched `main` shows the failure this fixes: ``` print(ask(0, 500)) # 3 - correct, stops before the item print(ask(3, 500)) # 500 - wrong, splits the 766-token item ``` ## Contribution notes (per `AGENTS.md`) - Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52306 in:body"` and `--search "disable_chunked_mm_input"` return nothing; the issue has no linked PR. - Not model-affecting in the eval sense (a scheduling boundary), so no eval numbers apply — though the user-visible symptom is degraded output for bidirectional-attention multimodal models, which is why the regression test asserts the boundary directly. - AI assistance was used in preparing this change. I read every changed line, checked the branch behaviour against `main` myself, and can defend it. The judgement call worth a reviewer's eye: the equality case now returns 0 rather than a partial schedule, which costs one scheduling step in exchange for never splitting the item.
