### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Your current environment - vLLM version: 0.14.0rc2.dev148+gaa7f37ccf - PyTorch version: 2.9.1+cu130 - CUDA version: 13.0 (Driver 580.126.09) - Python version: 3.12.12 - OS: Ubuntu Linux (x86_64) - GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000 x8 ## Describe the bug When using vLLM with the default `fork` multiprocessing method (`VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=fork`), the EngineCore child process fails to initialize CUDA with the error: ``` RuntimeError: CUDA driver initialization failed, you might not have a CUDA gpu. ``` This happens even though: - `nvidia-smi` shows all GPUs are available - `torch.cuda.is_available()` returns `True` - `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` returns `False` before forking ## Root Cause Analysis The issue is caused by **pynvml initializing the CUDA driver** before the fork, but this initialization is **not detected** by vLLM's `_maybe_force_spawn()` function. ### Proof of root cause: ```python import ctypes import multiprocessing # Calling cuInit() before fork (simulating what pynvml does) cuda = ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1') result = cuda.cuInit(0) print('Parent: cuInit result:', result) # Returns 0 (success) def test_cuda_in_child(): import torch try: torch.cuda.init() print('Child: CUDA init SUCCESS') except Exception as e: print('Child: CUDA init FAILED:', e) ctx = multiprocessing.get_context('fork') p = ctx.Process(target=test_cuda_in_child) p.start() p.join() ``` **Output:** ``` Parent: cuInit result: 0 Child: CUDA init FAILED: CUDA driver initialization failed, you might not have a CUDA gpu. ``` ### The detection gap: In `vllm/utils/system_utils.py`, the `_maybe_force_spawn()` function checks: ```python if cuda_is_initialized(): reasons.append("CUDA is initialized") ``` But `cuda_is_initialized()` in `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py` only checks: ```python def cuda_is_initialized() -> bool: if not torch.cuda._is_compiled(): return False return torch.cuda.is_initialized() # Only checks PyTorch's CUDA context! ``` This does **not** detect when the CUDA driver has been initialized at the driver level (via `cuInit()`), which happens when: - `pynvml.nvmlInit()` is called during platform detection in `vllm/platforms/__init__.py` - Any other library calls `cuInit()` directly ## Steps to reproduce ```python # test_vllm_fork_bug.py from vllm import LLM model_path = "any-valid-model-path" llm = LLM(model=model_path, trust_remote_code=True) ``` Run with default settings (fork method): ```bash python test_vllm_fork_bug.py ``` **Expected behavior:** LLM initializes successfully **Actual behavior:** EngineCore process crashes with CUDA initialization error ## Workaround Set the environment variable to use `spawn` instead of `fork`: ```python import os os.environ['VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD'] = 'spawn' from vllm import LLM def main(): llm = LLM(model=model_path, trust_remote_code=True) # ... if __name__ == "__main__": # Required for spawn method main() ``` ## Suggested Fix Modify `cuda_is_initialized()` in `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py` to also check for driver-level CUDA initialization: ```python def cuda_is_initialized() -> bool: """Check if CUDA is initialized (either PyTorch context or driver level).""" if not torch.cuda._is_compiled(): return False # Check PyTorch's CUDA context if torch.cuda.is_initialized(): return True # Check driver-level initialization via cuInit try: import ctypes cuda = ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1') # cuDeviceGetCount succeeds only if cuInit was called count = ctypes.c_int() result = cuda.cuDeviceGetCount(ctypes.byref(count)) if result == 0: # CUDA_SUCCESS means driver is initialized return True except Exception: pass return False ``` Alternatively, consider calling `pynvml.nvmlShutdown()` after GPU detection, or use a separate subprocess for pynvml queries to avoid contaminating the main process's CUDA state. ## Additional Context - This issue affects vLLM 0.14.x development versions - The `spawn` workaround works but requires code changes (`if __name__ == "__main__":`) - Setting `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0` also works but disables multiprocessing entirely ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Kernel] adding native nccl4py support
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose ### Summary This PR integrates **nccl4py** (NVIDIA's official Python bindings for NCCL) as the default NCCL backend for vLLM, replacing the legacy ctypes-based implementation. The legacy implementation is preserved and can be enabled via `VLLM_DISABLE_NCCL4PY=1` for rollback purposes. ### Motivation The existing ctypes-based NCCL wrapper has served vLLM well, but maintaining pure Python bindings for a complex C library introduces several challenges: - Version compatibility issues requiring manual updates - Limited type safety and error handling - No official support from NVIDIA **nccl4py** provides: - Official NVIDIA support and maintenance - Clean, Pythonic API with proper type hints - Automatic NCCL library discovery and version management - Better error messages and debugging support - Support for latest NCCL features (e.g., `ncclMemAlloc`, window registration) ### Changes #### New Files - `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl.py` - New nccl4py-based implementation - `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl_wrapper_legacy.py` - Moved legacy ctypes implementation #### Modified Files - `vllm/envs.py` - Added `VLLM_DISABLE_NCCL4PY` environment variable - `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/p2p/p2p_nccl_engine.py` - Updated for backend selection - `vllm/utils/nccl.py` - Updated documentation ## Rollback Support To use the legacy implementation: ```bash export VLLM_DISABLE_NCCL4PY=1 ``` This allows users to quickly rollback if any issues are encountered with nccl4py. ## Dependencies nccl4py is available via pip: ```bash pip install nccl4py[cu12] # For CUDA 12.x pip install nccl4py[cu13] # For CUDA 13.x ``` ## Test Plan - All existing `test_pynccl.py` tests pass with both implementations - Tested with CUDA graphs capture and replay - Verified with custom allreduce, symmetric memory, and standard NCCL paths ## Test Result Performed benchmarking on 8x H100 80GB HBM3 GPUs (500 trials, 100 warmup iterations). For small messages verified with Nsight that the kernels performance are the same ### PyNccl (Standard) Results | Tensor Size | nccl4py (ms) | Legacy (ms) | Difference | |-------------|--------------|-------------|------------| | 1 MB | 0.024 | 0.025 | -4% | | 2 MB | 0.037 | 0.037 | 0% | | 4 MB | 0.050 | 0.050 | 0% | | 8 MB | 0.077 | 0.080 | -4% | | 16 MB | 0.120 | 0.121 | -1% | | 32 MB | 0.197 | 0.196 | +0.5% | | 64 MB | 0.321 | 0.322 | -0.3% | | 128 MB | 0.577 | 0.575 | +0.3% | | 256 MB | 1.090 | 1.088 | +0.2% | | 512 MB | 2.112 | 2.112 | 0% | ### PyNccl-Symm (Symmetric Memory) Results | Tensor Size | nccl4py (ms) | Legacy (ms) | Difference | |-------------|--------------|-------------|------------| | 4 MB | 0.025 | 0.025 | 0% | | 16 MB | 0.083 | 0.083 | 0% | | 64 MB | 0.311 | 0.310 | +0.3% | | 256 MB | 1.199 | 1.198 | +0.1% | | 512 MB | 2.406 | 2.409 | -0.1% |

signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> This PR adds LoRA support for Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration and improves multimodal LoRA mapping correctness for mixed modalities. It is motivated by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31205 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31479. ## Key Changes - LoRA support: Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration now implements SupportsLoRA and provides multimodal token-counting logic compatible with vision and audio. - Modality-aware LoRA mapping: The LoRA mapping in the runner now handles modality-specific token counts. - Example improvements: only_thinker.py now supports optional LoRA arguments for easier testing. ## Why These Changes Mixed-modality token counts were previously computed with a vision-only formula, which breaks audio mappings. ## Testing - Ran only_thinker.py with a generated (fake) LoRA adapter successfully. - Real trained LoRA testing will be added later. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. - [ ] (Optional) Release notes update. signal.title: [GGUF] Fix loading of fused/shard-less quantized weights
signal.text: ## Summary When a GGUF checkpoint stores a fused tensor (e.g. a single pre-merged qkv weight) instead of individual shards, `MergedColumnParallelLinear.weight_loader` would fall through to the non-GGUF path and leave the parameter as `UninitializedParameter`, crashing at inference. This came up while working on Qwen3-Next GGUF support — some GGUF exports pack projections into a single tensor with no shard ID, which hit this path. I pulled the fixes out into a separate PR since they're not model-specific. **What's here:** - **Materialize `UninitializedParameter` for fused GGUF weights**: when a GGUF weight arrives without a `loaded_shard_id`, materialize the param, TP-slice it, and copy the data in directly, instead of falling through to the non-GGUF branch. - **Set `param.weight_type` for non-sharded loads**: `GGUFLinearMethod.apply()` expects `weight_type` on the non-shard branch — previously only `shard_weight_type` was populated, so the fused path would `AttributeError`. - **Add MXFP4 to quant type routing**: `WeightType.MXFP4` (type 39) was missing from `DEQUANT_TYPES`, `MMVQ_QUANT_TYPES`, and `MMQ_QUANT_TYPES`, so MXFP4 GGUF files were rejected at load time. - **Sort numeric shard IDs in `apply()`**: the shard iteration used insertion order, which could be wrong for numeric IDs (e.g. `[1, 0]`), silently producing incorrect output after `torch.cat`. - **Handle suffix-less GGUF name mappings**: some tensors (like bias) map directly without a `.weight`/`.bias` suffix — the old code unconditionally appended `"." + suffix`, breaking these. ## Test plan - [x] Load a GGUF model that uses fused (non-sharded) weight tensors — verified with Qwen3-Next GGUF - [x] Load an MXFP4-quantized GGUF file — verified it's accepted by the quant router - [ ] Verify existing GGUF models (Llama, Gemma, etc.) still load and produce correct output

signal.title: [Security] Add Host header validation and improve security guide
signal.text: Add --allowed-hosts CLI option using Starlette's TrustedHostMiddleware to validate the Host header on incoming requests. When binding to a localhost address (the default), Host header validation is enabled automatically, rejecting requests from untrusted domains. When binding to other addresses, validation is disabled for backward compatibility unless --allowed-hosts is explicitly set. GHSA-rx2h-752g-w9w4 Signed-off-by: Russell Bryant <rbryant@redhat.com>

signal.title: Fix random dataset parameter defaults silently overriding user input
signal.text: ## Problem The `--random-input-len` and `--random-output-len` parameters have argparse default values (1024 and 128) that silently override user-specified `--input-len` and `--output-len` values when using `--dataset-name random`. This causes silent data corruption in benchmarks where users specify different token lengths but all benchmarks run with the same workload. ### Example ```bash # User specifies 256 tokens vllm bench throughput --dataset-name random --input-len 256 --output-len 256 # But vLLM actually uses 1024 input and 128 output (from defaults) # User has no idea their parameters were ignored ``` This affects ANY token size (128, 256, 512, 2048, etc.), not just specific values. ## Root Cause The fallback logic checks `if random_input_len is not None`, but since argparse sets defaults, `random_input_len` is never None (it's always 1024), so the fallback to `args.input_len` never happens. ## Solution 1. **Remove argparse defaults** - Set `default=None` for both parameters ## Testing ***Before (Broken): *** ```bash # User specifies 256, but silently gets 1024/128 from argparse defaults vllm bench throughput --dataset-name random --input-len 256 --output-len 256 ``` ***After (Fixed):*** ```bash # Option A: User specifies values → uses them vllm bench throughput --dataset-name random --input-len 256 --output-len 256 # Option B: User omits values → gets defaults (1024/128) from RandomDataset vllm bench throughput --dataset-name random ```

signal.title: [Bug]: qwen3_5_mtp fails to load at tensor-parallel-size >= 2 (drafter weight shape mismatch)
signal.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... uv is set ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 4.2.3 Libc version : glibc-2.43 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 (main, Apr 7 2026, 20:45:25) [Clang 22.1.1 ] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-29-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.43 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.2.78 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 2: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 3: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti GPU 4: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 5: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 6: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Nvidia driver version : 610.43.03 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 Vendor ID: AuthenticAMD Model name: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9955WX 16-Cores CPU(s): 32 NUMA node(s): 1 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 [pip3] numpy==2.3.5 [pip3] torch==2.13.0 [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0 [pip3] transformers==5.15.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.27.1 GPU Topology (relevant pair): GPU0 <-> GPU1: NODE (PCIe, no NVLink) ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` (equivalently `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp`) fails to load at `--tensor-parallel-size >= 2` for a Qwen3.5-architecture dense model (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, `model_type: qwen3_5`) with a shape-assertion crash inside the MTP drafter's weight loader. It works fine at TP=1 (modulo a separate, likely-unrelated OOM covered at the bottom, on a 24GB GPU specifically). The crash reproduces with both the Qwen3.5-specific and the generic MTP method name, so the method name isn't the variable — it looks like the drafter (loaded via a code path separate from the main model, in `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`) ends up with an effective tensor-parallel/world size that's inconsistent with the main model's requested TP degree. **Model:** a Heretic-abliterated, NVFP4-quantized (via NVIDIA Model-Optimizer's `hf_ptq.py`, `--qformat nvfp4`) finetune of `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (dense, `mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1`). The base model's config declares `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings: false`. Not a MoE model, no `--quantization moe_wna16`/GPTQ/AWQ involved, so this isn't #39475's `moe_wna16` MTP KeyError, and I confirmed `packed_modules_mapping` in `qwen3_5_mtp.py` is correct (`["q_proj","k_proj","v_proj"]` / `["gate_proj","up_proj"]`), so this isn't #35031's `gate_up_proj` copy-paste bug either — those are the two closest prior issues I could find and neither matches. The checkpoint's own `mtp.*` tensors were preserved unmodified from the original release (spliced back in from the raw upstream checkpoint after an unrelated finetuning step dropped them — `transformers`' `Qwen3_5PreTrainedModel._keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected = [r"^mtp.*"]` means any `AutoModel.from_pretrained()` round-trip silently discards `mtp.*` weights, so they have to be reattached from the original checkpoint afterward). I want to flag this clearly in case it's relevant, but I don't believe it's the cause of the crash below — see the "ruled out" list. #### Repro ```bash vllm serve \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Also reproduces identically with `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp --spec-tokens 3` in place of the JSON `--speculative-config` form. #### Observed ``` (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id) (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 989, in weight_loader_v2 (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] param.load_merged_column_weight( (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] File ".../vllm/model_executor/parameter.py", line 175, in load_merged_column_weight (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] AssertionError ``` Both `Worker_TP0` and `Worker_TP1` crash identically, on the first fused (`qkv_proj` or `gate_up_proj`) weight loaded for the MTP block's single decoder layer (`mtp.layers.0.*`). #### Diagnosis With `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the MTP block's `mlp.down_proj` (a plain row-parallel weight, loaded through a different, less strict code path than the fused-column weights) loads *successfully* right before the crash, with logged shape `torch.Size([5120, 4352])`. The raw checkpoint's `mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight` is `(5120, 17408)`. `17408 / 4352 = 4` — not `17408 / 2 = 8704`, which is what correct TP=2 row-parallel sharding should produce. That means the drafter is loading with an effective world size of 4 for at least this tensor, while the rest of the process (main model included) is correctly running at TP=2. The very next fused-column weight for the same MTP layer hits the strict `assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape` in `load_merged_column_weight`, which — unlike `down_proj`'s loader — doesn't tolerate the inconsistency. I wasn't able to pin down exactly where inside `llm_base_proposer.py`'s model/parallel-config construction for `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor` the world size diverges — didn't have a local vLLM checkout set up to add print statements at `get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()` in the drafter's construction path specifically. The `down_proj` shape is solid, reproducible evidence of *that* the divergence happens; not *why*. #### Ruled out - **Not the method name / CLI form**: identical crash with `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp` and with the generic `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` form. - **Not an NVFP4-quant-exclusion config issue**: tested directly against `ModelOptNvFp4Config.is_layer_excluded()` in a Python shell with the checkpoint's real `hf_quant_config.json` — `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj` and all sibling MTP linear-layer names correctly resolve as excluded from NVFP4 quantization. The destination parameters are being allocated as plain unquantized `nn.Parameter`s, same as the main model's, so this isn't a quantization-format/exclude-list matching problem. - **Not an actual architecture incompatibility.** I initially assumed the checkpoint's `q_proj` being unusually wide (12288, which is 48 attention-heads'-worth against a nominal 24-head config) was the root cause. That's wrong: the *main* model's decoder layers have the identical `q_proj=(12288,5120)` shape (likely related to `attn_output_gate: true` in the config) and load/serve correctly at TP=2. `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.__init__` explicitly constructs its single layer via the exact same `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer` class the main model uses for its full-attention layers, so this shape is not MTP-specific and not the bug. - **Disappears entirely at TP=1** — all weight loading succeeds, including everything that crashes at TP=2. (At TP=1 on a single 24GB GPU I then hit a separate `torch.OutOfMemoryError` while constructing `Qwen3_5MTP`'s `ParallelLMHead`, which persisted even after cutting `--max-model-len` from 262144 down to 32768 with no change in the reported memory figures — suggesting the MTP drafter may be allocating its own dedicated `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` regardless of the checkpoint's `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings: false`, though I haven't confirmed that with an actual memory snapshot at the crash site, just arithmetic that happens to line up — `vocab_size=124160, hidden_size=5120` gives ~1.27GB per duplicated embed/lm_head tensor. Flagging this separately since it may or may not be related; happy to open it as its own issue if it turns out to be unrelated to the TP crash above.)

signal.title: [Bug]: Sleep-mode Level 2 wake does not reload speculative-decoding draft weights — silent ~2x decode slowdown, acceptance drops to 0
signal.text: # [Bug]: Sleep-mode Level 2 wake does not reload speculative-decoding draft weights — silent ~2x decode slowdown, acceptance drops to 0 ## Summary After waking a vLLM server from Level 2 sleep using the documented staged sequence (`wake_up(tags=["weights"])` → `collective_rpc("reload_weights")` → `wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])` → `reset_prefix_cache`), MTP speculative decoding stops working entirely: every drafted token is rejected, and decode throughput drops to roughly the no-speculation rate. **Outputs remain correct** (verification rejects the garbage drafts), which makes the bug silent — nothing crashes and no quality signal fires; you only notice via throughput or the SpecDecoding metrics line. ## Environment - vLLM: `0.1.dev493+g4d9600003` (installed); bug also verified present on current `main` (fetched `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` and `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py` on 2026-08-15 — `reload_weights` still iterates the main model's `named_parameters()` only, and `wake_up` still restores draft *buffers* only) - GPUs: 2x RTX 5090 (SM120), TP=2 - Model: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (dense, FP8), `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2, "num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size":[[1,2,2],[3,16,0]]}'` - Server flags: `--enable-sleep-mode`, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`, kv-cache fp8, prefix caching on, custom all-reduce on - PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0 ## Reproduction (serving API) ``` # 1. cold boot with MTP spec decoding enabled; confirm baseline: # SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 2.6-2.8, ~110 tok/s decode # 2. sleep level 2 curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/sleep?level=2' # 3. documented staged wake curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/wake_up?tags=["weights"]' curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/collective_rpc' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"method":"reload_weights"}' curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/wake_up?tags=["kv_cache"]' curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/reset_prefix_cache' # 4. generate; observe metrics: # SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 # decode ~55 tok/s (vs ~110 baseline) ``` Measured on our box (3-run medians, 256-token generations, ~1k-token prompt): baseline 111.9 tok/s → post-wake 51.8 tok/s (46% of baseline). A cold restart of the same config restores full speed, so it is not a config issue. ## Root cause (source-level) Level 2 sleep discards all weight memory — main model **and drafter** — and saves only *buffers* to CPU (`gpu_worker.sleep`: `_sleep_saved_buffers` and `_sleep_saved_draft_buffers` from `named_buffers()`). On wake, `gpu_worker.wake_up` restores those buffers and re-reserves memory, but the subsequent `reload_weights` call (`v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py::reload_weights`) builds its load set from the **main model's** `named_parameters()`: ```python model = self.get_model() weights_to_load = {... for name, _ in model.named_parameters()} ... loaded_weights = model.load_weights(weights_iterator) ``` `get_draft_model()` (→ `drafter.model`) is a separate module, so the MTP drafter's parameters are never written after the L2 discard. The drafter runs on reserved-but-uninitialized memory → acceptance 0 → the verifier rejects everything → correct outputs at no-spec speed. The buffer save/restore path already treats main and draft models symmetrically (`wake_up` lines restoring `_sleep_saved_draft_buffers`); the parameter reload path simply lacks the symmetric handling. ## Impact - Silent ~2x decode slowdown after every L2 wake with MTP/EAGLE-style speculative decoding (any backend whose drafter is a separate module). - Model-switch setups (the documented sleep-mode use case) hit this on the first swap and never recover without a restart. ## Related - #29341 (L2 wake produces gibberish main-model outputs — same "L2 restore incomplete" family, different layer) - #16564 (L2 wake weight load failures) - #28606 (reload_weights issues with quantized formats) - #46725 (open PR: Runtime Draft Weight Update for Speculative Decoding — adjacent machinery) - #15254 / #30359 (RFCs on wake-up weight-update design) ## Proposed direction Extend the L2 wake reload path so drafter parameters are reloaded from the same checkpoint stream (or via the drafter's own load path) before KV-cache wake. Happy to submit a PR — pointers on preferred shape (extend `reload_weights` vs. a drafter-specific hook) welcome. --- *Bug found and reported by an AI agent (Hermes/Aether, operated by Greg Weyer) during serving-infrastructure debugging; reproduction and source analysis verified against the installed build.*

signal.title: Fix MRV2 Gumbel sampling for non-finite logits
signal.text: ## Summary Fix MRV2 Gumbel sampling when the candidate logits contain `-inf` entries. The current Gumbel path only clamps the uniform draw away from zero. If the draw reaches the upper endpoint after floating-point rounding, the Gumbel noise becomes `inf`. Adding that noise to a masked/non-candidate `-inf` logit produces `NaN`, and a subsequent Triton reduction can return an invalid token index. This change: - clamps fp32/fp64 uniform draws away from both `0` and `1`; - only adds Gumbel noise to finite logits; - adds a CUDA/Triton regression test that deterministically reproduces the `-inf + inf -> NaN` edge case. ## Why this matters We hit this downstream in a Kimi K2.6 MRV2 speculative decoding deployment with DCP8 and Eagle/MTP. The failure surfaced during spec-decode/logprobs warmup as an invalid sampled token id and then a CUDA illegal memory access: ```text Invalid sampled token ids for spec logprobs: count=1 vocab=163840 idx=[508] vals=[9223372034707292159] ``` The DCP8/Kimi setup makes the bug easy to trigger, but the root cause is not DCP-specific. It is the generic Gumbel sampler being asked to sample from residual logits where rejected tokens are represented as `-inf`. A minimal deterministic reproduction of the arithmetic issue is: ```python logits = -inf u = 1.0 gumbel_noise = -log(-log(u)) # inf logits + gumbel_noise # NaN ``` After this patch, the same case stays `-inf` and does not poison the reduction. ## Tests ```text python3 - <<'PY' import importlib.util path = "tests/v1/sample/test_gumbel.py" spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("test_gumbel_direct", path) mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) spec.loader.exec_module(mod) mod.test_gumbel_noise_does_not_turn_negative_inf_logits_into_nan(False) mod.test_gumbel_noise_does_not_turn_negative_inf_logits_into_nan(True) print("direct test passed") PY python3 -m py_compile vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py tests/v1/sample/test_gumbel.py git diff --check ``` I could not run the repository pytest entrypoint in this local container because `tests/conftest.py` imports `tblib`, which is not installed in the environment: ```text ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tblib' ```

signal.title: Streaming input: per-chunk arrival cost is O(cumulative prompt), making long multimodal sessions quadratic
signal.text: ## Summary With streaming input (#28973), the per-chunk **arrival cost grows with the cumulative prompt instead of the chunk**: in a live multimodal chat session, sending a constant-size delta (~300-600 tokens + 0-1 image) per turn costs ~150 ms *more* on every successive turn — ~130-600 ms on turns 1-6 rising to **1.4-3.5 s by turn 16** (three independent runs), i.e. O(everything) per arrival and O(n²) for a whole conversation. The same client protocol driving SGLang's session API stays flat (~410 ms at turn 16), so the growth is engine-side, not client- or workload-side. ## Setup - vLLM v0.25.1 (cu129 image), gemma-4-31B-it (multimodal), TP=4, `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 32}'`, mm processor cache **on** - A thin HTTP shim over `AsyncLLM.generate()` with an async generator of `StreamingInput` chunks (one long-lived anchor per session, per the blog's pattern; `max_tokens=1` throwaway chunks used where applicable) - Chunks are per-turn deltas of a chat conversation with interleaved images (voice-assistant workload; ~26 images resident by turn 16). Nothing is re-sent: engine counters confirm full KV reuse (~15k+ cached tokens/turn, only the delta computed) and no image re-delivery. ## What we ruled out Preprocessing (cache on — same slope as cache off), TP re-broadcast (patched per #52041 — same slope), prefill (KV counters show full reuse), decode (constant). The growth survives all of them, which leaves per-arrival CPU work in the front half (input processing / session update / scheduling). ## Root-cause hypothesis (with a receipt) At arrival, the update path merges the chunk into the anchor request (`prompt_token_ids = old + kept_output + new`, likewise the mm item list) and then runs existing whole-request machinery on the merged result. The old/new boundary — which *is* available at arrival time (`anchor` and `update` are separate arguments) — is discarded by the merge, so downstream processing (multimodal placeholder application, validation, array rebuilds) has no choice but to re-walk everything. Direct evidence that the mm walk is cumulative: sending a chunk containing a second image raises ``` InputStreamError: Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][1] ``` i.e. the placeholder machinery enumerates the request's full accumulated image list per arrival (index [1] on a 1-image chunk). ## Related defects hit on the same path (all reproducible on v0.25.1) 1. **Stop strings rejected** in streaming mode (`Input streaming not currently supported ... with stop strings`) — combined with the documented discard-last-sampled-token behavior, chat models that need their stop/turn tokens recomputed (the blog's own caveat) have no supported path. 2. **One bad session can kill the whole engine**: corrupted session state escalated to `RuntimeError: Invalid request status: RUNNING` in `scheduler.schedule` → `EngineDeadError` (reproduced twice). Per-request failure would be the expected blast radius. 3. **>1 image in a single chunk asserts** (the `mm_items['image'][1]` error above) — worked around by splitting to one image per chunk. 4. **`AssertionError: Expected a cached item for mm_hash=...`** when a client (buggy, in our case) re-sends an image with an identical hash into a session — a graceful reject would be preferable to an assert. ## Notes / in progress Our chunks used the text-prompt path (we saw the raw-prompt deprecation warning); a token-id-chunk comparison and a py-spy attribution of the exact hot function are in progress and will be appended. The blog's Future Directions already names "optimizing the anchor request pattern" and "expanding support for multi-modal streaming" — this issue is intended as first hard measurements of exactly those two gaps, from a production-shaped voice+vision workload. ## Ask Preserve the old/new boundary at arrival and process updates incrementally (offset-based placeholder mapping, append-only array updates) so arrival work is proportional to the chunk. Happy to contribute the fix if maintainers indicate the preferred design direction.
signal.author: sseanliu

signal.title: [Bugfix][AMD] Annotate draft KV cache groups on the hybrid grouping path
signal.text:
## Purpose Serving **Kimi-K3** (`KimiLinearForCausalLM` — 93 layers: 24 full-attention MLA + 69 KDA linear-attention) with the **DSpark MTP draft** (`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`) and a CPU KV offload tier, the external prefix cache never serves anything: `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` stays pinned at exactly 0 for the life of the server while `vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes_total` grows without bound. The offload tier writes continuously and reads back nothing. The same latent defect affects any hybrid (attention + Mamba) model with an EAGLE-family drafter that reaches the general multi-group KV-cache grouping path. ## Root cause `is_eagle_group` is set in exactly one place in the tree: `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`). It is gated on `model_version == "deepseek_v4"` and is reachable only from the `group_and_unify_kv_cache_specs` branch of `get_kv_cache_groups`. Kimi-K3 is MLA + Mamba, so it lands on the general multi-group path and **no group is annotated at all**. Consumers respond to "no group annotated" by flagging *every* group as a draft group — both `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` and the `OffloadingConnector` scheduler (`offloading/scheduler.py`, `eagle_groups = set(range(len(kv_cache_groups)))`). That fallback is documented as conservative, and it is — for full-attention groups. For a **Mamba** group it is not: 1. `get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks` returns `1` for a `MambaSpec` — "Mamba depends on a single state". 2. The eagle flag then applies `required_window += 1` → **2**. 3. `_sliding_window_lookup` reports a hit only on `consecutive_hits == sliding_window_size`, i.e. **two adjacent stored chunks**. 4. Under `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, exactly one state checkpoint is materialized per scheduler step; the chunks in between are null blocks (`block_id == 0`) and are skipped on store. 5. Two adjacent mamba chunks are therefore **never both stored**, so the group can never report a hit. 6. `_lookup` takes the minimum across groups, so `num_hit_chunks == 0` zeroes the whole request. ## What this means concretely for Kimi-K3 + DSpark The Mamba page forces a **1536-token block**, and the draft's 5 MLA layers are the smallest spec bucket, so `group_size` collapses to 5 — giving **20 KV cache groups: 5 target-MLA, 14 Mamba, 1 draft**. (Consistent with the two page-padding warnings every DSpark run logs: `4.17% = 1/24` and `1.45% = 1/69`.) At `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` a KDA checkpoint lands every **21 chunks = 32,256 tokens**. | | Groups flagged | Mamba group lookup | Result | |---|---|---|---| | **before** | 20 / 20 | needs 2 adjacent chunks at a 21-chunk stride | unsatisfiable → `get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns 0 for every prompt-shaped request | | **after** | 1 / 20 (the draft) | window stays 1, satisfied by a single checkpoint | lookup is no longer structurally zeroed; the 5 target-MLA groups also stop taking the eagle last-chunk drop | The failure is silent today. A vetoed lookup is not counted as a *query* either, so the hit **rate** stays empty rather than visibly dropping — there is no counter an operator can watch go wrong. Hence the second half of this patch. ## The fix Annotate **by spec rather than by model version**. `non_causal_multi_token_decode` is set exactly on drafter attention layers (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py`), is declared on `MLAAttentionSpec` as "Marks draft groups that flatten a non-causal query block into decode rows", and is propagated through `MLAAttentionSpec.merge` via `any(...)`. So it identifies the draft group wherever grouping happens to land. Two functions, both called at the end of the general multi-group path: - `_annotate_eagle_groups_from_draft_spec` — flags groups whose merged spec carries the marker. - `_warn_if_unannotated_eagle_mamba` — warns when speculative decoding is on, no group could be identified, and Mamba groups are present. That combination still takes the flag-all path and should not fail silently. ## Why this is not a duplicate | PR | What it does | Why it does not cover this | |---|---|---| | **#47891** — Exclude DSpark draft KV-cache group from OffloadingConnector lookup poisoning | Adds `eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` so an *identified* draft group's miss does not veto the request | The flag is only ever set inside `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4`. On an unannotated model the exempt set is empty and nothing changes. The PR says so explicitly: *"Left empty in the 'flag all groups' fallback below … we conservatively keep the original behavior."* Kimi-K3 is precisely that case. | | **#48459** — core-tier half of #47891 | Same mechanism on `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` | Same single DSV4-gated setter; same gap. | | **#48375** — Honor `drop_eagle_block` in `MambaManager` | Fixes silent recurrent-state corruption on the GPU tier | Different bug. Does not touch group annotation or the offload lookup window. | | **#41640** — Add `is_eagle` in `AttentionSpec` | Generic annotation infrastructure that would attack the same root | Open and untouched since May 2026. If it lands, this patch should be rebased onto it. | No open PR mentions `required_window` or `_sliding_window_lookup` at all. **This patch is the missing precondition for #47891/#48459 rather than a competitor.** It stops the flag-all fallback from firing; they stop the identified draft group from vetoing. They compose, and on a hybrid model neither is sufficient alone. ## Test plan E2E KK3 test Four tests added to `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: - `test_draft_group_annotated_on_hybrid_general_path` — on an MLA + Mamba + draft-MLA fixture, exactly one group is flagged, it is the draft's, and no Mamba group is flagged. - `test_draft_group_not_annotated_without_spec_decode` — the marker alone flags nothing. - `test_unidentifiable_draft_with_mamba_warns` — the warning fires when no draft can be identified. - `test_no_warning_when_draft_group_is_identified` — and stays quiet when one can. ## Test result Unit tests: ``` tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_mla_draft_prefers_standard_layout_when_pages_can_be_unified PASSED [ 16%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_draft_group_annotated_on_hybrid_general_path PASSED [ 33%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_mamba_groups_never_flagged_even_when_draft_shares_a_group PASSED [ 50%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_draft_group_not_annotated_without_spec_decode PASSED [ 66%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_unidentifiable_draft_with_mamba_warns PASSED [ 83%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_no_warning_when_draft_group_is_identified PASSED [100%] ``` E2E Kimik3: on E2E I've measured the following improvements with the PR Config: ISL 8192 / OSL 1024 / conc 16, 24 sessions, TP8, DSpark, 64 GiB offload pool, GPU KV capped to 163,840 tokens so the 221 k working set evicts. ## Accuracy / serving eval Kimi-K3 gsm8k accuracy with CPU offload + DSpark MTP ---

signal.title: [ROCm] Give EngineCore cleanup grace after request abort
signal.text: AMD CI exposed a shutdown race where `shutdown_timeout=0` aborted requests as intended but also gave EngineCore no time to release ROCm resources before SIGKILL. This change preserves immediate request abort while giving the ROCm EngineCore process manager a bounded 60-second cleanup grace when both the configured and remaining process timeouts are zero. It keeps exhausted budgets for positive shutdown timeouts unchanged and extends the DP supervisor's outer deadline to cover the cleanup window. - The motivating failure is [AMD CI build 12007](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12007/list?sid=019ffc53-a1ab-472f-8b77-7c52a7d6edc0&tab=output). - The final request completed successfully, but EngineCore was force-killed immediately and GPU memory remained at 11.72 GB for the full 120-second release wait. - The `LLM()` to `vllm_runner()` migration does not cover this path because these tests launch a real out-of-process `vllm serve` server. - Add a ROCm-only 60-second EngineCore process cleanup grace when both the configured request timeout and remaining process timeout are zero. - Keep `shutdown_timeout=0` inside EngineCore so in-flight requests are still aborted immediately. - Preserve exhausted positive shutdown deadlines instead of accidentally granting them a fresh cleanup window. - Extend the DP supervisor's outer wait budget so it does not kill the process tree before EngineCore cleanup can finish. - Add manager and DP supervisor regression coverage in the existing test files.
signal.author: AndreasKaratzas

signal.title: [CI] Harden RemoteVLLMServer GPU cleanup checks
signal.text: This PR is stacked on `akaratza_enginecore_shutdown` and hardens `RemoteVLLMServer` cleanup after a server exits. GPU baselines and cleanup waits are tracked per child-visible physical device, including overlapping multi-server scopes, so one leaked allocation cannot be hidden by a later aggregate baseline. Unavailable telemetry and timed-out cleanup now fail closed and retain affected-scope state until recovery can be verified. The test server's outer termination window also covers the EngineCore cleanup grace introduced by the first PR. - Prevent a teardown failure from ratcheting leaked VRAM into the next server's `_pre_server_gpu_memory` baseline. - Measure the physical devices selected by each child server's visibility environment on ROCm and CUDA. - Preserve parent-logical ordinal measurement on XPU, where `torch.xpu.mem_get_info` cannot consume physical or tile mask IDs. - Retain cleanup poison while intentionally concurrent servers make recovery unverifiable, and fail closed for unsafe partial coverage. - Merge partially overlapping scopes and use the earliest per-device baseline so a broader server cannot hide a leak behind an earlier sibling's allocation. - Keep GPU-less render-server tests outside GPU release accounting.
signal.author: AndreasKaratzas

signal.title: [Bugfix][CPU][RISC-V] Fix FP16 rounding and cross-compilation capability handling
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR fixes two RISC-V CPU correctness issues. First, the FP32-to-FP16 constructors used the implicit-rounding form of the `vfncvt.f.f.w` intrinsic. The generated narrowing operation therefore used the current dynamic floating-point rounding mode in `frm`, making its results dependent on the caller's floating-point environment. The [RISC-V V specification](https://docs.riscv.org/reference/isa/unpriv/v-st-ext) states: > All vector floating-point operations use the dynamic rounding mode in the > `frm` register. The [RISC-V Vector C Intrinsic specification](https://docs.riscv.org/reference/vector-c-intrinsics/rvv-intrinsic-spec.html) provides an explicit-rounding interface for controlling this state: > The floating-point intrinsics with the `frm` argument are followed by an > `_rm` suffix in the function name. It defines `__RISCV_FRM_RNE` as the explicit intrinsic argument for RNE. The [RISC-V F specification](https://docs.riscv.org/reference/isa/unpriv/f-st-ext.html) defines RNE (`000`) as “Round to Nearest, ties to Even.” This PR therefore uses the explicit `_rm` intrinsic with `__RISCV_FRM_RNE`. This makes the FP32-to-FP16 result independent of the incoming rounding mode while preserving the caller-visible value of `frm`. This is related to [#47983](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47983), which proposes explicit RNE for float-to-integer conversions. However, #47983 remains open at the time of writing, so there is not yet a clear maintainer decision that the related RISC-V conversion paths should uniformly use RNE. The justification for this change is narrower and specific to FP32-to-FP16 conversion. The existing x86 implementation in [`csrc/cpu/cpu_types_x86.hpp`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/csrc/cpu/cpu_types_x86.hpp) passes `_MM_FROUND_TO_NEAREST_INT` explicitly, while the generic scalar fallback uses `float_to_fp16()` from [`csrc/cpu/float_convert.hpp`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/csrc/cpu/float_convert.hpp), whose software conversion implements round-to-nearest-even. This PR aligns the RISC-V FP32-to-FP16 path with those existing implementations without assuming a broader project-wide rounding policy. Second, riscv64 cross-compilation used the build host's `/proc/cpuinfo` to infer target FP16/BF16 capabilities. The RISC-V V specification describes VLEN as a property defined by each vector-capable hart: > Each hart supporting a vector extension defines two parameters, including VLEN. The target VLEN and supported vector floating-point extensions therefore cannot be inferred from the build host's `/proc/cpuinfo` during cross-compilation. The CMake changes: * skip host capability detection only when cross-compiling for riscv64; * add `VLLM_CPU_RVV_FP16=1`, matching the existing BF16 override; * require an FP16 or BF16 capability to be detected or explicitly enabled when `VLLM_RVV_VLEN > 0`; * reject an explicit RVV capability override combined with scalar `VLLM_RVV_VLEN=0`. This is a follow-up to [#47532](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47532), which guards VLEN auto-detection but does not guard the earlier FP16/BF16 capability detection. The changes intentionally do not modify BF16 conversion semantics, other architectures' cross-compilation logic, or oneDNN sub-build ISA selection. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and drafting. The author manually reviewed every changed line and the validation results. ## Test Plan ### FP32-to-FP16 conversion Cross-compile an out-of-tree harness against vLLM's production RISC-V headers using Clang 18, at both `-O2` and `-O3 -DNDEBUG`: ```bash clang++ --target=riscv64-linux-gnu --gcc-toolchain=/usr \ -march=rv64gcv_zvfh_zvl128b -mrvv-vector-bits=zvl -mabi=lp64d \ -std=c++20 -O2 -I csrc/cpu \ -isystem "${TORCH_INCLUDE}" -isystem "${TORCH_API_INCLUDE}" \ test_vllm_fp16_path_fixed.cpp -o test_vllm_fp16_path ``` Run the binaries on riscv64 hardware under RNE, RTZ, RDN, and RUP, using both direct `frm` writes and `std::fesetround`. Compare `FP16Vec8` and `FP16Vec16` against an explicit-RNE RVV oracle and a scalar RNE oracle. ### Cross-compilation configuration Use a fresh build directory for each case. Set or unset `VLLM_CPU_RVV_FP16` and `VLLM_CPU_RVV_BF16` in the environment as required for each test case: ```bash cmake -S . -B "${BUILD_DIR}" -G Ninja \ -DVLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \ -DVLLM_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE="${PYTHON}" \ -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="${RISCV_TOOLCHAIN}" \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \ -DVLLM_RVV_VLEN="${VLEN}" ``` Omit `-DVLLM_RVV_VLEN` for the missing-VLEN case. Test scalar, missing-capability, FP16, BF16, missing-VLEN, and conflicting scalar/RVV inputs. Also run a native x86_64 configuration and inspect the generated `_C` commands in `compile_commands.json`. ## Test Result FP32-to-FP16 runtime results on riscv64 hardware: ```text -O2: 96 cases, 0 failures, PASS -O3 -DNDEBUG: 96 cases, 0 failures, PASS ``` The results matched RNE under all tested caller rounding modes, and the caller's `frm` was preserved. Disassembly showed explicit RNE setup, narrowing, and `frm` restoration in both constructor implementations. Cross-compilation configuration results: | Input | Result | | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | | `VLLM_RVV_VLEN=0` | Success; `_C` uses `-march=rv64gc` | | `VLLM_RVV_VLEN=128`, no capability override | Expected failure requesting the target capability | | `VLLM_RVV_VLEN=128`, `VLLM_CPU_RVV_FP16=1` | Success; `_C` uses `rv64gcv_zvfh_zvl128b` | | `VLLM_RVV_VLEN=128`, `VLLM_CPU_RVV_BF16=1` | Success; `_C` uses `rv64gcv_zvfh_zfbfmin_zvfbfmin_zvl128b` | | BF16 capability override without VLEN | Expected failure requesting an explicit VLEN | | `VLLM_RVV_VLEN=0` with FP16 capability override | Expected scalar/RVV conflict failure | | Native x86_64 | Success; existing AVX detection unchanged | ```text git diff --check: PASS ``` Not run: a complete vLLM cross-build, model evaluation, the full pre-commit suite, or VLEN=256 validation. The PR should remain a draft until the required model evaluation is added or maintainers confirm that the targeted numerical validation is sufficient. No user-facing documentation change is included. The new FP16 override is described by the CMake diagnostics and this PR, and no existing user-facing documentation was found for the sibling BF16 override. Maintainer guidance is welcome on whether both overrides should be added to the CPU build documentation. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> * [x] The purpose of the PR, including related upstream work. * [x] The test plan and commands. * [x] The test results and before/after behavior. * [x] Documentation impact was considered. </details>

signal.title: [compile] Remove layer_name from unified_kv_cache_update
signal.text: ## Summary Passing `layer_name` as a string constant to `unified_kv_cache_update` forced PyTorch Dynamo to generate constant guards for every attention layer, splitting the compiled FX graph into 65 separate submodules and causing severe cold-start compilation overhead (~100s). ## Changes - Remove `layer_name` string parameter from `unified_kv_cache_update` custom op signature. - Track `static_all_kv_layers` in `CompilationConfig` / `ForwardContext` to sequentially resolve attention layer contexts. - Add `hasattr(v, "kv_cache")` fallback filtering in `get_attention_context()` for hybrid models (e.g. `Qwen3.5-27B`). - Remove `unified_kv_cache_update` from `splitting_ops`. ## Performance Impact - Tested on `Qwen3.5-27B` (TP=4, 4x NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs). - Compilation Time: Reduced from **99.61s** to **87.56s** (⚡ **12.05s / 12.1% speedup**). - Graph Compilation (1, 8192): Reduced from **67.57s** to **62.22s**. - Zero runtime overhead; generate function verified at **17.91 toks/s**. Ref #33267
signal.author: bandham-manikanta

signal.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash think-until-cap / empty turn under concurrent DSpark + breakable CUDA graphs
signal.text: ## Summary On **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** with the official DSpark recipe, concurrent `/v1/chat/completions` requests (same greedy tool-calling turn) intermittently **never leave the reasoning channel**. Generation runs to `max_tokens` with: - `finish_reason: "length"` - empty `message.content` - **no** `tool_calls` - `reasoning_content` is a tight loop (never emits a think-end token), repeating e.g. `Wait, the user wants to upgrade XEHM4B to business, then cancel it.` This is a **real decode loop**, not only a parser mis-bucket. Healthy replies on the same prompt are short tool-calls (~181 tokens). Failed replies burn the full cap (`max_tokens=16384` in the numbers below). The high-rate failure needs **all three**: 1. **DSpark** speculative decoding 2. **Breakable CUDA graphs** (this nightly auto-enables `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`) 3. **In-flight concurrency ≥ 10** `--enforce-eager` does **not** reproduce. The same prompt at the same concurrency is **0/1024** on SGLang (DSPARK) and TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc23 / 1.3.0rc25 (DSpark). ## Environment | Item | Value | |------|--------| | Image | `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-acb0f1dcdb668d90bbbf50e57552d2f6f0987c87` | | Digest | `sha256:6b084be85c1806afcb69df24d853ebf240b9f0dfca3eaa2252d0096a46a12c58` | | Version | `0.27.2rc1.dev110+gacb0f1dcd` | | Hardware | 2× NVIDIA B200, TP=2 + expert parallel | | Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` | | HF snapshot | `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062` | | Startup log | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` auto-enabled; `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`; separate DSpark CUDA-graph capture | Hub image `ENTRYPOINT` is `["vllm","serve"]`. ## Serve command (repro / default recipe) Flags follow [recipes.vllm.ai DeepSeek-V4-Flash](https://recipes.vllm.ai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash), adapted to TP2. ```bash # SNAP = local HF snapshot of deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 # (7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062) docker run --gpus '"device=0,1"' --network=host --ipc=host --shm-size=32g \ -v "$HF_HOME:$HF_HOME" -e HF_HOME -e PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \ vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-acb0f1dcdb668d90bbbf50e57552d2f6f0987c87 \ "$SNAP" \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}' \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \ --max-model-len 70000 \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune ``` ## Payload + curl Multi-turn airline tool-calling conversation (tau2-style): system policy, prior `get_reservation_details` / `get_flight_status` / `get_user_details` results, last user turn: > Upgrade XEHM4B to business first, then cancel it. Use the card ending in 2135. Also, do I have any other upcoming flights? What’s the total cost of those? Full body: **17 messages, 14 tools**, `temperature: 0`. Gist: **https://gist.github.com/dsingal0/8973a0fb9166beb38e6aaf1fb1df20e9** ```bash # force the length-cap path curl -sS -L -o payload.json https://gist.githubusercontent.com/dsingal0/8973a0fb9166beb38e6aaf1fb1df20e9/raw/deepseek_v4_flash_airline_toolcall.json jq '.max_tokens=16384 | .temperature=0' payload.json > /tmp/req.json # single request curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary @/tmp/req.json | jq '{ finish: .choices[0].finish_reason, content: .choices[0].message.content, n_tools: (.choices[0].message.tool_calls|length), reasoning_len: (.choices[0].message.reasoning_content|length), completion: .usage.completion_tokens }' ``` **Hit** = `finish_reason=="length"` AND empty/whitespace `content` AND no `tool_calls`. **Healthy** = `finish_reason=="tool_calls"`, ~181 completion tokens. A hit’s `reasoning_content` never contains a think-end token; it loops the upgrade/cancel sentence until the cap. Concurrent repro (need **≥ 10** in flight; **32** is reliable). Fire N identical POSTs, then repeat sequential waves: ```bash # example: 8 sequential waves of 32 in-flight python3 - <<'PY' import json, time from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed from urllib.request import Request, urlopen url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions" payload = json.load(open("/tmp/req.json")) payload["max_tokens"] = 16384 payload["temperature"] = 0 def one(i): t0 = time.time() req = Request(url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST") body = json.loads(urlopen(req, timeout=7200).read()) ch = (body.get("choices") or [{}])[0] msg = ch.get("message") or {} content = (msg.get("content") or "").strip() tools = msg.get("tool_calls") or [] finish = ch.get("finish_reason") hit = finish == "length" and not content and not tools return {"i": i, "finish": finish, "hit": hit, "n_tools": len(tools), "sec": round(time.time() - t0, 2), "completion": (body.get("usage") or {}).get("completion_tokens")} for wave in range(8): with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=32) as ex: rows = [f.result() for f in as_completed(ex.submit(one, i) for i in range(32))] hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"]) print(f"wave {wave}: {hits}/32 hits") PY ``` ## Conditions required | Condition | Needed for high-rate repro? | |-----------|-----------------------------| | Greedy (`temperature=0`) | Yes (all numbers below) | | Tools + this multi-turn prompt | Yes | | `max_tokens` large enough (4096 often misses; **16384** used) | Yes | | In-flight concurrency **≥ 10** | Yes | | DSpark `num_speculative_tokens: 7`, greedy draft | Yes for ~30% rate | | Breakable CUDA graphs (default on this nightly) | Yes for ~30% rate | | Prefix caching | On in all runs (not ablated) | | `--enforce-eager` | **Suppresses** the bug | | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | **Almost suppresses** | Serial (`c=1`) after a polluted server: rare (1/16). Cold start + high concurrency: the first ~256 requests can be clean, then the rate climbs. ## Observed frequencies Same image, same weights, same payload, `max_tokens=16384`, `temperature=0`. **Default recipe (DSpark + breakable graphs), 64 in-flight, 1024 requests: 298 / 1024 (29.1%)** `finish`: 697 `tool_calls`, 309 `length`, 18 `stop`. All 298 hits used the full 16384 tokens. By 64-id bucket: first 256 requests **0%**, then 23% → **67%** on the last bucket. **Default recipe, sequential waves of 32 (already-warm server), 256 req: 103 / 256 (40%)** | Wave | Hits | Local slots that hit | |------|------|----------------------| | 0–3 | **6/32 each (18.75%)** | **always 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31** | | 4 | 11/32 | spreading downward | | 5–7 | 21–24/32 (66–75%) | high slots dominate | **Concurrency threshold** (3 waves each, polluted default server): | In-flight | Hits | Rate | |-----------|------|------| | 4 | 0/12 | 0% | | 7 | 0/21 | 0% | | 8 | 0/32 | 0% | | 9 | 0/27 | 0% | | **10** | **4/30** | **~13%** (first consistent hits) | | 12 | 9/36 | 25% | | 16 | 21/48 | 44% | | 24 | 49/72 | 68% | | 26 | 55/78 | 71% | | 28 | 61/84 | 73% | | 32 | 103/256 | 40% (escalating across waves) | **Ablations** (same prompt/cap; 8×32 waves = 256 unless noted): | Setup | Hits | Rate | |-------|------|------| | DSpark + breakable graphs (**default**) | 298/1024 | **29.1%** | | DSpark + `--enforce-eager` (`cudagraph_mode=NONE`) | **0/256** | **0%** | | DSpark + `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | 2/256 | 0.8% | | **No** `--speculative-config` (graphs still on) | 10/512 | 2.0% | | SGLang nightly + DSPARK, same payload, 64 in-flight | 0/1024 | 0% | | TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc25 + DSpark, same payload | 0/1024 | 0% | | TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc23 + DSpark, same payload | 0/1024 | 0% | DSpark without breakable graphs ≈ 0–2%; graphs without DSpark ≈ 2%; **both + c≥10 ≈ 30% and climbing**. The last-6-of-32 slot pattern on early waves is deterministic enough that this is unlikely to be sampling noise (`temperature=0`). ## Notes - `ParserEngine.adjust_initial_state_from_prompt` is a no-op in this build. Empty `content` here is because generation never leaves reasoning, not only a CONTENT↔REASONING flip. - Think-parser `initial_state` issues (e.g. #51296) can also empty `content` when think-end is missing; they do **not** explain the 16k self-loop or the CUDA-graph / batch-index dependence. - Workarounds that held here: `--enforce-eager`, or `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, or keep concurrency ≤ 9. Eager is the only config that was **0/256**. ## Expected The same greedy prompt should keep producing the ~181-token tool-call path at c=32, as SGLang and TensorRT-LLM do, and as vLLM does under `--enforce-eager`.

signal.title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Revert adaptive C128A metadata packing
signal.text: ## Summary Revert the adaptive C128A top-k width and packed persistent-buffer views introduced by #50004. The C128A metadata builder runs before FULL CUDA graph replay, but the sparse decode consumer is captured and reuses its capture-time row layout. With #50004, runtime metadata writes packed rows using a batch-dependent `active_topk_width`, while the captured consumer retained the capture-time row stride. Row 0 still started at offset 0, but later rows could be read from stale offsets. This change restores: - `c128a_max_compressed` as the metadata width - capacity-strided slices of the persistent decode and prefill buffers - each persistent buffer's `stride(0)` for Triton metadata writes - removal of the test that asserted the packed layout being reverted Fixes #52448. ## Validation ```text git diff --check .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py ``` All applicable hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, lazy-import, and forbidden-import checks. The full revert was also evaluated with the exact #52448 request on 2x NVIDIA GB300 using `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` revision `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062`, TP=2 plus expert parallelism, DSpark-7, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `max_model_len=70000`, concurrency 32, and `max_tokens=16384`: - 256 priming requests plus 256 measured requests - 0/256 issue-signature hits - 0 request errors and 0 `length` finishes - 253 `tool_calls` finishes and 3 `stop` finishes - 8.445 s median measured latency ## Contribution notes - Not a duplicate: `52448 in:body` found no other open PR. The open C128A/sparse-MLA keyword matches (#48805, #41836, and #41834) address warmup, prefill, or model enablement rather than reverting #50004. This updates the existing #51318 instead of opening another PR. - AI assistance was used for investigation, patch preparation, validation, and this PR update. The submitting human must review every changed line and be able to defend the change before merge.

signal.title: [V1 Scheduler] Fix Priority Queue Preemption Re-admission (#41951)
signal.text: Fixes #41951 ### Context & Root Cause Under `scheduling_policy="priority"`, `PriorityRequestQueue` delegates queue sorting to `Request.__lt__`. Currently, `Request.__lt__` compares `(priority, arrival_time)`, omitting `num_preemptions`. When a running request gets preempted and prepended back into `PriorityRequestQueue`, newly arrived requests with earlier timestamps pop ahead of the preempted request. This causes the preempted request to sit waiting while incoming requests overwrite its freed GPU KV cache blocks in VRAM, forcing a full prompt re-computation from scratch upon eventual re-admission. ### Solution 1. Update `Request.sort_key` and `Request.__lt__` in `vllm/v1/request.py` to include a bounded preemption re-admission boost `-min(self.num_preemptions, 3)`: ```python @property def sort_key(self) -> tuple[int, int, float, str, int]: return ( self.priority, -min(self.num_preemptions, 3), self.arrival_time, self.request_id, id(self), ) • In Python min-heaps, num_preemptions=1 evaluates to -1, popping preempted requests before fresh requests (0) to preserve their KV cache. • Capping the boost at 3 avoids queue starvation / livelock vulnerabilities for oversized prompts. 2. Align victim preemption selection in vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py (_select_victim_to_preempt) to match Request.sort_key. 3. Add unit tests in tests/v1/core/test_priority_preemption.py. ### Test Plan • pytest tests/v1/core/test_priority_preemption.py (2 passed) • pytest tests/v1/core/test_priority_scheduler_random.py (12 passed) • pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/request.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_priority_preemption.py (all passed)

signal.title: [Frontend] Add reusable TP1 initialized-engine snapshots
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 MD041 --> ## Purpose RFC #34303 and #37921/#37925 separate in-process CUDA checkpoint primitives from CRIU disk persistence. #35934 explores a CRIU-safe engine lifecycle. #42790, #46089, and #52132 use provider or runtime-sleep boundaries. #40323 tested a pre-model image containing Python imports and a CUDA context. My closed #48996 measured the earlier boundary at about 29.08 seconds ordinary versus 29.09 seconds restored, n=3 per arm. Engine construction still happened after restore. This PR captures a TP1 engine after initialization and a deterministic generation canary, but before HTTP bind. The same-host artifact serves operators who repeatedly activate the same stopped engine. They exchange local disk and host privilege for activation time. ```bash vllm snapshot create MODEL --snapshot-dir PATH --revision MODEL_SHA [serve args] vllm snapshot inspect PATH vllm snapshot restore PATH --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 ``` Restore validates artifact identity before CRIU, then restores the process tree and CUDA state. It binds HTTP only after the public API reproduces the captured token IDs, text, and sampled-token log probability. It fails closed and does not silently fall back to ordinary startup. ## Measured The largest matched campaign used source `5dd888926ffecb2409874810bd07402f3bc7dd3c`, Qwen3-32B BF16 TP1, and one H100 PCIe 80 GB. Model and generated-cache files were fully resident. Compact artifact files were fully evicted before each restore. Each arm ran three times through the first checked public token. | Path | Median activation | Samples | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Ordinary warm process | 54.7029 s | 3 | | Compact snapshot restore | 20.3795 s | 3 | | Reduction | 34.3234 s, 62.7% | 3 per arm | The compact artifact used 5,879,914,496 allocated bytes, about 5.88 GB. Creation took 78.5275 seconds, n=1. The model files remain external and totaled 65,540,298,478 bytes. Counting creation, the measured saving breaks even on the third activation. Every accepted trial returned token ID `12095` and text ` Paris`. Each completed six additional exact-token requests and left no matching process or GPU process. Restore logs contained no CUDA graph recapture markers after the captured boundary. The earlier matched full-state result used Qwen3-0.6B FP16 TP1 with warm local caches, n=5 per arm: | GPU | Ordinary warm process | Full-state restore | Reduction | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | NVIDIA A10 | 23.9121 s | 9.4234 s | 14.4888 s, 60.6% | | RTX 4090 Laptop GPU | 15.7790 s | 5.5488 s | 10.2302 s, 64.8% | On Qwen3-8B FP16 TP1 on the A10, compact state reduced allocated storage by 78.8 percent, from 24,231,231,488 to 5,144,281,088 bytes. Compact restore was 21.2396 seconds versus 23.7633 seconds for full-state restore, median n=3 per path. This cell uses a different model and starting state from the full-state benchmark, so the savings are not additive. Cold or slow model storage can reverse the compact latency result. ## The fix `vllm snapshot create` defaults to compact capture. The existing sleep level 2 lifecycle releases reloadable model and KV state. Creation restores that state, reruns the canary, then releases it again before capture. Restore reconstructs the released state before HTTP bind. `--include-model-state` keeps full state for local or mutable model sources and speculative decoding. It also supports deployments that prefer a larger artifact over model reload. The user contract includes: - strict manifest validation over the supported host, software, model, engine arguments, selected environment, process tree, sockets, and checkpoint tools, - private atomic artifact publication only after a complete dump, - exact token ID and text validation plus a bounded sampled-token log-probability comparison before readiness, - pidfd-pinned ownership for post-restore cleanup, with no signaling from an untrusted numeric PID, - fail-closed rejection of unsupported topology, external established TCP connections, active `io_uring`, mutable compact model sources, and incompatible runtime options, and - no concurrent initialized-snapshot or external CRIU link-remap workflow in the shared `/dev/shm` namespace. ## Review update This revision addresses the four maintainer review points: - The console entry point is `vllm.entrypoints.cli.main:main`. There is no top-level `vllm_bootstrap` package. - Top-level and snapshot-restore parsing happen before runtime imports. `vllm --help` and the useful core surface of `vllm serve --help` stay lightweight, while rich serve help uses the canonical parser. - Snapshot create and restore preserve the caller's complete `VLLM_*` mapping. Child-only defaults are passed through a copied subprocess environment. - The official Linux x86-64 runtime image builds pinned CRIU 4.2.1 and its matching CUDA plugin from source. It also builds a pinned Apache-2.0 helper from NVIDIA Dynamo against the public CUDA Driver checkpoint APIs. The install is gated to x86-64, and initialized snapshots remain unsupported on arm64. The obsolete `VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1` examples are removed because #51219 is merged. Compact capture is now the default, and `vllm snapshot restore` accepts only the artifact plus frontend bind arguments. The H20 report on the previous public head found three issues. CRIU dump and restore now use `--file-locks`. The documentation includes external package, library, and generated-cache files in the artifact-lifetime contract. GPU identity now comes from the actual CUDA-holder PIDs rather than `nvidia-smi --id=0`. ## Verified on exact current head The feature patch was rebased onto canonical main `925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749`. `git range-diff` reported all 56 feature commits unchanged. The resulting head is `da56fe43ea242bb59c2dd2e3aa64f5536a2a8943`. A fresh exact-head image passed a compact-default V2 acceptance cell on one RTX 4090 Laptop GPU, n=1. Creation took 31.1366 seconds and restore took 2.8608 seconds. The public API returned token ID `12095`, text ` Paris`, and sampled-token log probability `-0.42565488815307617`, exactly matching the captured scalar. The image also passed runtime CUDA allocation, CRIU 4.2.1, CUDA checkpoint helper/plugin, `nvcc`, and RDMA-header compile probes. Cleanup left zero containers and zero GPU processes. The H100 campaign observed two sampled-token log probabilities across separate ordinary engine initializations. Raw pre-capture fit gates produced both values before CRIU was involved, while every restore exactly reproduced its captured oracle. A free 4090 control across ordinary and sleep-enabled processes did not reproduce a snapshot-specific difference. The product therefore keeps the captured-engine restore-fidelity contract instead of treating unrelated cross-process numerical variability as a restore failure. ## Test plan Focused verification on the exact current head: ```bash pytest -q \ tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_launch_cli.py \ tests/cuda/test_cuda_compatibility_path.py ``` ```text 54 passed, 1 unchanged base warning ``` The branch adds 16 test functions and 22 collected feature cases, all folded into the existing CLI suite. There is no standalone snapshot test file. The retained cases cover the four maintainer requests, both lifecycle boundaries, the public canary, cleanup, PID ownership, and private paths. They also cover CRIU file locks, GPU identity, TCP preflight, and `io_uring` preflight. Ruff 0.14.0, scoped mypy, Docker dependency metadata generation, lazy-import checks, `git diff --check`, and all 56 DCO signoffs pass. The current head still needs its upstream CI run after this update. ## Product envelope and tradeoffs - Linux x86-64, one NVIDIA GPU, TP1, PP1, DP1, and prefill-context parallel size 1. - Same trusted host and GPU, with matching driver, kernel, runtime, engine arguments, selected environment, and checkpoint tools. - Compact capture requires an immutable remote model revision. Full-state capture supports local or mutable model sources by retaining model state. - Root or passwordless `sudo`, plus a compatible kernel and NVIDIA driver. - One plaintext HTTP frontend without built-in API authentication, TLS, custom middleware, or a Unix domain socket. - No external established TCP peer at capture and no active `io_uring` descriptors. - A private local artifact that can contain process memory, model state, and secrets. - Package files, shared libraries, model files, and generated-cache roots must remain available for the artifact lifetime. - No cross-host migration, GPU relocation, multi-GPU communicator restore, concurrent restore, or automatic ordinary-start fallback. This is adjacent to, but does not replace, in-process sleep and provider orchestration. The boundary stays narrow because that is where the correctness and hardware evidence stops. AI assistance was used. I reviewed the changes and can defend the implementation, constraints, and measurements.

signal.title: fix(pooling): validate BGE-M3 combined task ownership
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51801. BGE-M3 can resolve to the internal `embed&token_classify` task. That combined task belongs to the sparse IO-processor plugin, which also converts the combined model output into the public dense/sparse response. Registering a generic pass-through processor would avoid the original `KeyError`, but it would not perform that conversion. This revision keeps the combined task plugin-owned: - fail at startup with an actionable error when `embed&token_classify` is selected without an IO processor plugin; - register only the plugin processor when the plugin is available; - pin the documented sparse server to `token_classify` and require a restart with `token_embed` for ColBERT. This does not restore dynamic per-request task switching or change model weights, kernels, pooling math, or output values. I checked the issue Development section and searched open PRs for `#51801`, `embed&token_classify`, and BGE-M3 pooling processor changes. No overlapping PR was found; #44530 is about asymmetric ColBERT encoding and is unrelated. AI assistance was used for investigation, code drafting, test scaffolding, and review. I reviewed every changed line, reproduced the factory behavior, and understand the change well enough to maintain it. ## Test Plan - `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py -q --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/pooling` - `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ruff check vllm/entrypoints/pooling/factories.py vllm/entrypoints/pooling/pooling/io_processor.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py` - `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ruff format --check vllm/entrypoints/pooling/factories.py vllm/entrypoints/pooling/pooling/io_processor.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py` - `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m py_compile vllm/entrypoints/pooling/factories.py vllm/entrypoints/pooling/pooling/io_processor.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py` - `git diff --check` Model evaluation is not applicable because the revision changes factory validation and documentation only; it does not affect model execution or numerical outputs. ## Test Result - Focused factory regression: `2 passed` - Ruff check: passed - Ruff format check: passed - Python compile check: passed - Diff check: passed --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose and linked issue are described. - [x] The test plan includes the commands used. - [x] Test results are included. - [x] Documentation is updated for the fixed-task serving contract. </details>

signal.title: [ROCm][CI] Fix intermittent GPU memory fault during sleep-mode wake-up
signal.text: ROCm sleep-mode wake-up can intermittently abort the EngineCore on MI300 while remapping roughly 172 GiB, as seen in [build 12090](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12090/list?sid=01a004a6-9a94-48ba-8be1-20f23544b8e0&tab=output) and the earlier signature-matched [build 11862](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11862/list?sid=019fe4e5-8d10-4dca-8454-8c50409fefda&tab=output). Both failures occurred about 0.53 seconds into the first wake on different MI300 hosts, with the same GPU address-`nil` fault and `create_and_map -> wake_up` stack, while their MI355 jobs passed. PR #44972 added an allocator-wide ROCm `hipMemset` after VMM remapping to scrub stale VRAM on older amdgpu drivers and prevent discarded Mamba/GDN state from corrupting generation. That memset is the only device-wide access at the observed fault point and unnecessarily touches the full attention KV allocation, making it the high-confidence vLLM trigger even though the underlying defect may be a ROCm VMM race. A controlled restoration of the old leaf passed 40/40 local cycles, so this remains an intermittent mitigation rather than a deterministic native A/B reproduction. This change forward-ports the unmerged `0ab7e793` design by clearing only bound Mamba/GDN state after KV remapping and preserving packed cache offsets and strides. It preserves the functional motivation of #44972 but intentionally does not retain its broader allocator-wide scrubbing guarantee for discarded bytes on affected old drivers. Proposed changes: - Remove the ROCm whole-allocation `hipMemset` from `create_and_map`. - Rebuild packed Mamba cache views with their configured byte offset and per-block stride in both model runners. - Zero only bound Mamba/GDN conv and recurrent state views after a full or KV-tagged wake, without touching attention KV or weights-only wakes. - Deduplicate aliased state views so shared storage is cleared once. - Add assertion-level regression coverage that fails 4/4 on the pre-fix implementation and passes 4/4 with this change.

signal.title: [CI/Build] Hold StatelessProcessGroup test ports until bind
signal.text: ## Purpose Remove the probe-to-bind race from the same-node and node-count StatelessProcessGroup test harnesses.
