signal.title: [Core] Use FlashInfer workspace sizing helper
signal.text: ## Purpose Use FlashInfer's caller-owned workspace sizing helper when available so vLLM can reserve the workspace size required by FlashInfer attention planning instead of always reserving the default FlashInfer workspace size. This keeps the existing fallback path intact: if the helper is unavailable or cannot size a particular shape, vLLM still uses FlashInfer's default workspace allocation behavior. The workspace state shared by FlashInfer wrappers now keeps only weak references to wrappers, so profiling-time or temporary wrappers do not stay alive solely because the shared workspace state saw them once. This PR requires a FlashInfer build that includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3741 for the caller-owned workspace sizing helper. That FlashInfer change has been merged to FlashInfer main, but it is not part of the 0.6.13 release. Until the first FlashInfer release containing it is available and the vLLM pins are bumped to that version, this PR should be tested with a FlashInfer main checkout/build. AI assistance: Codex was used during implementation and PR preparation; the submitter reviewed the changes. ## Test Plan - Run syntax, lint, and format checks for the modified FlashInfer backend and CUDA graph profiling tests. - Run focused CUDA graph memory profiling tests with a FlashInfer checkout that provides the workspace sizing helper. - Let the repository commit hooks run for the cleanup commits, including ruff, format, mypy, SPDX, and repository policy checks. - After this branch is integrated with the serving branch, run Qwen3.6 long-context nvfp4 serving smoke to verify the workspace reserve path before CUDA graph lock. ## Test Result Syntax, lint, format, and whitespace checks: ```bash python -m py_compile \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_cudagraph_memory_profiling.py python -m ruff check \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_cudagraph_memory_profiling.py python -m ruff format --check \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_cudagraph_memory_profiling.py git diff --check ``` Result: passed. Dependency version checks: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m json.tool docker/versions.json git grep -n "0\.6\.12" -- requirements docker tools pyproject.toml git grep -n "flashinfer-python==0\.6\.13\|flashinfer-cubin==0\.6\.13\|FLASHINFER_VERSION=0\.6\.13\|v0\.6\.13" -- requirements docker tools pyproject.toml ``` Result: JSON validation passed and no FlashInfer 0.6.12 references remain in the checked requirement and Docker paths. The checked paths still pin FlashInfer 0.6.13; those pins need to move to the first FlashInfer release that includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3741 once it is published. Before that release, testing should use a FlashInfer main checkout/build. Focused CUDA graph profiling test: ```bash PYTHONPATH=<flashinfer checkout> FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_cudagraph_memory_profiling.py -q ``` Result before the latest reserve-path test additions: `5 passed`. signal.title: [Bugfix] Enforce deterministic cuDNN convolution under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
signal.text: ## Purpose `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` is meant to make model execution deterministic across batch sizes/shapes. `init_batch_invariance()` disables TF32 and forces IEEE rounding for matmul/conv/RNN via `fp32_precision = "ieee"`, but that setting only constrains numeric *precision* — it does not pin cuDNN/MIOpen's *algorithm selection* for convolution. cuDNN can still choose a nondeterministic reduction order for `conv2d`/`conv3d`, so any model with a convolution in its forward path (e.g. Qwen2.5-VL's conv3d patch-embed, diffusion VAE blocks) stayed non-deterministic under batch invariance despite the flag being set. This PR sets `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True` alongside the existing `fp32_precision` overrides in `init_batch_invariance()`, so convolution algorithm selection is pinned as well. The change is inside the existing `if envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT:` guard, so it has no effect on the default (non-batch-invariant) path, and no effect on models without a convolution in their forward pass. Fixes #52155. ## Test Plan - Added `tests/model_executor/layers/test_batch_invariant_conv_determinism.py`, a CPU-only unit test that calls `init_batch_invariance()` with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and asserts `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic` is set to `True`. - Manually exercised the same code path with a standalone repro script since I did not have GPU access to run the existing GPU-gated e2e determinism suite in `tests/v1/determinism/`. ```python import os os.environ["VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT"] = "1" import torch from vllm.model_executor.layers import batch_invariant as bi bi._batch_invariant_MODE = False bi.init_batch_invariance() assert torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic is True ``` - `ruff check` passes on both changed files. ## Test Result Before the fix, `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic` remained at its PyTorch default (`False`) after calling `init_batch_invariance()` with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. After the fix, it is `True`, matching the `fp32_precision = "ieee"` overrides already applied to matmul/conv/RNN. ```text cudnn.deterministic after init: True OK ``` **Note on AI assistance:** this PR description was drafted with Claude Code. I (the submitter) reviewed the description and reasoning above myself. I do not have GPU hardware available to run the existing GPU-gated batch-invariance e2e suite (`tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` and related), so that suite was not exercised for this change only the new CPU-only unit test and the manual repro above. Left as draft until that gap is closed or a maintainer/CI can cover it. - [x] The purpose of the PR: fixes #52155 (convolution not covered by `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`). - [x] The test plan: see above. - [x] The test results: see above. - [x] No documentation update needed — this is an internal determinism fix, not a new model/feature.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix divergent warp collectives in partial NeoX QK-Norm+RoPE
signal.text: ## Summary ## Author: Drew Jin, SJTU & Qwen Team, <drewjin0827@sjtu.edu.cn> Solving Issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51049 This PR fixes silent Q/K corruption in the partial-NeoX path of `fused_qk_norm_rope`. When `rotary_dim < head_dim`, the multi-head-per-warp kernel produces incorrect Q/K values for every head after the first in each warp chunk. On H200, `token_heads_per_warp=8` can additionally produce NaNs. Verified against `upstream/main` at commit `005fa017566177e1a66d75eba7908d326c5acd60`. ## Root cause In the NeoX branch, only the rotary lanes entered the RoPE section, while the branch invoked warp collectives using the full-warp mask: ```cpp if (laneId < rotary_lanes) { __syncwarp(); rotated = __shfl_xor_sync(FINAL_MASK, value, pairOffset); __syncwarp(); } ``` For partial RoPE, `rotary_lanes < warpSize`. Therefore, `FINAL_MASK` names lanes that do not execute the collective, which is undefined behavior. `warpReduceSum` itself is not the issue. In the packed kernel, the invalid RoPE collective occurs before the next head’s RMSNorm reduction, causing the observed corruption in subsequent heads. The single-head kernel contains the same latent UB, but it has no following packed-head iteration that exposes the failure. ## Fix The NeoX shuffle is now executed by every lane named by `FINAL_MASK`. Only rotary lanes consume the shuffled value, access the cos/sin cache, and update the rotated elements. The fix is applied to both the single-head and multi-head-per-warp kernels. The implementation retains the platform-specific `FINAL_MASK` rather than constructing a narrowed 32-bit mask. This preserves the existing CUDA and ROCm wave64 mask semantics and avoids undefined expressions such as `1u << 32`. ## Tests Added regression coverage for the previously untested packing paths: - Force `token_heads_per_warp` to `1`, `2`, `4`, and `8`, and compare each variant directly against the existing unfused PyTorch reference. - Cover `head_dim ∈ {64, 128, 256}`, `rotary_ratio ∈ {1.0, 0.5, 0.25}`, NeoX and interleaved layouts, and fp16/bf16. - Verify that the V segment remains bitwise unchanged. - Verify that packed and auto-selected outputs are bitwise identical to the single-head implementation. - Exercise the SM90 auto-selected pack4 and pack8 paths with large-token inputs. Verified on NVIDIA H200 (SM90). `compute-sanitizer` racecheck and synccheck are clean. Because these tools do not report this divergent-mask UB, the regression is enforced by numerical tests. ## Impact The QK-Norm+RoPE Inductor fusion is currently opt-in and disabled by default, so this issue does not affect default vLLM inference. The observed packed-head corruption requires all of the following: 1. per-head Q/K RMSNorm routed through this fused operator; 2. NeoX-style RoPE; 3. partial RoPE (`rotary_dim < head_dim`); and 4. dispatch to the multi-head-per-warp kernel. On SM90 with `head_dim <= 128`, the dispatcher at the target commit uses: ```text U = num_tokens × (num_q_local + num_kv_local) U < 10240 → token_heads_per_warp = 1 10240 ≤ U < 40960 → token_heads_per_warp = 4 U ≥ 40960 → token_heads_per_warp = 8 ``` Large prefills can therefore enter the affected packed paths. Confirmed partial-NeoX configurations include GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7, Ring-1T, and the partial-RoPE attention layers in Step-3.5-Flash and Laguna-XS.2. Full RoPE, interleaved RoPE, and models not routed through this fused operator do not trigger this issue. ## Performance The fix also removes the slowdown observed in the affected packed path. Benchmark configuration: ```text GPU: NVIDIA H200 (SM90) PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA: 13.0 dtype: bf16 head_dim: 128 Q heads: 16 KV heads: 4 Timing: CUDA events Warmup iterations: 30 Measured iterations: 300 Statistic: latency per call ``` | Tokens | Pre-fix auto | Post-fix auto | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2,048 | 22.5 µs | 15.9 µs | 29% | | 8,192 | 68.5 µs | 43.9 µs | 36% | | 16,384 | 125.6 µs | 80.1 µs | 36% | The single-head path is essentially unchanged. ## ROCm ROCm was not tested. The patch preserves the existing platform-specific `FINAL_MASK` and wave64-compatible code path; it does not introduce a CUDA-specific 32-bit active mask. ## AI assistance This PR was developed with AI assistance. I reviewed all changed lines, validated the behavior on H200, and understand the implementation and test coverage.

signal.title: [Model] Register model capabilities directly
signal.text: ## Purpose #7168 moved model inspection into a subprocess so model imports and CUDA initialization stay out of the parent. #9208 changed its result transport, #9233 consolidated capability checks into one child per implementation, #23558 cached the result, and #46567 fixed package-submodule invalidation. #51746 added an explicit cache-preparation command. Simon closed it because he was concerned users would not pre-bake and re-check entries, then asked for a first-principles study of the subprocess inspection path. This PR lets a lazy registration carry a typed `ModelInfo` declaration. Built-in declarations return before source lookup, cache access, model import, or child launch. Registrations that omit metadata keep the existing cache-backed subprocess path, so existing two-argument plugins are unchanged. This is not a duplicate of #51746. It removes the preparation command from the product shape: 320 built-in implementations declare class-derived metadata directly, while five dependency-sensitive implementations retain runtime inspection. The catalog is keyed by `(module, class)`, validates exact registry coverage at import, and shares 55 sparse profiles instead of repeating 22 fields per implementation. The optional public plugin declaration and its limits are documented. The fallback cache now validates its schema, vLLM version, model module hash, and extractor hash. Source lookup uses `PathFinder` without importing package parents. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_registry.py \ --deselect='tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[HCXVisionForCausalLM]' \ --deselect='tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[KananaVForConditionalGeneration]' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/models/test_registry.py::test_model_info_declaration_contract \ tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_inspects_builtin_without_import_or_cuda \ tests/models/test_registry.py::test_lazy_model_info_fallback_is_typed \ tests/models/test_registry.py::test_lazy_model_info_source_lookup_does_not_import_parent ``` Run Ruff format and lint checks, scoped mypy, the import-light probe, and `git diff --check` on the changed files. ## Test Result - The supported local registry suite passed: 365 passed, 18 skipped, and 2 deselected. The unfiltered file has two environment-only failures because this local environment lacks optional `timm` for `HCXVisionForCausalLM` and `KananaVForConditionalGeneration`. - A Linux CUDA acceptance run on one NVIDIA RTX 4090 Laptop GPU (driver 595.71.05, Torch 2.13.0+cu132, CUDA runtime 13.2) compared every direct declaration once with fresh legacy subprocess inspection, n=1 per implementation. All 320 implementations matched across all 22 fields and runtime types, with zero mismatches, and parent CUDA remained uninitialized. The five dynamic implementations stayed on the fallback path. - A sequential n=5-per-arm mechanism screen with a fresh empty ModelInfo cache for each process measured median Qwen inspection at 4.6166 seconds through the legacy path and 5.154 microseconds through the direct path. This is isolated lookup time, not end-to-end serving latency or a causal performance comparison. - This branch collects 385 registry cases versus 392 on upstream main. It adds one test function and no new test file. - Ruff, scoped mypy, the import-light probe, and `git diff --check` passed. All nine commits carry DCO signoffs. H200 and MI300 registry CI remain the cross-platform acceptance gate. This PR changes metadata discovery, not model implementations, sampling, or output semantics, so no model evaluation result is expected to change. AI assistance was used. signal.title: [Bugfix] Release ParentRequest state when an n>1 request is aborted
signal.text: ## What is broken `OutputProcessor.abort_requests` never drops the `ParentRequest` when an `n>1` request is aborted by its external id. An external id maps to the child internal ids, so the abort loop finds a `RequestState` for every child and takes the `if req_state is not None:` branch. That branch pops the child from `self.request_states` but never touches `self.parent_requests`. The parent cleanup lives in the `elif parent := self.parent_requests.get(request_id)` branch, which only runs when `req_state` is `None`, so it never fires here. `_finish_request` cannot clean up either, since the child states are already gone. The result is one `ParentRequest` left in `self.parent_requests` for the life of the engine, holding its `child_requests` set and its output aggregator. This needs `n>1` plus an abort or a client disconnect. Normal completion and `n=1` aborts are unaffected, so it is a slow leak on servers that see parallel sampling with cancellations, not a leak on every request. ## Fix In the `if req_state is not None:` branch, resolve the parent from the child's own `req_state.parent_req`, discard the child, and pop the parent once its last child is gone. This mirrors what `_finish_request` already does. The existing `elif` branch is unchanged. ## Test Added `test_abort_parallel_sampling_request` in `tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py`. It builds an `n=3` request with a `ParentRequest` and three children, aborts by internal ids and by external id, and asserts `parent_requests`, `request_states` and `external_req_ids` are all empty afterwards. I could not run the test file on my machine: importing the test harness pulls in `vllm.v1.engine.llm_engine` and the process dies with SIGBUS on macOS/CPU before collection. I verified the fix with a standalone script driving `OutputProcessor` directly with the same setup as the test. It fails on main with `{'request-0': <ParentRequest>}` still in `parent_requests` and passes with this change, for both the internal-id and external-id abort paths. CI should be the judge of the pytest run.

signal.title: [K3] support recoverssm for K3
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose This PR adds RecoverSSM, a Kimi-K3-specific state recovery path for speculative KDA decoding on NVIDIA Model Runner V2. It is enabled through `--use-replayssm`, is intended for Kimi-K3 serving with DSpark, and supports `mamba_cache_mode=align` prefix caching. Without RecoverSSM, KDA speculative decoding materializes a full recurrent state for every speculative position. RecoverSSM keeps one checkpoint and compact per-token records, then reconstructs the state at the accepted position after every verify. Under the tested TP8 Kimi-K3 configuration, this increases the effective cache capacity by 10.97% at the same 46.48 GiB cache-memory budget. ## Design ### Kimi-K3-specific MRV2 integration The implementation is contained in the Kimi-K3 KDA metadata, layer, and RecoverSSM operator paths. The metadata builder gives speculative rows one KDA checkpoint slot and creates a model-specific post-sampling committer. RecoverSSM is selected through the existing `--use-replayssm` option. The regular KDA prefill and non-speculative decode paths are unchanged. ### Verify records FP32 corrections KDA verify reads the checkpoint without modifying it and computes the normal speculative outputs. For each speculative token it records: - the correction vector `u` in FP32; - the key and raw gate in the activation dtype. Recording `u` removes `v` and `beta` from the commit path and avoids recomputing the state-dependent correction. FP32 is used for `u` to preserve reconstruction accuracy; keys and gates remain BF16 in the evaluated configuration. ### Direct accepted-position reconstruction After verification determines the accepted length, one Triton kernel reconstructs the required checkpoint directly. For the KDA recurrence: ```text S_t = S_{t-1} * exp(g_t) + u_t outer k_t ``` The accepted state is: ```text S_p = S_0 * exp(sum(g_1 ... g_p)) + sum_j u_j outer (k_j * exp(sum(g_{j+1} ... g_p))) ``` The commit kernel evaluates this expression in reverse token order. It loads the original state once and does not recursively update or write intermediate states. The loop bound is the runtime accepted length rather than the complete eight-token DSpark activation window. In align mode, the same launch also reconstructs the next prefix-cache boundary when the accepted range crosses it. Convolution history is compacted to the accepted position and to the boundary using the same commit plan. ### Cache layout Each KDA page contains: ```text (convolution state, KDA checkpoint, FP32 correction records, key/gate records) ``` Recovery records are transient and are not included in prefix-cache state copies. The checkpoint and convolution state remain the prefix-cache boundary state. ## Scope - NVIDIA Kimi-K3 KDA - Model Runner V2 - speculative decoding, validated with Kimi-K3-DSpark and seven draft tokens - `mamba_cache_mode=align` prefix caching Shared changes are limited to the derived KDA RecoverSSM flag, state-layout helpers, and the post-sampling commit lifecycle. The recovery algorithm and cache layout remain Kimi-K3-specific, and this PR does not add Mamba2 support. ## Test Plan and Results ### Unit tests ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py -v ``` Result: `69 passed`. The 18 RecoverSSM cases cover: - the actual eight-token DSpark window; - partial and full acceptance lengths; - direct final-state and align-boundary reconstruction; - both convolution-state layouts; - request-index remapping; - gates with and without a lower bound; - cache shape and dtype derivation. ```bash .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_utils.py vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py ``` Result: all hooks passed. ```bash .venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual ``` Result: passed for Python 3.12. ### End-to-end accuracy Controlled setup: - Kimi-K3 target and Kimi-K3-DSpark draft model, TP8 on two GB300 nodes; - seven greedy draft tokens and block rejection sampling; - align-mode Mamba cache, prefix caching, FP8 MLA cache, FlashInfer MLA, and fastsafetensors; - identical datasets, prompts, scorers, and serving parameters for RecoverSSM ON and OFF. | GSM8K, 1,319 samples | RecoverSSM ON | OFF | ON - OFF | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Flexible extract | 96.3609% | 96.1334% | +0.2274 pp | | Strict match | 96.0576% | 95.9060% | +0.1516 pp | The paired 95% confidence intervals were `[-0.4549, +0.9098]` pp for flexible extract and `[-0.6065, +0.9098]` pp for strict match. Both runs completed all 1,319 requests with zero request errors. Independently initialized greedy serving runs are not bitwise deterministic, so the paired score comparison is used instead of exact generated-text equality. | MRCR, 40 long prompts run cold and warm | RecoverSSM ON | OFF | |---|---:|---:| | Cold score | 0.74879 | 0.66791 | | Warm score | 0.74879 | 0.66791 | | Cold/warm exact-output consistency | 100% | 97.5% | | Warm prefix-cache token hit rate | 89.13% | 90.50% | The MRCR prompts ranged from 16,757 to 33,772 tokens and contained 991,216 prompt tokens per pass. RecoverSSM completed both passes without request errors. Total DSpark acceptance was 53.3514% with RecoverSSM and 53.4062% without it, a difference of -0.0548 percentage points. GSM8K-only acceptance was 50.0899% with RecoverSSM and 50.0336% without it. ### Memory capacity Both variants used a fixed 46.48 GiB cache-memory budget. | Metric | RecoverSSM ON | OFF | Difference | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Effective cache capacity | 2,856,170 tokens | 2,573,777 tokens | +10.97% | | Max 262k-request concurrency | 10.895x | 9.818x | +10.97% | ### Nsight Systems profile The profile used batch 32, 128 forced output tokens, and 80 captured decode steps per GPU on the same two-node TP8 setup. The aggregate results below include eight initial small-batch steps. | KDA work per decode step | Initial recurrent recovery | RecoverSSM | |---|---:|---:| | Verify | 3.115 ms | 3.540 ms | | Commit | 4.793 ms | 1.464 ms | | Commit auxiliaries | 0.081 ms | 0.081 ms | | Total | 7.989 ms | 5.085 ms | The direct reconstruction makes the commit kernel 3.27x faster and reduces total RecoverSSM KDA time by 36.34%. The FP32 correction write increases verify time by 13.66%, but commit time falls by 69.45%. Native KDA without recovery took 2.772 ms per step in the corresponding OFF trace. The 72 steady batch-32 steps each verified 256 tokens. Their CUDA-graph model-forward GPU wall time was 65.208 ms with RecoverSSM and 64.873 ms without it, a 0.335 ms or 0.52% difference. Kernel residence exceeds wall time because kernels on concurrent streams overlap. | RecoverSSM ON steady forward kernel residence | Time per step | Share | |---|---:|---:| | DeepGEMM and nvJet GEMM | 38.760 ms | 56.5% | | MoE routing and packing | 8.121 ms | 11.8% | | SiTU activation | 7.682 ms | 11.2% | | TP collectives | 6.136 ms | 8.9% | | RecoverSSM verify | 3.791 ms | 5.5% | | KDA convolution and normalization | 0.938 ms | 1.4% | | MLA attention kernels | 0.519 ms | 0.8% | | Other kernels | 2.658 ms | 3.9% | | Total kernel residence | 68.603 ms | 100% | RecoverSSM verify runs inside model forward and replaces the native KDA recurrent kernel. Its steady kernel residence was 3.791 ms versus 3.009 ms for native KDA, an increase of 0.782 ms. The smaller 0.335 ms forward wall-time difference reflects kernel overlap and run-to-run variation. Commit runs after sampling determines the accepted length, so it is not part of model forward. Across the 72 steady batch-32 steps it took 1.711 ms per step and varied with the accepted length. | Post-sampling RecoverSSM commit | Time per step | Share | |---|---:|---:| | FP32 correction state reconstruction | 1.618 ms | 94.5% | | Convolution-state compaction | 0.081 ms | 4.7% | | Commit-plan preparation | 0.0069 ms | 0.4% | | Align bookkeeping | 0.0061 ms | 0.4% | | Total | 1.711 ms | 100% | Adding the steady model-forward difference and post-sampling commit gives an estimated RecoverSSM GPU critical-path cost of 2.046 ms per batch-32 decode step, before common sampling and postprocessing work. ## Duplicate-work check The following searches were run against open vLLM PRs: ```bash gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "ReplaySSM Kimi K3" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA speculative decoding" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "ReplaySSM in:title,body" ``` No other open PR implements this Kimi-K3 KDA RecoverSSM integration. Related work is materially different: - #49847 targets Mamba2; - #49887 targets Gated DeltaNet; - #50140 is a WIP FlashInfer ReplaySSM kernel; - #42792 adds generic Mamba align-prefix speculative support rather than Kimi-K3 KDA RecoverSSM. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, profiling analysis, model evaluation analysis, and this PR description. The submitting human must review every changed line, reproduce the relevant tests, and understand and defend the design end-to-end. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR. - [x] The test plan and exact commands. - [x] Unit, end-to-end accuracy, memory, acceptance, and performance results. - [x] Duplicate-work check and AI-assistance disclosure. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>**

signal.title: [Bug]: 0.27.1 crashes in custom_all_reduce (illegal memory access) during CUDA graph capture on Hopper TP=4; identical config works on 0.26.0
signal.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ```text vLLM (failing) : 0.27.1+cu129 vLLM (working) : 0.26.0+cu129 PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu129 (0.26.0 env: 2.11.0+cu129) CUDA (torch built): 12.9 Python : 3.10.12 OS : Linux-5.15.0-94-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 GPU : NVIDIA H800, compute capability 9.0 (Hopper / SM90) Driver : 575.57.08 Parallelism : TP=4, single node, no PP, no DP, no EP Model : deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (FP8 checkpoint) KV cache dtype : fp8 ``` The two vLLM versions are installed in **separate virtualenvs** on the same host, so the comparison below changes exactly one variable: the vLLM version. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug A TP=4 configuration that has been serving reliably on **0.26.0** for weeks fails to start on **0.27.1**. The engine dies during CUDA graph capture with an illegal memory access originating in the custom all-reduce kernel: ``` Failed: Cuda error /workspace/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:164 'an illegal memory access was encountered' torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` Immediately before the crash, 0.27.1 logs: ``` Auto-enabling VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1. Set VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 to opt out. VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH is set, disabling vLLM's torch.compile pipeline. Equivalent to -cc.mode=none. ``` followed by `Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 0%| | 0/51` and then the fault on all four ranks. #### Reproduction The command line is **copied verbatim** from the working 0.26.0 systemd unit — same model, same `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, same `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, same `--gpu-memory-utilization`, same environment variables. Only the interpreter (virtualenv) differs: ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8012 ``` - On **0.26.0**: starts normally, serves traffic. - On **0.27.1**: crashes as above, reproducibly, every attempt. #### What I ruled out I ran this twice with different configurations to isolate the cause: | Run | Config | Result | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0.27.1 **with** `--speculative-config` (DSpark), `gpu-mem-util 0.88`, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}'`, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` | illegal memory access | | 2 | 0.27.1 **without** speculative decoding, no `expandable_segments`, parameters byte-for-byte identical to the working 0.26.0 unit | **same crash**, `custom_all_reduce.cuh:164` | So the failure is **not** caused by speculative decoding, not by the lowered memory utilization, and not by `expandable_segments` — run 2 has none of them and still crashes. The only remaining variable is the vLLM version itself. #### Possibly relevant `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh` was heavily refactored between the two releases — `git diff v0.26.0..v0.27.1` shows **+20 / −296** for that file, with the implementation moved into a new `custom_collective_common.cuh`. Given the crash site, that refactor seems like a plausible place to look. #### Not a duplicate of I checked the closest-looking existing reports; none match this configuration: - **#51758** — same headline symptom ("upgrade 0.26.0 → 0.27.0, DeepSeek V4 Flash error"), but that environment is **RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) + CUDA 13.0**, and the comments trace it to a DeepGEMM scale-factor layout regression missing the `arch_major == 12` branch. This report is **Hopper SM90 / cu129**, and the fault is in the all-reduce kernel, not DeepGEMM. - **#46253** — illegal memory access under `breakable_cudagraph`, but that is a **cross-node** GB10 setup where NCCL falls back to a host-staged transport without GPUDirect. This is a **single-node** TP=4 case. - **#45604** — same file, 4 GPUs, but the reported fault is `invalid argument` in the FlashInfer AllReduce **norm fusion** path with MXFP8. - **#42609** — `custom_all_reduce` IPC handles vs `expandable_segments`, requires DP>1 **and** TP>1; here DP=1, and run 2 does not set `expandable_segments` at all. #### Happy to help I have both versions installed side by side on the same host and can run additional diagnostics (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, compute-sanitizer) if that would help narrow it down — just say which would be most useful. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lengthy documentation-related questions.

signal.title: [Bug] XPU qnorm/rope kernel: overlapping stores in one program corrupt the KV cache nondeterministically
signal.text: **File:** `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_qnorm_rope_kv_fp8_insert.py` **Confirmed present in v0.27.1** (tag `6e448d0ea9bf`) and on `main`. ## Summary In the KV branch, the kernel stores all 512 elements of `kv` — RoPE region included, still unrotated — and then overwrites that region with the rotated values at stride-2 addresses: ```python # lines 93-94 kv_full = tl.load(kv_base + offs) tl.store(kv_out_base + offs, kv_full) # writes the unrotated rope region ... # lines 106-107 tl.store(kv_out_base + even_offs, new_even) # overwrites it, stride-2 addresses tl.store(kv_out_base + odd_offs, new_odd) ``` Two stores to the same addresses within one program, with different lane-to-address mappings and no ordering between them. Nothing guarantees the rotated store wins. ## Evidence On MTT S5000 (MUSA), 4096 tokens × 64 heads, compared against FlagGems' fused kernel, which is byte-exact against the pure-torch reference on the same inputs: - **30 tokens** of 4096 have a cache RoPE region that differs - **29 of those 30** hold values exactly equal to the **unrotated** `kv` — i.e. the bulk store landed last - the remaining one is partially overwritten, consistent with a lane-granular race - a **second run on identical inputs gives 29, not 30** — nondeterministic Concretely, token 96: the cache holds `[1.023, 0.262, -1.516, -0.277]`, exactly the raw `kv` values, where the correct rotated values are `[-0.441, 0.961, 1.531, -0.132]`. ## Fix One line, and it is also cheaper — mask the bulk copy so the overlap never exists: ```python tl.store(kv_out_base + offs, kv_full, mask=offs < NOPE_DIM) ``` This skips 64 redundant stores per KV token as well. With it applied, output is byte-identical to the reference. ## Note XPU scheduling may simply never expose this, but the ordering assumption does not hold on any backend. We found it because MUSA schedules differently.

signal.title: [Bugfix][CPU] Enable C++ causal_conv1d GDN path and float32 SSM cache on non-AMX AVX-512BF16 CPUs
signal.text: ## Purpose CPU GDN attention (Qwen3.5) selects its causal-conv1d implementation via `torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()`: AMX CPUs (Intel GNR) use the C++ kernels (`causal_conv1d_fwd_cpu` / `causal_conv1d_update_cpu`), everything else falls back to `causal_conv1d_fn_cpu` / `causal_conv1d_update_torch`, a pure-PyTorch per-sequence loop. The C++ conv kernels (`csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/conv.cpp`) do not use AMX tiles but `is_amx` gate blocks it from running on non-AMX platforms that support AVX-512BF16. The float32 SSM state(currently gated by `is_amx` is required for entire CPU GDN path, not just AMX This PR fixes this gating logic. ## Test plan Extended `tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py` (all gated on `_is_avx512_bf16_supported()`, so they run on non-AMX CPUs too). Expected Result: 105 passed, 0 skipped on both Intel GNR and AMD Turin. ```bash python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py -v ``` Qwen-3.5 workload run before and after the patch on both Intel GNR and AMD EPYC Turin ``` VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-63 VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=40 vllm bench throughput \ --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \ --trust-remote-code \ --dataset-name random \ --input-len 1024 \ --output-len 1024 \ --num-prompts 128 \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --dtype bfloat16 ``` Lmeval ``` VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-63 \ VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=40 \ lm_eval \ --model vllm \ --model_args "pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B,dtype=bfloat16,trust_remote_code=True,max_model_len=4096" \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --batch_size auto ``` ## Test result Python GDN test Result: 105 passed, 0 skipped on both Intel GNR and AMD Turin. Workload Qwen3.5-9B, BF16, ISL/OSL 1024/1024, 64-core instance (median of 3 runs) Intel GNR is unchanged (it takes the identical path both ways, so no regression). AMD EPYC Turin gains about 9-10% on this memory-bound, decode-heavy shape, which is the hardest case for a conv speedup to show up. ## Correctness `lm_eval` gsm8k, 5-shot, full set (n=1319), Qwen3.5-9B BF16, before vs after: | Platform | Metric | Baseline | After | |----------|--------|---------:|------:| | Intel GNR (AMX) | exact_match | identical | identical | | AMD Turin (Zen5) | flexible-extract | 0.8696 +/- 0.0093 | 0.8749 +/- 0.0091 | | AMD Turin (Zen5) | strict-match | 0.8734 +/- 0.0092 | 0.8779 +/- 0.0090 | GNR is bit-identical (same code path both ways). On Turin, before/after differ by less than one standard error, so there is no accuracy regression. The C++ conv accumulates in fp32 and is numerically no less accurate than the torch fallback(both round to bf16 at store), which the unit tests also assert against an fp32 oracle. ## Duplicate Check Searched open PRs/issues for GDN / causal_conv1d / Zen / AVX-512BF16 CPU conv work; found none addressing the non-AMX conv fallback. This PR Fixes #49640

signal.title: [bot] Enable google/gemma-4-E4B-it-assistant inference on Intel XPU
signal.text: ## Motivation `google/gemma-4-E4B-it-assistant` uses heterogeneous attention head dimensions (head_dim=256 for sliding window layers, head_dim=512 for global layers). This causes `AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError` with transformers >=5.15 and requires per-layer attention backend routing on XPU since Flash Attention only supports head_size<=256. ## Technical Details 1. **Handle per-layer config for heterogeneous head_dim**: Catch `AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError` in config loading and fall back to per-layer attribute access for `head_dim` 2. **Per-layer attention backend routing on XPU**: Route Flash Attention for layers with head_size<=256 (sliding), Triton attention for layers with head_size>256 (global) 3. **Skip global Triton forcing on XPU**: Since per-layer routing handles backend selection, avoid forcing all layers to Triton 4. **Fix hf_config identity check**: Use `==` instead of `is` for multimodal config detection 5. **Use per_layer_config in Gemma4DecoderLayer**: Read head_dim from per-layer config when available ## Files Changed - `vllm/config/model.py` — Fix identity check (`is` → `==`) - `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py` — Handle AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError - `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py` — Per-layer head_dim in decoder layer - `vllm/platforms/xpu.py` — Per-layer attention backend routing - `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` — Catch per-layer config errors - `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py` — Per-layer fallback ## Performance - Model: `google/gemma-4-E4B-it-assistant` (Gemma4 architecture, ~4B params) - Hardware: Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550 / Arc Pro B60 - Successfully loads and runs inference with mixed Flash+Triton attention backends

signal.title: [bot] Enable Gemma4 E4B inference on Intel XPU with per-layer heterogeneous head_dim
signal.text: ## Motivation Google's Gemma4 E4B model uses heterogeneous head dimensions across layer types (e.g., head_dim=256 for sliding attention, head_dim=512 for full/global attention via `per_layer_config`). The existing vLLM code forces a global TRITON_ATTN backend when head dimensions differ, but on Intel XPU the Flash Attention SYCL kernel can handle both head sizes natively via per-layer routing. ## Technical Details 1. **`vllm/model_executor/models/config.py`** — Derive `global_head_dim` from new transformers `per_layer_config` when not explicitly set. Skip forcing global TRITON_ATTN on XPU (per-layer routing in `xpu.py` handles heterogeneous head dims). 2. **`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py`** — Read per-layer `head_dim` from `per_layer_config[layer_idx]` for both full-attention and sliding-attention layers, falling back to legacy `global_head_dim`/`head_dim` attributes. 3. **`vllm/platforms/xpu.py`** — Allow head_size > 256 in XPU Flash Attention selection (Max 1550 SYCL kernel supports larger head dims). 4. **`vllm/config/model.py`** — Set `allow_global_per_layer_attribute_access = True` on heterogeneous configs so vLLM can query per-layer attributes globally where needed. 5. **`vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`** — Compute max head_dim across `per_layer_config` entries for buffer allocation sizing. ## Hardware - Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550 (Xe-HPC, 68.7 GB HBM) - TP=1

signal.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix PEFT 0.18+ target_parameters LoRA loading for 3D MoE experts
signal.text: # [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix PEFT 0.18+ target_parameters LoRA loading for 3D MoE experts ## Problem PEFT 0.18+ can train a LoRA against a fused 3D MoE expert parameter via `target_parameters` (e.g. `mlp.experts.gate_up_proj` / `down_proj`), reading it `[E, dim1, dim2]` as `[E, in, out]`. vLLM's `add_lora_w13` / `add_lora_w2` punica kernels use the opposite `nn.Linear` `[out, in]` convention, so per expert `ΔW_vllm = ΔW_peft^T`. On stock vLLM, `_stack_moe_lora_weights` reshapes with the wrong semantics and `set_lora` raises a shape mismatch that drops the adapter (e.g. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B `down_proj`: `512 vs 2048`). ## Fix - `peft_helper.py`: parse `target_parameters` from `adapter_config.json`. - `lora_model.py`: propagate it onto `LoRAModel` (ctor, `clone()`, `from_lora_tensors`). - `model_manager.py`: in `_stack_moe_lora_weights`, detect the PEFT 3D layout and swap `lora_A`/`lora_B` + transpose the trailing two dims **after** the EP-aware expert slicing. Detection is required, not assumed: `create_dummy_lora_weights` builds dummies in the native layout with the same flat shape, so an unconditional transpose would corrupt them. Primary signal is `target_parameters` naming a fused expert weight; fallback is `lora_a` trailing dim != `hidden_size`. ## Testing ``` python -m pytest -v \ tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py::test_peft_helper_target_parameters_direct \ tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_target_parameters_indicates_3d_lora \ tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_from_lora_tensors_propagates_target_parameters \ tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py::test_peft_helper_pass \ tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py::test_from_lora_tensors ``` → **10 passed** (the discriminator test is parametrized over 6 cases). **End-to-end (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B expert LoRA).** The raw PEFT adapter crashes the unpatched loader with the `512 vs 2048` error. With the fix, the directly-loaded adapter is **bit-identical** (chosen-token logprobs, 32 tokens × 5 prompts) to an independent offline-converted oracle that self-checks `max|ΔW_vllm − ΔW_peft^T| = 0` over 320 experts, while both shift logits measurably vs base — so the adapter takes effect and the in-loader transpose matches the verified transform. Logprobs, not decoded text: for an experts-only (8-of-256, rank-32) adapter, greedy text is a false-negative trap since the adapter shifts logits without always flipping the argmax on short prompts. ## Latency impact None expected. The transpose runs inside `_stack_moe_lora_weights` — the adapter-load path, once per adapter (two `.transpose(-2, -1).contiguous()` per fused expert weight). The per-forward hot path (`add_lora_w13` / `add_lora_w2`) is not touched. ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance was used to author this change. A human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Save exact Mamba boundary states
signal.text: ## Summary Fix Mooncake Store persistence for Mamba `align` mode by saving the exact core-selected boundary-state blocks and keeping those physical blocks alive until every worker rank has finished the asynchronous store attempt. This fixes a correctness bug that could persist null, stale/reassigned, or live speculative Mamba state under a valid prefix hash. A later external prefix hit could then restore poisoned recurrent state and produce garbled or runaway output. ## Root cause Mooncake's normal save path resolved each group's source block positionally from a worker-side snapshot of the request's block IDs. That is valid for append-only attention block tables, but a Mamba `align` table is sparse and mutable: - superseded state positions are replaced by the null block and their physical blocks are freed; - speculative scratch blocks are relocated to different logical positions; - the connector's block-ID mirror is append-only and does not observe those in-place changes. Consequently, a positional Mamba save could interpret `NULL_BLOCK_ID` as a physical source, or read a block that had already been freed, reassigned, or was still speculative, while using the correct chained prefix hash as its key. Mooncake's `batch_is_exist` deduplication could then preserve the bad value and prevent a later correct save from replacing it. The production symptom was exposed by the DSpark/EAGLE lookup path landing on an affected interior key. Without that path, a later valid CoW boundary key could win and mask the corruption. ## Design - Core emits exact `(group_id, block_id, boundary_tokens)` entries for committed Mamba `align` boundary states, including the CoW target for a sub-block partial tail. The connector never reconstructs these source IDs positionally. - Mooncake excludes Mamba groups from the normal positional `store_mask`; exact boundary handoffs are the only Mamba writer. The normal path also skips null or missing source IDs for every group as a defense-in-depth guard. - The scheduler claims each accepted physical block with `BlockPool.touch()` before it can be recycled. Consumer-only roles are gated before claiming or queueing handoffs. - Each claimed block receives a monotonic handoff ID. A one-ID/one-pin mapping makes reference release and the bounded in-flight capacity exact, even though a request-level batch ID could work while all entries in a request complete together. - Workers report a cross-rank completion watermark. After seeing its first handoff, a rank reports watermark `0` while that handoff is pending rather than omitting metadata; this prevents aggregation from ignoring a lagging rank and releasing a block early. Dedup, successful upload, pressure drop, cancellation, and store failure are all terminal outcomes for lifetime purposes. - The scheduler releases the connector-owned refs only through `BlockPool.free_blocks()` after the aggregated watermark says every rank is terminal. The configurable in-flight cap bounds pinned GPU blocks if acknowledgements stop; saves beyond the cap remain best-effort and are dropped. - Resumed prefills use the tracked prefill/save boundary, not the request's original prompt length, so replayed generated tokens retain the same cross-group save coverage. - Mamba speculative scratch relocation remains an in-table move, but now fails closed unless `BlockPool.is_block_writable()` confirms the block is non-null, exclusively owned (`ref_cnt == 1`), and unhashed. If shared or pinned speculative blocks become valid in the future, this path must use CoW instead of relocating them. This implementation is intentionally limited to Mamba `align` mode. Mooncake Store's configuration validation rejects incompatible non-align/`all` Mamba layouts; this PR does not add `all`-mode support. ## Retention semantics `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` remains effective even though Mooncake's positional `store_mask` is false for Mamba: 1. Core `MambaManager.cache_blocks()` applies the retention policy first. 2. Only retained/materialized states receive a block hash. 3. Handoff emission skips null or unhashed blocks. 4. Mooncake stores the exact retained states from those handoffs. Therefore dense default retention, sparse interval checkpoints, and replay-boundary behavior are preserved. External persistence is still best-effort: an eligible checkpoint may be absent if the handoff cap is reached or the store operation fails. ## Scope and overlap This is not duplicate work: - #50359 validates external lookup boundaries. - #46896 and #46906 concern Mamba all-mode support and retention policy. - #51362 independently adds the same defensive null/missing-block check to Mooncake's normal save loop. That check is included here, but this PR also removes unsafe positional Mamba saving and fixes exact source selection, asynchronous lifetime, retention-aware handoff, partial-tail handling, and speculative ownership. In that sense, this PR subsumes #51362's behavior rather than relying on it. ## Validation Focused Mooncake Store and prefix-cache suites were run through the final design, including exact block-ID handoff, dense and sparse retention, partial tails, resumed prefills, more than two Mamba groups, null/missing sources, consumer skip-save behavior, cross-rank watermarking, bounded pins, failure paths, and exclusive speculative ownership. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py ``` Result: 183 passed. Additional focused reruns after the watermark, save-gate, and ownership-invariant changes passed (195 tests), and a broader Mooncake Store + prefix-cache run in the k3-debug container on a GB300 worker passed (219 tests). Ruff and `git diff --check` also passed. Serving/model evaluation on `k3-pd-mooncake aa-lcr`: - post-fix: 0/200 garbled responses; - `llm_judge`: approximately 0.77/0.76; - external prefix hit rate: approximately 91–98%; - pre-fix baseline: garbled/runaway outputs, with `llm_judge` approximately 0.76/0.78. No model kernels or numerical computation were changed. AI assistance was used. The human submitter reviewed the changes and is responsible for understanding, testing, and defending the final submission.

signal.title: [Attention][MiniMax-M3] Add FlashInfer MSA backend for SM120/SM121
signal.text: ## Purpose Give MiniMax-M3 sparse attention a fast path on consumer Blackwell (SM120/SM121). These GPUs currently run the Triton fallback for both the lightning indexer and the block-sparse attend, since the vendored MSA kernels are SM100-only. FlashInfer `vX.Y.Z` <!-- placeholder: first release containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3655 --> ships MSA kernels for SM120/SM121 ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3655](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3655)). This PR wires them into the existing impl dispatch, selected the same way as the SM100 MSA path; every other configuration keeps the Triton fallback. Design: - The indexer issues one scoring call and one top-k call for the entire batch, prefill and decode tokens together, so kernel-launch overhead stays constant per step and there is no separate decode/prefill code path. - FlashInfer's top-k takes batch-wide settings only, so M3's per-token selection rules (the forced local window and the causal range clamp) are applied in Python, before and after the kernel call. - The attend runs the FlashInfer prefill and decode kernels on vLLM's paged KV cache exactly as stored, so the path adds no per-step copy or re-layout of KV data; fp8 KV scales fold into the kernels' existing scale arguments. - The FlashInfer indexer and attend must be enabled together: they exchange top-k results in a different buffer layout than the Triton pair, and a mixed pairing would attend to the wrong blocks without any error. A single predicate (`minimax_m3_use_flashinfer_msa`) therefore drives both selections. - Two feature probes in `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py` gate the path; older FlashInfer releases keep the Triton fallback. Dependencies: - FlashInfer >= `vX.Y.Z` <!-- placeholder: first release containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3655 and #4039 --> for `flashinfer.msa_ops`, including its packed KV-cache support ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4039](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4039)): the attend reads K/V views split from vLLM's packed KV cache, a capability FlashInfer advertises as `msa_ops.SUPPORTS_PACKED_KV`. Scope notes: - The FlashInfer path engages only for `sparse_topk_blocks == 16` and decode GQA group sizes up to 16, narrower than the Triton path; M3 configurations satisfy both limits, and anything outside them keeps the Triton fallback. - `fp8_e5m2` KV caches and `nvfp4` indexer caches also stay on the Triton fallback. ## Test Plan Both new tests are in `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py`: - `test_flashinfer_indexer_impl_matches_triton`: runs the FlashInfer and Triton indexer impls on the same batches through their real metadata builders and asserts they select the same blocks, over bf16/fp8 index caches and local-window settings, including a short decode request. - `test_flashinfer_sparse_attention_matches_reference`: runs the FlashInfer attend at the impl's exact call shape (K/V views split from the contract-allocated cache) against the same reference the Triton kernels are tested with, over both KV-cache layouts, mixed prefill batches, and decode. - End-to-end and performance runs wait on a FlashInfer release containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4039; that is why this PR is a draft. ## Test Result - Indexer and attend parity: all cases pass on RTX 5080 (SM120) with FlashInfer built from source at the #4039 branch. - On FlashInfer releases without packed-KV support the attend rejects the K/V views at call time, so a version mismatch fails loudly instead of producing wrong results. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Performance]: Native MTP draft acceptance rate decays with total context length (Qwen3.6-27B, in-range context, no --hf-overrides)
signal.text: #### Before submitting an issue, please make sure the issue hasn't been already addressed by searching through [the existing and past issues](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues?q=is%3Aissue+sort%3Acreated-desc+). Related but distinct from #37435 and #40756 — details below. ### Proposal to improve performance `SpeculativeConfig`/the V1 scheduler currently apply `num_speculative_tokens` as a fixed, engine-lifetime constant (`scheduler.py`, `gpu_model_runner.py`) — there doesn't appear to be a way to gate or scale speculative decoding per-request based on the request's current sequence length. Given the data below, a static global on/off leaves speedup on the table at short context while actively regressing long-context throughput. Would maintainers be open to a per-request (or at least length-bucketed) toggle/threshold for spec decode, similar in spirit to how BFLA-style sparse attention gates on a min-length threshold? ### Report of performance regression On Qwen3.6-27B (dense, `num_hidden_layers=64`), MTP speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens=6`) gives a large decode speedup at short context but the *net* speedup shrinks steadily as total context grows and turns into a net **loss** well before the model's native context limit. This happens entirely within the model's native `max_position_embeddings` (262144, `rope_type: "default"`, no scaling) — no `--hf-overrides` used — so it looks distinct from #37435 (specifically about `--hf-overrides` not propagating to the draft config when extending past native length via injected YaRN scaling). It's also a different symptom than #40756 (crash + degenerate 100%-acceptance/-1-draft-token state on the same model) — what I see is a smooth, reproducible decline, not a sudden crash. **Decode tok/s, MTP (n=6) vs no-MTP, otherwise identical config:** | ctx (tokens) | MTP n=6 | no MTP | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | 2048 | 138.04 | 60.39 | +129% | | 4096 | 119.51 | 60.49 | +98% | | 8192 | 88.25 | 60.10 | +47% | | 16384 | 51.03 | 59.13 | **-14%** | | 30720 | 26.81 | 54.55 | **-51%** | Single-stream, greedy (`temperature=0`), one real code-gen prompt (padded with filler to hit each context length), `max_tokens=300`. Measured via `stream_options.include_usage` for the server-reported `completion_tokens` — worth noting that naively counting SSE delta chunks undercounts real tokens under MTP, since an accepted run gets flushed as one multi-token delta; that cost me a while to catch. **Per-position draft acceptance rate** (same n=6 runs, from the `SpecDecoding metrics` log line), short vs long context: ``` ctx≈2048: Per-position acceptance rate: 0.935, 0.829, 0.715, 0.585, 0.463, 0.366 (avg 64.9%) ctx≈30720: Per-position acceptance rate: 0.721, 0.512, 0.395, 0.326, 0.256, 0.140 (avg 39.1%) ``` Note every position shifts down, not just the tail — even position-1 acceptance drops (0.935 → 0.721) as total context grows, on top of the already well-known within-round decay toward later positions. **Smaller `num_speculative_tokens` does not help** — n=3 is worse than n=6 at every context length tested, and crosses below the no-MTP baseline even earlier: | ctx (tokens) | n=6 | n=3 | no MTP | |---|---|---|---| | 2048 | 138.04 | 101.41 | 60.39 | | 4096 | 119.51 | 88.21 | 60.49 | | 8192 | 88.25 | 58.72 | 60.10 | | 16384 | 51.03 | 35.06 | 59.13 | | 30720 | 26.81 | 20.21 | 54.55 | ### Misc discussion on performance Working hypothesis: `mtp_num_hidden_layers=1` vs target `num_hidden_layers=64` is a large capacity gap. At short context, the target model's final hidden state already encodes most of what's needed to extend a few tokens, so one extra shallow layer suffices. At long context, correctly extending text in a way that stays consistent with far-back context increasingly needs the kind of multi-hop, long-range attention a single extra layer has little capacity for — so the gap between "what the 1-layer head guesses" and "what the 64-layer target would actually pick" widens with length, independent of the standard within-round positional decay. This is consistent with general commentary around DeepSeek's own MTP-1 (part of the motivation cited for their DSpark replacement — "in realistic multi-turn coding sessions, performance can degrade as context grows, because the acceptance of draft tokens decreases"), though I haven't seen it isolated/quantified against total context length specifically the way the tables above do, as opposed to the well-documented within-round tail decay. Is this expected/already-understood behavior for shallow single-layer MTP heads, or does it look like a bug in how the draft model consumes long-context state (analogous in spirit to #37435's draft/target config divergence, even though the specific `--hf-overrides` mechanism doesn't apply here)? Happy to share the exact benchmark script and raw logs if useful. ### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary) ```text vLLM: SM70 (Tesla V100) ported fork, version string vllm-0.23.1.dev92+g8d5a0d3d0.d20260702 Model: Qwen3.6-27B, W8A16 asym (compressed-tensors), dense (not MoE) MTP draft head: mtp_num_hidden_layers=1, mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings=false (shares embeddings/lm_head with target) rope_parameters: {"rope_type": "default", "rope_theta": 10000000, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, ...} — no scaling max_position_embeddings: 262144 (native); all tested context lengths (<=30720) well within native range, no --hf-overrides used TP=4, DP=1, --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":6}' ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [X] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Drop incomplete tool-call markup in non-streaming to match streaming
signal.text:
## Purpose Fixes #47137 When generation terminates (`max_tokens`/`length` or a `stop` string) inside a `<tool_call>` opener that has not been promoted to a tool call, the streaming path drops the buffered markup but the non-streaming path returned it as `content` — the two paths disagreed for identical model output. Contrary to the hope in the issue thread that #46875 had fixed this, I re-ran the issue's no-server unit reproduction on current main (`978de83`) and **the divergence still reproduces** (confirming @TheDuyIT's July 1 retest): ``` 2 '<tool_call>
' stream= '' nonstream= '<tool_call>
' DIVERGE 3 '<tool_call>
<' stream= '' nonstream= '<tool_call>
<' DIVERGE 4 '<tool_call>
<function' stream= '' nonstream= '<tool_call>
<function' DIVERGE ``` Root cause: in `DelegatingParser._extract_tool_calls`, the no-tool-calls branch returned the raw `content` instead of `tool_call_info.content` — the tool parser's cleaned content, which already strips incomplete tool-call markup while preserving any real content generated before the opener. This is "Direction B" from the issue, matching @bbrowning's stated expected behavior ("non-streaming should now match streaming and drop the incomplete markup until we have a valid tool call"). ## Changes - `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`: the auto-tool-choice no-tool-calls branch now returns the tool parser's content (scoped to engine-based parsers per review). - `vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py`: deferred-content flush keeps original text order around unpromoted tool blocks (review round 2, patch by @TheDuyIT). - `vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py` + `adapters.py`: `skip_reasoning_parsing` flag so tool parsers pass reasoning markup through verbatim when no reasoning parser is configured (review round 3, reported by @TheDuyIT). - `tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py`: regression tests for all of the above — truncated-opener parity cases, content-order preservation, think-markup passthrough for both engine failure modes, and sanity checks that complete tool calls still promote. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR The issue timeline has no cross-referenced PRs and `gh pr list --search "47137"` returns none (checked immediately before opening). @IMvision12 and @Kronten28 expressed interest in the thread (Jun 30 / Jul 1) but no PR was opened in the days since, and the thread stalled on the open question of whether the bug still exists — which the reproduction above settles. ## Test Plan As of 5b35c31b8 (current merge state with `main`): ``` $ pytest tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py -k "TruncatedToolOpener or ThinkMarkup" -v 10 passed $ pytest tests/parser/ # full parser suite 3779 passed $ pytest tests/tool_parsers/ 885 passed, 3 skipped, 34 xfailed $ pre-commit run --files <changed files> ruff check / ruff format / typos / mypy: Passed ``` Also re-ran the issue's part-D reproduction with the fix: all three truncation points now MATCH between streaming and non-streaming. ## Test Result All new and existing parser tests pass on macOS CPU (source build, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`). --- This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude Code); the diff was reviewed and the tests were run locally as described above. cc @bbrowning @TheDuyIT

signal.title: [Frontend] Enforce max_tool_calls for Responses built-in tools
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR makes `ResponsesRequest.max_tool_calls` effective for Responses built-in tool execution. The Responses API already accepts and returns `max_tool_calls`, but the built-in tool generation loop did not enforce it before calling tools. This change threads the request value into the loop and stops executing further built-in tool calls once the configured limit is reached. I checked existing open PRs/issues for `max_tool_calls responses` and did not find an overlapping change. signal.title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Validate sparse MLA top-k buffer
signal.text: ## Purpose Addresses #46726. This PR improves SM120 FlashInfer sparse MLA construction error handling and adds regression coverage for skip-topk layers that rely on a shared `topk_indices_buffer`. The current implementation already supports the valid skip-topk path where `indexer is None` and the implementation falls back to the shared `topk_indices_buffer` passed by the upper MLA path. This PR keeps that behavior, and adds targeted tests to make sure it remains covered. This PR also replaces the internal assertion for the missing top-k buffer case with an explicit `ValueError`. This makes the failure mode clearer when neither an `indexer` nor a shared `topk_indices_buffer` is available. I checked for duplicate work before opening this PR: ```bash gh issue view 46726 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "46726 in:body" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "SM120 sparse MLA topk_indices_buffer" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "FlashInfer sparse MLA indexer" ``` Results: * No open PR directly references #46726. * I did not find an existing open PR that adds this specific SM120 FlashInfer sparse MLA API coverage or replaces the missing top-k buffer assertion with an explicit `ValueError`. AI assistance was used while investigating the issue, reasoning about the sparse MLA construction path, and drafting parts of the PR description. I personally reviewed the changed code, verified that the implementation matches the intended behavior, and ran the tests listed below before submitting. ## Test Plan Run the relevant SM120 FlashInfer sparse MLA API tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -v tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py ``` Run the sparse MLA backend tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -v tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py ``` Run pre-commit on the modified files: ```bash pre-commit run --files \ tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py ``` The targeted tests cover: * Models without `index_topk` are rejected by the SM120 sparse backend. * Skip-topk layers with `indexer=None` can be constructed when a shared `topk_indices_buffer` is provided. * A clear `ValueError` is raised when both `indexer` and the shared top-k buffer are missing. ## Test Result Passed: ```text tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py: all relevant tests passed tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py: all relevant tests passed pre-commit run --files tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py: passed ``` Not fully validated locally: I do not have access to the original SM120 setup from the issue report, so validation from the issue reporter or maintainers on the original failing environment would be appreciated.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Parser engine: count reasoning tokens when <think> is pre-filled in the prompt
signal.text: ## Purpose `ParserEngine.count_reasoning_tokens` returned `0` for Qwen3.5 / `*-Thinking` templates (where `<think>` is pre-filled in the prompt, so the output only contains `</think>`), under-reporting `reasoning_tokens` in the Responses API usage. The fix seeds the reasoning state from `initial_state` instead of requiring a `<think>` token in the output, and applies to all engine-based parsers (Qwen3 / NemotronV3 / Gemma4). The fix and test originate in #40783 (against the pre-#45413 parser); this PR ports the count fix to the engine-based parser that replaced it. Not a duplicate of #44398: that PR fixes the same count for the text-based parsers (DeepSeek-R1) and adds Chat Completions reporting, but it does not touch `ParserEngine`, so the engine parsers introduced by #45413 stay affected. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_reasoning.py::TestCountReasoningTokens -v pytest tests/reasoning/test_qwen3_reasoning_parser.py::test_count_reasoning_tokens -v pytest tests/parser/engine/ -q ``` ## Test Result - `TestCountReasoningTokens`: 3 passed (the pre-prompt-`<think>` case failed before the fix). - `test_count_reasoning_tokens`: 3 passed on all three real tokenizers (failed on all three before the fix). - `tests/parser/engine/`: 191 passed, no regression. `ruff` clean. *AI assistance was used to adapt the test from #40783 and implement the fix; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.*

signal.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix wvSplitK OOB reads on strided activations
signal.text: ## Purpose Prevent ROCm skinny GEMMs from reading past a packed activation view. `wvSplitK` and `wvSplitKrc` do not consume strides, so their dispatch now materializes the activation only when its 2-D layout is not exactly dense row-major. Kimi-K3 KDA projects several outputs into one row and passes the 128-element `f_a` slice to `f_b_proj`. Under TP8 that view has `stride=(6288, 1)` and `storage_offset=6144`. The skinny kernel preloads a flat span; the view is valid for PyTorch indexing but the preload extends 12,288 bytes past it. | Rows | `is_contiguous()` | Available | Flat preload | Over-read | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | `True` | 288 B | 12,576 B | 12,288 B | | 4 | `False` | 38,016 B | 50,304 B | 12,288 B | The singleton case is why `is_contiguous()` is insufficient: PyTorch ignores singleton-dimension strides. Dense inputs, fallback GEMMs, NVIDIA, HIP kernel code, and dispatch thresholds are unchanged. ## Test plan Tested on 8x MI355X (`gfx950`) with the public Kimi-K3 image. Models: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3@9f62e4e9` and `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark@cf6b8244`. The command below pins the control and PR source revisions. Fetch and verify the candidate: ```bash git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git vllm git -C vllm fetch origin refs/pull/50618/head:pr-50618 test "$(git -C vllm rev-parse pr-50618)" = \ aa780f0db6e5f467378856dffda1e939bca53604 git -C vllm checkout --detach 9a7ae4b80866a322678ece31ca2854d9a174ab8d git -C vllm diff 9a7ae4b80866a322678ece31ca2854d9a174ab8d..pr-50618 \ --binary | git -C vllm apply - git -C vllm diff --check ``` Use the complete verified vLLM tree as an overlay on the public image; do not copy individual files. Verify `import vllm, vllm._C` before testing. Run: ```bash python -m pytest -q \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_rocm_unquantized_gemm.py ``` Launch TP8 with both exact model revisions: ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \ vllm serve /model --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code --moe-backend auto \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --max-num-seqs 4 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-model-len 1048576 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,4,64]}' \ --speculative-config \ '{"method":"dspark","model":"/draft","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA"}' ``` The focused test injects packed singleton and multi-row views into both skinny dispatches and asserts that the native kernels receive dense `(128, 1)` activations. The real-workload layout can also be proved without issuing the unsafe read by logging shape, stride, storage offset, remaining storage bytes, and `stride(0) * rows * element_size()` immediately before dispatch. ## Test results - Pinned-public focused suite: **4/4 passed in 4.46 s**. - Native MI355X B1/B4 checks reached `wvSplitK` with dense activations and matched `torch.nn.functional.linear` exactly (`max_abs_error=0`). - TP8 loaded 96/96 target shards and the draft; graph capture completed at 1/4/64 tokens; health and generation passed with no memory-access fault. - Full source-isolated GSM8K from the preceding runtime revision: control **1274/1319**, candidate **1276/1319**, zero invalid responses, 13 wins/11 losses (`p=0.8388`). The final commit changes only the stride predicate and singleton test coverage; the full run was not repeated at that final head. - Changed-file pre-commit, `git diff --check`, and DCO passed. ## Limits The unpatched fault is allocator-layout dependent: the unsupported read faults only when it crosses an unmapped page. The deterministic stride/storage probe establishes the over-read even when a serving run happens not to fault. ## Tool assistance Claude Opus and OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests, log/source analysis, and drafting this description.

signal.title: [MoE] Fuse SwiGLU into Triton W13 epilogue
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> PLEASE FILL IN THE PR DESCRIPTION HERE ENSURING ALL CHECKLIST ITEMS (AT THE BOTTOM) HAVE BEEN CONSIDERED. ## Purpose Interleave BF16 W13 gate/up rows at load time so each pair lands in one GEMM output tile, then apply the CUDA-compatible SwiGLU calculation directly in the Triton epilogue and store only the half-width result. This removes the routed-MoE activation launch and the full-width intermediate HBM round trip while preserving bitwise output parity, including expert-parallel zero-fill.
