signal.title: [Offloader] Prefetch weight offloading for large MoE models, plus a schedule planner
signal.text: ## Purpose Extends the prefetch weight offloader (#29941) so DeepSeek-V4 class MoE models run on hardware their expert weights do not fit on, and adds a way to choose an offload schedule without launching one server per candidate. Applying #29941 to DSv4 exposed three gaps: expert weights are heterogeneous after quantization, H2D copies contend with tensor-parallel collectives on the same links, and nothing reported which units were selected or how many bytes each moved. **Scope.** The mechanism is model-agnostic: units are discovered through `named_modules`/`named_parameters` and selected by parameter-name segment, with no model-class dispatch and no architecture-specific branches. The selectors cover fused (`experts.w13_weight`/`w2_weight`) and unfused (`experts.gate_up_proj`/`down_proj`) MoE layouts as well as `feed_forward.w*` and attention. DeepSeek-V4 is what it was developed and measured against, not what it is limited to — but it is the only architecture I have evidence for, so treat other models as untested rather than unsupported. Commit 1 is @Tom-Zheng's, submitted on his behalf with his authorization and unmodified. Commits 2–3 are mine. ## Not a duplicate Checked `weight offloading`, `prefetch offload`, `offload selectors`, `offload NUMA`, `prefetch slab pinned`, `offloader diagnostics manifest`, `offload planner`, `weight offload configuration`. - **#41474** (batch prefetch via `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`) is closest: it changes the copy submission API, this changes what is copied and when. Intents compose and I have not duplicated its `swap_blocks_batch` change, but both touch `prefetch.py` and will conflict textually — happy to rebase either way. - **#46337** (offload env vars → `OffloadConfig`) is a June draft; that migration landed independently, so commit 2 follows the existing convention. - **#43970** and **#49139** touch neighbouring DSv4 code, not the offloader. **#38261** is a *KV* offload planner — a different subsystem. ## What is in it **1. Prefetch offloading for DSv4-Flash** (@Tom-Zheng) — semantic parameter selectors (`routed_experts`, `shared_experts`, `dense_mlp`, `attention`), pooled slab and storage-group runtime buffers with a direct fallback for layouts that cannot be pooled, a planner resolving which ordered module positions become offload units, NUMA-aware process binding, and a read-only post-init manifest describing the resulting schedule. **2. Bounded slabs and collective-aware pacing** — the slab allocator could request a pinned host block per layout with no upper bound; now bounded. H2D copies are chunked and gated while a collective is in flight, behind `--offload-comm-aware`, so an unpaced copy cannot delay a collective every rank is blocked on. The offloader carries the flag and exposes `gates_collectives`, so low-level distributed code reads a boolean instead of `vllm.envs` and the common no-op case costs no context manager. Pacing engages only at TP > 1. Also moves the offloader tests from a new top-level `tests/weight_offload/` into `tests/model_executor/offloader/`. Not cosmetic: the old location was in no CI area's file list and outside the mypy hook's scope, so those tests were neither run by CI nor type-checked. The Model Executor area now also triggers on `vllm/config/offload.py`. **3. A schedule planner** — `python -m vllm.benchmarks.weight_offload.planner` Choosing `offload_group_size` / `offload_num_in_group` / `offload_prefetch_step` is guesswork, and a schedule that does not fit says so only by failing to start. Two exact quantities decide viability — bytes that stay resident, and bytes re-copied H2D each forward — but both need per-position sizes that only a running engine knows, which is what commit 1's manifest reports. Serve once with `VLLM_PREFETCH_LOG_SCHEDULE=1`, then score every other schedule offline. Results are deltas against that run, so schedule-independent terms (KV, non-offloadable weights, allocator slack, graph reserve) cancel and the operator enters nothing. It models memory, not latency, and says so: no bandwidth setting, because bytes over bandwidth gives the PCIe time a schedule occupies, not whether that time is hidden. This is also why the manifest lands with it — it is the only artifact that makes the identities checkable. ## Evidence ``` pytest tests/model_executor/offloader # 123 passed, 1 skipped pytest tests/benchmarks/weight_offload # 10 passed pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD ``` All clean on `main` @ `3a79957b62`; the three commits cherry-pick onto it without conflicts. ### Serving, TP8 DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8, RTX PRO 6000, `offload_group_size=3 offload_num_in_group=1 offload_prefetch_step=3 offload_params=experts`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.90`, 8000-token prompts with one output token at concurrency 1/2/4/8, cold prefix cache. Each arm is a separate server with the `torch.compile` cache disabled, so no arm inherits another's compiled graphs. Every flag in the baseline case already parses on `3a79957b62`. | arm | tree | TTFT @1 (ms) | steady req/s | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A | `main` @ `3a79957b62` | **does not reach readiness** | — | | B | + commit 1 | 1956.17 | 0.5165 | | C | + commits 1–3, pacing off | 1955.87 | 0.5165 | | C | + commits 1–3, pacing on | 1766.73 / 1764.43 | 0.5725 / 0.5726 | - **A cannot start.** Weights load, then CUDA graph capture aborts under `determine_available_memory` with `cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnjoined` at `breakable_cudagraph.py` `capture_end`, on six of eight ranks — precisely what commit 1's `join_after_forward` hook prevents. Commit 1 is a prerequisite for this configuration, not a speedup on a working one. - **Pacing off is free**: B and C differ by 0.02% at every concurrency, two independent instances on different trees. - **Pacing on is worth ~10%**: −9.7% TTFT and +10.9% throughput against the mean of the pacing-off arms, uniform across the sweep, at ~75× the observed run-to-run spread (≤0.13%). KV holds 10,171 tokens here, barely more than one 8000-token request, so concurrency above 1 measures queueing — TTFT @1 and steady throughput are the load-bearing numbers. ### Memory and transfer identities Same model and schedule. Byte counts from the post-init manifest, transfer figures from an Nsight Systems trace over explicit GPU-time windows. Measured 2026-08-04 on this code before the rebase onto current main; the rebase touched no selector or buffer arithmetic. | quantity | value | | --- | --- | | ordered candidate positions | 61 | | runtime units selected (predicted / observed) | 20 / 20 | | offloaded bytes per rank | 33,690,746,880 (31.38 GiB) | | runtime buffer bytes per rank | 5,053,612,032 (4.71 GiB) | | **net GPU bytes freed per rank** | **28,637,134,848 (26.67 GiB)** | | steady-request H2D per rank | 33.6911 GB, 0.001% from the analytical identity | | per-rank H2D bandwidth | 24.68 – 27.28 GB/s | | **copy union overlapped by compute** | **≥ 99.813%** | | steady copy-only exposure | 2.253 – 2.305 ms/rank | Manifest against the analytical model: −46,880 B offloaded and −12,032 B runtime buffer, both inside the log rounding interval. Reading that same manifest, the planner reproduces all of it — 20 units, identical byte counts, zero delta scoring the recorded schedule against itself — and reduces 10,446 enumerated schedules to 331 distinct outcomes. Caveats: per-position compute was not measured (aggregate divided uniformly gives 40.36 ms/position, a proxy). Synchronous TP is bounded by the slowest participant, 24.68 GB/s, not the 25.98 GB/s mean. These figures are instrumented and the latency table is not — separate measurements. ### One interaction worth knowing At `gpu_memory_utilization=0.952` both B and C reach readiness and then die identically on the first request: FlashInfer's CUTLASS fused-MoE workspace requests 1.32 GiB from `FusedMoeRunner::getWorkspaceInfo` *after* memory profiling has already passed. Offloading converts weight memory into headroom that gets respent on KV, so a workspace allocated outside vLLM's profiling becomes marginal exactly when offloading is doing its job. Not a defect in these commits and the fix is headroom rather than code, but it is the first failure an operator will hit. ## AI assistance Produced with AI assistance. Every changed line has been reviewed by the submitter, and the tests and measurements above were executed on the hardware described, with results reported as measured.

signal.title: [ROCm][K3] Extend FP8 asm MLA prefill to non-divisor small head counts
signal.text: ## Context The AITER FP8 MLA **prefill** path (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`) is gated on `num_heads % 16 == 0`. Kimi-K3 has 96 heads over `kv_lora_rank=512` → **12 heads/rank at TP8**, a non-divisor of 16, so its FP8 prefill falls back to the BF16 FMHA decompress path. That fallback builds a bf16 working set not covered by the FP8 KV-pool accounting and exhausts the activation arena at long context (K3 OOM'd at ~197k tokens, KV pool <4% used). This is the **prefill counterpart to #50578** (asm decode pad 12→16). MLA attention is independent per query head over the shared latent KV, so padding the query heads up to 16 and slicing the result back is exact. Rebased onto current `main` (includes merged #50578). Prefill-only diff: **+48 / −11**, one file (`rocm_aiter_mla.py`). ## Changes **FP8 prefill enablement (this PR):** - Relax the `_fp8_prefill_enabled` gate to also allow `0 < num_heads < 16`, and **gate it on FP8 KV** (`kv_cache_dtype_str == "fp8"` in the metadata builder; `is_quantized_kv_cache(kv_cache_dtype)` in the impl). Without this, a bf16-KV serve would reserve PS workspace unnecessarily. - In `_mla_fp8_prefill_attn`: replicate-pad Q/K/V to 16 via `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` (from #50578), run PS asm prefill + `mla_reduce_v1` at 16 heads, slice output back to `num_heads`. - Set `num_head_k = max(16, num_heads)` in `_init_fp8_prefill_ps_buffers` and `_build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata` so work/reduce maps match padded tensors — also cuts partial tiles (`gcd(16,256)=16` vs `gcd(12,256)=4`), reclaiming **~6 GiB** PS workspace. Decode padding / Gluon routing is **not** in this PR — that is #50578 (merged). ## Dependencies / related - **#50578** (merged) — `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` / asm decode for non-divisor heads. - **ROCm/aiter#4452** (merged `a63ede724`) — 64-bit paged-KV byte offsets for >4 GB addressing. - Composes with **#48712** (gate PS workspace on fp8 KV) — this PR includes the same gate locally. ## vllm serve command **Hardware:** 8× MI355X (gfx950), TP8 **Model:** `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (mxfp4) ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 export GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 export HF_HUB_CACHE=/dev/shm/hf-cache HF_HOME=/dev/shm/hf-cache export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600 export VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 export HIPBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=32768 export CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=32768 MODEL=/path/to/Kimi-K3 # e.g. /shared_nfs/models/Kimi-K3 vllm serve "$MODEL" --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --trust-remote-code --load-format auto --moe-backend aiter \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --enable-prefix-caching --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details --disable-uvicorn-access-log ## Test results ### Long-context prefill (functional) | | Before PR-A | After PR-A | |---|-------------|------------| | Fresh prefill @ util 0.95 | OOM ~197k tokens (BF16 FMHA fallback, KV <4%) | **470k (68 s)**, **590k (28.6 s)** OK | | PS workspace | ~4032 partial tiles (~12 heads) | ~960 partial tiles (~6 GiB saved) | ### Accuracy — GSM8K (lm-eval, full 1319-test split, 5-shot greedy, conc=32, ctx=16384) Patches applied for this run: **#50578 + PR-A + #50618 only** (no cgmem/MoE/kv_b_proj). Server at `gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`. ```bash export HF_HUB_CACHE=/dev/shm/hf-cache HF_HOME=/dev/shm/hf-cache export OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --include_path /path/to/InferenceX/utils/evals \ --tasks /path/to/InferenceX/utils/evals/gsm8k.yaml \ --output_path /tmp/eval_out --log_samples \ --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8888/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=32,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=16384" \ --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=12288,temperature=0,top_p=1" ``` | Run | n | strict-match EM | flexible-extract EM | |-----|---|-----------------|---------------------| | **With PR-A** (MI355X node 193, 2026-08-09) | 1319 | **97.04%** ± 0.47% | **96.97%** ± 0.47% | | Prior stack (cgmem+MoE+PR-A, node 1319, util 0.95) | 1319 | 96.89% ± 0.48% | 96.89% ± 0.48% | | Baseline replicate (stock + ASM deps, node 1319) | 1319 | 96.66% ± 0.49% | 96.66% ± 0.49% | No accuracy regression vs baseline; delta within run noise.

signal.title: [Core] Release NCCL communicator memory in sleep mode
signal.text: ## Replacement for #46234 This recreates #46234, which became unreopenable after its fork was detached. The original PR was not closed for a technical reason; all its review threads were resolved. ## What Sleep mode releases weights and KV-cache memory, but NCCL communicators retain their dynamic GPU buffers (~1 GiB/rank at TP4). This change releases that memory during sleep via NCCL's native `ncclCommSuspend(NCCL_SUSPEND_MEM)` / `ncclCommResume`, preserving communicator identity, topology, and connection state. Requires NCCL >= 2.29.7 (the vllm/vllm-openai image pins 2.30.7; the CUDA test lock 2.29.7). ## How (updated architecture) - `suspend()` / `resume()` hooks on `DeviceCommunicatorBase` (the generic surface requested in [#46234 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46234#discussion_r3504640029), ready for FlashInfer comm suspension); `CudaCommunicator` delegates to PyNccl. - `PyNcclCommunicator.suspend/resume` are **idempotent** (`_suspended` state). - Orchestration lives in the shared worker dispatch layer (`gpu_worker.sleep/wake_up`) — the same placement #46234 was reviewed with — gated by a new `SleepModeBackend.requires_communicator_suspend()` capability (`cumem` → True; process-checkpoint mechanisms that cover NCCL themselves → False, avoiding double handling). PyNccl-level idempotence makes staged wakes safe: each communicator suspends and resumes exactly once, and the worker holds no extra state. This differs from the first push of this PR, which called the walkers from inside `CuMemBackend`. That shape had a layer inversion (allocator module importing `parallel_state`) and a reproducible crash: the staged RL wake (`/wake_up?tags=weights` → `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`) called `ncclCommResume` twice, and the second call fails with `invalid usage`, killing the engine (`EngineDeadError`). Reproduced on GB200 TP4; fixed here by the PyNccl idempotence guard (unit-tested), with 7 edge scenarios (wake-without-sleep, double sleep, staged wake, mid-walk failure recovery, capability-off parity, XPU, TP=1) adversarially verified safe. ## Test - Unit: `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py` (9 passed) covers the capability contract and staged-wake single-resume ordering; `tests/distributed/test_pynccl.py::test_pynccl_suspend_resume_idempotent` covers the low-level guard. Pre-commit incl. mypy green. - E2E on 1×(4×GB200), vllm/vllm-openai:nightly, NCCL 2.30.7: full sleep/wake cycle and staged wake (weights → kv_cache), greedy 64-token output compared token-exact before/after. | Model | TP | NCCL freed/rank | Sleep L1 total freed/rank | Output preserved (full + staged wake) | |---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking | 4 | 1152 MiB (2 comms: tp, ep) | 155.24 GiB | ✓ | | NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 | 4 | 1152 MiB | 152.26 GiB | ✓ | Original #46234 validation (8×H200, TP2/4/8 ± EP/DP/PP, 958–1438 MiB/rank, output preserved) applies to the unchanged NCCL mechanism. **Additional GSM8K correctness pass, single-node TP4 and cross-node TP8** (vllm/vllm-openai:nightly, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507, 200 questions/run, `--moe-backend TRITON`; checkpoint loaded from `/dev/shm` — Lustre client-side cache tops out well under this model's 56.87 GiB checkpoint, so `--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch` stalls at 0% indefinitely on a network filesystem for a model this size, unrelated to this PR): | Topology | Comm memory released (per rank, both sleep cycles) | `invalid_rate` | Errors/tracebacks | |---|---|---|---| | TP4, single node | `Sleep mode freed 155.22 GiB` then `152.82 GiB` | 0.0000 (600/600 answers parsed) | none | | TP8, cross-node (2×4×GB200) | `Sleep mode freed 151.51 GiB`, `CuMemAllocator: sleep freed 149.10 GiB` — consistent across all 8 ranks on both hosts | 0.0000 (600/600 answers parsed) | none | Both runs show baseline/post-full-wake/post-staged-wake accuracy within ±1 question (TP4) or ±9 questions (TP8, out of 200) of each other — expected batch-composition floating-point non-associativity for greedy decoding under concurrent load, not output corruption (zero invalid/unparseable answers, zero errors across both runs). The TP8 cross-node run also empirically confirms the FlashInfer limitation above: `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: CUDA error code=800 (CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED)` — a non-fatal warning, vLLM falls back cleanly and this PR's NCCL-only release is unaffected. Cluster caveat, unrelated to this PR's code: this rack is GB200 NVL72 with MNNVL (rack-scale NVLink fabric), but the site's Slurm/Pyxis container build has no device-injection option for the IMEX channel — confirmed by bind-mounting `/dev/nvidia-caps-imex-channels` into the container (visible via `nvidia-smi -L`, host IMEX daemon healthy) and still hitting `ncclCommInitRank`/NVLS proxy setup failure. The TP8 run above therefore exercises `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume` over plain socket transport (`NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=0`), not the NVLink fabric path — both are the same NCCL communicator-suspend code this PR adds, but a rack with working IMEX container injection would be a stronger cross-node signal. ## Scope NCCL only. FlashInfer's all-reduce-fusion workspace (and MoE all2all workspace) GPU memory is **not** released during sleep in this PR. Investigated and deferred, not overlooked: - FlashInfer's `AllReduceFusionWorkspace` (MNNVL/TRTLLM) has no suspend/resume primitive analogous to `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume` — only `checkpoint_prepare()`/`checkpoint_restore()` (added for #46877's separate checkpoint lifecycle, flashinfer >= 0.6.16). - Wiring `CudaCommunicator.suspend()`/`resume()` to call those checkpoint hooks directly (reuse, no new machinery) was tried and reverted: `checkpoint_prepare()`/`checkpoint_restore()` are reachable via `async_llm.checkpoint_prepare()`'s independent RPC path with no mutual exclusion against `sleep()`/`wake_up()`, so an interleaved call would double-release/rebuild the same workspace. Matches [galletas1712's #46234 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46234#discussion_r3504640029) that "NCCL checkpoint and ncclCommSuspend are not really composable." - `DeviceCommunicatorBase.suspend()/resume()` (this PR) is the generic override point galletas1712 requested for future FlashInfer comm suspension; it's ready to host a real implementation once flashinfer exposes a dedicated suspend/resume primitive. ## Why this is not duplicate work No open PR implements `ncclCommSuspend`/`ncclCommResume`. #46877 is the separate process-checkpoint lifecycle (its hooks are deliberately no-ops for NCCL); #35934 tears down communicators for CRIU; RFC #52125 (L3 snapshot) references this PR as the ordinary-sleep counterpart. ## AI disclosure AI assistance (Claude, Codex) was used for the redesign analysis, implementation, and on-node validation; three candidate architectures were implemented and validated head-to-head before choosing this one. The submitter reviewed every changed line.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Anthropic] Return 4xx for client-caused errors in /v1/messages
signal.text: Fixes #52088 ## Purpose Invalid user input that passes the Anthropic request schema but fails the Anthropic→OpenAI conversion (e.g. more than `VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS` stop sequences) currently surfaces as an HTTP 500: the `except Exception` in `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py` swallows the `pydantic.ValidationError` raised while constructing `ChatCompletionRequest` and turns it into an `internal_error`. The schema half of #52088 was already addressed by #51997 (`max_length` on `stop_sequences`). This PR fixes the remaining robustness gap: client-caused errors must be 4xx, never 500. ## Changes - `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py` - Both `POST /v1/messages` and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` now route exceptions through `create_error_response` (the consolidated entrypoint exception-handling logic), which maps client-caused errors (`pydantic.ValidationError`, `VLLMClientError`, etc.) to 4xx, while genuine server errors stay 500. - `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` - New `TestClientErrorResponses` class: conversion `ValidationError` → 400, `VLLMValidationError` → 400, generic `RuntimeError` → 500 (regression guard), and the `count_tokens` route → 400. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k TestClientErrorResponses python -m ruff check vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py python -m ruff format --check vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py ``` ## Test Result - `py_compile` + `ruff check` + `ruff format --check`: clean. - Error-mapping behaviour verified against a real `pydantic.ValidationError` (6 stop sequences): maps to `BadRequestError` / 400; `VLLMClientError` → 400; `RuntimeError` → 500. - Rebased onto the latest `main` (including #52261 exception-handler consolidation); no merge conflicts.

signal.title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Respect dynamic K=0 from scheduler in AutoRegressiveSpeculator
signal.text: ## Problem When Dynamic Speculative Decoding (DSD) selects K=0 at higher batch sizes, `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` ignores the scheduler's runtime K and executes the configured maximum number of draft steps. Those drafts are not used, so this wastes GPU work. The scheduler already publishes the selected K in `SchedulerOutput.num_spec_tokens_to_schedule`; MRV2 did not propagate that value to proposal execution. Fixes #51510. ## Solution - Propagate `num_spec_tokens_to_schedule` through `ExecuteModelState` into `speculator.propose()`. - For K=0, run draft prefill to keep the draft KV cache synchronized, then return an empty-width draft tensor without running draft decode. - Pass only the returned draft width to `DraftTokensHandler`, preventing stale columns in the reusable draft buffer from becoming phantom draft slots. - Preserve prior behavior when the runtime K is `None` or positive. Other speculator implementations accept the optional argument but do not act on it. ## Related work / duplicate check Searches for #51510 and MRV2 dynamic-K fixes found no other PR addressing this bug. #49652 is complementary, not duplicate. It fixes CUDA graph capture-shape derivation for autoregressive draft decode under dynamic SD. This PR carries the scheduler's runtime K into proposal execution and skips draft decode when that K is zero. A deployment using FULL CUDA graphs needs #49652's capture fix as well as this runtime behavior fix. ## Tests ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py -q ``` Result: `23 passed`. The new regression tests verify that: - K=0 still runs draft prefill but does not prepare or execute draft decode; - the K=0 proposal has shape `(num_requests, 0)`; - the scheduler-selected K reaches `speculator.propose()`; and - stale columns in the persistent draft buffer do not reach `DraftTokensHandler`. As a red/green check, removing the K=0 early return and active-width slice made the two new tests fail with width 2 instead of 0. Restoring the fix made them pass. ```bash uvx pre-commit run --files \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/multi_module_mtp/speculator.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py ``` Result: all applicable hooks passed. `git diff --check` passed. ## Benchmark 2× RTX 5090, ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B-FP8, MRV2, TP=2, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, and DSD `[[1,2,2],[3,16,0]]`: | Sessions | Before | After | Change | No-spec reference | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 107 t/s | 108 t/s | +1% | 107 t/s | | 4 | 193 t/s | 211 t/s | +9% | 209 t/s | | 8 | 364 t/s | 399 t/s | +10% | 393 t/s | At one session the schedule selects K=2, so no K=0 improvement is expected. At four and eight sessions, K=0 is active. Instrumentation showed that the unpatched path spent approximately 7 ms on two unused draft-decode passes per K=0 step. ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with analysis, code drafting, and test drafting. I reviewed the changes and validation results and can explain and maintain the patch.

signal.title: [Perf] Cache streaming parser drop metadata
signal.text: ## Summary - cache immutable special-token drop metadata used by streaming parser engines - key the bounded cache by the config and tokenizer content the builder actually reads - verify equivalent per-request parser configs hit the cache ## Why `StreamingParserEngine` is created per request, while its config and tokenizer contents are effectively engine-wide. Each construction currently recompiles escaped special-token regexes and rebuilds the same immutable `LexerShape`. In the originating B200 profile at a batch around 975, parser construction accounted for 1.9% of engine-thread samples, primarily in this builder. The cache is content-keyed rather than object-identity-keyed, so equivalent config instances share an entry and tokenizer special-token changes naturally miss. It is capped at 64 entries. ## Duplicate check I searched open vLLM PRs for `build drop info reasoning parser cache` and `_build_drop_info`. I found no open PR changing or caching this path; the broad search results were unrelated model, parser-regression, and kernel work. ## Measured performance A pinned-hardware Nebius B200 A/B (`qwen35_per_request_patch_ab_2026-08-06.md`) used an Intel Xeon Platinum 8580 host, structured mode, 1,000 concurrency, and 180-second unprofiled runs: - Output throughput was **11,857 → 11,890 tok/s (+0.28%)**, inside the independently measured **0.32% noise floor**; both arms had zero errors. - In separate py-spy captures, `_build_drop_info` fell **1.5% → 0 samples** of the EngineCore main thread. Its `_get_reasoner` parent fell **1.9% → 0.4%**. - `scheduler.schedule` fell **33.5% → 32.0%**, while `gpu_wait` rose **9.7% → 12.1%**, consistent with the removed CPU work becoming main-thread slack on an already GPU-saturated workload. The benchmark used the SafetyKit memo implementation rather than this bounded `lru_cache`, but it memoized the same pure `_build_drop_info` result. The unambiguous result is removal of the targeted parser-construction work; the +0.28% throughput delta is noise, not a claimed serving-throughput win. ## Validation - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py -q` — 38 passed - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q` — 3,738 passed - targeted Ruff check and format hooks — passed - commit-time pre-commit suite — passed The planned Nebius validation adds a serving-level reasoning/tool-call corpus comparison and an A/B/A high-concurrency profile to confirm output identity and reduced parser initialization samples. ## AI assistance This change was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand and defend the implementation, and run the listed Nebius validation before marking the PR ready.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Propagate decode SWA index width for DSpark + FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4
signal.text: DSpark non-causal draft batches allocate `decode_swa_indices` with `noncausal_index_width` (wider than `window_size`). FlashInfer DSV4 sparse MLA still reshaped / passed `self.window_size` into `build_flashinfer_mixed_sparse_indices`, which crashes those drafts, e.g.: ``` RuntimeError: shape '[7, 128]' is invalid for input of size 1792 (at `flashinfer_sparse.py` `_build_sparse_index_metadata` when reshaping `decode_swa_indices`). ``` - Add `decode_swa_width` to `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata` and set it in the SWA builder (`window_size` or `noncausal_index_width`). - Use that width in FlashInfer `_build_sparse_index_metadata` and the ROCM ragged conversion path. ## Test Plan - [x] `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py` - [x] Manual: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark with `attention_backend: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Model] Add Orthrus model support
signal.text: ## Summary Adds first-class Orthrus checkpoint support for vLLM's standard autoregressive serving path. - Adds an `OrthrusConfig` so `model_type="orthrus"` checkpoints can load without requiring remote config code. - Registers `OrthrusLM` and `OrthrusForCausalLM` as text-generation architectures. - Adds an Orthrus model implementation based on Qwen3, including the extra Orthrus diffusion projection/norm parameters so public Orthrus checkpoints can map their weights. - Adds focused config and registry coverage for the public `chiennv/Orthrus-Qwen3-1.7B` checkpoint family. This PR intentionally does not expose Orthrus diffusion-mode speculative decoding yet. That path needs additional scheduler/attention metadata work to share the autoregressive KV cache with diffusion queries safely. The implementation uses vLLM's normal AR model path. Addresses part of #43786. ## Duplicate-work check Required checks were run before opening this PR: - `gh issue view 43786 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments` showed no existing implementation discussion in the CLI output. - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "43786 in:body"` returned no open PRs. - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Orthrus speculative decoding"` returned no open PRs. ## Tests - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_orthrus_config.py -v` passed. - `.venv/bin/python -c 'from vllm.model_executor.models import is_text_generation_model; from vllm.model_executor.models.registry import ModelRegistry; cls = ModelRegistry._try_load_model_cls("OrthrusLM"); assert cls is not None; assert is_text_generation_model(cls); cls2 = ModelRegistry._try_load_model_cls("OrthrusForCausalLM"); assert cls2 is cls; print("Orthrus registry import ok")'` passed. - `.venv/bin/python -c 'from tests.models.registry import HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS; from vllm.model_executor.models.registry import ModelRegistry; missing = ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs() - HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS.get_supported_archs(); assert not missing, missing; print("registry coverage ok")'` passed. - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/models/registry.py tests/transformers_utils/test_orthrus_config.py vllm/model_executor/models/orthrus.py vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py vllm/transformers_utils/config.py vllm/transformers_utils/configs/__init__.py vllm/transformers_utils/configs/orthrus.py` passed. ## AI assistance codex

signal.title: [Feature]: split local/external prefix-cache hits in prompt_tokens_details  #52137
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR adds full support for exposing **local vs external prefix‑cache hits** across the OpenAI chat and completion endpoints. vLLM already tracks `num_local_cached_tokens` and `num_external_cached_tokens` internally, but only the summed `cached_tokens` reached the serving layer. This PR completes the data plumbing so users can see the full breakdown in both streaming and non‑streaming responses. This resolves the feature request to expose distributed prefix‑cache source information for observability, debugging, and pricing use cases. ### Summary of changes **Engine / Core** - Added `num_local_cached_tokens` and `num_external_cached_tokens` to `RequestState`. - Forwarded both fields from `prefill_stats` in `OutputProcessor`. - Added the same fields to `RequestOutput` so offline `LLM().generate()` users receive them. **OpenAI Protocol** - Extended `PromptTokenUsageInfo` with `local_cached_tokens` and `external_cached_tokens`. - Fixed docstring placement so `multimodal_tokens` retains its documentation and new fields have their own. **Chat Endpoint** - Added support for both fields in streaming and non‑streaming paths. - Updated `_make_prompt_tokens_details` to make new parameters optional, preserving existing test calls. **Completion Endpoint** - Added streaming support: capture local/external cached tokens on first iteration and populate them in the final usage chunk. - Added non‑streaming support in `request_output_to_completion_response`. **Tests** - Added streaming + non‑streaming tests for both chat and completion endpoints. - Reused existing mock helpers instead of introducing new ones. - Added invariant checks: `cached_tokens == local_cached_tokens + external_cached_tokens`. - Generalized `_collect_metrics_stream_chunks` to accept a `RequestOutput`. --- Tests added: - Chat: streaming + non‑streaming breakdown tests, helper‑level tests, invariant checks. - Completion: streaming + non‑streaming breakdown tests, invariant checks. All new fields behave correctly across: - streaming and non‑streaming - chat and completion - offline `LLM().generate()` - OpenAI protocol responses --- ## Test Result - **Chat tests:** 37 passed - **Completion tests:** 27 passed - **ruff check + format:** clean A teardown error from `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` occurs due to CPU‑only Windows environment and is unrelated to the changes. All invariants hold and all endpoints correctly surface the new fields. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results. </details>

signal.title: [XPU][Bugfix] Fix XPU crash with speculative decoding + prefix caching in Mamba models
signal.text: ## Purpose Model tested: cyankiwi/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ-INT4 HW Backend: XPU Hardware: Intel ARC Pro B70 vllm version: 0.27.1 If I only enable prefix caching, I see no error and vllm can process requests. If I only use spec decoding(MTP) that works fine too. But if I use both together I get following error: ``` ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long File "vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 767, in initialize_from_forward_context self.state_base_addrs[idx] = state.data_ptr() ``` Root cause: On XPU, `tensor.data_ptr()` can return memory addresses >= 2^63 — exceeding the signed `int64` range. The `MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext` class stores these addresses via element-wise assignment (`tensor[idx] = value`), which fails because PyTorch's `__setitem__` converts the scalar through C-level long() before any dtype check, regardless of the tensor's declared dtype. Fix applied: Two changes, both in `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`: 1. Change dtype from int64 to uint64 for state_base_addrs and block_table_ptrs — matching the existing pattern in block_table.py (# NOTE(woosuk): Use uint64 instead of int64 to cover all possible addresses). 2. Collect pointers into a list and bulk-create the tensor instead of element-wise assignment. torch.tensor(list, dtype=torch.uint64) correctly handles large pointer values; tensor[idx] = large_int does not (even with uint64 dtype). ## Test Plan Re-build and run the same model with both `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` and `--enable-prefix-caching`. Send a request and it should not throw following error. signal.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Preserve token IDs in non-streaming engine parsing
signal.text: ## Purpose Non-streaming serving already passes the generated token IDs to `Parser.parse()`, but `DelegatingParser` discarded them before invoking its reasoning and tool parser-engine adapters. The fallback text-only parse could therefore mistake ordinary text such as `[TOOL_CALLS]` or `[TOOL_RESULTS]` for a structural Mistral v11 token. This change keeps the original model text aligned with its token IDs and parses it once when the active reasoning and tool adapters use the same parser engine, or when only an engine tool parser is configured. Tool-only parsing starts in `CONTENT`, and `tool_choice="none"` still suppresses tool calls while preserving literal marker text. The shared `ParserEngine.parse()` method remains the public non-streaming entry point. A protected `_parse_non_streaming()` hook lets Mistral retain its pre-v11 JSON-array extraction without duplicating request initialization or tool-call conversion. Mixed/legacy parser combinations keep the existing text fallback; this PR does not pair transformed content with the original full token-ID span. ### Duplicate-work check I searched open issues and PRs using `Mistral v11 non-streaming markers`, `TOOL_RESULTS`, `TOOL_CALLS`, `parser engine token IDs`, and `non-streaming tool parser`. No open issue or PR covers this non-streaming token/text identity bug. PR #46529 identified the same general token-ID loss, but it remained a draft and was closed without merge. It added parallel token-ID methods to several reasoning/tool parser interfaces and attempted a two-stage handoff of rewritten content plus separately sliced IDs. This PR instead uses the existing `Parser.parse(..., model_output_token_ids=...)` contract and performs one pass only where both phases share the same engine (or only the engine tool parser is present), avoiding an expanded legacy interface and potentially misaligned text/ID pairs. PR #46843 subsequently merged the serving-side plumbing in three entrypoint files, so the current base already supplies token IDs; it does not make `DelegatingParser` consume them. The current Mistral engine-adapter path was merged later in #48947 and was not part of #46529. The closest open PRs are adjacent but non-duplicating: - #48320 fixes Mistral v11 streaming boundaries when content and multiple tool calls arrive in one delta. - #42868 skips tool parsing for streaming `tool_choice="none"`. - #50015 seeds Gemma4 non-streaming state from the prompt. ## Test Plan The regression coverage uses the public `ParserManager`/`DelegatingParser.parse` path and supplies text plus precisely aligned token IDs. It verifies: - literal `[TOOL_CALLS]` and `[TOOL_RESULTS]` text inside Mistral v11 arguments; - literal marker preservation with `tool_choice="none"`; - tool-only parsing beginning in `CONTENT`; - pre-v11 Mistral JSON-array behavior; - all registered same-engine reasoning/tool adapter replay samples. Commands: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py -q PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/tool_use/mistral/test_mistral_tool_calls.py -q -k ministral-3b .venv/bin/pre-commit run ``` ## Test Result Before the fix, ordinary marker text encoded as normal tokens was interpreted from its decoded spelling: `[TOOL_CALLS]` could split one call into two, while `[TOOL_RESULTS]` could be silently removed. The token-aware direct engine parse returned the expected single call. With this change: ```text tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py: 101 passed tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py: 892 passed tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py: 147 passed Ministral-3B tool-use evaluation: 7 passed, 7 deselected pre-commit: all hooks passed ``` ### Model evaluation The repository's Mistral tool-use E2E suite was run with `mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512` on an NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti (16 GiB). All seven selected cases passed, covering named, auto, required, none, no-tools, tool-result, parallel, streaming, and non-streaming behavior as provided by the suite. `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` was used because the local runner did not have a CUDA toolkit for FlashInfer JIT compilation. The exact literal-marker regression additionally uses the pinned `mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506` tokenizer revision `95a6d26c4bfb886c58daf9d3f7332c857cb27b43`. The 24B weights were not loaded on the 16 GiB development GPU; parser behavior was validated with the real tokenizer and aligned generated-token fixtures. ### AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex was used. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR is described. - [x] Test commands are provided. - [x] Regression and E2E results are provided. - [x] Duplicate work and #46529 are addressed. - [x] AI assistance is disclosed. - [x] The human submitter reviewed every changed line and verified the results. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][Structured Output][Spec Decode] Validate accepted blocks before commit
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #43338. this fix was done by 5.6-sol, fixes problems on ds4 flash. Structured-output requests using speculative decoding must satisfy this commit invariant: > Request history and grammar state advance through the same longest > grammar-valid token prefix. Any rejected suffix remains schedulable for > resampling. At `main@ac2ae8798c7ef59c1924d5c0447a4279fa645770`, the scheduler appends the verifier's accepted token block to request history before `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens()` checks the block. Prospective grammar masks reduce the chance of an invalid token, but they cannot establish the commit invariant when one accepted block crosses either of these state transitions: 1. deferred grammar activation at the end of model reasoning; 2. grammar termination before the final accepted token in the block. The invalid suffix is therefore already visible in request state when `accept_tokens()` rejects it. Depending on the serving path, that produces an invalid structured response or terminates the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`. This PR validates accepted multi-token structured-output blocks before `Scheduler._update_request_with_output()` mutates request history. It uses the non-advancing `StructuredOutputGrammar.validate_tokens()` interface, commits only the valid prefix, and leaves the existing post-commit path as the sole grammar-state advancement operation. ### Resulting behavior - Reasoning content through a deferred end marker remains unconstrained. - Tokens after the marker must form a valid grammar prefix. - Blocks sampled after reasoning has ended are validated in full, including suffixes that follow grammar termination. - Rejected suffix tokens decrement `num_computed_tokens` and asynchronous output placeholders so they can be sampled again. - Speculative metrics count only committed draft tokens. Rejecting only the target-sampled tail does not reduce the accepted-draft count. - Unstructured requests, stale outputs, non-speculative output, and single-token output blocks retain their existing fast paths. Reasoning-boundary detection exposes prior request tokens through a read-only concatenated `Sequence`; it does not copy the committed history. A block that does not contain a boundary requires one parser call. A block that contains a boundary is scanned through cumulative delta prefixes, which supports single-token markers, multi-token markers, and markers split across scheduler steps. Each detection call uses an isolated copy of the request-scoped parser, so a stateful parser cannot consume its transition before the standard post-commit path observes it. ## Provenance and related work The state boundary is produced by the composition of two supported features, not by a single isolated regression: - #14702, merge commit `34120f5acd693924cc783dfaa33733afbe9ae8b0`, enabled structured output with speculative decoding and introduced per-position grammar-mask simulation. - #16577, merge commit `2fc9075b82e05007f460992b3f9d42d2746c41cb`, deferred structured-output grammar activation while a request is reasoning. Several changes cover narrower parts of the lifecycle: - #36138, head commit `94f4dc2e98d63dc1a3ff7cca2b35a9235df667e1`, detects reasoning activation inside a speculative window but does not establish pre-commit validation. - #44297, merge commit `e7c9df944969c251bdceed7b9d7bbcc7fec3639b`, constrains scheduled rows after a reasoning boundary, including the bonus row. It operates prospectively on scheduled draft candidates, not on the authoritative verifier result. - #44993, merge commit `0416dab275d51327b331a1c6baaec754a68d7764`, advances grammar state across an accepted reasoning boundary. The accepted block is still appended before grammar acceptance. - #45560, merge commit `dc818c198d3ff50a16f38eba567da006478239c8`, constrains GPT-OSS through a Harmony structural-tag grammar active from token zero. It is specific to the GPT-OSS path and does not cover deferred reasoning parsers or grammar termination for other models. - #43424, commit `4e96809853442f1cf9dacf83f166fc32482b6632`, supplies the pre-commit design used for the reasoning-boundary case. This PR credits its author and extends the contract to every accepted structured speculative block, avoids copying committed history, isolates stateful reasoning probes, updates speculative metrics, and covers grammar termination. A boundary-only build still fails the qualified runtime test. - #51870, commit `c3573d92f69cda2d42d3e74f80f00d0e932e5010`, replaces a mutating operation during draft-window mask simulation. It intentionally does not alter accepted output or scheduler accounting. - #48200, commit `21265a9a4841812b5088cb062fc5356abcb979d9`, refactors structured-output management. Its scheduler still appends `new_token_ids` before accepting them into the grammar, so the commit invariant remains separate from that refactor. The scope difference from #43424 is also recorded in #43338: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43338#issuecomment-5302532715 ## Compatibility and limitations - The patch changes Python scheduler and grammar-management code only. It does not change model kernels, sampling distributions, API schemas, or compiled components. - XGrammar and Guidance have direct backend tests. Outlines and LM Format Enforcer implement the same non-advancing, longest-prefix `validate_tokens()` interface but do not have model-serving qualification in this PR. - Runtime qualification uses XGrammar 0.2.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and DSpark K5. Other speculative methods exercise the same scheduler interface, but their model-serving behavior was not separately benchmarked. - The additional work is bounded by the accepted speculative block length. The reasoning-only path performs one parser check, and request history is not copied by the manager. - A direct Step3.5 parser test verifies that pre-commit boundary detection does not consume the parser's pending-transition state. ## Test Plan ```bash uvx --from pre-commit pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py \ vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py \ tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py \ tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py ``` The tests cover: - XGrammar and Guidance rejection at a reasoning boundary; - rejection after grammar completion; - multi-token markers within a block and across committed/new token storage; - constant-history sequence access and one-check reasoning-only behavior; - preservation of request-local state in a Step3.5 reasoning parser; - synchronous and asynchronous rollback for bonus-only, partial-draft, and complete-block rejection; - speculative acceptance totals and per-position metrics; - scheduler commit, emitted output, and grammar advancement through one identical filtered prefix; - bypass behavior for unstructured requests. ## Test Result ### Source qualification - Repository pre-commit hooks: passed, including Ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, and configuration checks. - Four relevant pytest modules: `207 passed` in 89.47 seconds. - `git diff --check`: passed. Negative control at `main@ac2ae8798c7ef59c1924d5c0447a4279fa645770`: - four XGrammar/Guidance boundary and termination tests fail because accepted blocks have no pre-commit validation; - the scheduler behavior test commits `[10, 11, 12]` instead of the valid prefix `[10, 11]`. The same five discriminator cases pass with commit `20c2def63adceb4af700386b29ad74d39e847213`. ### Model-serving qualification Runtime conditions: ```text model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 topology: TP2 / DCP1 target backend: B12X W4A8 speculative decoding: fixed probabilistic DSpark K5 structured-output backend: XGrammar 0.2.5 scheduler: asynchronous CUDA graph row cap: 48 concurrency: 8 ``` The runtime branch contains #44297 and #44993. The accepted-block validation is the source change in local-inference-lab/vllm#320. - Unfiltered source fails the deterministic growing strict-tool test by round 11. - A boundary-only filter fails at round 29 when a speculative suffix follows grammar termination. - Complete-block validation finishes 32 rounds and 256 HTTP requests at up to 225,634 prompt tokens per request. Of those responses, 255 contain one schema-valid tool call. One response reaches its configured 768-token output limit while still reasoning and reproduces that output-limit result on retry. - The committed source composition passes 24/24 deterministic strict-tool requests: eight buffered or streaming requests at C1 and 16 requests at C8. - An independently supplied 282,817-byte request payload returns one valid JSON tool call in each of eight concurrent replays. - Ordinary no-tool C1 decode measures 194.3 tok/s. Same-host controls with the same launch profile measure 194.02-194.81 tok/s, so no throughput regression is measurable at the precision of those runs. Reproducible image: ```text tag: voipmonitor/vllm:infernal-invocation-vllm91e2adf-b12xec2f97d-fi1ac6942-cu133-torch213-20260815-r14 digest: sha256:9fe1d1b0e8370df578f92c6431af41a9fc36076ccbebac18c77a8ae99a3454e3 ``` Detailed serving evidence: - https://github.com/local-inference-lab/vllm/pull/320 - https://github.com/local-inference-lab/rtx6kpro/blob/master/models/ds4dspark-infernal-invocation-r14.md - https://github.com/local-inference-lab/rtx6kpro/issues/67 ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex assisted with source analysis, implementation, tests, negative controls, and PR drafting. The human submitter is responsible for the change and must complete line-by-line review before marking this draft ready for maintainer review. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] Purpose and affected invariant are specified. - [x] Test commands and results are included. - [x] Model-serving evaluation is included because output correctness changes. - [x] Related and partially overlapping PRs are distinguished. - [x] No user documentation change is required; the patch preserves the public API and corrects an internal commit invariant. </details>

signal.title: [V1] Fix CPU sampler ignoring request seeds in mixed batches (#51226)
signal.text: Correct the logic check in TopKTopPSampler.forward_cpu to ensure we only skip to the compiled unseeded random sampler if all requests in the batch have no custom generators (seeds). If even one request in the batch has a seed, we fall back to the native path to correctly isolate and apply each request's seed generator. Also make uvloop optional in llm/v1/utils.py to allow importing and running test suites on Windows/macOS. ## Purpose Fixes issue #51226. Currently, `TopKTopPSampler.forward_cpu` selects the compiled unseeded random sampler whenever `len(generators) != batch_size`. This causes request-specific seeds to be completely ignored on CPU when running in a batch alongside unseeded requests. This PR changes the check to `len(generators) == 0` so that the compiled unseeded sampler is only used when no request in the batch is seeded. If any request is seeded, the sampler falls back to the native Gumbel sampling path which correctly applies the request generators. Additionally, this PR makes the `uvloop` import in `vllm/v1/utils.py` optional (falling back to standard library `asyncio`) so that vLLM V1 can be imported and unit-tested on Windows/macOS. ## Test Plan I added the unit test `test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding` in `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py` which creates a batch of two requests (one seeded, one unseeded) and verifies that the seeded request remains fully deterministic across runs while the unseeded request remains non-deterministic. Run the test command: $env:PYTHONPATH="."; .venv\Scripts\python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -v -k test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding ## Test Result tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py::test_cpu_sampler_mixed_seeding PASSED [100%] =================== 1 passed, 131 deselected in 3.08s =================== --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Kimi-K3] MoRIIO KV transfer of hybrid mamba/KDA (conv+ssm) recurrent state (READ + WRITE)
signal.text: ## Purpose Enable MoRIIO 1P1D disaggregated serving for a **hybrid attention + mamba/KDA model running a speculative drafter**. The core of the PR transfers the KDA (Kimi Delta Attention / GDN linear-attention) **conv+ssm recurrent state** alongside the existing attention/MLA KV — without it the decoder starts from an uninitialised recurrent state. The other four commits are what end-to-end bring-up turned out to require; each is small and independently justified: | commit | what it does | without it | |---|---|---| | 1 | transfer the conv+ssm recurrent state (READ + WRITE), per-region sessions, `SupportsHMA` block-group split, producer-side N-1 truncation | hybrid decode starts from empty recurrent state | | 2 | reconcile decode-side geometry under a drafter: lookahead-extended block list, draft-only layers, spec align window | session build raises `KeyError`, or reads land in the wrong slots | | 3 | exclude draft-only buckets when choosing the KV-cache group size | prefill and decode group their mamba layers differently, so the two sides disagree on transfer geometry | | 4 | allow per-layer KV block length instead of asserting one uniform `block_size` | registration aborts: `block size mismatch ... 1536 != 3072` | | 5 | wait for **every** layer's read before the forward, batched, with load-error reporting | a request is judged by one transfer status and can run against KV still in flight | The recurrent-state slot rides the existing `remote_block_ids` channel as `[attn, mamba]`, so the disaggregation router needs **no model-specific changes**. Commit 3 is the only one outside the connector; it keys on the existing `non_causal_multi_token_decode` spec flag, which has a single producer in-tree and defaults to `False`, and it excludes a bucket only when *all* of its specs are marked — so a model without a drafter takes a bit-identical path. ## Test Plan - Unit (CPU): MoRIIO layout geometry, HMA scheduler split / N-1 accounting / offset-cache equivalence, `as_attn_mamba` round-trips, and transfer-completion semantics across both mori generations. - E2E: real Kimi-K3 MXFP4 weights, MI355X (gfx950), ROCm + AITER, **TP8 per leg, 1P1D cross-node over RDMA**, fp8 KV cache, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs, speculative decoding on both legs. - GSM8K 5-shot (`lm_eval`, `gsm8k.yaml`) through the disaggregation proxy, with a **matched single-engine control** on the same image and config, so the disaggregated number has a meaningful reference. - Draft-acceptance sweeps over prompt length, concurrency and multi-turn prefix reuse, against the pair and against a single engine on a dedicated node, since a transferred recurrent state can be wrong in ways that accuracy on short prompts would not reveal. ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_wait_all.py ``` ## Test Result **Unit:** 69 passed. **GSM8K 5-shot, full dataset (1319 questions), concurrency 32**, every arm running the same connector code so that only the transfer mode and the mori build differ: | arm | mori batched wait | exact_match | |---|---|---| | single engine, same image (control) | — | 0.9674 | | 1P1D **READ** | available | **0.9689** | | 1P1D **WRITE** | available | **0.9689** | | 1P1D **READ** | absent → Python-poll fallback | **0.9666** | | 1P1D **WRITE** | absent → Python-poll fallback | **0.9674** | The four disaggregated arms span 0.9666–0.9689, i.e. **three questions out of 1319**, with the single-engine control at 0.9674 sitting inside that span and a standard error of ±0.0048 (≈6 questions) on each. Disaggregated serving is therefore at parity with a single engine, and the two wait paths are indistinguishable. `strict-match` and `flexible-extract` agreed on every arm except fallback WRITE, where they differ by one question (0.9674 / 0.9682). Remaining misses are model arithmetic errors on coherent output, not transfer corruption. Which path was live was read from the logs rather than assumed (`MoRIIO batched transfer wait (wait_all) available: True|False`). **Disaggregation verified from engine counters**, not assumed: on the full run the prefill leg served 1320 requests, *all* `finished_reason=length` with exactly 1320 generation tokens — one per request, i.e. the handoff — while the decode leg served 1320 with `finished_reason=stop` and 151,921 generation tokens, with zero aborts, errors or preemptions on either side. ### Draft acceptance Accuracy alone is a weak signal for the recurrent-state transfer: the decoder recomputes the last prompt token locally, so a slightly wrong `h` can still produce a correct answer. Draft acceptance is far more sensitive, because the drafter conditions on the same state and a corrupted `h` shows up immediately as rejected proposals. With `num_speculative_tokens=2` the ceiling is an acceptance length of 3.0. Measured on the decode leg over the GSM8K runs above: | arm | mean acceptance length | per-position accept | |---|---|---| | 1P1D READ, batched wait | 2.68 | 0.92 / 0.76 | | 1P1D WRITE, batched wait | 2.66 | — | | 1P1D READ, poll fallback | 2.77 | — | | 1P1D WRITE, poll fallback | 2.77 | — | A drafter reading a corrupted recurrent state lands near 1.0 (every proposal rejected), so 2.66–2.77 across all four arms says the transferred state is usable, not merely close enough to keep the answer right. ### Long context, concurrency, and multi-turn prefix reuse GSM8K prompts are ~1k tokens and single-turn, which exercises none of the paths where a recurrent state is hardest to get right: chunked prefill over a long prompt, several requests interleaving their mamba slots, and a partial prefix-cache hit where only part of the prompt is recomputed. Each was measured directly, comparing the pair against a single engine on a dedicated node running the same build. Acceptance is computed per request from the `vllm:spec_decode_num_{drafts,draft_tokens,accepted_tokens}_total` counters read either side of it; two repeats per cell, 256 output tokens, coherent prose. Prompt length, one request in flight: | prompt tokens | single engine | 1P1D READ | |---|---|---| | 1,069 | 2.59 / 2.60 | 2.44 / 2.59 | | 7,785 | 2.22 / 2.31 | 2.27 / 2.62 | | 31,119 | 2.66 / 2.64 | 2.65 / 2.31 | | 99,116 | 2.62 / 2.62 | 2.59 / 2.69 | Acceptance is flat in prompt length and the two arms are indistinguishable at every size, including 99k tokens where prefill is chunked into many passes and the recurrent state must be snapshotted at the final chunk. **Scope:** homogeneous TP between prefill and decode (heterogeneous TP is gated with `NotImplementedError`); both legs must run the same speculative config, since the recurrent-state transfer handles symmetric grouping only; validated on one GPU family. ## Essential Elements checklist - [x] Purpose clearly stated. - [x] Test plan included. - [x] Test results included (unit + real-weights 1P1D E2E with a matched control). - [x] No router-side / proxy changes required; backward compatible with existing MoRIIO deployments. - [x] Models without a drafter are unaffected by the KV-grouping change.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Guard tool call argument JSON parsing in chat message postprocessing
signal.text: Fixes #47761 ## Purpose `_postprocess_messages` in `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py` re-parses the `arguments` string of every assistant tool call a client replays. That parse is unguarded, so an `arguments` value that is not a valid JSON object takes down the request. The important part is that the offending value lives in **conversation history**. The client replays the same assistant message on every subsequent turn and receives the same error each time, so the conversation is unrecoverable rather than merely degraded. The only way out is to discard the session. ### Two independent triggers, one chokepoint | | Reporter | Surface | Model | Cause | Payload | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | @rnogueira-tech | Chat Completions | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 | Generation hit `max_tokens` mid-string | 18,356 chars, later 36,946 chars | | 2 | @iMMIQ | Responses (non-Harmony Simple path) | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Generation stopped at EOS with the string still open | 54 bytes, 297 output tokens | Observed on 0.24.0 and 0.25.1. The two failures are mechanically identical, down to the offsets. Trigger 1's payload begins `{"contents": "` and reports *Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 14 (char 13)*. Trigger 2's begins `{"cmd": "` and reports *line 1 column 9 (char 8)*. In both cases the offset is exactly the index of the opening quote of the value that never closes. They do not share an upstream cause, and no single upstream fix covers both: - Reporting `finish_reason: "length"` on cap-truncated tool calls would not have caught trigger 2, where no cap was involved. - Validating on the Responses Simple path would not have caught trigger 1, which is Chat Completions streaming. `_postprocess_messages` is the only point where both converge, which is why the fix belongs here regardless of what else gets fixed upstream. ### Neither case is a client bug In both reports vLLM generated the malformed string and then reported the tool call as complete: - Trigger 1: generation was cut mid-string by the token cap, and `finish_reason` was reported as `"tool_calls"`, not `"length"`. - Trigger 2: generation stopped at EOS with the string open, and `emit_simple_tool_call_done` emitted the item with `status: "completed"` and no JSON validation. The clients replayed the assistant message they were handed. Reconstructing trigger 1's arguments from the SSE deltas and comparing against the replayed request gives 18,356 bytes on both sides, md5 `d1be3623820564162172c1f5ebff5893` — byte-identical. ### What was ruled out | Hypothesis | Result | |---|---| | Tool parser serialising invalid JSON | Ruled out. `qwen3_coder`, `qwen3_xml` and `mimo` all resolve to `Qwen3EngineToolParser`; `_qwen3_arg_converter` returns `json.dumps(params, ensure_ascii=False)` for both full and partial output | | Client mis-escaping the payload | Ruled out by the byte-identity check above | | Chat template or `--reasoning-parser` configuration | Ruled out; reporter tried `hermes`, `qwen3_xml`, custom templates, and `enable_thinking: false` | | Version regression | Ruled out; reproduced on 0.23.0, 0.24.0 and 0.25.1 | | Raising `max_tokens` as a workaround | Insufficient. 16384 overflows the 32768 context window; 8192 reproduces the same failure at the new cap | ### What this PR changes In `_postprocess_messages`, only `dict` values now reach `function["arguments"]`: - A malformed `arguments` string is coerced to `{}` and a warning is logged with the tool name and payload length. - A value that parses to valid JSON but is not an object (`"[]"`, `"42"`, `"true"`, `'"hello"'`) is also coerced to `{}` with a warning. - Dict values and valid JSON object strings are unchanged. - Missing, empty or `"null"` arguments continue to become `{}`. The payload itself is never logged; the linked issue's payloads contain user source code. ### Design note: coercion vs 400 on the malformed branch An earlier revision of this PR passed the original string through on the failure path. That was wrong and has been removed — chat templates require a mapping, `examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja` raises explicitly on a string, `toolace` and the pythonic templates raise `TypeError`, and `gemma3_pythonic` iterates character by character. Thanks to @bbrowning for the concrete example and to @zqzten for the wider template survey. As of the latest push, this PR and #50861 behave identically on every branch except one: when the JSON is **malformed**, #50861 raises `VLLMValidationError` → 400, and this PR coerces to `{}` with a warning. That branch decides whether #47761 is fixed or relabelled, and this PR coerces for three reasons. 1. **A 400 does not resolve #47761.** The malformed value is in history, so the client replays it every turn and receives the same rejection indefinitely. On the routes in that issue the current behaviour is already a 400, since `json.JSONDecodeError` subclasses `ValueError`. Raising `VLLMValidationError` gives a clearer message for the same dead conversation. 2. **Coercion is already the established pattern.** #43862 (merged) coerces `arguments: "null"` to `{}`. #47555 extends that to scalars, #50861 to lists. Malformed JSON is the same category of unusable input, and currently the only member singled out for a hard failure. 3. **The malformed data originates from vLLM in both reported cases,** and was reported to the client as complete. Clients should not have to re-validate JSON the server has declared finished. That is the only open question left on this PR, and I'm happy to implement whichever behaviour maintainers prefer. ### Scope Deliberately not in this PR, to keep it single-purpose. Both will be filed separately: - Reporting `finish_reason: "length"` when a tool call is truncated by the token cap. - Validating before `emit_simple_tool_call_done` writes `status: "completed"` on the Responses Simple path, plus the missing done event @iMMIQ observed. Related work on the same function: #43862 (merged), #47555, #50861, and #50997 for the Anthropic path. ## Test Plan Unit tests in `tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py` covering: - dict arguments pass through unchanged - valid JSON object string parses normally - malformed JSON from trigger 2, the captured payload `'{"cmd": "mkdir -p /tmp/mmadtest && cat > /tmp/mmadtest'`, coerces to `{}` - malformed JSON at truncation scale, a representative ~18 KB payload cut mid-string, coerces to `{}` - valid but non-object values `"[]"`, `"42"`, `"true"`, `'"hello"'`, `"null"` coerce to `{}` - missing, `None` and empty arguments coerce to `{}` - a warning is logged on coercion and includes the tool name, and no warning is logged for valid dict arguments - with two tool calls in one message, only the malformed one is coerced The two malformed cases use the payload shapes captured in #47761: a tool call cut mid-string by the token cap, and one cut at an EOS token. The behaviour can also be confirmed against a running server without a GPU and without generating anything, since `_postprocess_messages` runs before sampling. Reproducer contributed by @iMMIQ: ```bash curl -sS http://VLLM_HOST:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "ANY_MODEL", "max_tokens": 1, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [ {"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "foo", "arguments": "{\"cmd\": \"mkdir -p /tmp/x"}} ]} ] }'

signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52434 `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8.create_weights` did not initialize the partition metadata consumed by `ParallelLMHead` weight loading. Initialize both partition-size attributes and add a focused regression test using the real `ParallelLMHead` type while mocking allocation and kernel setup. Duplicate-work check: on 2026-08-15, open-PR searches for `#52434`, the exact `ParallelLMHead` attribute failure, and the affected compressed-tensors FP8 scheme found no PR addressing this bug. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and test execution. The human submitter reviewed the resulting two-file diff and remains responsible for the change. ## Test Plan - Run the focused regression test before and after the implementation change. - Run the existing `ParallelLMHead`-related tests in `test_compressed_tensors.py`. - Run Ruff format/static checks and Git whitespace validation on the changed files. ## Test Result - Before the fix: focused regression failed as expected with `AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'output_size_per_partition'` (`1 failed, 47 deselected`). - On latest `origin/main` (`d4801990a`) after the fix: - `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv-test/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k w8a8_fp8_sets_partition_sizes_for_parallel_lm_head -q` -> `1 passed, 47 deselected`. - `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv-test/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k parallel_lm_head -q` -> `4 passed, 44 deselected`. - `ruff format --check` on both changed files -> `2 files already formatted`. - `ruff check` on both changed files -> `All checks passed!`. - `git diff --check` -> passed. - Model evaluation was not run: this change restores layer partition metadata during initialization and does not alter inference math or model outputs. The regression test mocks device allocation and kernel setup to isolate that behavior. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, including the issue it resolves. - [x] The test plan and commands. - [x] The before/after and related test results. - [x] Documentation update considered; none is needed for this internal bug fix. </details>

signal.title: [Bug] PR #36138 grammar-mask spec-decode fix doesn't handle multi-token reasoning boundaries (gpt-oss/openai_gptoss still bleeds; Qwen3 fixed)
signal.text: ## Symptom PR #36138 ("Grammar was ignored when reasoning ended within speculated tokens") fixes the spec-decode × structured-output bypass for reasoning parsers whose end marker is a **single token** (e.g., the `qwen3` parser's `</think>` — tested by the PR with Qwen/Qwen3-8B and confirmed by me with Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8). It does **not** fix parsers whose end marker is **multi-token** — most notably `gpt-oss` (`openai_gptoss`), where the boundary is `<|channel|>final<|message|>` (3-4 tokens after tokenization). Effect in practice: a vLLM build at PR #36138's HEAD SHA (`94f4dc2e98d63dc1a3ff7cca2b35a9235df667e1`) serving `openai/gpt-oss-120b` with EAGLE3 + `response_format: {type: "json_schema", strict: true}` still produces ~27% of responses with garbage-prefix-before-JSON (e.g. `**Best{...}`, `(no{...}`, `chunk_0{...}`) — identical pattern to pre-patch behavior. By contrast, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (using the `qwen3` reasoning parser) + MTP + the same patched vLLM shows **0% prefix-bleed**. ## Reproducer (gpt-oss, fails) ``` vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --reasoning-parser openai_gptoss \ --max-model-len 131072 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"model":"<eagle3-draft>","num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"eagle3","draft_tensor_parallel_size":1}' ``` Send a chat completion with `response_format: {type: "json_schema", json_schema: {strict: true, schema: {...}}}`. ~27% of responses come back with non-JSON prefixes glued to otherwise-valid JSON: `(no{"relevantChunkIds":[]}`, `**Best{"results":[...]}`, etc. ## Counter-test (Qwen3.6 with `qwen3` parser, works) Same vLLM build, same `response_format` request, with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 weights and the `qwen3` reasoning parser: ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_next_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' ``` **0% prefix-bleed across 150 production prompts.** Confirms the PR fix engages and works correctly for single-token boundaries. ## Root cause analysis The PR's transition detector in `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py::_find_reasoning_end_in_tokens` scans for the boundary only **within `spec_token_ids`** (the 2-5 token speculative batch): ```python def _find_reasoning_end_in_tokens(self, token_ids: list[int]) -> int | None: if self.reasoner is None or self.enable_in_reasoning: return None for i, token in enumerate(token_ids): prefix = token_ids[: i + 1] if self.reasoner.is_reasoning_end_streaming(prefix, [token]): return i return None ``` - For the `qwen3` parser (`</think>` = 1 token; covers Qwen3.x family including 3.6): the boundary token appears in `spec_token_ids` whenever the model crosses it. Detection works. - For `openai_gptoss` (`<|channel|>final<|message|>` = 3-4 tokens after tokenization): the full sequence is **almost never** fully contained in a 2-5 token spec batch. `is_reasoning_end_streaming(small_prefix)` falls back to the base `is_reasoning_end(small_prefix)` which scans the prefix in isolation — never finds the boundary. `is_reasoning_end_streaming(prior_context, spec_batch)` would be detectable IF the detector were passed prior context that includes the analysis-channel tokens preceding the spec batch. Currently it only sees `spec_token_ids`. ## What I tried that doesn't help I overrode `reasoning_start_str` / `reasoning_end_str` on the `GptossReasoningParser` to silence the auto-init warning and populate `ReasoningConfig._reasoning_end_token_ids`. This doesn't change the detector's behavior because `_find_reasoning_end_in_tokens` doesn't consume those token IDs — it calls `is_reasoning_end_streaming` directly on the small spec batch. ## Proposed fix direction `identify_constrained_draft_tokens` already has access to `request` (so it has `request.all_token_ids`). The detector could be passed the prior context: ```python def _find_reasoning_end_in_tokens( self, spec_token_ids: list[int], prior_token_ids: list[int] = None, # tokens already accepted before the spec batch ) -> int | None: if self.reasoner is None or self.enable_in_reasoning: return None prior = list(prior_token_ids or []) for i, token in enumerate(spec_token_ids): # Pass the cumulative input so multi-token boundaries can be detected # when they straddle the (prior, spec_batch) boundary. full_prefix = prior + spec_token_ids[: i + 1] if self.reasoner.is_reasoning_end_streaming(full_prefix, [token]): return i return None ``` Then `identify_constrained_draft_tokens` passes `request.all_token_ids` as `prior_token_ids` (the tokens accepted up to but excluding the spec batch). This generalizes the PR cleanly to multi-token boundaries without changing single-token behavior. ## Test data Run | Variant | Prefix-bled rate ---|---|--- N | gpt-oss + EAGLE3 + json_schema (pre-PR) | 51% (156/300) A | gpt-oss + EAGLE3 + PR coherent build | 27% (81/300) B | gpt-oss + EAGLE3 + PR + reasoning_start/end_str port | 26% (79/300) **C** | **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (`--reasoning-parser qwen3`) + MTP + PR coherent build** | **0% (0/150)** (N is the pre-PR baseline, A/B/C use a from-source build of PR head SHA `94f4dc2e`.) ## Build notes Anyone needing to reproduce: `vllm/docker/Dockerfile` builds cleanly at the PR SHA with `--build-arg RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false --build-arg torch_cuda_arch_list=9.0a --build-arg max_jobs=24 --build-arg nvcc_threads=2` on a 48-vcpu / 192GB box in ~40 min. The default `vllm-openai` target wheel is 630MB which exceeds the 500MB CI sanity threshold, hence the disable. cc @sfbemerk @njhill — original PR author and reviewer.

signal.title: [Bugfix][XPU] Skip oneCCL warm-up all_reduce when world_size == 1
signal.text: ## Purpose Skip the oneCCL warm-up all_reduce in `XPUWorker.init_device()` when `world_size == 1`. The warm-up is guarded only by `is_xccl_available()`, so single-device XPU serving still requires a working oneCCL communicator. On platforms where oneCCL cannot enumerate GPU topology this aborts engine startup, even though no collective is issued during inference. Fixes #52386 ## Test Plan - Single XPU (`--tensor-parallel-size 1`): server starts and serves; no behavioral change on hardware where oneCCL already worked, since the communicator is created lazily on first use. - Multi-XPU (`--tensor-parallel-size 2`): warm-up path unchanged. ## Test Result Verified on Intel Arc B390 (Xe3) with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, TP=1: engine starts, `/v1/chat/completions` returns correct output. Multi-device verification would be appreciated from someone with an Arc Pro B60/B70 system. Multi-device (`--tensor-parallel-size > 1`) is not covered by my hardware. The changed condition is a strict narrowing, so the warm-up still runs whenever more than one worker is present. Verification on an Arc Pro B60/B70 system would be appreciated.

CMake configuration. ## Purpose Implements one item from #9129: Warn that PTX builds are not currently supported (post [CI/Build] Per file CUDA Archs (improve wheel size and dev build times) #8845), currently if there is a +PTX in TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST this will be ignored.
