signal.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return all n choices from /inference/v1/generate
signal.text: FIX #52398 ## Purpose A non-streaming `POST /inference/v1/generate` with `sampling_params.n > 1` returns fewer than `n` choices, non-deterministically and without an error — the response is a well-formed `GenerateResponse`, the completions are simply missing. `/v1/completions` with the same `n` always returns `n`. Root cause, as diagnosed in the issue and confirmed here on `main`: `serve_tokens` set `output_kind` only for streaming, ```python if request.stream: sampling_params.output_kind = RequestOutputKind.DELTA ``` so non-streaming requests kept the `SamplingParams` default, `RequestOutputKind.CUMULATIVE`. `serve_tokens_full_generator` keeps only the last output it sees (`final_res = res` in the `async for`) and then iterates `final_res.outputs`. Under `CUMULATIVE` that last output carries only the sequences updated in that step, so sequences that finished earlier never reach `choices`. This is the outlier: `openai/completion/protocol.py:392`, `openai/chat_completion/protocol.py:738`, `openai/responses/protocol.py:448`, both speech-to-text protocols and `offline_utils.py:561` all use `DELTA if stream else FINAL_ONLY`. ## Test Plan `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_generate_returns_all_choices`, parametrized over `n = 2, 4`, asserts `len(choices) == n` and that the indices are exactly `0..n-1`. The existing tests in that file only ever request `n = 1`, which is why this went unnoticed. ## Test Result I have no GPU on this machine, so I could not run the `RemoteOpenAIServer`-backed suite locally — that run is CI's. What I did verify locally: the diagnosis against current `main` (the `CUMULATIVE` default reaching `serve_tokens_full_generator`, and the sibling entrypoints that already do this correctly), and `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on both files. The reporter's own numbers on the unpatched server, 10 runs per `n`, expected `{n: 10}`: ``` 2 {1: 6, 2: 4} 4 {2: 5, 3: 3, 4: 2} 8 {5: 2, 7: 5, 3: 1, 6: 2} ``` and they confirmed 10/10 correct for `n = 2/4/8` when `output_kind` is forced to `FINAL_ONLY` through the request body, which is exactly what this patch makes the default. ## Contribution notes (per `AGENTS.md`) - Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52398 in:body"`, `--search "output_kind"` and `--search "serve_tokens output_kind"` all return nothing; no other PR touches `scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py` for this. - Not a model-affecting change: it selects the `RequestOutputKind` used to assemble the response, so no eval results apply. - AI assistance was used in preparing this change. I reviewed every changed line, confirmed the root cause against `main` myself, and can defend it end-to-end. The uncertain part I want a reviewer's eye on is whether any caller depends on passing `output_kind` explicitly in `sampling_params` (the workaround in the issue); this makes `FINAL_ONLY` the default, and unlike the OpenAI-compat endpoints it still overrides an explicitly supplied value, which I kept for consistency with those endpoints rather than changing here.
signal.author: Chessing234

signal.title: [Core] DBO ++: Overlap TP all-reduce with compute
signal.text: ## Purpose ### TL;DR The overlap yield wrappers on `main` are inside the EP all-to-all path. TP all-reduce contributes a noticeable fraction of prefill latency (~19% on Qwen3-32B TP=4), with even higher communication cost on PCIe than NVLink systems. **Make TP all-reduce run in parallel with model compute, instead of serially.** On Qwen3-32B + TP=4 this delivers up to **−7.5%** prefill wall / **+8.1%** prefill throughput and **−4.4%** e2e wall / +4.6% e2el (matrix below). The mechanism is Dual-Batch Overlap (DBO): split a forward into two micro-batches and issue each ubatch's all-reduce on a separate CUDA stream while the other ubatch keeps using the compute stream. AR latency that today serializes with compute becomes **hidden behind** compute. ### What "AR ↔ compute overlap" looks like A single TP forward pass on `bs=4, pl=4096`, Qwen3-32B, looking at one TP rank's GPU streams (this is from the nsys traces attached in `Test Result` below; exact numbers, not sketches): ``` Without DBO (today, vllm0.21): compute_stream: [ GEMM_0 AR_0 GEMM_1 AR_1 GEMM_2 AR_2 ... ] wall = 1110 ms comm_stream: (unused) └────────── 1086 ms busy, AR is 248 ms inline ──────┘ With DBO (this PR): compute_stream: [ GEMM_0a GEMM_1a GEMM_2a ... GEMM_0b GEMM_1b ... ] wall = 1047 ms comm_stream: [ AR_0a AR_1a AR_2a ... AR_0b ... AR_Nb ] ↑ overlapped 95.7% with compute_stream ``` The AR kernels (`ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_bf16_RING_LL`) move from the compute stream to a dedicated comm stream and run **concurrently** with the next ubatch's GEMMs. 95.7% of AR kernel time is hidden behind compute. ### How DBO achieves this DBO is two-thread-per-rank micro-batching: 1. The forward is split into 2 ubatches (`UBatchSlice`) along the token axis. 2. Two Python threads run each ubatch's forward concurrently. They share GPU but use **two separate CUDA streams**: a `compute_stream` and a `comm_stream`. 3. Every TP all-reduce site (`tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`) yields between the two threads: - thread A: `yield_to_comm()` → issue AR on `comm_stream` → `yield_to_compute()` - while A's AR is in flight on `comm_stream`, thread B's compute for the next layer keeps running on `compute_stream` 4. `dbo_enabled()` checks at runtime whether a yield context is live so the same `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` works as a vanilla AR when DBO is off. This matches the `comm_stream / compute_stream` design vLLM already uses for EP all-to-all DBO (`fused_moe/modular_kernel.py`, `prepare_finalize/deepep_ht.py`). What this PR does is **plug it into the dense TP all-reduce path**. ### What this PR changes 1. **TP AR yield wrapper** in `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`: issue the AR with `dbo_yield_and_switch_*` so it runs on `comm_stream` when DBO is active. Behaves as a vanilla AR otherwise. 2. **Custom-op registration** to survive `torch.compile`. AR is registered as `torch.ops.vllm.vllm_dbo_all_reduce`, which dynamo treats as opaque, so the runtime `dbo_enabled()` check survives tracing. 3. **DP=1 entry to the DBO scheduling path**: `coordinate_batch_across_dp` no longer early-exits on `dp_size==1`; the gate in `gpu_model_runner` becomes `num_ubatches > 1`; `gpu_ubatch_wrapper` accepts `dp_metadata=None`. This documentation was AI-assisted (Claude). We reviewed every line. ## Files changed 9 files, +153 / −37 lines. 0 model files. 0 C++/CUDA. 0 fusion-pass files. 0 new env vars (and 4 previously-required env vars folded into config). | File | + | − | Role | |---|---:|---:|---| | `vllm/distributed/communication_op.py` | 43 | 2 | DBO AR yield wrapper + always-on custom-op registration | | `vllm/v1/worker/dp_utils.py` | 37 | 2 | DP=1 fast path; pass through `num_scheduled_tokens_per_request` | | `vllm/v1/worker/ubatching.py` | 12 | 1 | Brief busy-spin before blocking yield wait | | `vllm/v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py` | 16 | 3 | `check_ubatch_thresholds` reads new gates | | `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` | 6 | 4 | `cache_key += ubid`; gate on `num_ubatches > 1` | | `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py` | 18 | 14 | Allow `dp_metadata=None` for DP=1 | | `vllm/config/vllm.py` | 11 | 11 | Loosen EP-only assert | | `vllm/config/parallel.py` | 4 | 0 | `dbo_prefill_min_seq_len: int = 2048` | | `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` | 6 | 0 | `--dbo-prefill-min-seq-len` CLI flag | ## Usage This PR is opt-in. No environment variables — all behavior is controlled by `LLM(...)` kwargs (or the equivalent `vllm serve` flags). The new public surface introduced by this PR is exactly **one** kwarg: | New (this PR) | Type | Default | Effect | |---|---|---:|---| | `ParallelConfig.dbo_prefill_min_seq_len` | `int` | `2048` | Skip DBO on prefill batches whose `max_prompt_len` is below this. Below the floor, DBO setup overhead dominates and the cell regresses. Set `0` to disable the gate. | CLI counterpart: `--dbo-prefill-min-seq-len `. The other flags below already exist in vLLM today; this PR makes them **actually deliver speedup when combined**, by fixing the torch.compile + DBO incompatibility and adding the dense-TP yield path. ### Minimal — turn the optimization on Three additional kwargs vs an unoptimized `LLM(...)` call: ```python from vllm import LLM from vllm.config import CompilationConfig from vllm.config.compilation import CompilationMode, CUDAGraphMode llm = LLM( model="Qwen/Qwen3-32B", tensor_parallel_size=4, dtype="bfloat16", enable_dbo=True, # existing flag — flip on compilation_config=CompilationConfig( # existing API mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE, cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE, ), ) ``` ### Tunable — recommended production config ```python llm = LLM( model="Qwen/Qwen3-32B", tensor_parallel_size=4, dtype="bfloat16", enable_dbo=True, # existing dbo_decode_token_threshold=8, # existing, tunable dbo_prefill_token_threshold=64, # existing, tunable dbo_prefill_min_seq_len=2048, # NEW (this PR), tunable; # 0 disables the gate compilation_config=CompilationConfig( # existing API mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE, cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE, ), async_scheduling=False, # existing flag; recommended # for prefill DBO (avoids # extra prefill chunking, # ~+1 pp speedup). gpu_memory_utilization=0.92, ) ``` CLI equivalent: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --enable-dbo \ --dbo-decode-token-threshold 99999 \ # disable DBO on decode --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 64 \ --dbo-prefill-min-seq-len 2048 \ # NEW (this PR) --compilation-config '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": 1}' ``` ## Test Plan ### Microbenchmark — prefill + e2e wall Each cell runs **one** LLM instance and measures both timings on it: - `max_tokens=1` × 10 reps → **prefill wall** (TTFT) - `max_tokens=128` × 10 reps → **e2e wall** (prefill + 127 decodes) Both `baseline` and `ours` use `mode=VLLM_COMPILE + cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE + async_scheduling=True` (vLLM defaults). The only delta is `enable_dbo` (and the three `dbo_*` knobs). Decode never ubatches: `dbo_decode_token_threshold=99999` (see Usage). Fresh `~/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache` per run. ```python # bench_pr.py import argparse, json, os, statistics, time E2E_MAX_TOKENS = 128 def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--config", required=True, choices=["baseline", "ours"]) ap.add_argument("--bs", type=int, required=True) ap.add_argument("--pl", type=int, required=True) ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=10) ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="./bench_results") args = ap.parse_args() os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARNING") from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams from vllm.config import CompilationConfig from vllm.config.compilation import CompilationMode, CUDAGraphMode extra = {} if args.config == "ours": extra = { "enable_dbo": True, "dbo_decode_token_threshold": 99999, # decode does NOT ubatch "dbo_prefill_token_threshold": 64, # dbo_prefill_min_seq_len uses default (2048). } llm = LLM( model="Qwen/Qwen3-32B", tensor_parallel_size=4, max_model_len=8192, max_num_batched_tokens=131072, enforce_eager=False, compilation_config=CompilationConfig( mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE, cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE), gpu_memory_utilization=0.92, dtype="bfloat16", disable_log_stats=True, enable_prefix_caching=False, **extra, ) sp_p = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1, ignore_eos=True) sp_e = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=E2E_MAX_TOKENS, ignore_eos=True) def make(seed): return [{"prompt_token_ids": list(range(1+i*args.pl+seed, 1+(i+1)*args.pl+seed))} for i in range(args.bs)] for _ in range(2): llm.generate(make(int(time.time()) % 1000), sp_p, use_tqdm=False) llm.generate(make(int(time.time()) % 1000), sp_e, use_tqdm=False) p_walls, e_walls = [], [] for r in range(args.reps): t0 = time.perf_counter() llm.generate(make(12345 + r * 1000), sp_p, use_tqdm=False) p_walls.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000) t0 = time.perf_counter() llm.generate(make(54321 + r * 1000), sp_e, e_sd = statistics.stdev(e_walls) if len(e_walls) > 1 else 0.0 out = { "config": args.config, "bs": args.bs, "pl": args.pl, "prefill_median_ms": p_med, "prefill_stdev_ms": p_sd, "e2e_median_ms": e_med, "e2e_stdev_ms": e_sd, "e2e_output_tps": (args.bs * E2E_MAX_TOKENS) / (e_med / 1000), "prefill_walls_ms": p_walls, "e2e_walls_ms": e_walls, } os.makedirs(args.out_dir, exist_ok=True) json.dump(out, open(f"{args.out_dir}/{args.config}_bs{args.bs}_pl{args.pl}.json", "w")) print(f"CSV,{args.config},bs={args.bs},pl={args.pl}," f"p={p_med:.2f}±{p_sd:.2f},e2e={e_med:.2f}±{e_sd:.2f}") if __name__ == signal.title: Move DP sync to a dedicated CUDA stream
signal.text: Async scheduling + (multi-node) DP + spec dec has bubbles caused by the DP synchronization steps because of the Gloo comms (NCCL falls back to Gloo for DP synchronization with async to avoid a GPU sync). This fix keeps NCCL comms but moves then onto a dedicated stream to avoid a gpu sync. As far as I can tell, this affects all `async_scheduling` + DP configs, but is aggravated by: - multi-node / high rank DP - speculative decoding (more DP syncs) This is why the regression only showed up on certain models, in the other cases the advantages from async were masking it. This fix improves performance across the board Results: MS4 (DP8) ISL=4096 | bsz | current TTFT(ms) | fix TTFT(ms) | delta TTFT | current decode TPS | fix decode TPS | delta TPS | | --: | -----------: | -----------: | ---------: | -----------: | -----------: | ---------: | | 1 | 434.0 | 386.9 | −10.9% | 216.9 | 269.8 | +24.4% | | 2 | 941.7 | 818.8 | −13.1% | 174.1 | 240.4 | +38.1% | | 4 | 1851.8 | 1423.9 | −23.1% | 214.3 | 234.5 | +9.4% | | 8 | 3532.0 | 2871.2 | −18.7% | 208.1 | 220.5 | +6.0% | | 16 | 7158.4 | 5618.7 | −21.5% | 211.9 | 202.8 | −4.3% | | 32 | 14169.3 | 11370.4 | −19.8% | 175.3 | 178.8 | +2.0% | | 64 | 28510.2 | 22422.6 | −21.4% | 121.2 | 126.5 | +4.3% | ML3 (DP32) ISL=4096 | bsz | current TTFT(ms) | fix TTFT(ms) | delta TTFT | current decode TPS | fix decode TPS | delta TPS | | --: | -----------: | -----------: | --------: | -----------: | -----------: | ---------: | | 1 | 1347.3 | 1242.7 | −7.8% | 73.2 | 103.2 | +41.0% | | 2 | 2713.0 | 2550.8 | −6.0% | 70.8 | 99.5 | +40.4% | | 4 | 5368.6 | 5071.1 | −5.5% | 74.8 | 92.8 | +24.1% | | 8 | 10880.0 | 10295.0 | −5.4% | 75.7 | 76.0 | +0.5% | | 16 | 21699.0 | 20628.2 | −4.9% | 62.6 | 55.1 | −12.0% | | 32 | 43062.0 | 40946.3 | −4.9% | 45.0 | 42.4 | −5.6% | | 64 | 73615.7 | 69112.0 | −6.1% | 26.3 | 26.7 | +1.5% | Traces: ms4 sync w/ 1.5ms bubble ms4 async w/ 5.1ms bubble ms4 fix w/ 1.5ms bubble ml3 sync w/ 3ms bubble ml3 async w/ 15ms bubble ml3 fix w/ 0ms bubble

signal.title: fix: prevent PyNvVideoCodec decoder slot limit bypass via ClassVar shadowing
signal.text: Move mutable decoder-pool state (_decoder_slots, _active_decoder_slots, _decoder_slot_cond, _max_decoder_slots) out of ClassVar attributes on PyNvVideoCodecVideoBackendMixin into a module-level _PyNvDecoderPool singleton. This prevents subclass augmented assignment (cls._active += 1) from creating independent shadow counters per concrete class, which allowed multiple subclasses to independently exceed the configured process-wide hw_decoders limit.
signal.author: jperezdealgaba

signal.title: [Model] Use native packed audio attention for Qwen2.5-Omni to remove standalone flash-attn dependency
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR replaces the Qwen2.5-Omni audio tower's standalone `flash_attn`/HF attention dependency with a vLLM-native implementation backed by `MMEncoderAttention`. The audio tower now follows the native Qwen-style structure more closely: - uses packed `QKVParallelLinear` and `RowParallelLinear` - remaps HF `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` weights into packed vLLM `qkv` - preserves HF behavior for the biasless `k_proj` by zeroing the packed K-bias shard - returns audio features as a tensor directly, matching the Qwen3-Omni audio tower call pattern This removes the standalone `flash_attn` dependency from the Qwen2.5-Omni thinker path while keeping audio attention on vLLM's native multimodal attention backend. ## Test Plan - [x] Compile the modified model and test files. - [x] Run focused Qwen2.5-Omni audio tower unit tests. - [x] Run real offline GPU multimodal inference with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B`. - [x] Run OpenAI-compatible `vllm serve` multimodal request with audio + image input. - [x] Confirm the Qwen2.5-Omni thinker path no longer imports standalone `flash_attn`. ## Test Result ```bash python -m py_compile \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_omni_thinker.py \ tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni_audio_tower.py ``` Passed. ```bash pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni_audio_tower.py ``` Result on NVIDIA L40S: ```text 5 passed ``` Offline real multimodal inference with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B` on NVIDIA L40S completed successfully and produced a coherent audio+image response. OpenAI-compatible server validation: ```text POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP 200 The audio is a synthetic tone, and the image contains a red square and a blue circle. ```

signal.title: [Quant][MTP] Reuse packed FP8 logits inputs
signal.text: ## Purpose Fuse the sparse DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5.2 MTP layer's final all-reduce and RMSNorm with packed FP8 quantization for its shared LM head. The draft layer returns two deliberately different values: - a packed `QuantizedActivation` for logits projection; and - the post-final-norm BF16 hidden state recycled into the next MTP position. The logits processor and both autoregressive speculators preserve and index this contract without unpacking and requantizing it. ## Dependencies - #51938: select/register the sparse MTP architecture - #51939: DeepGEMM block-linear prequantized-input contract - #51942: all-reduce/RMSNorm/packed-FP8 producer The branch contains only the seven-file MTP integration diff against `main`. Until #51942 lands, isolated mypy reports the expected missing collective helper. ## Duplicate-work check No issue number was provided. I searched open PRs for `DeepSeek V3.2 fused norm quant MTP`. The only exact prior implementation was the superseded draft #51936. ## Tests The portions independent of the missing prerequisite symbol pass directly: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/fusion/test_quant_activation_contract.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py -q # 23 passed ``` On the integrated branch: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v32/test_sequence_parallel.py -q # 5 passed ``` All hooks other than the expected prerequisite-related mypy error pass. ## Model evaluation Two-node GB200, TP=8, C1, random 8K input / 1K output, MTP=3, ten measured prompts, temperature 0: | Model | Overall | Position 0 | Position 1 | Position 2 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 | 83.47% | 90.83% | 83.00% | 76.57% | | nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 | 89.82% | 93.79% | 90.15% | 85.53% | Both runs completed all ten prompts without failures. ## AI assistance disclosure This change was developed with OpenAI Codex assistance. This is a blocked draft PR; the human submitter must review every changed line and confirm they understand and can defend the change before marking it ready.
